author: pgsharma
body:
> Part of epic #151 — Phase 3 grounding singletons. Closes #148.

## What

Adds `SamGovItemSource` (`src/metalworks/research/sources/samgov.py`) — the marquee Phase-3 grounding singleton — a `yields_units` `ItemSource` over the **SAM.gov Opportunities API v2** (`https://api.sam.gov/opportunities/v2/search`).

Public procurement is the one B2B layer nothing else in the corpus reaches: government buyers post explicit unmet needs **with a dollar value and a deadline attached, named** (the contracting agency). A solicitation is a self-representing demand artifact — verbatim statement of need + stable permalink + attributable author — so cite-or-die is a feature here, not a problem.

- **pull** runs the brief's terms as the `title` keyword search over the posted-date window (`postedFrom`/`postedTo`, `MM/dd/yyyy`, one-year cap). Each notice → `CorpusRecord` (title + solicitation summary; `uiLink` permalink; contracting agency `fullParentPathName` as the "author"). `yields_units=True` (ranker measures breadth by distinct agency/domain, like ATS/web); `comments_for` returns `None`.
- **Signal** — a notice carrying an award attaches `{"rfp_budget": <award.amount>}`, the literal willingness-to-pay magnitude. It is **OMITTED (never 0.0)** when absent. `rfp_budget` was already registered `is_magnitude=True` — **no new `register_signal`**.
- **Auth** — free registered key (`SAM_GOV_API_KEY`): `auth="key"`, `access="free_key"`, `env=("SAM_GOV_API_KEY",)`, passed when present; the selector's access gate skips the source cleanly when unset.
- As a `yields_units` grounding source it is **rule-5 exempt** (its only signal is the magnitude `rfp_budget`) — verified by the conformance sweep.
- **`description` is a SAM.gov URL**, not inline prose, so the quotable body is the title + solicitation number; the description URL is kept in `extra` for a downstream deep-fetch.

### Registration & scope
- Registered via the single `BUILTIN_SOURCE_MODULES` map (#139) — **one place**. Verdict band untouched.
- `docs/sources.md` regenerated (`gen_sources_md --check` green).
- **USAspending award-$ overlay:** left as a docstring TODO — it's a lane-② `MagnitudeProvider` (a separate source shape), not part of the grounding deliverable. EU TED is a fast-follow on this same shape.

## Tests
`tests/test_source_samgov.py` (offline, stub httpx client): search→notice→unit with agency as author, `rfp_budget` attached / omitted-not-zero, keyword+window+`api_key` request shape, unkeyed-skip, one-year window clamp, `check_item_source` conformance, registry resolution, plus a `network`-marked live smoke. Conformance sweep + `test_source_spec` extended to include `samgov`.

## Gate — BOTH matrices green

**1. `--all-extras`:** `ruff check` ✓ · `ruff format --check` ✓ (240 files) · `pyright` ✓ (0 errors) · `pytest -q` ✓ (**1017 passed, 11 deselected**) · `gen_ts_types --check` ✓ (89 interfaces + 5 enums) · `gen_sources_md --check` ✓ (11 sources).

**2. bare venv** (`uv venv /tmp/sam-bare`, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`): `pytest tests/test_source_samgov.py tests/test_conformance_sweep.py -q` ✓ (**30 passed, 1 deselected**).

author: erickmobltda
body:
## The bug
The sign-in modal couldn't be used — typing in the **email/password** fields did nothing (see screenshot). Root cause: the practice screen registers a **global `window` keydown listener** and calls `preventDefault()` on every printable key (plus Backspace/Tab). With a form field focused, the lesson swallowed the keystrokes before they could reach the field. The custom-text settings box had the same problem.

## The fix
Add an `isEditableTarget` guard: the lesson's key handler now **returns early** when the event target — or the focused element — is an `input`, `textarea`, `select`, or `contenteditable` element. Those keystrokes flow to the field normally; the game only captures keys when nothing editable is focused.

Extracted to `src/components/dom.ts` so it's unit-tested in isolation.

## Verification
- ✅ `tsc` clean · ✅ `eslint` clean · ✅ **36 tests pass** (added `dom.test.ts`)
- ✅ In-browser:
  - Email field focused → keystrokes produced **0 lesson hits** (field gets the input; no more `preventDefault` stealing it)
  - No field focused → typing the lesson still registers hits normally (no regression)

author: mergify[bot]
body:
Closes #2186 (also fixes the user-visible failure mode reported in #1558).

## Summary

Speeds up `crm.api.session.get_users` from ~11 s to ~64 ms on large sites and unblocks the CRM frontend on initial load.

Three independently reviewable commits, each with measurable impact and no scope creep:

1. **`perf(session): batch N+1 lookups in get_users`** — replace per-user `frappe.get_roles()` and `db.exists("CRM Telephony Agent")` with two batched queries. Also fixes a `is_telphony_agent` → `is_telephony_agent` typo on the frontend that silently broke `isTelephonyAgent()` for every user.
2. **`perf(session): drop 173k-IN-list filters; safety-net Administrator`** — drop the per-call IN lists from the batched queries (they were serializing ~5 MB of SQL text on large sites for no benefit) and add an explicit `Administrator → System Manager` classification since the Has Role child table is not guaranteed to contain it on every install.
3. **`feat(session): split UI-blocking vs background user fetch`** — `get_users()` now returns only users with a CRM role by default (filtered at SQL level). A new optional `include_all=True` param (honored only for System Manager — silent downgrade otherwise) returns the full enabled user list. The frontend uses the fast call to unblock the UI immediately, then fires the full-list call on `requestIdleCallback`. A new `get_user_info(users)` endpoint resolves individual user records on demand for the race window between first paint and the background fetch landing.

Commits 1 and 2 have **no API contract change** — maintainers who want only the perf win can stop there. Commit 3 changes the default return shape of `get_users()` (documented below).

## Why

Root cause and reproduction documented in detail at #2186; same symptom previously reported at #1558. On a site with ~173 k enabled `User` records (real customer scenario, where bulk-imported contacts/employees landed as User rows on a shared Frappe/ERPNext/HRMS site), the CRM frontend either hangs on a white screen for ~11 s or, worse, redirects to "Not Permitted" because the `get_users` response never arrives in time.

Root cause is a tight per-user loop in `crm/api/session.py`:

```python
for user in users:                                  # 173k iterations
    user.roles = frappe.get_roles(user.name)        # ← 1 DB hit per user
    ...
    user.is_telephony_agent = frappe.db.exists(     # ← 1 DB hit per user
        "CRM Telephony Agent", {"user": user.name}
    )
```

Each iteration also runs role-priority logic, builds Python dicts, and so on. Even with `frappe.get_roles` cached in redis after the first hit, the function:

- Issues ~173 k SQL calls
- Returns a ~54 MiB JSON payload to System Manager sessions (the per-row `roles` array via `frappe.get_roles()` blows up the payload further on Administrator)
- Takes ~11 s of wall-clock time
- Blocks the entire CRM frontend on initial load

## Benchmark progression

Same site, same data (173,539 enabled users, 33 CRM users), median of 3 warm runs:

| Stage | Admin wall-clock | Sales Mgr wall-clock | SQL calls | Admin payload |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 10,760 ms | 10,884 ms | 173,540 | 53.6 MiB |
| After commit 1 (batch N+1) | 2,185 ms | 2,407 ms | 3 | 52.3 MiB |
| After commit 2 (drop IN lists) | 764 ms | 773 ms | 3 | 52.3 MiB |
| **After commit 3 (fast path, default)** | **64 ms** | **66 ms** | **4** | **59 KB** |
| After commit 3 (`include_all=1`, background) | 789 ms | n/a (downgraded) | 4 | 52.3 MiB |
| `get_user_info(2 names)` | 0.2 ms | 0.2 ms | 1 | 297 B |

**Net effect on user-visible behavior:** CRM frontend is interactive in ~64 ms instead of ~11 s — **~168× faster** — and the background fetch costs the *same* server time as commit 2 but doesn't block the UI.

## API contract

| Endpoint | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `crm.api.session.get_users()` (no args) | `(all_enabled_users, crm_users)` for System Manager; `(crm_users, crm_users)` otherwise | `(crm_users, crm_users)` for everyone |
| `crm.api.session.get_users(include_all=True)` | n/a | `(all_enabled_users, crm_users)` for System Manager; `(crm_users, crm_users)` otherwise (silent downgrade — no escalation) |
| `crm.api.session.get_user_info(users)` | n/a | New whitelisted endpoint, gated by CRM-role membership, capped at 200 names per call |

The breaking surface is small: the only known internal consumer of the full `allUsers` list is `EmailMultiSelect.vue`, updated in the same commit to read from the store-level computed (which transparently picks up the background fetch).

External callers of `crm.api.session.get_users` that need the full list should now pass `include_all=1` explicitly.

## Why the System-Manager carve-out was the wrong default

Pre-PR, `get_users()` returned the full enabled-user table to System Manager sessions but only `crm_users` to everyone else. This carve-out's intent was to populate the frontend's `usersByName` cache for arbitrary-email profile lookups (comment authors, doc owners, email recipient typeahead, etc.).

In practice that cache is only needed for the small subset of users that are *referenced* in CRM activity — usually a few dozen. Shipping the entire user table up front to populate a cache that may never be fully used isn't a great trade at any scale, and at 173 k users it becomes a denial-of-service vector against System Managers themselves.

The new design: send the small, blocking part synchronously; send the large, optional part asynchronously after first paint; fall back to point lookups for the race window. Costs the same total work for huge sites and is dramatically cheaper for typical sites where most users in the table never get referenced.

## Notes for reviewers

- The Administrator special-case in commit 2 (always classified as System Manager regardless of Has Role contents) is intentional — it mirrors Frappe's existing `frappe.get_roles("Administrator")` behavior which returns every role implicitly. Without this, sites where Administrator's Has Role child table doesn't explicitly contain "System Manager" would lock the admin out of CRM. This same correctness issue exists today in the pre-PR code for any code path that doesn't go through `frappe.get_roles()`, so it's worth catching here.
- The IN-list drop in commit 2 fetches a few extra rows from `Has Role` for users not in our in-memory set (e.g. role assignments for disabled users). These sit harmlessly in a dict that nobody looks up. The memory cost is a few KB.
- The frontend `getUser()` change preserves backwards compatibility — it still returns synchronously, the cached object is reactive, and stub records get upgraded in place when records resolve. No consumer needs to await anything.
- `get_user_info` is capped at 200 names per call to bound enumeration cost. The coalesced microtask-batched flush from the frontend stays well under that on any realistic page.
- Commit boundaries are intentionally split so that maintainers can stop at commit 1 (pure perf, no contract change), commit 2 (more perf, still no contract change), or take the full commit 3 (perf + UX + new endpoint + contract change). Each is independently mergeable.

body:
Builds on the merged #604 (osv Dockerfile) and #611 (the `dockerfile` input). This is **wrangle's first internal use of `build_and_publish_container`**, and the thing that finally ships an image.

## What
A workflow that builds + publishes + attests `ghcr.io/tomhennen/wrangle/osv` from `tools/osv/Dockerfile`, passing the new **`dockerfile`** input so the build uses the **repo root** as context (the Dockerfile builds osv-scanner from `tools/go.mod` and bundles the adapter, which reads `lib/sanitize.sh` — all outside `tools/osv/`).

## Triggers
- `push` to `main` touching the osv Dockerfile / its sources (`tools/go.mod`, `lib/sanitize.sh`, …) → builds + **attests** (`main-and-tags`).
- tags → same.
- `workflow_dispatch` → ad-hoc build/push.

## Bootstrap (publishing the first image)
The Dockerfile is already on `main`, so a path-triggered push won't re-fire. After this merges, to publish the first **attested** image either cut a tag or push a no-op change to a watched path; `workflow_dispatch` gives an immediate (unattested) image if you just want to unblock PR2's wiring. I'll drive whichever you prefer.

## Why it matters
Once a real `ghcr.io/tomhennen/wrangle/osv@sha256:…` exists, **PR2** (run.sh `docker run` + the tool catalog) becomes writable-and-green — that's the last piece.

## Security
Requests `packages: write` + `id-token: write` + `attestations: write` for the L3 publish/attest, mirroring the documented container-caller permission set. The publish workflow itself only runs on `main`/tags/dispatch (never on PRs).

author: ljagged
body:
## What

PR 2 of the v1 robo-player: the `src/bot/` module — a handcrafted-evaluation alpha-beta search that consumes the rules engine as a library and reasons only from the **honest** fog-filtered view a human seat sees.

> PR 1 (#11) is already merged into `main`; this PR targets `main` and its diff is just the bot module.

## Modules

- **`view.ts`** — `gameStateFromView` reconstructs a searchable `GameState` from the seat's `GameView` + a public-state bundle (`config`, `history`, `castling`, `enPassant`) + the bot's observation history. Own phased pieces exact; enemy phased pieces exist only if observed, with **assumed** timers. Rings collapse assumptions to certainty, resolving origin collisions to the earliest pending return (**F4**).
- **`evaluate.ts`** — material + light piece-square, plus variant terms: time-indexed phased material (§5.1), phase-aware threats (§5.2/§5.3), ring-near-king (§5.4).
- **`search.ts`** — negamax αβ + iterative deepening + deterministic fixed-depth mode. Terminal scoring via engine `status` (inherits §4.1). **TT key = `positionKey` + phased-state digest** (positionKey alone is unsound for search — **F2**).
- **`index.ts`** — `chooseAction(view, publicState, seatEvents, opts)`, routed through the normal `makeMove`/`phaseOut` path in PR 3.

## Honesty boundary

Enforced via a property sweep (no observations ⇒ never invents enemy phased) and an injection-invariance test. Bot-side analogue of the engine privacy invariant.

## Tests — 22 new (120 total)

`view` 10 · `evaluate` 5 · `search` 5 (F2 + determinism) · `index` 2. test/typecheck/build all green.

## Corrections

- Decision A input contract (build from view + public bundle, never touch enemy `state.phased`).
- Spec §7.4: a single phase-out can't deliver a ringed check; reframed as a discovered-check phase-out mate.

Deferred: F5 runtime spike + weight tuning (pre-PR-3). Minor bump `0.3.1 → 0.4.0`.

body:
﻿## What changed

Fixes the co-op roll bug where the wrong browser could show/click a stale dice modal and the resolved DM narration treated the shared check like a solo roll.

- Client now only opens the dice modal for the character whose `characterId` matches `actingCharacterId`.
- Partner screens clear any stale dice modal and stay in co-op waiting state until the resolved narration arrives.
- Local temporary awaiting-roll events now carry `actingCharacterId`, `rollContext`, and scene image metadata so the direct API path behaves like realtime.
- Co-op roll resolution no longer delegates to the solo resolver. It now generates a shared roll outcome with both characters and both submitted actions in the prompt.
- Added regression coverage proving the co-op roll outcome prompt preserves both player actions.

## Why

Root cause: co-op awaiting-roll setup was saved for both players, but the direct action-response UI path did not check who actually owned the roll. Then the server resolved the accepted roll through the solo roll path, so the partner's contribution could disappear from the outcome.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test --prefix server`
- `npm run test:playtest`
- `npm run build`
- `git diff --check`

body:
Fixes #1603

## Problem
list_directory_for_agent and read_file_for_agent use std::fs blocking calls (read_dir, read_to_string). When called directly from the async execute_tool function, they block the tokio runtime thread, potentially starving other async tasks.

## Fix
Wrap both function calls in tokio::task::spawn_blocking to move the blocking I/O off the async runtime threads. The owned data (path string, vault_root PathBuf) is cloned and moved into the blocking closure.

author: the-9880
body:
## Summary

Relates to https://github.com/grafana/synthetic-monitoring/issues/541

Implements the agent-side scraper behaviour for tenant-controlled label prefix removal. Depends on #1878 (`feat(proto)`), which must merge first.

## What this adds

**`TenantLabelMode` provider — separate from `LabelsLimiter`**

Follows the same pattern as `TenantCals` for cost attribution labels. A new `internal/labelmode` package exposes a `LabelMode` struct backed by a `TenantProvider` to return the label mode of a tenant by ID.

**`buildUserLabels()` — mode-aware label emission**

Accepts an explicit `LabelMode`. Behaviour by mode:

- `PREFIXED` (0, default): `env=prod` → `label_env="prod"` (unchanged)
- `DUAL_WRITE` (1): all prefixed forms first, then all un-prefixed — `[label_foo, label_bar, foo, bar]`. 
  - If the label limit for Loki is exceeded, remaining labels spill into the `StructuredMetadata`.
  - The ordering ensures the `label_`-prefixed labels are retained to avoid breaking dependencies on indexed labels.
- `UNPREFIXED` (2): `env=prod` → `env="prod"` only

Reserved system label names are **not filtered**. The API enforces that tenants clear all reserved-name collisions before entering `DUAL_WRITE`, so any post-migration collision can only be caused by a new label we add to the reserved set. In that case the user-defined value should win — preserving existing tenant behaviour is preferable to silently overwriting/breaking it.

**`userLabelsForExecution()` — user labels on check execution metrics**

In `DUAL_WRITE` and `UNPREFIXED` modes, un-prefixed user labels are appended to the shared label set applied to all check execution metrics (`probe_success`, `probe_duration_seconds`, `probe_http_*`, etc.). Only the un-prefixed form is added to execution metrics in `DUAL_WRITE` — the dual-write of both prefixed and un-prefixed forms applies only to `sm_check_info` and Loki streams.

Enables label-based cost attribution and direct PromQL filtering without a join to `sm_check_info`, e.g. `rate(probe_success{env="prod"}[5m])`.

**Log label overflow to `StructuredMetadata`**

When the combined system and user label count would exceed Loki's 15-stream-label cap, excess user labels spill into `logproto.Entry.StructuredMetadata` rather than being silently truncated. Structured metadata is queryable in LogQL but not indexed as stream labels.

**Unit tests**

- `TestBuildUserLabels_*` — all three modes, check-overrides-probe, DUAL_WRITE ordering (`[label_foo, label_bar, foo, bar]`), reserved name passthrough (user value preserved)
- `TestUserLabelsForExecution_*` — PREFIXED returns nil, DUAL_WRITE/UNPREFIXED return un-prefixed only, reserved names pass through, check overrides probe

## State machine note

The state machine (`PREFIXED → DUAL_WRITE` irreversible, `DUAL_WRITE ↔ UNPREFIXED` reversible) is enforced by the API, not the agent. The agent reads `LabelMode` from the tenant cache and applies it — no transition logic lives here.

## Stale series note

When a tenant enters `DUAL_WRITE`, existing execution metric series (without user labels) become stale and new series (with user labels) are created. This is expected — tenants entering `DUAL_WRITE` are in a label migration context and should anticipate schema changes to their series.

author: troopdegen
body:
## What & why
**PR2 = Phase 3** of the Competitor Pricing Sources plan — a **real Amazon MX competitor source** that scrapes `amazon.com.mx` and parses with cheerio, plugged into the **PR1 `CompetitorSource` seam** (#39). This is the ToS-sensitive scraper, isolated in its own PR for review.

It lifts competitor coverage past Mercado Libre's ~24% ceiling — but **eyes open**: from the Railway datacenter IP, Amazon yield will likely be low (CAPTCHA/blocks). That's *expected*; the design's first job is to **fail soft** so Amazon never breaks a run, and the `coverage-probe` extension lets us *measure* the real lift before investing in residential proxies.

## Architecture — pure parser + fail-soft shell
- **`parseAmazonSearchHtml()` — a PURE function** (unit-tested against 4 saved fixture HTML files, zero network): detects CAPTCHA/bot-check pages, picks the best card by **title-token overlap** (not lowest price), parses Mexican price format, classifies `ok | blocked | no_result | parse_error`.
- **`createAmazonMxSource()` — the fetch shell**: realistic UA, `es-MX`, AbortSignal, single attempt, optional `proxyUrl`. Returns `null` on any non-200 / block / miss / network error — **never throws** (triple-guarded: parser try/catch, lookup try/catch, and the PR1 gather-loop `.catch`).

## Wiring — opt-in per tenant, fail-soft
- Registered as integration `amazon-mx` (`category: 'competitor'`): registry + re-exports + `IntegrationClients` merge (`CompetitorSource`).
- Worker factory is **opt-in**: throws unless `${PREFIX}_AMAZON_MX_ENABLED` is truthy → **disabled by default** → resolver "not configured" → the workflow's `try { ctx.integration('amazon-mx') }` simply omits it.
- `pricing-draft` picks it up via the existing §3.4 composition. When enabled, Amazon quotes flow through the **unchanged PR1 min-accepted aggregation** (`competitorMinMxn` / `chosenSource` / `summary.bySource`); when disabled or blocked, the run is **byte-identical to ML-only**. Apply chain untouched (additive).
- `coverage-probe.ts` now reports **ML / Amazon / combined** coverage.

## Adversarial verification (and 2 real bugs caught + fixed)
A 5-skeptic panel cleared fail-soft, factory gating/blast-radius, pricing-draft non-regression, and deps/no-live-network — and **caught two real parser defects**, both fixed with regression tests:
1. **Strikethrough list price could win over the sale price** → overstated competitor. Fixed: take the lowest *non-strikethrough* `.a-offscreen` price.
2. **A zero-overlap results page emitted the first priced card as a false match.** Fixed: require title overlap ≥ 1, else fail soft to `no_result`.

## Tests (870 green, 15/15 typecheck)
17 parser/shell tests (incl. the 2 regressions); +4 worker factory tests (disabled-by-default, opt-in, blast-radius); registry count updated. **No test hits the live network** — fixtures + stubbed `fetch` only.

## Out of scope (deferred)
Residential-proxy infra (the real yield unlock — a separate cost/vendor decision); per-tenant DB-driven source selection; the productized report download path + glass-box run view.

author: opariffazman
body:
## Problem
Installed PWA shows a blank screen + the browser's native "no internet" page when offline, and a direct load/refresh of `/trends` (or `/cuts`) returns `{"detail":"Not Found"}`.

## Root cause
`server/app.py` serves the static build via `StaticFiles(html=True)`, which only maps `/` → `index.html` and serves **exact** files — the prerendered routes `/trends`, `/cuts` 404. That 404 is fatal twice:
- **Online:** a direct/refresh load of `/trends` 404s.
- **Offline:** the Workbox service worker precaches those routes (keyed extensionless: `{url:"trends"}`, `{url:"cuts"}`). One 404 during `install` rejects the whole precache → the SW never activates → never controls the page → offline navigation hits the network → browser "no internet" page. Verified in a live headless browser: `registration: null`, `controller: null`, and a partial precache missing exactly `/`, `/trends`, `/cuts`.

Invisible to CI because `web/audit-responsive.mjs` runs against `vite preview` (which resolves those routes); only the production FastAPI server 404s them — a dev/prod parity gap.

## Fix
`SPAStaticFiles` does `try_files`: exact file → `<path>.html` → SPA shell `index.html`. Server-only change, no web rebuild. API routes stay registered before the mount, so they're matched first and never hit the fallback.

## Test
`server/test_app.py::test_prerendered_route_and_spa_fallback` — `/trends` → 200 (serves `trends.html`), unknown route → SPA shell, `/healthz` + `/data/app.json` unaffected. All server + integration tests pass (12).

## Deploy
Rebuild + redeploy the `statement-app` image (server-only; `build/` unchanged). Then one online load per device lets the now-succeeding SW install + precache; offline works after that.

body:
Closes #15
Closes #24

## Was

Macht die Preview lesbar: Text ist markier-/kopierbar und per Ctrl+F durchsuchbar, ohne die Checkbox-Interaktion zu verlieren — plus drei Settings, die das neue Verhalten konfigurierbar machen (Defaults reproduzieren das Verhalten exakt). Ein PR, schliesst beide Issues (geteilte Preview-Oberflaeche).

- **#15 — Selektion/Copy + Toggle-Gating (Variante B).** `media/webview.css`: `body` traegt `user-select: text`; `user-select: none` bleibt nur auf `#minimap` und neu auf den Checkbox-Inputs (`.task-row input[type=checkbox]`, `input.cell-task`). `media/webview.js`: die Toggle-Entscheidung faellt zur Klickzeit statt per CSS-Sperre. Direkter Klick auf einen Checkbox-Input toggelt immer; ein blanker Klick im Row-/Label-Bereich oder in einer Einzel-Checkbox-`td` toggelt nur, wenn `getSelection()` leer ist UND `e.detail === 1`. Batch-Gesten (Shift/Ctrl) auf der Checkbox.
- **#24 — In-Preview-Suche, erst nativ.** `enableFindWidget: true` an beiden `WebviewPanel`-Pfaden in `src/extension.js`. Ctrl+F wird von VS Code automatisch verdrahtet; der Keydown-Handler faengt nur `Escape`.
- **Drei Settings (`contributes.configuration`, Default = obiges Verhalten 1:1):**
  - `markdownWorkbench.preview.textSelection` (bool, default `true`): `false` → `user-select: none` wie vor 0.30.0, Klick irgendwo in der Zeile toggelt ungated.
  - `markdownWorkbench.preview.taskBatchSelect` (`checkbox` default / `row`): wo Shift/Ctrl-Batch feuert. `checkbox` haelt es auf der Checkbox (Shift im Label = Textselektion); `row` feuert ueberall in der Zeile (Preis: Shift im Label verlaengert keine Textselektion mehr).
  - `markdownWorkbench.preview.taskRowTextCursor` (bool, default `false`, nur bei `textSelection: true`): Text-Cursor auf der `.task-row`, Pointer-Hand auf der Checkbox.
  - Konfig laeuft ueber `configuredViewConfig()` (`src/views.js`, defensive Defaults) und die bestehende `type:'config'`-Message; der Webview spiegelt die Flags auf Body-Klassen (`mw-no-text-select`, `mw-task-text-cursor`) und einen `bareClickToggles`-Wrapper.

## Was bewusst nicht geändert wurde

- Default-Verhalten bleibt exakt #25 — alle drei Settings sind reines Opt-out/Opt-in, kein Migrationspfad.
- Keine Custom-Suche (Minimap-Match-Marker, Task-Filter, eigene Highlight-DOM) — erst bei nachgewiesenem Bedarf.
- Cursor-Setting gilt nur fuer `.task-row`, nicht fuer Einzel-Checkbox-Tabellenzellen (s. Offene Fragen).
- Copy/Suche arbeiten auf dem gerenderten DOM-Text, nicht auf dem Markdown-Quelltext.
- Version/Lockfile bleiben `0.30.0`; CHANGELOG-Abschnitt `## 0.30.0` erweitert, kein neuer Header.

## Entscheidungen

- `docs/DECISIONS.md #28`: Variante B — Toggle geometrisch/zustandsbasiert gegated (`canToggleFromBareClick`), Batch checkbox-getriggert statt CSS-Sperre.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md #29`: In-Preview-Suche erst nativ via `enableFindWidget`.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md #30`: die drei Knoebe mit Tradeoff-Matrix `textSelection` x `taskBatchSelect` — `true/row` ist eine bewusste Shift-Kollision (Batch ueber Label kostet die Label-Textselektion); Cursor-Regel nur bei `textSelection` an, da ein Text-Caret auf unselektierbarem Text luegen wuerde.

## Wie getestet

- `npm test` — 270 grün (24 neu): #15/#24-Basis plus Config-Defaults + Pass-Through, `bareClickToggles`-Unit (Selektion aus → immer toggeln; an → delegiert an `canToggleFromBareClick`), Body-Klassen nach `config` (`mw-no-text-select` nur bei `textSelection:false`; `mw-task-text-cursor` nur bei `textSelection:true` UND `taskRowTextCursor:true`), Row-Batch ueber Label vs. Checkbox-Default-Plain-Toggle, `textSelection:false` toggelt trotz Selektion/Doppelklick, CSS-Contract der neuen Selektoren.
- `npm run coverage` (CI-Gate), `npm run build`, `npm run bundle-smoke` — alle grün.

## Offene Fragen

- **Drag-Ende-auf-Row-Kante:** zuerst der simple `getSelection()`-Check; ein `mousedown`-Range-Vergleich nur bei nachweisbarem Fehlklick (aus #15).
- **On-Device-Sichttest ist Pflicht und nur manuell pruefbar:** die vier Matrix-Kombinationen (`textSelection` x `taskBatchSelect`), die Cursor-Umschaltung (`.task-row` Text-Caret, Checkbox Pointer), Selektion/Copy von Absatz/Code/Tabelle, Checkbox-Toggle + Batch, Ctrl+F in Custom-Editor und Side-Preview (inkl. Editor-Suche bei fokussiertem Quell-Editor).
- **Cursor-Setting fuer Tabellenzellen:** Einzel-Checkbox-`td`s folgen dem `taskRowTextCursor` vorerst NICHT (nur `.task-row` im Scope) — bei Bedarf nachziehbar.

`run  [--reuse-test (optional)pipeline-id --disable-fail-fast --skip-test --stage-list "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx" --gpu-type "A30, H100_PCIe" --test-backend "pytorch, cpp" --add-multi-gpu-test --only-multi-gpu-test --disable-multi-gpu-test --post-merge --extra-stage "H100_PCIe-TensorRT-Post-Merge-1, xxx" --detailed-log --debug(experimental)]`

Launch build/test pipelines. All previously running jobs will be killed.

`--reuse-test (optional)pipeline-id ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Allow the new pipeline to reuse build artifacts and skip successful test stages from a specified pipeline or the last pipeline if no pipeline-id is indicated. If the Git commit ID has changed, this option will be always ignored. The DEFAULT behavior of the bot is to reuse build artifacts and successful test results from the last pipeline.

`--disable-reuse-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Explicitly prevent the pipeline from reusing build artifacts and skipping successful test stages from a previous pipeline. Ensure that all builds and tests are run regardless of previous successes.

`--disable-fail-fast ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Disable fail fast on build/tests/infra failures.

`--skip-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Skip all test stages, but still run build stages, package stages and sanity check stages. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--stage-list "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the specified test stages. Examples: "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx". Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--gpu-type "A30, H100_PCIe"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the test stages on the specified GPU types. Examples: "A30, H100_PCIe". Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--test-backend "pytorch, cpp"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Skip test stages which don't match the specified backends. Only support [pytorch, cpp, tensorrt, triton]. Examples: "pytorch, cpp" (does not run test stages with tensorrt or triton backend). Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub pipeline status.

`--only-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the multi-GPU tests. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--disable-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Disable the multi-GPU tests. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--add-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Force run the multi-GPU tests in addition to running L0 pre-merge pipeline.

`--post-merge ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Run the L0 post-merge pipeline instead of the ordinary L0 pre-merge pipeline.

`--extra-stage "H100_PCIe-TensorRT-Post-Merge-1, xxx"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Run the ordinary L0 pre-merge pipeline and specified test stages. Examples: --extra-stage "H100_PCIe-TensorRT-Post-Merge-1, xxx".

`--detailed-log ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Enable flushing out all logs to the Jenkins console. This will significantly increase the log volume and may slow down the job.

`--debug ` *(OPTIONAL)* : **Experimental feature**. Enable access to the CI container for debugging purpose. Note: Specify exactly one stage in the `stage-list` parameter to access the appropriate container environment. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

For guidance on mapping tests to stage names, see `docs/source/reference/ci-overview.md`
and the `scripts/test_to_stage_mapping.py` helper.

Kill all running builds associated with pull request.

### skip

Skip testing for latest commit on pull request. `--comment "Reason for skipping build/test"` is required. IMPORTANT NOTE: This is dangerous since lack of user care and validation can cause top of tree to break.

author: jeanzinho509
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: A path traversal vulnerability existed in the `deleteImage` endpoint of `server/controllers/upload.controller.js`. User input (`imageUrl`) was parsed and appended using `path.join()`, allowing an attacker to pass payloads like `/uploads/../../../../etc/passwd` to delete arbitrary files on the server.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could delete critical system files, application source code, or other users' files, potentially leading to denial of service or further exploitation.
🔧 Fix: Replaced `path.join()` with `path.resolve()` for both the upload directory and the target file path. Added a strict security boundary check using `startsWith(resolvedUploadDir + path.sep)` to ensure the resolved file path remains strictly inside the intended upload directory.
✅ Verification: Tested locally by passing malicious payloads (e.g. `/uploads/../../../../etc/passwd`), which now correctly return a `403 Forbidden: Invalid file path`. Valid deletion requests still return `200 OK`.

## Summary

Adds the admin panel Aimee requested and moves the generator off static GitHub Pages onto a SQLite-backed Next.js server app (deployable to Railway).

- **Admin panel (`/admin`)** to add/remove dropdown options (URL Handle, UTM Source, UTM Medium), edit per-field tooltips, and edit per-source auto-fill OTG/TBZ campaign IDs.

| `SITE_PASSWORD` | main generator gate |

author: xandfcosta
body:
## Summary
Phase 2 item 3 from book-rules backlog. Pure-function resolvers for combat math from PDF book p230-235.

Encodes:
- **Ataque**: `d20 + bônus ≥ Defesa` (p230)
- **Acerto crítico**: raw d20 ≥ weapon margem; NO confirmation roll (p231)
- **Dano de crítico**: weapon dice × multiplicador + atributo (NOT mult) + extras like Ataque Furtivo (NOT mult) (p231)
- **Dano base**: corpo a corpo / arremesso = arma + Força; disparo = arma sem Força (p230)
- **Iniciativa tie-break**: higher modifier, then reroll (p231)
- **Action economy**: 1 padrão + 1 movimento; padrão → movimento OK, movimento → padrão NOT OK; ação completa consome ambos (p233)
- **Investida**: +2 ataque, -2 Defesa (p235)

## What's in
- `t20-data/src/combat.ts`
  - `INVESTIDA_ATTACK_BONUS` / `INVESTIDA_DEFENSE_PENALTY` constants
  - `ActionKind` type (`padrao | movimento | livre | reacao | completa`)
  - `isAttackHit(d20Result, attackBonus, defense)` with defensive d20 range check
  - `isCriticalHit(d20Result, weaponCritRange, hit)` — raw d20 vs margem; only crits if the attack already hit
  - `damageTotal({ weaponDice, attributeBonus, extraDice, isCrit, critMultiplier })` — multiplies weapon dice only, never attribute or extras; clamps at 0
  - `attackAttributeBonus(weaponPurpose, attackerStrength)` — folds in Força for melee/arremesso, zero for ranged
  - `initiativeOrder(entries)` — stable sort: total DESC, then modifier DESC; equal-equal preserves input order (caller rerolls per PDF rule)
  - `isLegalTurn({ padrao, movimento, completa })` — full action-economy validator
- `t20-data/src/__tests__/combat.test.ts` — 30 specs:
  - hit at `=`, above, below; invalid d20 rejected
  - crit at margem boundary (17/18/19/20 vs critRange=18); crit-range without hit → no crit
  - damage: normal vs ×2 vs ×3 (only weapon dice multiplied); negative bonus clamps to 0
  - attribute bonus: melee/thrown add Força; ranged does not; negatives apply to melee/thrown
  - iniciativa: total → modifier → reroll preserved input order
  - investida constants pinned
  - action economy: standard, trade-down, illegal inverse trade, ação completa exclusive, two-completas illegal, negative counts rejected, empty turn legal

## What's NOT in (follow-up PRs)
- Ataques extras (Trespassar, Quebrar Aprimorado, Piqueiro, Disparo Rápido, Arremesso Múltiplo) — these are individual class/general powers triggered situationally with PM cost; belong in the powers catalog.
- Acertos extras / dados de ataque furtivo computation — depends on Ladino catalog.
- Atropelar (free during Investida) — uses manobras resolver from #32.
- Cobertura, flanquear, terreno difícil — situational modifiers; belong in their own module.
- Dano não letal (book p236).

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm test` — 443 t20-data / 143 backend / 112 frontend passing
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean

body:
입력 DTO의 앞뒤 공백을 제거하는 재사용 `@Trim()` 데코레이터를 추가하고, **식별자·표시용 문자열 필드에만 옵트인** 적용.

### 왜 전역(무조건) trim이 아닌가
- **비밀번호**: 평문 공백은 정당한 문자 → trim하면 사용자의 비밀을 변형하고 가입/로그인 해시 불일치 위험. 제외.
- **콘텐츠(게시글/댓글 본문)**: 의도된 공백·들여쓰기가 있을 수 있어 제외.
- 전역 제외 리스트 방식은 새 필드 추가 시 누락되기 쉬워(안전 기본값이 위험 쪽) 비채택 → 명시적 옵트인.

### 적용
- 신규: `src/common/transform/trim.decorator.ts` (+ spec)
- 적용: signup(email·name), login(email), create-post·update-post(title), create-building(name·address), create-unit(name), redeem-invite(code)
- 비적용: 모든 password, post/comment content, 머신 ID, 응답 DTO
- 전역 `ValidationPipe({ transform:true })`가 켜져 있어 검증 전에 trim 수행.

> 참고: M6의 `UpdateProfileDto.name`은 별도 브랜치(feature/m6-settings)라 이 PR에 없음 — M6는 이미 엔티티 `rename` trim으로 안전하며, 머지 후 후속으로 `@Trim()` 적용 가능.

### 테스트
- Jest 55 suites/172 tests 통과(데코레이터 spec 포함), lint·build 통과.

author: copilot
body:
Issue Monster currently treats `assign_to_agent` failures with `ignore-if-error: true` as skipped successes, so failures to find Copilot or authenticate never reach failure issue/comment reporting. This change preserves those failures as reportable signals and adds direct token setup guidance in the failure narrative.

- **Failure signal propagation from `assign_to_agent`**
  - Preserve error text on skipped (`ignore-if-error`) assignment attempts.
  - Include skipped-with-error entries in `assignment_errors` outputs so downstream conclusion/failure handling can consume them.

- **Unified assignment-failure rendering in `handle_agent_failure`**
  - Introduce a shared assignment error context builder and reuse it for both:
    - failure issue body
    - failure comment body
  - Eliminate duplicated formatting logic and keep issue/comment content aligned.

- **Actionable Copilot token guidance**
  - Add explicit remediation text in assignment failure context:
    - configure `GH_AW_AGENT_TOKEN`
    - required write scopes for issue/PR assignment
    - link to Copilot engine/token docs

- **Representative behavior change**
  ```js
  // assign_to_agent output aggregation now keeps ignored assignment failures visible
  _allResults
    .filter(r => r.error && (r.skipped || !r.success))
    .map(r => `${prefix}:${number}:${r.agent}:${r.error}`)
    .join("\n");
  ```

author: manus-use
body:
## What & Why

Single-shot `manus-use "task..."` runs produce human-readable Rich terminal output — helpful for interactive use but unusable in scripts, CI pipelines, and tool compositions. Two complementary features address this:

**1. `--format json` flag**

```bash
manus-use --format json "List prime numbers up to 50"
# stdout: {"task":"...","agent":"manus","mode":"single","result":"..."}

manus-use --format json --output result.json "task"
# writes the same JSON object to result.json

# pipe into jq
manus-use --format json "Get latest CVEs" | jq .result
```

**2. Session history log + `manus-use history`**

Every single-shot run appends one JSONL record to `~/.manus-use/history.jsonl`:
```json
{"timestamp":"2026-06-25T00:01:00+00:00","task":"...","agent":"manus","mode":"single","format":"text","success":true,"result":"..."}
```

`manus-use history` shows past runs in a Rich table. Flags: `--limit N`, `--format json`, `--grep PATTERN`, `--clear`.

```bash
manus-use history                   # rich table, 20 most recent
manus-use history --grep CVE        # filter by substring
manus-use history --format json     # JSON array, pipeable
manus-use history --limit 5         # last 5 only
manus-use history --clear           # wipe the log
manus-use --no-history "task"       # skip logging for this run
```

## Changes

- `src/manus_use/cli.py`
  - `_append_history()` — writes one JSONL record to `~/.manus-use/history.jsonl`
  - `_run_single_shot()` — new `fmt` and `no_history` kwargs; JSON branch writes via `sys.stdout.write` (no Rich colours, safe for pipe consumers); text+file branches updated
  - `_build_history_parser()` + `_cmd_history()` — full `manus-use history` subcommand with limit/format/grep/clear
  - `_build_run_parser()` — `--format {text,json}` and `--no-history` flags
  - `main()` — `history` subcommand dispatch; validates `--format` requires a task; updated epilog with examples
  - `_HISTORY_PATH` constant (`~/.manus-use/history.jsonl`); `_SUBCOMMANDS` updated

- `tests/test_cli.py`
  - 18 new tests covering `--format` flag parsing, JSON stdout/file output, `_append_history` file creation and multi-append, `--no-history` skipping, `history` subcommand dispatch, `_cmd_history` text/json/grep/clear/limit paths
  - Updated `_invoke_main` helper and 2 existing tests for new `_run_single_shot` signature

- `tests/test_init_doctor.py`
  - Updated `TestBackwardCompat.test_single_shot_still_works` mock signature

## Tests

- `tests/test_cli.py` — 32 pass (14 existing + 18 new)
- Full suite: **164 pass**, 3 pre-existing failures in `test_tools.py` (covered by open PR #28)
- `ruff check src/manus_use/cli.py tests/test_cli.py tests/test_init_doctor.py` — clean

author: nehal96
body:
## What

Adds `record` to the article-export toolkit — the moving sibling of `shoot`. It captures an interactive figure's animation as a looping **GIF**, framed identically to the screenshot (same capture region + padding), encoded with ffmpeg `palettegen`/`paletteuse`.

The reusable capture core (`prepareFigure` / `setFigureFrame` / `padAndResize`) is extracted in `capture.mjs` and shared with the still screenshotter, so GIF frames match stills exactly.

## Three capture modes (auto-detected per figure)

Real-time capture tears — a headless screenshot is far slower than an animation frame — so every mode drives the animation deterministically:

- **scrub** — Mol\* morph players: drive the frame slider one step at a time, waiting for the engine to settle. Play-button glyph forced **play → pause → replay** so the loop reads like a real recording.
- **tween** — 2D toggle figures (T↔R switch, BPG doorstop) that animate a `requestAnimationFrame` + `performance.now` tween on a button click: install a **virtual clock** (queue rAF, freeze `performance.now`), click the toggle, advance the clock in even steps and snapshot each — *advance time, let React render, capture*. Captured as a round trip so the loop is seamless. No per-figure pose maths.
- **sweep** — slider charts: walk a continuous slider through checkpoints (raw values or **preset-button labels**, clicked to read where the slider lands), pausing at each and looping back to close the cycle. e.g. `--sweep "lungs,resting tissue,working muscle"` drives pO₂ 95 → 40 → 20.

## A recordings manifest

`pages/essays/<slug>/recordings.json` makes an essay's GIFs declarative and regenerable:

```bash
node scripts/article-export/cli.mjs record hemoglobin              # every recording
node scripts/article-export/cli.mjs record hemoglobin --only bpg-doorstop
node scripts/article-export/cli.mjs record hemoglobin --figure 14 --name foo --sweep "lungs,working muscle"  # ad-hoc
```

Each entry is a spec — `name` plus any `recordFigure` option; `defaults` apply to all; mode is auto-detected, so one manifest mixes morphs, toggles and charts. Adds the hemoglobin manifest (6 figures).

## Notes

- Generated GIFs land in `docs/<slug>/export/`, now gitignored.
- Needs `ffmpeg` on `PATH` (or `FFMPEG_BIN`).
- Verified both paths (batch via `--only`, single ad-hoc) and that the refactor leaves the existing screenshot path unchanged.

author: derekadams
body:
Part of the stacked device-management series. **Base is `feat/phase2-attribute-model` (PR #10) — merge #9 then #10 first.** GitHub retargets this to `main` once #10 lands.

## What
Closes the biggest **standards** gap from the IoT-expert review (gap #3): telemetry was structurally opaque — a measurement was `name` + `double` with no unit, no type, no meaning. Per **ADR-016**, a Device Profile (the `DeviceType` entity) now declares typed, unit-bearing **metric definitions**.

## Details
- **model** — `MetricDataType` vocabulary (`DOUBLE`/`INT`/`BOOLEAN`/`STRING`); `MetricDefinition` declared on `DeviceType` with `MetricKey` (referenced by measurement events), `DataType`, **UCUM `Unit`**, optional `Min`/`Max` bounds, optional `Enum` (allowed values), and an optional **WoT `@type` `Descriptor`** — the forward path to a self-describing WoT Thing Description without committing to the full ontology now.
- **api** — full CRUD plus `MetricDefinitionsByDeviceType`, the loader the ingest validation/normalization path (reject-non-conforming → dead-letter subject) will consume.
- **schema** — `MetricDefinition` table with a composite **unique** index on `(device_type_id, metric_key)` so a profile can't declare a key twice.
- **graphql** — `MetricDefinition` type/queries/mutations + a `metricDefinitions` field on `DeviceType`; validated by `MustParseSchema`.
- **test** — `MockApi` methods; `MetricDataType.Valid` unit test.

## Notes
- Definitions hang off the **profile** (not each event) — keeps the hot path cheap and the fleet consistent, mirroring how alarm rules / OTA targets attach to the profile.
- **Ingest-time validation/normalization** (validate a measurement against its metric definition, normalize units, dead-letter non-conforming) is a follow-up — it touches the event-resolver/persistence path. This PR lands the model + the profile declaration + the lookup API the validator will call.

## Verification
`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` (clean), `go test ./...` — all green across `device-management` (incl. `MustParseSchema`).

author: nerdalert
body:
## Summary

  Adds a live Codex passthrough demo for the OpenAI Responses API.

  This demo shows a real Codex CLI session using Praxis as its OpenAI-compatible provider. Codex sends native /v1/responses traffic to a local
  Praxis listener, Praxis rewrites the client-facing model alias to the configured upstream OpenAI model, and the request is forwarded to
  api.openai.com.

  The demo lives at:

  demos/openai-responses-codex-passthrough/

  ## What This Demonstrates

  - Codex CLI can use Praxis as a custom Responses API provider.
  - Praxis can rewrite a stable client model alias, such as codex-openai-demo, to a real upstream OpenAI model.
  - Praxis can inject a default model when a Responses request omits model.
  - Native Responses JSON requests pass through without protocol translation.
  - SSE streaming Responses requests pass through Praxis.
  - Codex model discovery via GET /v1/models passes through to OpenAI.
  - Codex keeps ownership of the local tool loop; Praxis only proxies and rewrites request metadata.
  - Praxis publishes effective-model routing metadata so operators can route by the backend model selected by policy.

  ## Included

  - .env.example for runtime configuration without secrets.
  - praxis.yaml.tmpl for the local Praxis listener and OpenAI upstream.
  - scripts/check-prereqs.sh for local environment validation.
  - scripts/start-praxis.sh and scripts/stop-praxis.sh for controlled process management.
  - scripts/smoke-responses.sh for alias, default-model, SSE, and direct OpenAI control checks.
  - scripts/run-codex.sh for the real Codex CLI end-to-end proof.
  - scripts/run-narrative.sh for a single narrated end-to-end demo flow.
  - scripts/verify-evidence.sh for artifact and credential-leak validation.
  - A detailed README covering setup, architecture, capabilities, safety notes, and limitations.

  ## Live Validation

  Validated with the all-up flow:

  - Responses alias rewrite passed.
  - Default model injection passed.
  - SSE streaming passthrough passed.
  - Direct OpenAI control request passed.
  - Codex CLI created the expected proof file through Praxis.
  - Evidence verification passed.
  - Credential leak scan passed.

  ## Safety Notes

  The demo requires --live before making paid upstream API calls.

  The OpenAI API key is supplied at runtime by the client and is not rendered into the Praxis config. Runtime artifacts are ignored by git.

  For container environments where Codex cannot create a workspace-write sandbox, the narrative script requires an explicit --allow-danger-full-

author: s243a
body:
## Summary
Three refinements to the SimpleMind `.smmx` parser (`parse_smmx.py`) + its Haiku skill
(`SKILL_understand_smmx.md`), making the parsed mindmap graph faithful enough to feed the
human-judge (`corpus=mindmap`) pipeline. Prototype only; no model/training code touched.

## What changed

### 1. Directional `cloudmapref` (sub vs super by path)
When no container tags a cross-map link's relation, infer it from the relative-path
direction (the folder layout *is* the taxonomy):
- `../` **up** to a parent folder → `super_category` (target map is a broader parent tree)
- **down** into a subfolder → `subcategory` (target is narrower — a dedicated sub-map)

Replaces the generic `cloudmapref` relation. (Cybernetics' upward chain → all
`super_category`; System Theory → `subcategory` for chaos/complex/dynamical/LTI sub-maps.)

### 2. Name the target from the linked map's ROOT
Super-category / parent (and many cloudmapref) holder nodes are **unnamed** in the source
map — the real name + Pearltrees slug live on the **linked map's central theme**. The
parser now resolves each relative path, opens that `.smmx`, and reads its root topic's
title + slug as the target identity (cached; `--no-resolve` falls back to the filename).
It even fixes source typos (`Differentail Equation` node → linked root `Differential
Equation`); a node linking down to its own sub-map collapses to a self-edge and drops.

### 3. `bridge` relation — mindmap node ⟷ enwiki category/page
A node tagged `wiki`/`Wikipedia`/`enwiki` (or with a direct `en.wikipedia.org` urllink)
emits a typed **`bridge`** edge to the *same concept* in enwiki — a `category` (if
`Category:…`) or `page`. Same concept, **different node-type** (`mindmap_node` ⟷
`category`/`page`), possibly different name — the cross-corpus join key. `nodes.tsv`
gains a `node_type` column.

Bridges are **scarce in the maps** (System Theory: 1, `network_theory → Category:Network_theory`;
most enwiki links live in the Pearltrees data) and therefore **valuable**: the differing
endpoint types under one relation are exactly the **within-operator type diversity** that
makes the node-type token informative (`REPORT_nodetype.md`) — a primary source of the data
that activates `--use-nodetype`.

## Output
- `*_nodes.tsv`: `node_key · node_type · title · pearltrees_slug · pearltrees_id · enwiki_alias`
- `*_edges.tsv`: `src_key · dst_key · relation` — vocabulary now
  `subtopic | subcategory | see_also | super_category | bridge | assoc`

## Verified
Run on Cybernetics (29 nodes) and System Theory (115 nodes: 114 `mindmap_node` + 1
`category`; 133 edges incl. 26 `super_category`, 1 `subcategory`, 23 `see_also`, 1
`bridge`, 5 `assoc`), with cloudmapref targets correctly named from linked-map roots.

author: bordumb
body:
## Multi-sig: `sign_partial` was a blind-signing oracle

Found by adversarial review of the matrix's untested-sensitive backlog (`multi_sig::sign_partial` had zero test coverage).

### The bug
`sign_partial` signed the bundle's stored `canonical_bytes` (read from disk) **directly**, without verifying they equal `serialize_for_signing(bundle.event)`:

```rust
let sig = keypair.sign(&bundle.canonical_bytes);   // signs whatever the bundle says
```

Meanwhile `combine` / `validate_signed_event` re-derive the canonical bytes **from the event**. So the bytes a signer signs and the bytes a verifier checks could diverge. A tampered bundle — `event` = a benign event shown to the operator, `canonical_bytes` = the canonicalization of a **malicious** event (e.g. a rotation adding the attacker's key) — yields a valid signature the attacker assembles into the malicious event. The signer approves X, signs Y. For a multi-sig whose whole point is independent per-signer approval, that breaks the guarantee.

### The fix (fail-closed)
`bundle_canonical(bundle)` recomputes the canonical bytes from the event (the source of truth) and returns a typed `MultiSigError::BundleMismatch` if the stored bytes disagree — **before any key is loaded**. `sign_partial` signs the recomputed bytes. Legitimate bundles (where `begin_multi_sig_event` wrote consistent bytes) are unaffected; tampered ones are refused loudly. This also brings `sign_partial` into line with `combine`, which already trusts only the event.

### Adversarially verified — two findings refuted
The same review raised two threshold bypasses on `combine` and **refuted both** (kept honest):
- **Duplicate-index quorum** — refuted: `Threshold::is_satisfied` dedupes indices via a `HashSet`, so `[idx 0, idx 0]` counts as one signer.
- **Loose caller `expected_kt`** — refuted: `validate_signed_event` enforces the event's *own* `kt` over *verified* indices, so a caller's looser expectation can't widen the real threshold.

### Tests
- `bundle_canonical_rejects_a_tampered_bundle` — the defense (would not have rejected before this change).
- `bundle_canonical_accepts_a_consistent_bundle` — legitimate path unaffected.
- 5/5 `multi_sig` tests pass (3 pre-existing `combine` tests still green).

Note: the gate is wired into `sign_partial` (`let canonical = bundle_canonical(&bundle)?;`) before any key access; the unit tests exercise the check directly.

Part of matrix ROADMAP_2 R2 (adversarial coverage of untested operations).

author: dotdevdotdev
body:
## Root cause

`send_verified()` pasted the first message with `enter=True` (submit immediately), slept `settle=2.0s`, then captured only the last **60 visible lines** and checked for the prompt's first-line fragment or the `[Pasted text …]` placeholder. A fast **bypass** agent consumes + submits the prompt and emits tool output within the 2s window, scrolling the placeholder/fragment past the 60-line tail → `message_visible` returns False → false-negative "first message not delivered". `--json` then returned `first_message_delivered: false`, a duplicate-dispatch hazard. This hit **every worktree session** (bypass posture).

## What changed (`agentwire/session_ready.py`)

1. **Verify against scrollback.** Verification now captures `VERIFY_SCROLLBACK_LINES=200` (via the existing `capture_pane` `-S -<N>` wrapper — no duplicated tmux call), so a submitted prompt that scrolled up is still found.
2. **Capture early + late.** Snapshot ~150ms after the paste (catches the placeholder/fragment before the agent scrolls it away) **and** after `settle`. A hit at either time counts.
3. **Positive "consumed" signal.** If the input box went empty (`prompt_router.prompt_is_empty`) **and** the pane shows activity (spinner / token counter / esc-to-interrupt / tool glyphs), treat as delivered — a submitted-and-working agent is the success case the old check mistook for failure.

**False-positive guard kept:** empty box **and** no activity **and** nothing in scrollback still returns `False` (genuine vanish). The council explicit-marker path is unchanged in semantics and benefits from the scrollback capture.

## Tests

Extended `tests/unit/test_session_ready.py`: scrolled-out-but-working → delivered; placeholder-only in scrollback → delivered; genuine vanish → not delivered; plus activity-detection and scrollback-request assertions. Full fast suite green (`1701 passed`).

Closes #478

author: devonjones
body:
## What

`_classify_family` (`lexicon/strata.py`) sat at the McCabe-10 ceiling — while its own docstring already described exactly **two passes**. This extracts each pass into a named helper so the code structure matches the documentation:

- **`_self_language_proposals(db, self_lang_to_stratum)`** — pass 1: the ancestor/period varieties (proto-Brittonic, middle-welsh, …) assigned directly by their own `language`.
- **`_ancestor_walk_proposals(db, *, modern_lang, strata_order, ancestor_to_stratum, default_stratum)`** — pass 2: the modern variety classified by ancestor languages reached through the chunked `etymon_descent` join.

`_classify_family` becomes a two-line composition: pass-1 proposals, then `.update()` with pass-2.

## Why

- Complexity drops **10 → ~1** for the parent; each helper sits under the ceiling.
- The function body now mirrors its "Two passes" docstring, and each pass is independently readable/testable.

## Behavior

Strictly behavior-preserving, including **dict insertion order** (which the downstream `by_stratum` counters + `format_enrichment_run` sections depend on — Phase 3 byte-diff). The two passes' etymon sets are disjoint by `language`, so `dict.update` never overwrites and preserves the same overall order (self-language ids first, then modern ids, each `ORDER BY id`) the prior single-dict build produced.

Verified **byte-identical** (order-sensitive, `list(proposals.items())`) to the prior `_classify_family` across **8 seeded scenarios** — native-default / latin-loan / self-language-only / latin>brittonic priority / mixed-with-a-merged-loser / no-modern-rows / self-language-but-merged-skipped / multi-ancestor — running old (from `origin/main`) vs new on identical DBs. `ruff format --check` + `ruff check` clean; the 124 strata tests pass.

No kenning invariant affected — pure read that proposes `etymon.stratum` values (the caller decides whether to persist); touches no mining evidence and no scoring.

- **Content selector**: `div.article-body.transcript-content` — stable class name

**Motley Fool is the best transcript source for a personal portfolio agent.** Free, full text, 8,000+ words per call. The main risk is HTML structure changes — but the `article-body transcript-content` class has been stable. Can be used as primary source, with FMP Starter as paid fallback if Motley Fool goes behind a paywall.

author: aarav261
body:
Adds [Sentry](https://sentry.io) error monitoring to the Flask backend, wired through the app factory.

## Changes
- **`app.py`** — initialise `sentry_sdk` before the Flask app, gated on a `SENTRY_DSN` env var. When the DSN is unset (local dev), Sentry never initialises and no events are sent. The Flask integration auto-attaches via the `[flask]` extra.
- **`requirements.txt`** — add `sentry-sdk[flask]~=2.0`.
- **`.env.example`** — document `SENTRY_DSN` and `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`.

## Config choices
- `send_default_pii=False` — this backend handles student emails/usernames, so request headers, IPs, and PII are **not** sent to Sentry.
- No `traces_sample_rate` — performance tracing is off; this is pure error monitoring.
- `enable_logs=True` — `logging.*` records are forwarded to Sentry.

## To enable in prod
Set `SENTRY_DSN` (and optionally `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`) in Railway. No DSN lives in source.

Verified `app.py` compiles and `sentry_sdk` resolves in the venv.

body:
## Release v5.4.1 — ship to NuGet + npm

This is the **publishing** release PR for **v5.4.1**. The prior dev→main PR (#3105) merged but did not publish; v5.4.1 was never released to NuGet (`sarif.sdk` shows 5.4.0) or npm, and no `v5.4.1` tag exists. We are reusing the version — nothing under it has shipped — and folding in the one feature that landed on dev since: the CWE category API (#3106).

### Content delta vs `main`
The only code difference between `main` and `dev` is #3106:

- **NEW: CWE Category API in `@microsoft/sarif-multitool-ts`** — bundles `assets/CweCategories.json` and exports `getCweCategories`, `isCweCategory`, `getCweCategoryName`, mirroring the .NET `CweCategories` helper. A Category (e.g. `CWE-16` "Configuration") is an organizational grouping, never a valid `result.ruleId` mapping target, and does not appear in `CweTaxonomy.sarif` — so it cannot be recovered from the taxonomy's `cwe/abstraction` field.

### Already on `main` from #3105 (the v5.4.1 body, recapped)
- BUG: `emit-finalize --validate` channel convergence — structured verdict receipt to stdout on every run, capped human summary to stderr on failure, full findings to `<output>.validate-report.sarif` (kept on fail, deleted on conform); .NET and `@microsoft/sarif-multitool-ts` channel identically.
- BUG: `AI1004` / whole-log contract exempt `--no-repo` finalized runs.
- BUG: `get-skill` registers the `publish-to-ghas` skill.
- NEW: `emit-finalize --no-repo` in `@microsoft/sarif-multitool-ts`.

### Verification
- TS unit: 23/23 green (10 CWE + 13 existing). C#: EmitFinalize 52/52, ReleaseHistoryStyle 2/2.
- Merge to `main` is clean (no conflicts); the only `ReleaseHistory.md` delta is the CWE `NEW` bullet in the v5.4.1 section.
- `build.props` `VersionPrefix` = `5.4.1` on both branches.

body:
#### 0b85f13185f5720036900ad6ae7ffe726c47a98c 
REGRESSION (Safari 18.x): Copy main menu item is enabled with no selection in the web page
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=313835
rdar://176061974

Reviewed by Megan Gardner and Wenson Hsieh.

288559@main changed Editor::canCopy to return true for carets in non-editable
positions so that document.execCommand("copy") would fire copy events even
without a range selection. This regressed the Copy menu item, which is now
enabled whenever the caret was anywhere on a non-editable page.

Fix by reverting canCopy to require a range selection (restoring the correct
menu item state), and instead preserving 288559@main's execCommand behavior
via allowExecutionWhenDisabledCopyCut: when the copy/cut command is disabled
from a DOM source, allow execution anyway if clipboard access is currently
permitted (i.e. there is a user gesture or JavaScriptCanAccessClipboard is
true). This lets oncopy handlers fire from user-gesture-driven execCommand
calls on pages without a selection, while keeping programmatic calls without
a user gesture fully blocked (including suppressing the copy event).

Also, return the actual copy/cut success from executeCopy/executeCut instead
of always returning true, and only beep on failed copy/cut when the call
originates from the menu or a key binding.

- Move Zod from a peer dependency to a runtime dependency of `@workflow/world`.
- Update the lockfile and add a patch changeset for the packaging fix.

## Why

`@workflow/world` exports Zod schemas such as `EventSchema`, and `@workflow/world-vercel` composes those schemas into response validators. If `@workflow/world` resolves a consuming application's incompatible Zod version, those validators can fail locally after a successful workflow-server response with errors like `Invalid element at key "event": expected a Zod schema`.

Owning the Zod runtime dependency keeps exported schemas on the package's expected Zod version instead of depending on the application install.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec tsc -p packages/world/tsconfig.json --noEmit`
- `pnpm exec biome check packages/world/package.json .changeset/world-zod-dependency.md`

Note: repo-wide `pnpm lint` currently fails on unrelated existing generated/docs/benchmark diagnostics.

author: mrmeg
body:
## Summary
Migrates the app's primary navigation from a custom JS-rendered responsive tab bar (+ wide-screen rail) to a single **Expo Router Native Tabs** navigator (`expo-router/unstable-native-tabs`). On native this renders a real `UITabBar` (iOS) / `BottomNavigationView` (Android); on web it uses Native Tabs' built-in CSS fallback.

Implements spec `native-tabs-migration` (local `Agent/` spec; not included in this PR).

- **Base branch:** `dev`
- **Starting SHA:** `df4333da961d58cd3b278cb1bce85f32d8a8cc0b`

## Goal
Adopt a modern, platform-native tab bar on all platforms and simplify the navigation layer by removing the bespoke responsive-rail system.

## What changed & why
- **`app/(main)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`** — rewritten to render one `<NativeTabs>` with `NativeTabs.Trigger` per `NAV_DESTINATIONS` entry. Colors derive from `useTheme()` *inside* the component (so React Compiler / `babel-plugin-react-compiler` memoization can't freeze them). Icons reuse the existing Feather family via `NativeTabs.Trigger.VectorIcon` **on native only**.
- **Deleted** the rail/bridge modules — they existed only to feed navigator state to the wide-screen rail, which Native Tabs (no custom `tabBar` prop) can't support and which the spec removes:
  `ResponsiveRail.tsx`, `ResponsiveTabBar.tsx`, `RailNavItem.tsx`, `RailNavStateContext.ts`, `ContentHeader.tsx`.
- **`client/features/navigation/index.ts`** — dropped exports for the deleted modules; kept `canGoBack`, `WebBackButton`, `NAV_DESTINATIONS`, and its types.
- **`client/features/navigation/MainLayout.tsx`** — the `(tabs)` stack header now shows at **all** widths (`headerShown: true`); previously it was suppressed on wide screens because the now-removed rail/`ContentHeader` owned the top inset. Removed the now-unused `useDimensions`/`isSmallScreen`.

## Web crash fix (important)
Native Tabs' web fallback never renders icons, but it still resolves a `VectorIcon` through `expo-font.renderToImageAsync`, which **throws `UnavailabilityError` on web** (fires per tab, per navigation). Fixed by omitting the `<NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon>` child when `Platform.OS === "web"` — web shows a labels-only bar; native is unaffected.

## Validation (fresh output, this shift)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun run typecheck` | ✅ clean |
| `bun run lint` | ✅ 0 errors (11 pre-existing `no-explicit-any`/unused-var warnings in untouched files) |
| `bun run check:features` | ✅ 9 features OK |
| `bun run test:ci` | ✅ 585 passed / 585 |
| `bun run docs:llms:check` | ✅ up to date (no doc regeneration needed) |

**Web (Playwright, post-fix):** ✅ Home + `/media` `/profile` `/settings` load with **no error overlay and no `UnavailabilityError`**; all 4 `[role=tab]` render with correct labels and active-state tracks on URL navigation. No left-side rail at any width.

## Known limitations / left for review
- **Web tab bar is cosmetically weak (accepted):** the upstream fallback renders as a top-center floating pill (`position: fixed; top: 24px`) that overlaps the stack header, and physical taps can be intercepted by the header (URL navigation works). This is upstream `native-tabs.module.css` behavior; styling it properly is out of scope for this PR. Decision on this PR was *fix the crash, accept the weak web fallback*.
- **Native NOT verified this session:** Argent MCP device-control tools were not available in the session (CLI installed, MCP surface absent), so I could not drive the iOS Simulator / Android emulator. **Reviewer should confirm on a real device/simulator:** native `UITabBar`/`BottomNavigationView` renders with 4 tabs + Feather icons, accent tint on the selected tab, working navigation, and live color update on light/dark toggle.

## Out of scope
Native-stack migration of `MainLayout`; tab badges / `BottomAccessory` / SF Symbol (`sf`) / Material (`md`) icon variants; re-introducing any wide-screen rail; expo-router `Color` API adoption.

author: xiaguan
body:
## What

Replace the Qwen3 prefill QK RMSNorm+RoPE kernel (`prefill_qk_norm_rope_kernel`, one thread per dim + shared-memory reduce / RoPE swap) with a warp-per-token implementation.

- One warp owns one `(head, token)`; each lane holds 4 contiguous dims as a `float2` bf16 load.
- RMSNorm reduces via a shuffle butterfly; RoPE swaps the rotate-half partner via `__shfl_xor_sync(.., 16)` (`lane^16 == dim ± half`). No shared memory, no `__syncthreads`.
- All four independent loads (q/k, norm_w, cos, sin) are issued up front for memory-level parallelism — the kernel is DRAM-latency-bound at ~88% occupancy, so the lever is per-warp MLP, not more warps.
- Hard-wired to `head_dim == 128` (the only caller is Qwen3; TP shards head count, not head_dim) and asserted; the old general kernel is removed.

## Prefix cache

Per-token RoPE positions come from the plan's `positions[]` array (each row's absolute position), so a request resuming from a cached prefix rotates at its true offset — not from position 0.

## Correctness

Numerics are bit-identical to the old kernel except the sum-of-squares accumulation order (ULP-level). `hf_golden_gate` passes, including the prefix-cache cached-replay and cuda-graph paths (logit Δ mean ~0.03 / p99 ~0.11 nat, within bf16 tolerance). A standalone diff harness with non-contiguous prefix-cache positions shows max|Δ| = 1 bf16 ULP (0.0002% mismatched).

## Performance (sm_120, RTX 5070 Ti / 5090)

| level | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| kernel cold, seq 4096 (`kernel_report`) | 281.6 µs | 114.9 µs | **2.45×** |
| 5090 `ncu` cold, seq 4096 | 52.1 µs | 49.5 µs | DRAM SOL 50.5% → 53.4%, ~88% occ |
| end-to-end prefill TTFT (`bench_serving`, batch 1, 512–8192) | | | **−1.2 to −1.7%** |

End-to-end is small because prefill is GEMM-dominated; this memory-bound kernel is only a few % of TTFT.

body:
Correção do menu lateral que eu tinha errado duas vezes (mexendo no componente errado). Desta vez **rodei o app no navegador e VI o problema** antes de mexer.

## 🐛 Causa real da rolagem (rail)
O menu de ícones nunca rolava em janela baixa. Medindo no navegador: o container de rolagem ficava com **916px (= altura do conteúdo)**, não limitado à janela. É a armadilha clássica do flexbox — um filho `flex-1` tem `min-height: auto`, se recusa a encolher abaixo do conteúdo e **nunca gera overflow** → sem rolagem, sem setas. As tentativas anteriores não pegaram isso.

## ✅ Correções
- **`min-h-0`** no container de rolagem do **rail** e do **menu clássico** (mesmo bug nos dois). Agora respeita a altura da janela → rolagem com roda do mouse + setas que auto-scrollam ao pousar o mouse.
- Detecção de overflow via `offsetHeight` do conteúdo (o `scrollHeight` do container, com `overflow:visible` necessário pro magnify, ficava = clientHeight e mascarava o overflow).
- **Tiles do rail no modo escuro**: mais definição (borda + vidro mais presentes) pra lerem como botões, igual ao claro — em vez de quadrados chapados.

## 🔬 Como verifiquei (não chutei)
Rodei o frontend (Vite) no Chromium headless e tirei screenshots do rail em claro e escuro, em janela baixa. Confirmei: a **seta de rolagem aparece** e os tiles ficam definidos. (O harness de teste foi removido do commit.)

author: troyjr4103
body:
## What

Make the Linux release binaries (`kin`, `kin-daemon`) fully static and portable
across any Linux distro, not just modern glibc + OpenSSL 3.

- **`reqwest`** → `default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls-tls"]`.
  kin's HTTP path uses rustls (ring) instead of OpenSSL / native-tls.
- **`release.yml`** → the two Linux legs build the core (`kin`, `kin-daemon`)
  for `*-unknown-linux-musl` (static by default) instead of `*-unknown-linux-gnu`,
  and install `musl-tools` for the C deps (ring, oniguruma, sqlite, tree-sitter).
  The VFS leg stays on gnu (`vfs_target`); see below.

## Why

The published Linux binary was dynamically linked against glibc + OpenSSL 3
(`NEEDED libssl.so.3` / `libcrypto.so.3`, interpreter `ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`).
It ran on Ubuntu 24.04 but failed on Alpine/musl and would fail on older
OpenSSL-1.1 distros. A static musl build removes both the glibc and OpenSSL
coupling: one binary runs everywhere.

## VFS shim

`libkin_vfs_shim.so` is an LD_PRELOAD libc interceptor, so it is intrinsically
libc-specific: one shim cannot serve both musl and glibc hosts. The core
`kin`/`kin-daemon` are the portability priority and are now static-musl. The VFS
leg (cli + shim) builds against gnu (`vfs_target`) so the shim can preload into
the host distro's glibc programs (the majority of Linux installs). The
macOS/Windows legs are unchanged (`VFS_TARGET` falls back to the core target).

## Verification (aarch64 musl, built natively on arm64)

`file kin` → `ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, statically linked`
`readelf -d kin` → no dynamic `NEEDED` entries (no libssl/libcrypto); no PT_INTERP

```
# alpine:3 (MUSL)
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 -v out:/k:ro alpine:3 /k/kin --version
kin 0.2.3 ...
$ ... /k/kin-daemon --version
kin-daemon 0.2.3 ...

# ubuntu:24.04 (GLIBC)
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 -v out:/k:ro ubuntu:24.04 /k/kin --version
kin 0.2.3 ...
$ ... /k/kin-daemon --version
kin-daemon 0.2.3 ...
```

With the kin-db change below in place, `cargo tree -i openssl-sys` is empty and
the TLS backend is `ring` (no `aws-lc-rs`).

## ⚠️ Merge / release order (required)

The OpenSSL pull on the embeddings path comes from **`kin-db`** (`hf-hub`'s
default `native-tls`), not just reqwest. This PR removes kin's *own* OpenSSL use,
but the musl Linux legs build OpenSSL-free only once `kin-db` ships the matching
fix:

1. Merge + publish **firelock-ai/kin-db#64** (hf-hub → rustls, drop `esaxx_fast`).
2. Bump kin's `kin-db` dependency to that version and re-lock.
3. The musl Linux release is then OpenSSL-free and green.

Until step 2, registry `kin-db 0.2.23` still pulls OpenSSL + a C++ dep, which the
musl legs cannot build. **Do not tag a release off this branch before the kin-db
bump.** (PR-time CI is unaffected: the musl matrix only runs on release tags.)

body:
Home page content was wrapped in a `<section>` element that rendered as a real HTML node inside `.main.main-app`, offsetting the Bootstrap grid and breaking the DashByte layout. The reference template has content directly inside `.main.main-app` with no intermediate wrapper.

## Changes

- **`templates/pages/home.html`** — Replace `<section>` wrapper with `<th:block th:fragment="homeContent">` (Thymeleaf synthetic tag, emits no HTML); update `th:replace` selector accordingly

  ```html
  <!-- Before: rendered a <section> inside .main.main-app -->
  <html th:replace="~{layouts/app :: layout(~{::title}, ~{::section}, ~{::th:block[@id='pageScripts']})}">
  <section> ... </section>

  <!-- After: content sits directly inside .main.main-app -->
  <html th:replace="~{layouts/app :: layout(~{::title}, ~{:: homeContent}, ~{::th:block[@id='pageScripts']}, ~{::th:block[@id='pageStyles']})}">
  <th:block th:fragment="homeContent"> ... </th:block>
  ```

- **`templates/layouts/app.html`** — Add 4th `pageStyles` parameter to `layout(...)` fragment; remove globally-loaded `jqvmap.min.css` and `apexcharts.css` from `<head>` (were loaded on every dashboard page)

## Problem

Follow-up to #1725 (already merged).

The review at https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/1725#pullrequestreview-4561336221 pointed out that using `@mousedown.prevent` on the save button dropped device-independent activation — keyboard/assistive users can't trigger save because `mousedown` doesn't fire for those input methods.

body:
## ปัญหา (เคสจริง 2026-06-25)
ลูกค้าสั่งหนังสือคู่มือ ระบุครบ (A5 · 32 หน้า · ปอนด์ 80 · ปกอาร์ทการ์ด · **พิมพ์ 4 สีทั้งเล่ม**) + qty → แต่ AI **ถามซ้ำ "สีปก 4 สีใช่ไหม?" 2 รอบ** ทั้งที่ลูกค้าบอก "4 สีทั้งเล่ม" ไปแล้ว

## Root cause
- `prompt.ts` สั่งหนังสือ "ต้องถามเสมอ: ...สีปก/สีเนื้อใน" + ไม่มี hard-rule "ครบพอตีราคา" สำหรับหนังสือ → Haiku ที่ระวังเลยถามสีปกซ้ำ
- spec มี `cover.color` แยกจาก `inner.color` → โมเดลไม่ map คำว่า "ทั้งเล่ม" ไปที่ปก

## แก้ (prompt-only — `lib/ai-quote/prompt.ts`)
1. **default ปก = 4 สี** (assume-and-disclose) → ปกออกจาก always-ask
2. เกณฑ์ "ครบพอตีราคา" หนังสือ: `+ สี` → `+ สีเนื้อใน` (ปกไม่ gate แล้ว)
3. **สีเนื้อใน ยังถามเสมอ** (ตัวขยับราคาแรง — คงตาม decision 6/24)
4. กฎ **"X สีทั้งเล่ม"** → set ทั้งปก+เนื้อใน = X + worked example หนังสือ (เลียนเคส screenshot)

## Test
+6 regression assertions (`tests/ai-quote-prompt.test.ts`) — pin default ปก, ปกออกจาก always-ask, กฎ "ทั้งเล่ม", worked example, ครบพอตีราคา = สีเนื้อใน. **170→176 tests** · type-check/lint/build เขียว Node 22

## ⚠️ ก่อน merge — ต้อง live smoke บน preview
behavior ฝั่ง Haiku → soft prompt อาจไม่พอ. ทดสอบบน preview: หนังสือ A5 + เนื้อใน + ปอนด์ 80 + **"4 สีทั้งเล่ม"** + qty → ต้อง **ตีราคาเลย ไม่ถามสีปก**. ถ้ายังถาม → ต้อง hard-rule เพิ่ม (บทเรียน 6/24)

## Out of scope
กระดาษ "อาร์ทการ์ด 210" ไม่อยู่ในลิสต์ (มีแค่ Art Card 300/350) → เคสนี้อาจ escalate เรื่องกระดาษ. เพิ่มราคากระดาษต้องใช้ราคาจริง → แยกงาน

author: natefinch
body:
Part of #1729, Stage 2 of #1738 ("unify replacement and cost-modifier filters on Selection"). Follow-up to #1813/#1815 (cost-modifier stages).

Routes two replacement-effect object/card filters through canonical `game.Selection` + `matchSelection`:
- `CounterRecipientTypes` + `CounterRecipientTypesAny` → single `CounterRecipientSelection *Selection` (`RequiredTypes` for the conjunctive "creature" recipient; `RequiredTypesAny` for the "artifact or creature you control" union).
- `EntersTappedTypes` → `EntersTappedSelection *Selection` (`RequiredTypesAny`).

Runtime matching now flows through `matchSelection` via new helpers (`counterRecipientMatchesSelection`, `permanentMatchesReplacementSelection`, `entersTappedGroupSelectionMatches`) — semantically exact (`permanentHasType` reads the same `effectivePermanentValues().types` as `subjectPermanent`). Replacement-specific context (event identity, ordering, recipient controller scope, "any permanent" anchoring) stays outside Selection. Renderer reads `RequiredTypesAny` back out, so generated source is byte-identical.

Behavior-preserving: generated_count 14244 → 14244; newly_unsupported 0; corpus byte-identical (`diff -rq` clean). Build, `go test ./...`, race, vet, lint pass. Added `TestCounterRecipientSelectionMatchesTypeUnion`/`TestEntersTappedSelectionMatchesTypeUnion`; replacement-ordering tests unchanged.

Left for follow-up (reported, with reasons): DamageSourceTypes/Colors (LKI color-precedence), RedirectTypeFilter (moving-card LKI), Token*Types (token is *CardDef), the shared trigger/replacement event-match core restructuring, and RuleEffect SpellTypes normalization.
