author: acmerfight
body:
Closes #224

**Problem:** Local `pnpm test:coverage` verifies global coverage but did not catch PR patch coverage gaps before pushing. That made `codecov/patch` failures show up only after CI/Codecov, especially for changed uncovered lines and branch partials.

**Solution:** Add a repository-owned `pnpm coverage:patch` command backed by `scripts/coverage-patch.ts` and `src/core/coverage-patch.ts`. The checker compares `origin/main...HEAD` using `git diff --relative`, reads `coverage/lcov.info`, fails on changed `DA:...,0` lines, fails on changed lines with untaken `BRDA` branches, and reports changed lines that are absent from LCOV as not present in coverage data. The `/slice` skills and testing docs now include the new pre-push step, and Codecov patch target is explicit `100%`.

**Why:** This matches the real local inputs already produced by `pnpm test:coverage` while avoiding the `diff-cover-ts` limitations from the issue discussion: no mismatched CLI binary, no missing branch-partial handling, and correct path matching when Keel is nested under the repo root.

**Effect:** A slice author can run `pnpm test:coverage && pnpm coverage:patch` before push and get actionable `path:line reason` output for changed coverable code that would fail patch coverage remotely.

**Verification:**
- `pnpm vitest run tests/cli/coverage-patch.test.ts` — 9 tests passed
- `pnpm lint` — passed
- `pnpm typecheck` — passed
- `pnpm build` — passed
- `pnpm eval:check` — passed
- `pnpm knip` — passed
- `pnpm test:coverage` — 67 files / 1198 tests passed, 99.69% line coverage
- `pnpm coverage:patch` — passed, 102/102 changed coverable lines covered

**Review notes or remaining risks:** Empty-context review found a blocker where git diff paths were repo-root relative while LCOV paths were Keel-relative. Fixed by using `git diff --relative` and adding a nested git-root fixture. No known remaining risks.

body:
Brings Mounce to the tip of duff `main` (PR #318) and does a UX pass on the controls bar / session selector that the required/optional discussion prompted.

## duff #318 (`b66a8b2e`) — the iOS-freeze fix, ported in full
- **`sw.js`**: the navigation fetch is now **bounded** — it races the network against a **4 s `NAV_TIMEOUT_MS`** and falls back to the cached shell on error *or stall* (a stalled, not-errored launch fetch otherwise hangs forever, which on iOS standalone PWAs renders a frozen page). New `cachedShell()` helper; the network keeps running past the timeout to refresh the cache.
- **`main.js`**: `visibilitychange` now re-surfaces `showAppUpdateBanner` when a worker is already waiting on resume, so a backgrounded PWA reopened later no longer sits silently on the old version.

## duff #317 (`c5c2d399`) — ADAPTED
#317 made the spaced-reset labels name the required-only scope. But **Mounce's core vocab is all `required:true`** (zero `required:false`), so that split only ever excluded selected supplemental/advanced extras — pointless here. So Mounce **drops the required/optional scope from the reset flow entirely**: removed the "Required cards only" checkbox from both reset modals, the "Reset required" button, and `resetRequiredOnly()`; labels are static **"Set selected to now" / "Reset selected"** (keeping #317's "selected"-not-"all" clarification).

## Mounce-specific Advanced-settings + selector cleanup
- **Parsing-step toggles no longer leak into vocab/grammar**: the 8 step toggles + value-filter `<details>` + optional-forms are wrapped in a new **`#parsingStepOptions`** container, hidden as a unit outside parsing mode.
- **Removed `#requiredToggle`; `runtime.requiredOnly` forced `false`** everywhere, so the deck = whatever the user selected (no silent filtering of optional extras).
- **`#splitSelectionToggle` defaults ON** (separate vocab/grammar chapter selections).
- **Dropped grammar counts from the selector** — vocab count only, or **"grammar only"** for a 0-vocab set.
- **New "no vocab" card**: a vocab deck empty because the selected chapters are grammar-only now shows *"Selected chapter(s) have no vocab — use the Grammar section for chapter practice."*

Cache-bust **v160 → v161**; `docs/index-structure.md` + `CLAUDE.md` updated.

`node --check` on all changed JS; a headless-Chromium pass confirming: required toggle gone, split ON by default, `#parsingStepOptions` hidden in vocab / shown in parsing, no grammar counts in the selector, the no-vocab card renders, **0 page errors**.

author: bradleyjames
body: ## Description Adds Markdown to the languages the editor syntax-highlights. Opening a `.md` / `.markdown` file in Warp's code editor (Raw view) now highlights block-level structure instead of rendering as plain text. Markdown is highlighted with arborium's bundled Markdown query — the same source every other language uses — plus a small extension to Warp's shared capture-name → color mapper so it understands the nvim-style capture names arborium's Markdown query emits. ### What's supported Block-level Markdown constructs: - Headings — ATX (`#`–`######`) and setext, markers and text - Fenced and indented code blocks — fence delimiters and the code body - Lists — bullets (`-` `*` `+`) and ordered (`1.` `3)`) - Blockquotes (including multi-line continuation) and thematic breaks - Link **reference definitions** — `[label]: url "title"` - Backslash escapes ### What's not supported yet **Awaiting upstream arborium query rules** — the grammar produces these nodes, but arborium's bundled Markdown query has no rule for them, so they render in the default color (to be added in arborium): - YAML / TOML front matter - Task markers `[x]` / `[ ]` - Pipe tables - HTML blocks - Entity / numeric character references (`&`) **Inline** (styling *within* a line of text) — needs the separate Markdown *inline* grammar, which arborium does not yet package upstream: - Emphasis — `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~strikethrough~~` - `` `inline code` `` - In-text links — `[title](url)`, autolinks ``, reference *uses* `[text][label]` ## Implementation - Enable arborium's `lang-markdown` grammar and register `markdown` in the `languages` crate (`.md` / `.markdown` extensions, `md` alias). - Highlight Markdown with arborium's bundled Markdown query (`arborium::lang_markdown::HIGHLIGHTS_QUERY`), the same path every other language uses. - Extend Warp's shared capture-name → color mapper (`convert_capture_name_to_color`) to resolve arborium's nvim-style capture names — `text.title`, `text.literal`, `text.uri`, `text.reference`, and `punctuation.*` — which previously fell through to no color. The mapper is shared across languages, so any grammar whose query uses these names now colors them (e.g. punctuation in Rust); the impact is minor and additive (see the cross-language screenshots below). - Sync `ProgrammingLanguage::to_extension` so fenced ` ```markdown ` blocks in agent output highlight through the same path. ## Linked Issue Closes #9042. - [x] The linked issue is labeled `ready-to-spec` or `ready-to-implement`. - [x] Where appropriate, screenshots or a short video of the implementation are included below. ## Testing - [x] I have manually tested my changes locally with `./script/run` - **Unit:** `crates/languages` — `markdown_extensions_resolve_to_markdown` and `all_supported_languages_load_successfully` (loads Markdown via arborium's query); `app` — `to_extension` covers the `markdown`/`md` fence aliases. Full presubmit (clippy + nextest) is green apart from pre-existing environment-only SSH integration tests. - **Manual:** verified highlighting in the editor's Raw view against Markdown fixtures and representative Rust/Python files. ### Screenshots / Videos Captured in the editor's **Raw** view (dark theme). #### Markdown **1. Headings** — `01-headings.md` **2. Lists, quotes & rules** — `02-lists-quotes-rules.md` **3. Code blocks** — `03-code.md` **4. Links & reference definitions** — `04-links-table-html-inline.md` #### Cross-language impact of the shared mapper Extending `convert_capture_name_to_color` colors `text.*` / `punctuation.*` in any language whose query uses those names. Before / after on a representative file: **Python — before** **Python — after** **Rust — before** **Rust — after** ## Agent Mode - [ ] Warp Agent Mode - This PR was created via Warp's AI Agent Mode --- CHANGELOG-IMPROVEMENT: Markdown files now have syntax highlighting in the editor.

author: stevenphtan
body:
_Recreated from #53 (commit history cleaned; supersedes that PR)._

Implements #35.

A pure-Go `EnergyProvider` that scrapes a node-local **dcgm-exporter** Prometheus endpoint (default `http://localhost:9400/metrics`) — for clusters already running dcgm-exporter (e.g. via the GPU Operator) alongside, or instead of, in-process NVML.

### What it does
- **Energy** — `DCGM_FI_DEV_TOTAL_ENERGY_CONSUMPTION` (mJ cumulative counter): `BeginWindow` snapshots it, `EndWindow` returns the joules consumed in between, summed across all GPUs on the node (mJ→J). A counter reset (driver reload) clamps to 0 — never negative.
- **Idle power** — sum of `DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE` (W).
- **Devices** — enumerated from the energy-series labels.
- Registered as `dcgm`; selectable via `-energy-provider dcgm` / `energyProvider.type: dcgm`.

### Design notes
- Pure Go, no CGO or Python, cross-platform (unit-testable without GPUs).
- Resolution is bounded by the dcgm-exporter scrape interval; for the tightest window alignment prefer `nvml`. Noted in the package doc and the compatibility matrix.

### Tests
12 `httptest`-based unit tests — interface compliance, registry wiring, multi-GPU window delta, counter-reset clamp, idle-power sum, device enumeration, metric-absent & unreachable errors, config defaults/overrides, metric-line matching. All pass.

### Not in this PR (needs hardware/CI)
Full `measurement-agent` build (pulls in the linux-only nvml/amd providers) and on-GPU validation — tracked under the GPU CI runner (#36).

### Files
- `internal/provider/energy/dcgm/` — provider + tests
- `cmd/measurement-agent/main.go` — register `dcgm`, extend `-energy-provider` help
- `helm/aitra-meter/values.yaml`, `docs/reference/{configuration,compatibility}.md` — docs

author: delozz
body:
…oured

Bets are placed 12-94h ahead of kickoff, but announced lineups exist only ~1h before, so the existing lineup nudge was 0.0 on every real bet - Ronaldo and Haaland never entered the math. Adds a squad-strength signal that works at any horizon, derived from each squad's top-11 season player ratings (the full-squad mean dilutes stars; top-4 is too noisy).

- features/squad.py: squad_strength (top-11 mean) + squad_strength_delta in [-1,1]
- strategy/edge.apply_squad_prior: tilts the full {H,D,A} vector toward the stronger squad and renormalizes (calibration-safe; also trims the draw, which the per-leg lineup nudge never touched)
- signal_gen: fetch cached squad ratings per team in run_live, apply before edge
- combined ELO+squad filter (risk.py): block draw/upset legs when ELO gap >= 150 AND the squad confirms the same favourite - catches the Portugal/Uzbekistan tie (ELO 182) without lowering the pure-ELO 200 threshold
- SQUAD_WEIGHT=4.0 default, chosen from a weight-sweep replay against real bets

Replay: France/Iraq and Portugal/Uzbekistan draw bets now blocked; Egypt/Iran (Iran genuinely the stronger squad) correctly strengthened.

author: alchemy-openclaw
body:
## Summary

The SMS adapter is the only major platform adapter that does not resolve per-channel prompts. Telegram and Slack both call `resolve_channel_prompt()` to inject ephemeral system prompts (e.g. persona/role instructions) into sessions. SMS sessions currently have no way to receive a channel prompt.

This PR adds the same `resolve_channel_prompt()` call used by Telegram, with a `"*"` wildcard fallback so a default prompt can be applied to all SMS sessions without pre-registering every phone number.

## Use case

Multi-tenant SMS workflows (e.g. a community calendar where bar owners text events to a Twilio number). Each phone number gets its own session, but they all share a common persona/instruction prompt. Without this patch, there is no mechanism to inject a system prompt into SMS sessions — `channel_prompts` in config.yaml is silently ignored for SMS.

## Changes

- `plugins/platforms/sms/adapter.py`: resolve `channel_prompt` via `resolve_channel_prompt()` with `"*"` wildcard fallback before constructing the `MessageEvent`

## Config example

```yaml
sms:
  channel_prompts:
    "*": "You are Annika, responding via SMS for the Space Coast Kava Calendar..."
```

## Behavior

- The prompt is ephemeral (injected at API call time, never persisted to transcript history), matching the behavior on Telegram and Slack.
- Per-number prompts take precedence (exact match on `channel_id` = phone number), with `"*"` as the default.
- No breaking changes — if no `channel_prompts` are configured, behavior is unchanged (`resolve_channel_prompt` returns `None`).

## Pattern

Follows the exact pattern already in `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`:

```python
from gateway.platforms.base import resolve_channel_prompt
_channel_prompt = resolve_channel_prompt(self.config.extra, chat_id_str)
```

The only addition is the `"*"` wildcard fallback, which SMS needs because phone numbers are not known in advance.

author: michaelmdiamond
body:
## What

A closed feedback loop that turns ambient Bee transcripts into a self-correcting view of *how* Michael speaks — not what he committed to (that's the existing task pipeline), but his communication habits.

## The loop

1. **Weekly** (`bee_speech_profile.py`, Mon 9am) — analyzes the week's transcripts for filler/hedging, commitment phrasing, recurring topics, and register shifts. Picks **one focus pattern** and writes:
   - an Obsidian profile note (`Speech Profile/{week}.md`)
   - a machine-readable sidecar (`.bee_speech_profile/{week}.json`) — the contract the agent reads
2. **Every ~2h** (`bee_agent.py`) — reads the active focus and runs one extra evidence-gated Claude pass over buffered conversations, logging live instances of the pattern (with quotes) to `.bee_speech_flags/`. Task extraction stays at 30 min; the speech pass is throttled via a disk buffer (`.bee_speech_pending.jsonl`) + clock (`.bee_speech_state.json`).
3. **Next weekly run** ingests those flags so "changes since last week" is graded against **actual logged counts**, not the model's memory.

## Respects the repo's hard rules

- Subscription, not API — all calls via `claude -p`
- Stdlib only — no new deps
- Evidence or it didn't happen — every flag requires a real transcript quote; low-confidence dropped
- Privacy — all new captured/derived data under gitignored `.bee_speech_*` paths
- The speech pass is wrapped so it can never break task extraction, and stays silently inactive until the first weekly sidecar exists

Also gitignores `.bee_labels/` (pre-existing captured task-review data that was untracked but should never be committed).

## Verification

- Both scripts compile; profiler ran end-to-end (49 convs → note + sidecar)
- Detection tested against real 06-23 transcripts — correctly flagged 3 mid-sentence-pivot instances with quotes
- 2h gate simulated: due on first run, false right after a pass, true after 2h+

## Cost

~35–40 extra `claude -p` calls/week (~90–100k tokens) — bounded worst case, batched on busy days.

## Summary
Brings the published cite-check skill bundle in line with two upstream viewer changes that have shipped in `dingduff-mcp` but never made it across to this repo's copy. Version bumps from **v1.7 → v1.8**.

## What the viewer copy was missing
1. **Dark mode** ([DingDuff/dingduff-mcp#263](https://github.com/DingDuff/dingduff-mcp/pull/263)) — tokenized 7 previously-hardcoded contextual colors, added `<meta color-scheme="light dark">`, added a `--on-status-fg` token for white-on-saturated-fill text, added a dark token block. Until this PR, the standalone `review.html` built from this skill was light-only.

2. **Host-context theme** ([DingDuff/dingduff-mcp#279](https://github.com/DingDuff/dingduff-mcp/pull/279)) — inline FOUC bootstrap in `<head>`; a `data-theme` attribute on `<html>` now drives the dark CSS; the bridge now captures `hostContext.theme` from the `ui/initialize` result and listens for `ui/notifications/host-context-changed`. This is what makes the MCP App panel actually follow Claude's in-app theme (`prefers-color-scheme` on an iframe reads the OS, not Claude's theme).

For the standalone `build_review.py` bundle (which is what this repo's skill is for), #263 is the load-bearing change; #279 is a no-op for standalone use (no host bridge) but the inline bootstrap keeps the FOUC-prevention contract consistent.

## Version-bump checklist (per the publishing protocol)
- [x] `dist/dingduff_citation-check_v1.7.skill` → `dist/dingduff_citation-check_v1.8.skill` (same 12-entry zip layout: 4 directories + 8 content files)

body:
Implements **ask H.3** of Jonah's 2026-06-23 response to `OMNICURSOR_DISPATCHER_PLAN.md`: *"Route emit through the shared platform emit path, not a bespoke transport."* OmniCursor must use the same transport policy as the rest of the architecture — the divergent Cursor-only sidecar/drainer is removed so emission flows through the shared platform emit daemon.

### Deleted (bespoke transport — never imported by any hook)
- `src/omnicursor/sidecar/` (daemon, socket_listener, status_server)
- `src/omnicursor/drainer/` (loop, reader, transform, publisher, kafka_publisher, omnidash_bridge, omnidash_publisher, cursor)
- `tests/test_{drainer,sidecar,omnidash_publisher,watch_outbox}.py`
- `scripts/run_{sidecar,omnidash_bridge,bc_stack}.sh`, `scripts/smoke_test.py`

### Kept (not transport)
- **`session_outbox.py`** — durable **local** session-outcome record (`~/.omnicursor/outbox.jsonl`), written by the `stop` hook; `tests/test_session_outbox.py` retained.
- `scripts/watch_outbox.py` — read-only outbox viewer.
- `.cursor/hooks/lib/emit_client.py` — the stdlib producer (unchanged).

### Routing through the shared path (verified, not changed)
The hook's `emit_client` wire protocol — `{"event_type","payload"}\n` → `{"status":"queued","event_id"}\n` plus ping/pong — **matches `omnimarket/node_emit_daemon/socket_server.py` byte-for-byte**. So the shared platform daemon owns `~/.omnicursor/emit.sock` and OmniCursor inherits the platform transport (OMN-13213) with no Cursor-side change. **Daemon provisioning/ensure (W3) is out of scope here** — this PR only removes the divergent stack and confirms the producer already speaks the shared protocol.

### Docs
Removed the Option-C / "event pipeline & sidecar" narrative across README, CLAUDE.md, and `docs/{ARCHITECTURE,CURRENT_STATE,INDEX,QUICKSTART,README}.md` + `src/omnicursor/README.md`; rewrote ARCHITECTURE §8 as "Event emission"; the durable local outbox is preserved throughout. Test count updated 710/28 → 640/24.

### Verification
- `ruff check src/ tests/ .cursor/hooks/` → clean
- `pytest tests/` → **640 passed**

author: johngeorgesample
body:
## What

Adds the schema for a shop hours-of-operation feature:

- **`shop_hours`** — canonical, source-agnostic weekly schedule (`day_of_week` 0=Sun..6=Sat, local `America/New_York` times, split hours = multiple rows, `spans_midnight` flag). Public-read RLS, no public write.
- **`shop_hours_meta`** — per-shop provenance + Google-specific operational data (`source`, `status`, `google_place_id`, `match_distance_m`, `fetched_at`). Admin-only, no RLS policies.
- **`hours-schema-rollback.sql`** — `DROP ... CASCADE` for both tables.

Schema only — applied by hand (no migration framework), matching the `descriptions-backfill.sql` convention.

## Why the hours data isn't in this PR

The populated load (`migrations/hours-backfill.sql`, 173 shops bootstrapped from Google Places API New) is **gitignored**. Google Maps Platform terms permit caching Places content — including opening hours — for at most 30 days, after which it must be deleted; only the Place ID is exempt. Committing the parsed hours would put 30-day-max cached content permanently in git history, defeating the compliance design (14-day refresh + per-run 30-day sweep). The hours load is a regenerable, apply-once artifact.

## Status

- [x] Schema + rollback
- [ ] Apply schema + hours load to the database (pending)
- [ ] Display/UI wiring + required "Powered by Google" attribution (separate, out of scope)

Draft until the schema + first hours load are applied and verified.

author: karajanchang
body:
## Problem

The Hub's auto-update check ran **once, on mount** (`DashboardApp.tsx`, `useEffect(…, [])` — no polling, no re-check on focus). A Hub instance left open never notices a release published after it launched.

Concretely: a **2.26.9** instance open before **v2.27.0** went live checked once, saw nothing newer, and never looked again — so no update banner, even though `latest.json` correctly advertised `2.27.0`. (`brew upgrade mur` only updates the CLI; the Hub `.app` is a separate Tauri bundle that self-updates.)

## Fix

Re-run the same check whenever the window regains focus — the common case (user comes back to the app). Listener is cleaned up on unmount.

- skipped: a polling timer. `focus` covers coming back to the app; add an interval only if it must notice while the window stays focused for hours.

## Test

`tsc --noEmit` clean. Manual: open Hub on an older version, publish a newer `latest.json`, switch away and back → banner appears.

author: alexskrypnyk
body:
Closes #2719

## Summary

Introduces a single, platform-agnostic `task` runner at `vendor/drevops/vortex-tooling/src/task` so the Acquia Cloud hooks dispatch operations through one entrypoint - `task <operation>` - instead of calling the individual `task-*-acquia` scripts directly. This unblocks #2715 (exposing the tooling scripts as `vendor/bin/` binaries), where `task` becomes the public entrypoint and the platform-specific `task-*-acquia` scripts stay internal.

The runner resolves a platform-agnostic operation to the implementation for the configured hosting platform - `task-<operation>-<platform>` - reusing the existing `notify` router pattern. The platform is read from `VORTEX_TASK_PLATFORM`, falling back to `VORTEX_PLATFORM`; the Acquia hooks export `VORTEX_PLATFORM=acquia`. Both the operation and the platform are validated against whitelists before the sibling path is built, and the sibling is required to be executable, so only approved scripts can run.

## Changes

### Task runner

- New `.vortex/tooling/src/task` dispatches `task <operation> [args...]` to `task-<operation>-<platform>`. It validates the operation (`copy-db`, `copy-files`, `purge-cache`) and the platform (`acquia`, `lagoon`) against whitelists, requires the resolved sibling script to be executable, and forwards trailing arguments. It fails with a clear message on a missing or unknown operation, a missing or unsupported platform, or an operation that the platform does not implement.

author: uwgzq
body:
## Summary

Adds **MMMU-Pro** (`MMMU/MMMU_Pro`) — the harder, more-robust successor to MMMU — as a new
**image-QA** benchmark for the released HF `allenai/Molmo2-4B`, evaluated through the same
`HuggingFaceProvider` multimodal path (preset `molmo2-4b`).

A single **`mmmu_pro`** task runs all three official settings and produces **one `metrics.json`**
with `standard_10_accuracy`, `standard_4_accuracy`, `vision_accuracy`, and the **primary
`overall` = (standard-10 + vision) / 2** — the number SOTA models report.

It is **decoupled from the existing `mmmu` task** (its own prompts, parser, and scorer; no reuse of
`mmmu_parsing.py` / `MmmuScorer` / `format_mc_question`), faithful to the official
`MMMU-Benchmark/MMMU` `mmmu-pro` repo, and is added to the `molmo2_imageqa` suite (its `overall`
counts as one 0-1 entry, like the other image-QA benchmarks).

## Verified — Molmo2-4B (fp32 + bf16 autocast, full run, 5190 examples)

| Metric | Score |
|---|---:|
| **overall** (= (standard-10 + vision)/2) — primary | **26.01%** |
| standard_10_accuracy | 35.20% |
| standard_4_accuracy | 44.62% |
| vision_accuracy | 16.82% |

## Faithful to the official MMMU-Pro protocol

- **Direct prompts, verbatim** from `prompts.yaml` (CoT mode not used): standard = `"Answer with the
  option letter from the given choices directly."`; vision = the same + `" The last line of your
  response should be of the following format: 'Answer: $LETTER' …"`.
- **Standard** = `question + "A. …\nB. …" + direct prompt` (A–J for 10 options) with **all
  interleaved images attached in `<image i>` token-appearance order** — options are shuffled, so
  token order need not match `image_i` key order (official `replace_images_tokens`, `<image i>` →
  `<image>`). **Vision** sends only the instruction + the single screenshot (`image` column); the
  question/options are rendered inside the screenshot.
- **Answer parser** (on the raw response, MC-only): last `Answer:` marker → `(A)` → `"A "` → `"A."`
  → option text; multiple → last occurrence; per-example seeded fallback for re-run determinism.

## Changes

- `src/olmo_eval/common/image_qa/mmmu_pro.py` (new) — prompts, prompt assembly,
  `replace_images_tokens`, and the official `parse_multi_choice_response` / `mmmu_pro_score`.
- `src/olmo_eval/common/scorers/mmmu_pro.py` (new) — `MmmuProScorer` (raw response, no
  `clean_prediction`).
- `src/olmo_eval/evals/tasks/mmmu_pro.py` (new) — the single `mmmu_pro` task (3 settings,
  interleaved), per-setting + `overall` metrics, and a `format_request` that attaches the
  multi-image (standard) or single-screenshot (vision) tuple.
- `src/olmo_eval/evals/suites/molmo2.py` — `"mmmu_pro"` added to `MOLMO2_IMAGE_QA_TASKS`.
- `tests/evals/tasks/test_mmmu_pro.py` (new) — CPU-only: parser ladder, shuffled image-order,
  prompts, per-setting + overall metrics, request construction.

No new dependencies (pure HF hub; `MMMU/MMMU_Pro` cached like `MMMU/MMMU`).

## Verification

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean; `ty check` clean on the new files; full suite
**1773 passed, 5 skipped**. Full GPU run completed and produced the numbers above.

## Fix

The previous PR used inline SQL timezone expressions (`AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'`) which caused a PostgreSQL syntax error → 500 → "Something went wrong" on the analytics page.

Replaced with a JS helper `istDayBounds()` that computes IST midnight as UTC ISO strings and passes them as parameterized values (`$1`, `$2`) to the query.

- Today: `created_at >= <IST midnight today UTC> AND created_at <= NOW()`
- Yesterday: `created_at >= <IST midnight yesterday UTC> AND created_at < <IST midnight today UTC>`
- 3 Days / Week / Month: unchanged rolling window

author: grhohertz
body:
## Summary

Adds `:update --drain` — a staged **graceful** self-update so a mid-session upgrade no longer kills in-flight work or abruptly severs interactive sessions. (TASK-203 / S9.4)

`:update` is unchanged (atomic swap + advise restart). The new `--drain` flag runs a strict, gated sequence:

```
quiesce (checkpoint+detach attached runs, bounded await of background work)
   └─ (gate) ─▶ swap (update::perform — the pure atomic binary swap)
                   └─ (gate) ─▶ restart (re-exec the new binary in place)
```

**Headline safety invariant (AC5):** the swap is reached only after quiesce returns, and the restart only after a *successful* swap — a swap failure never restarts (no half-updated restart).

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `update.rs` | `drain()`, `perform_with_drain()`, `restart_in_place()`, `run_staged()` gate model, `DrainCtx`/`DrainReport`/`DrainOutcome`, `CHECKPOINT_SENTINEL`, `AISH_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (default 120s) |
| `container.rs` | `current_selection()` / `current_backend_is_container()` reuse `resolve_selection` so drain detects host-vs-container backend identically to `run_worker` |
| `coordinator.rs` | `fold_operator_messages` strips `CHECKPOINT_SENTINEL` so the control token never reaches the model; reaching the round boundary *is* the checkpoint |
| `repl.rs` | `:update --drain` parsing, AC8 host-subprocess confirmation gate, staged-path wiring + report output, `:help` entry |

## Behavior notes

- **Container-backed workers (S9.1)** have their own PID 1 and survive the restart → they are *not* awaited (AC3/AC4). Only host-subprocess work is bounded-awaited to a checkpoint.
- **Host workers** die on restart, so `--drain` shows an explicit confirmation gate first (AC8).
- Checkpoint broadcast reuses the `coordinator_messages` mailbox (same channel as `:tell`).

## Tests

7 new unit tests covering gate ordering (swap unreachable unless quiesce ok; restart unreachable unless swap ok), the drain-report partition, `AISH_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` parsing, the sentinel constant, and the host-drain warning. Full `cargo build` + targeted test runs green.

## Deferred (integration-gated)

AC3 container survival and AC6 post-restart rediscovery light up once S9.5 lands; the hooks are in place and noted in the spec.

🤖 Draft for review.

author: chirag30sharma
body:
This pull request introduces a new enhanced offline/online sync architecture for the TLC app, focusing on robust conflict detection and resolution, improved sync status tracking, and richer local data management. The changes lay the groundwork for advanced offline-first capabilities, including a new IndexedDB schema, a context provider for sync state, and modular conflict resolution logic.

**Key changes:**

### 1. Enhanced Local Database Schema and Utilities
- Introduces `enhancedDb` (`enhancedDb.ts`) with new tables for master data, transactional records, sync queue/history, and device metadata, supporting advanced sync and conflict tracking. Includes utility functions for device ID management and device info initialization.

### 2. Sync State Management via React Context
- Adds `EnhancedSyncContext` (`EnhancedSyncContext.tsx`), a React context/provider that tracks sync status, statistics, conflict records, and local data freshness. Exposes actions for syncing, refreshing master data, and resolving conflicts. Includes automatic periodic sync and stats refresh logic.

### 3. Modular Conflict Detection and Resolution
- Implements `conflictResolutionService.ts`, providing functions to detect version conflicts, resolve them with multiple strategies (client wins, server wins, merged, manual), and generate human-readable conflict descriptions. Includes logic to determine the best resolution strategy based on entity type and conflict age.

### 4. API Client Extensions for Sync Operations
- Extends the API client (`apiClient.ts`) with generic CRUD methods and sync-specific endpoints to facilitate flexible, entity-agnostic sync and conflict resolution flows.

These changes collectively enable a more resilient offline experience, sophisticated conflict handling, and improved transparency for users and developers regarding sync status and data integrity.

author: sacor10
body:
## What

On phones, the Stumble **profile** page (`/stumble/u/:username`) was rough — the avatar, `@handle`, Following/Followers counts, the "This is you / Change username" badge, and the "Stumble their likes" button were all jammed onto one overlapping row, and the top **Stumble!** back button had disappeared.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Header crams onto one line, "This is you" overlapping the counts; no way back to the feed | Avatar + handle + counts on row 1; badge and full-width "Stumble their likes" stack below; Stumble! back button restored |

## Why

The phone (≤640px) rules introduced for the feed view in #55 were **unscoped**. Both routes render the same `.su-toolbar` / `.su-subbar` classes, so those rules also hit the profile route, which has no bottom action bar:
- `.su-toolbar .su-stumble-btn { display: none }` hid the profile's only back-to-Stumble button.
- `.su-subbar { flex-wrap: nowrap }` forced the profile header (`.su-profile-bar`, also a `.su-subbar`) onto one line → the overlap.

## How

- Tag the two route roots: `su-root--feed` (StumblePage) and `su-root--profile` (StumbleProfilePage).
- Scope the feed-only phone rules (hide top Stumble button, tighten/`nowrap` the sub-bar, hide the moved controls) to `.su-root--feed`, so the profile route is unaffected.
- Add a phone layout for `.su-root--profile .su-profile-bar`: it wraps, with avatar + identity on the first row and each action (`self-badge` / `Follow` / `Stumble their likes`) dropping to its own full-width row; tab row scrolls horizontally if needed.

Desktop/tablet layout is unchanged on both routes.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` + `npm run build` pass.
- Verified with Playwright at 390px (self view) and 360px (other-user view) — clean wrapped header, Stumble! back button present — and 1100px (desktop header unchanged).

## Note

This stacks on **#55** (the rigid mobile feed layout), which introduced the unscoped rules — so it's based on that branch and the diff here is just the profile fix. Once #55 merges to `main`, I can retarget this to `main`.

body:
## Bloco 8a — Testes do inventory-service

Estabelece a base de testes do inventory-service com Jest, ts-jest e Supertest, cobrindo a lógica de estoque, estrutura, constraints e validação de ambiente. Inclui as correções da revisão e o fechamento da lista de testes planejada para a fase.

### Cobertura final: 30 testes em 4 suítes

| Suíte | Testes | O que cobre |
|---|---|---|
| concorrencia.test.ts | 1 | Reserva atômica sob requisições simultâneas (teste de integração com banco real) |
| stock.service.test.ts | 21 | setStock, getAvailability, reserveStock, releaseStock + todos os caminhos de erro |
| estrutura.test.ts | 5 | /health, separação app/server, 3 constraints CHECK do banco |
| env.test.ts | 8 | Validação de variáveis obrigatórias e porta no boot |

### Destaque: teste de concorrência
O teste mais importante da fase. Dispara duas reservas simultâneas do último item via Promise.allSettled e prova que exatamente uma passa e uma falha (INSUFFICIENT_STOCK), com reserved final nunca ultrapassando quantity. Valida a correção atômica (`$executeRaw` com UPDATE condicional) do Bloco 5 — a única forma de provar que não há overselling sob concorrência real.

### Isolamento do banco de testes (correção de segurança do review)
- Banco dedicado `inventory_test_db` com migrations aplicadas (tabela + 3 constraints)
- `.env.test` separado (bloqueado no .gitignore)
- `tests/setup.ts` recusa rodar se a DATABASE_URL não apontar para um banco com 'test' no nome — trava contra execução acidental em banco real
- Verificado: 0 registros de teste no banco de dev após execução

### Correções aplicadas da revisão
- **Constraints (reforçado):** cada teste verifica o nome específico da constraint na mensagem (quantity_nao_negativa, reserved_menor_igual_quantity, reserved_nao_negativa), não um erro genérico — um erro de conexão não passaria por engano
- **Separação app/server:** teste agora verifica que importar o app não faz o Express escutar porta (app.listening undefined), em vez de só checar que é função
- **tsconfig.dev:** sobrescreve types ["node"], impedindo globais do Jest no código de produção
- **releaseStock simétrico:** adicionados casos de amount zero, negativo, float, string e produto inexistente
- **Matriz Jest 30 / ts-jest 29:** verificada compatível (deduped no lockfile)

### Refatoração de testabilidade
O server.ts validava ambiente com process.exit() solto no nível do módulo — não testável sem matar o test runner. Lógica extraída para funções puras em config/env.ts que lançam erro; o server.ts captura e encerra apenas no ponto de entrada. Mesmo comportamento externo, agora testável e reutilizável.

### Arquitetura de testes
- 4 tsconfig separados (editor, dev, build, test) — mesma estrutura validada no auth-service
- globalTeardown centraliza e tolera o disconnect do Prisma (sem --forceExit, sem vazamento de conexão)
- Script de teste com --ci (evita o RangeError do reporter)

### Adiado — Bloco 8c
Testes HTTP de rotas de stock (status codes, payloads inválidos, autorização via API) serão agrupados com os testes de integração HTTP do product-service. Os testes atuais cobrem a camada de service, onde mora a lógica atômica.

### Checklist
- [x] 30 testes passando em banco isolado
- [x] Teste de concorrência obrigatório (provado)
- [x] Todas as correções do review aplicadas
- [x] .env e .env.test bloqueados no .gitignore
- [x] Sem vazamento de conexão no teardown

body:
Three fixes to the baseline solver:

- **Determinism:** the solver iterated over and randomly sampled from Python `set`s of orders, so results varied from run to run and `random.seed` had no effect on RDGA. The order pool is now a list in a fixed order with deterministic tie-breaking, so both algorithms reproduce exactly.
- **Item goal:** stop adding orders to a batch once the (remaining) item goal is reached, matching the inner-loop condition `|I| < IG` in Algorithm 1 of the paper. Previously the batch filled up to `max_orders_per_batch` regardless of the goal, overshooting it.
- **Efficiency:** RDGA samples one order in O(1) (random index + swap-pop) instead of re-sorting the whole pool each step.

author: digitalidentitywallet-team
body:
## Resolve `path_nested` against the `$.vp` root for `jwt_vp_json`

### Summary

For `jwt_vp_json` presentations, wallets conventionally set the
`presentation_submission` `path_nested` to `$.vp.verifiableCredential[...]`
— rooted at the decoded VP-JWT, which carries a `vp` claim. OpenCred strips the
`vp` wrapper before applying that path, so the standard path resolves to
nothing and verification fails with *"VC not found in presentation."* This adds
a `{vp}`-wrapped fallback so both the wrapped and unwrapped paths resolve.

### Motivation

In `verifyJwtSubmission` (`lib/workflows/common/oid4vp-shared.js`), the VP-JWT is
decoded via `unenvelopeJwtVp(vp_token)`, which **strips the `.vp` wrapper** and
returns the inner presentation object. The `path_nested` selector (`vcQuery`)
is then applied to that unwrapped object.

However, per the OpenID4VP / Presentation Exchange convention for
`jwt_vp_json`, wallets express `path_nested` relative to the **decoded VP-JWT**,
whose payload has the form `{ "vp": { "verifiableCredential": [...] } }`. So a
conformant wallet sends:

```json
{ "path_nested": { "path": "$.vp.verifiableCredential[0]", ... } }
```

Applied to the already-unwrapped object, `$.vp.verifiableCredential[0]`
matches nothing → the credential is never located → verification fails even
though the presentation and credential are valid. This blocks interop with
wallets (e.g. EUDI Wallet) that use the standard `$.vp`-rooted path.

### Approach

After the existing lookups fail to locate the VC, try the selector against a
`{vp}`-re-wrapped structure:

```js
if(!vc && vcQuery) {
  vc = vcQuery({vp});
}
```

This makes both forms resolve:

- `$.verifiableCredential[...]` (against the unwrapped object — existing path)
- `$.vp.verifiableCredential[...]` (against the `{vp}`-wrapped object — standard)

The fallback runs **only** when the prior lookups returned nothing; the located
VC still goes through full VC-JWT signature verification and the
`trustedCredentialIssuers` check downstream, so no verification step is skipped.

### Backward compatibility

Fully backward compatible. The new branch is a fallback reached only when the
existing selectors return no VC; submissions that resolve today are unaffected.

### Testing

Adds `test/unit/workflows/16-path-nested-vp.test.js`, asserting that a
production-shaped `vcQuery` (built from a `$.vp.verifiableCredential[...]`
`path_nested`) does **not** resolve against the unwrapped VP but **does**
resolve once the VP is re-wrapped as `{vp}` — i.e. the fallback this change
adds.

Also verified end-to-end with a wallet that sets `path_nested` to
`$.vp.verifiableCredential[...]`: the credential is now located and verified,
where it previously failed with "VC not found in presentation."

author: alexcos20
body:
Closing #2099 
# Add Service-on-Demand ("services") client support

## What

Adds client support for the new **Service-on-Demand** feature shipped in ocean-node
([oceanprotocol/ocean-node#1402](https://github.com/oceanprotocol/ocean-node/pull/1402)).

Service-on-Demand lets a consumer launch a long-lived container (JupyterLab, a vLLM
inference server, VS Code, etc.) on an Ocean node's compute environment, pay for a set
duration via escrow, and reach it through forwarded ports. Unlike compute jobs (which run
to completion and exit), services stay up until they expire, are stopped, or are extended.

This PR is the **ocean.js side only** — the node already implements the feature. It gives
SDK users the methods to drive the full service lifecycle.

## New API

All six methods are available on `ProviderInstance` and work over **both HTTP and P2P**
(the provider picks the transport automatically, same as compute):

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `getServiceTemplates(nodeUri)` | List the service blueprints a node offers (public, no signature) |
| `serviceStart(nodeUri, signer, params)` | Pay and launch a service container |
| `getServiceStatus(nodeUri, signer, serviceId?)` | Get a service's status + access endpoints |
| `serviceExtend(nodeUri, signer, serviceId, duration, payment)` | Pay to push the expiry forward |
| `serviceRestart(nodeUri, signer, serviceId)` | Recreate the container (same ports/expiry) |
| `serviceStop(nodeUri, signer, serviceId)` | Tear the service down |

Typical flow: `getServiceTemplates` → pick a template and a compatible environment
(via `getComputeEnvironments`) → `serviceStart` → `getServiceStatus` to read the endpoint URL.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Mirrors the existing compute / persistent-storage client patterns** — same signing
  (`consumerAddress` + `nonce` + signature, or an auth token), same endpoint discovery, same
  HTTP/P2P split. Nothing structurally new.
- **`userData`** (env vars passed into the container) is given as a plain object and is
  **encrypted client-side** to the node's public key before sending — the same ECIES approach
  already used for docker-registry credentials. It is never returned in responses.
- **New types** (`ServiceJob`, `ServiceTemplatePublic`, `ServiceStartParams`, …) and the six
  `SERVICE_*` protocol command strings, which match the node's values exactly.
- `ComputeEnvironment` gains an optional `features` flag so clients can tell which
  environments accept services.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`test/unit/Services.test.ts`) — verifies the protocol command strings, status
  enum, exposed methods, and the userData encryption round-trip. Runs without a node.
- **Integration** (`test/integration/Services.test.ts`) — exercises the full lifecycle
  (templates → start → status → extend → restart → stop) against a live node. It **skips
  cleanly** when the node has no Service-on-Demand configured, so it won't break CI on a
  standard barge setup.

Build, type-check, and lint all pass.

* **Bug Fixes**

author: gorbeia
body:
## Why

A user hit a `word-order` (reassemble-the-sentence) drill that marked a **grammatically correct** answer wrong:

- Expected: `Zuek herriko danborrada entzuten duzue goizean`
- Their answer: `Zuek herriko danborrada goizean entzuten duzue`

Both are valid Basque — the difference is only which constituent takes the pre-verb **focus** slot (the *galdegaia*). The root cause: `word-order` questions were auto-generated from *any* sentence in the 4–9 word range and graded against the single authored string. Because Basque's focus rule lets constituents move, most object-plus-adjunct sentences have several valid orders, so strict single-string grading is unfair.

## What changed

**Mechanism (fail-closed, opt-in):** `word-order` now only generates from a sentence variant explicitly tagged `wordOrderSafe: true` (checked in `meetsWordOrderThreshold` alongside the existing word-count window). Untagged sentences — the default — keep every other framing (`sentence`/`type-verb`/`negative`/…) but never become a reorder drill. The flag is kept **orthogonal to `validFor`** (it doesn't touch cross-verb distractor eligibility; the `validFor` gap baseline is unchanged).

**Curation (two passes, criteria documented):**

1. **Negatives** — single-complement negated sentences (`[Subject] ez [aux] [one complement]`, where the `ez`+aux sequence is grammatically pinned): `izan`/`egon`/`ibili`/`ukan`/`jakin`/`joan` (all persons), `etorri` (`ni` only).
2. **Affirmatives** — four-word periphrastic clauses (`[subject] [one complement] [participle] [aux]`), excluding `nori` (dative) verbs and any sentence with a trailing adjunct: `jan`/`edan`/`erosi`/`ikusi`/`hartu`/`ari`/`nahi`/`ukatu`/`itzularazi`/`dantzarazi`.

**~212 sentence fillings are now eligible across 17 verbs** (31 negative + 181 affirmative). Deliberately still untagged (a later fluent-reviewed pass): 5+ word affirmatives with a trailing time/place adjunct, synthetic-verb sentences with two complements (`eduki`), and all `nori` verbs.

## Docs

- `docs/EXERCISE_ENGINE.md` — "Word-order safety (`wordOrderSafe`)" mechanism + the per-pass coverage.
- `docs/LANGUAGE_DECISIONS.md` — the Basque criterion for what counts as a single-fair-order sentence (negatives + affirmatives).
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` — the design decision and the scripted-then-reviewed affirmatives pass.

## Testing

- `npm test` — 438 passing (added a gate regression test: a length-eligible but untagged sentence is never offered as `word-order`).
- `npm run lint` and `npm run build` clean.
- Merged latest `main` (object-axis pool work) into this branch; conflicts were only in the two newest-on-top decision logs, resolved by keeping both sides.

## Reviewer note (a Basque judgment call)

Plain transitive SOV affirmatives (e.g. `Nik ura edaten dut`) are tagged because SOV is the taught/neutral order, but Basque does permit focus-driven reorderings. If you'd rather be stricter and keep only the truly fixed frames (`ari`/`nahi`), the plain transitives can be pulled back out — happy to adjust.

body:
Closes #83

## What changed (tooling-only)
Adds **Lighthouse CI as an informational, non-blocking performance report** on PRs — the runtime-signal layer from GUIDELINES → Performance gates (CI).

- **`@lhci/cli`** + **`.lighthouserc.json`**: collects **3 runs**, reports the **median**, runs against the built web app (`staticDistDir: src/apps/web/dist`), and uploads to **LHCI temporary-public-storage** (report URL printed in the job log, reachable from the PR's checks).
- A **separate `Lighthouse (advisory)` workflow** (`.github/workflows/lighthouse.yml`) builds the app and runs `lhci autorun` on every PR — in its own workflow so it never slows or destabilizes the required `quality` job.
- **Non-blocking, documented explicitly:** every Lighthouse assertion is `warn` (never errors), and **both the job and the run step are `continue-on-error`**, so a low score can never fail the PR or block merge. The deterministic gate remains the size-limit budget; this is the runtime signal only.
- `pnpm lighthouse` script for local runs; `.lighthouseci/` output is git-ignored; README documents the advisory behavior and how to read it.

## Validation
- Ran `lhci autorun` **locally against the built app** (via Edge): Lighthouse loaded the page and completed all audits (FCP/LCP/CLS/INP/TBT…), confirming the static-dist collection + median config works. The only local error was a Windows-specific Chromium temp-dir cleanup `EPERM` after the audits finished — irrelevant on the Linux CI runners (which have Chrome preinstalled); the audit run itself succeeded.
- **Advisory behavior:** assertions are `warn` + `continue-on-error` at job and step level, and it is a non-required separate workflow — a perf regression lowers the reported score but cannot block merge.
- `pnpm validate` green; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes.

author: rasbandit
body:
## What this fixes
Running the #741 backfill on prod surfaced a deeper bug: `mix engram.utf8_audit --fix` reported `fixed: 5` but a re-scan kept finding `corrupt: 5` — all 5 were `#NNN–`-style tags.

**Root cause:** the inline-tag regex was compiled **without the `u` flag**:
```elixir
@inline_tag_re ~r{(?:^|\s)#([\w][\w/-]*)}
```
In byte mode, Erlang's `re` char tables count a multibyte char's **lead byte** (`0xE2` of an en-dash `–`) as `\w` but its continuation bytes as not. So valid content like `#628–` captured `628`+`0xE2` — an **invalid-UTF-8 tag emitted from perfectly valid content** — which got encrypted into `tags_ciphertext` and persisted at rest.

That explains both mysteries:
- The write-time **content** scrub (#740) never caught it — the *content* is valid; only the derived tag was mangled.
- The #741 backfill couldn't fix it — it repairs by re-saving content through `upsert`, which **re-derives tags via the same byte-slicing `extract_tags`**, reproducing the corruption every run.

## The fix
Add the `u` (unicode) flag so the scan is codepoint-aware: `–` is one non-word codepoint, the capture stops cleanly at `628` (then rejected as numeric → no tag). Real multibyte tags (`#café`, `#über`, `#area/sub`) are unaffected.

**No backfill code change needed:** once `extract_tags` is correct, re-deriving yields clean tags, so the existing `utf8_audit --fix` cleans the legacy prod rows on a re-run (verified by test).

## Tests
- `extract_tags` byte-slice regression (valid `#628–` content → no invalid tag) + real-multibyte-tag intact
- write path stores **valid tags at rest** for `#628–` content
- backfill drives the injected prod-shape tag corruption to `corrupt: 0`
- Full: `mix format` · `compile --warnings-as-errors` · `credo --strict` · Dialyzer (clean) · 157 affected tests, 0 failures

## Deploy plan
Ship via `release-v0.5.533`, then re-run `Engram.Notes.Utf8Backfill.scan(fix: true)` on prod — the 5 legacy rows clean to 0.

Follow-up to #740/#741; closes the root cause behind the prod `corrupt: 5`.

body:
## Summary

Browser horror FPS (Three.js r184 + Vite 8). Beyond the base game, this PR adds a full second wave of gameplay/atmosphere features and a win condition, all kept GPU-cheap for GTX 1650-class hardware (no new dynamic lights — lamps are emissive-only; one shadow caster; ≤4 active bulbs via distance culling).

New this round:

- **Tuning** (`constants.js`): `MOUSE_SENSITIVITY` 0.0022 → 0.00165 (~25% lower), flashlight `DRAIN_PER_SEC` 1.6 → 0.64 (~60% slower).
- **Detailed furniture & decor** (`map/Furniture.js`, wired in `Mansion._buildFurniture`): procedural tables, chairs, sofas, coffee tables, cabinets, wardrobes, dressers, beds, shelves, counters, appliances + rugs, paintings, vases, plants, plates. All double as colliders; placed clear of the ±5.5 doorway gridlines. Emissive wall/floor lamps flicker via `Furniture.update(dt)` (no PointLights added).
- **Static physical items** (`items/ItemEntity.js`): items rest on the floor/surfaces with a fixed yaw, no bob/spin; `update()` is a no-op. Picked up with `E`.
- **Working doors** (`map/Doors.js`): a hinged `Door` per interior doorway, `E` to open/close, swing animation (`pivot.rotation.y` lerps to `±0.62π`), creak SFX (`AudioManager.door`), and collision toggled via new `CollisionSystem.removeCollider/addCollider` (closed = blocks, open = passable).
- **Door jump-scares** (`Game._wireDoorScares`): on `DOOR_OPENED`, 40% chance the creature slams in front of the doorway (`EnemyManager.jumpScareAt` → `Enemy.jumpScareAt`) with a stinger, light brown-out and camera shake (`Player.shake`).
- **Creature crawl/stand** (`enemy/Enemy.js`): limbs blend between a crawl pose (wandering) and a reared stand pose (chasing/scare) via a `_stand` 0..1 blend.
- **Hidden exit & win** (`Doors._buildHiddenExit`, `ui/Overlays`, `Game`): a bookshelf on the living-room west wall. Two-step interact — *Search the bookshelf* (needs the rusty key; consumed) slides it aside, then *Escape into the night* emits `GAME_WON` → `GameState.WON` + "YOU ESCAPED" overlay.

Interaction was generalized: `InteractionSystem.extras` holds non-item interactables (doors, exit) implementing `{ position, range, prompt, interact() }`; items are still picked up via inventory, extras just call `interact()`.

Verified: `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass; in-browser smoke test confirmed furniture/lamps render, doors open with collision + swing, jump-scare places the creature + shakes the camera, and the key→bookshelf→escape flow reaches the win screen, with restart resetting all of it.

author: abdulbeast4-creator
body:
## Summary

Establishes structural string-size characterization over the `formatCompleteJson`
serialization utility (`hushh-webapp/lib/utils/json-to-human.ts`), pinning how it
handles very large (10,000+ char) string payloads.

## Truth-first scope correction

- The original task referenced `hushh-research/__tests__/utils/...`. There is no
  top-level `__tests__` in this repo; vitest (`hushh-webapp/vitest.config.ts`)
  only includes `__tests__/**` under `hushh-webapp`. The runnable file therefore
  lives at `hushh-webapp/__tests__/utils/format-string-lengths.test.ts`.
- The task asked to assert behavior "without memory or parsing limits." Truth:
  `formatCompleteJson` imposes **no string length limit and does not truncate
  text**. Scalar strings route through `formatValue → cleanMarkdown`, which only
  strips markdown markers (`***`, `**`, `*`, `` ` ``) and trims surrounding
  whitespace — the remaining characters are emitted in full. There is **no**
  ellipsis, byte cap, or `... and N more` applied to string fields.
- The only truncation paths in this module are array element caps
  (e.g. `holdings.slice(0, 10)`), not string-length caps. The suite asserts:
  - a 10k top-level string is emitted in full
  - a 10k string inside an object section is emitted in full
  - markdown wrappers are stripped while the 10k body survives
  - a 50k payload completes quickly without throwing (linear, no parser blow-up)
  - embedded newlines in a large multi-line string are preserved.

## Verification

- `npm test -- __tests__/utils/format-string-lengths.test.ts` → 5/5 pass
- `git status` limited to the single new test file; no production source changed

## CI gate checklist

- [x] PR Base Policy — targets `integration/pr-train`
- [x] DCO Verified — commit is signed off (`-s`)
- [x] Test Only Surface Change — zero production runtime risk
- [x] Truth-First — documents real no-length-limit / no-truncation string behavior

author: journeyspartner
body:
## 概要

2026-06-25 生成記事「外国アーティスト・スポーツ選手への報酬で消費税はどう処理する？」のまとめセクションが **「免税事業者・簡易」で途中切断**されていたが、review_comment は空で警告が出ず、user が気付くまで放置されていた。

調査の結果、**2 つの問題**が判明：

## 原因 1: PR #215 で truncation 検知コードが誤って削除されていた

PR #215「全個人事業者・全法人ペルソナを追加」の commit 7c2c727 が generate-draft.js を編集した際、**PR #195 で実装した truncation 検知ロジックが意図せず削除**されていた：
- `checkBodyTailComplete` 関数
- `generateWithOpenAI` の戻り値 `stopReason`
- `generateArticle` 内の truncation 警告ロジック

レビュー時に気付かず、本 PR で復元する。

## 原因 2: ensureDisclaimer が truncation を覆い隠す

`postProcess()` 内の `ensureDisclaimer()` は本文に免責文がなければ標準免責文を自動追加する。今回 LLM がまとめセクション中で切れて免責文を出力しなかったため：

1. `ensureDisclaimer` が末尾に標準免責文を追加
2. 結果の末尾が「。」になり `checkBodyTailComplete` が ok 判定
3. 警告ゼロで draft 化

## 対策（3 層判定）

truncation 判定を **raw 出力**（postProcess 前）に対して行う 3 条件で実施：

| 条件 | 検知対象 |
|---|---|
| ① `stop_reason === 'max_tokens'` / `'length'` | LLM が物理的に切れた |
| ② raw に免責文がない（`rawHasDisclaimer` 新規追加） | ensureDisclaimer が補完 = LLM が出力する前に止まった |
| ③ raw 末尾が句点で終わらない（`checkBodyTailComplete` 復元） | まとめ内などで途切れた |

いずれかに該当すれば review_comment に警告を埋め込み：

> ⚠ 末尾途切れの疑い（stop_reason=max_tokens / 免責文が生成されず自動補完 / 末尾が「○○」で句点なし — truncation 疑い） — 公開前に末尾を確認してください

## 検証

- 新規ロジック単体テスト: **7/7 PASS**
  - `rawHasDisclaimer`: 免責文あり/個別事情パターン/途中切断/空 を判別
  - `checkBodyTailComplete`: 「免税事業者・簡易」型の途中切断 / 正常終端 を判別
- 既存テスト: banned-phrases 44/44, nta-crawler 27/27 PASS（リグレッションなし）

## 後続

本 PR merge 後、該当 draft (`2026-06-25-deepdive-influencer_creator-specified-services-guide`) の末尾を手動補完する。

## Test plan

- [x] 新規ロジック単体テスト 7/7 PASS

- [ ] merge 後、次回の生成記事で warning が review_comment に出ること確認

author: automaat
body:
## Motivation

Pointing `--address` at a `200` endpoint whose body is not a JSON
control-plane index — an HTML login/ingress page, or a wrong subpath
such as `/gui` — surfaced a raw `decoding ...: invalid character '<'`
error. That obscures the real problem: the address does not point at a
Kuma control plane. Found during a full pre-ship manual test pass across
universal, k8s, and multizone clusters.

> Changelog: fix(client): clearer error for non-Kuma endpoint

## Implementation information

`client.index()` now treats a `200` whose body fails to decode as
not-a-Kuma-CP: it returns an empty `cpIndex` so `audit()` reports its
existing friendly `does not look like a Kuma control plane (GET /
returned no version)` message (exit 2). Connection failures (refused /
DNS / TLS) and non-200 statuses (404, etc.) keep their distinct
messages — only a `200` with an unparseable index body is reinterpreted.

Added `TestNonKumaEndpointReportsFriendlyError`, which asserts both the
friendly message and that no raw JSON decode text leaks.

## Supporting documentation

Verified end-to-end against a stub serving HTML on `/` and a live
Kong Mesh CP via `/gui`. All quality gates pass (test, golangci-lint 0
issues, nilaway, vet, gofmt).

author: larryro
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2117.

`tale deploy` hard-failed (exit 1, no retry) when the Convex push hit a **module-analyze timeout** (`InvalidModules` + `Function execution timed out (maximum duration: 2s)`), even though the condition is transient — an immediate re-run succeeds with zero code changes. The deploy error classifier in `services/platform/docker-entrypoint.sh` routed this error to the final `unclassified` `else` branch, which leaves `retry=false` and exits 1.

## Change

Add a classification branch in `deploy_convex_functions`, before the final `else`, that matches the push-analyze timeout (both `InvalidModules` **and** `Function execution timed out` present) and sets `retry=true`, so it reuses the existing 3× exponential-backoff retry loop — mirroring the `SearchIndexesUnavailable` retryable precedent.

Matching both strings together keeps this specific to the push-analyze timeout and avoids catching unrelated runtime/action timeouts. Non-transient push failures (`InvalidSchema`, `ModulesTooLarge`, `AuthConfigMissingEnvironmentVariable`, …) still fail fast — unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- ✅ A Convex push failing with `InvalidModules` + `Function execution timed out (maximum duration: 2s)` is logged as transient/retryable and auto-retried up to 3× with backoff instead of exiting 1.
- ✅ A deploy that previously needed a manual re-run now self-heals on retry.
- ✅ Non-transient push failures still fail fast — no behavior change.

author: vineethsai7
body:
Stack/base note: targets `main` from `codex/fix-upgrade-path-ci`. The local untracked `artifacts/` directory is intentionally excluded from this branch.

## Problem

`defenseclaw upgrade` could fail during 0.7.x -> 0.8.0 and older-version upgrade paths even after artifacts installed successfully. Two concrete failures were observed:

- old upgraders mixed cached in-process modules with the newly installed wheel, so `defenseclaw.migration_state.is_future_schema` could be missing while 0.8.0 migration code expected it
- Textual 7.x installs crashed in the TUI because `MetricTile` called `update_classes`, which only exists in newer Textual

CI also still had a custom/manual E2E path that was making main noisy, and there was no release-blocking live upgrade smoke before publishing artifacts.

## Current Situation

Release asset inspection found that `0.4.0`, `0.5.0`, `0.6.0` through `0.6.6`, `0.7.1`, and `0.7.2` have the wheel, gateway archives, and old `upgrade` command needed for live upgrade tests. `0.7.0` has no downloadable release assets, and `0.2.0` predates the upgrade command.

Older baseline wheels also expose two compatibility edges:

- `0.4.0` through `0.6.0` call `openclaw gateway restart` directly and crash when the `openclaw` binary is absent
- `0.7.x` can cache old migration/version modules before the new wheel is installed

## Solution

### Run migrations from the installed wheel

`cmd_upgrade.py` now runs migrations in a child interpreter from `~/.defenseclaw/.venv` after the new wheel is installed. That avoids mixing old `sys.modules` entries with the new migration implementation.

### Preserve legacy upgrade compatibility

`migrations.py` reloads stale migration/version modules when needed and installs a process-local `openclaw` restart shim for pre-0.6.1 upgraders when no real `openclaw` is on `PATH`. The shim returns non-zero so old upgrade code emits its existing warning instead of crashing.

### Support Textual 7.x and 8.x

`MetricTile` now uses `update_classes` when available and falls back to `set_class` loops on Textual 7.x.

### Add release upgrade smoke matrix

Added `scripts/test-upgrade-release.sh`, `make upgrade-smoke`, and `make upgrade-smoke-matrix`. The smoke harness builds or consumes candidate artifacts, serves them locally, installs an old baseline in a throwaway `HOME`, redirects the old upgrade command to the local release server, and verifies versions, migrations, known regression markers, and TUI metric refresh.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Candidate artifacts] --> B[Local release server]
  C[Historical baseline install] --> D[Patch old upgrade download URL]
  B --> D
  D --> E[defenseclaw upgrade]
  E --> F[Fresh installed venv migration runner]
  F --> G[Verify CLI, gateway, cursor, TUI refresh]
```

## What Changed (Where & How)

| Path | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` | Removed push, PR, and manual triggers; left scheduled E2E only. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Added upgrade smoke matrix job. |
| `.github/workflows/release.yaml` | Added pre-publish upgrade smoke matrix before release creation. |
| `Makefile` | Added `upgrade-smoke` and `upgrade-smoke-matrix` targets plus default historical baseline list. |
| `scripts/test-upgrade-release.sh` | New reusable live upgrade harness with single-baseline and matrix modes. |
| `cli/defenseclaw/commands/cmd_upgrade.py` | Runs migrations through the freshly installed managed venv. |
| `cli/defenseclaw/migrations.py` | Reloads stale modules and adds legacy `openclaw` restart shim for pre-0.6.1 upgrade paths. |
| `cli/defenseclaw/tui/widgets/native_metrics.py` | Adds Textual 7.x class-map fallback. |
| `cli/defenseclaw/tui/app.py` | Keeps overview connector filtering deferred while overview is active. |
| `cli/tests/**` | Adds regression coverage for migration reloads, legacy shim behavior, upgrade runner, and Textual fallback. |
| `docs/TESTING.md` | Documents upgrade smoke usage, mac/Linux flow, and supported historical baselines. |

## Breaking Changes

None.

## Open Issues / Follow-ups

None.

## Test Plan

- `bash -n scripts/test-upgrade-release.sh`
  - Result: passed.
- `uv run python - <<'PY' ... yaml.safe_load(...) ... PY`
  - Result: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yaml` parsed successfully.
- `uv run pytest cli/tests/test_migrations.py::TestRunMigrations cli/tests/test_cmd_upgrade.py cli/tests/test_remediation_upgrade.py cli/tests/tui/test_native_metrics.py cli/tests/tui/test_app_shell.py -q`
  - Result: `253 passed`.
- `make lint && make check-upgrade-manifest`
  - Result: passed; `golangci-lint` fell back to `go vet` because the installed linter was built with Go 1.25 while the repo targets Go 1.26.4.
- `make test`
  - Result: Python `4483 passed, 3 skipped, 11 warnings, 303 subtests passed`; Go race tests completed with `PASS`.
- `make upgrade-smoke-matrix ARGS="--baseline-mode seed"` on macOS darwin/arm64
  - Result: passed for `0.7.2`, `0.7.1`, `0.6.6`, `0.6.5`, `0.6.4`, `0.6.3`, `0.6.2`, `0.6.1`, `0.6.0`, `0.5.0`, and `0.4.0` -> `0.8.0`.
- Linux live test on `openclaw-vineeth` linux/arm64 using prepared candidate artifacts:
  - Command: `/tmp/test-upgrade-release.sh --release-root /tmp/defenseclaw-candidate-release-matrix-1782346164 --target-version 0.8.0 --from-versions "0.7.2,0.7.1,0.6.6,0.6.5,0.6.4,0.6.3,0.6.2,0.6.1,0.6.0,0.5.0,0.4.0" --baseline-mode seed`

author: d12frosted
body:
## What

In all three build jobs (`build-30`, `build-31`, `build-32`) of `Build Emacs.app`, pass the Homebrew gcc runtime to `./configure`:

- `LDFLAGS="-L$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib/gcc/current -Wl,-rpath,..."`
- gcc + libgccjit include dirs added to `CFLAGS`

This mirrors what `Formula/emacs-plus@*.rb` already does for native-compilation parity.

## Why

`configure` was failing with:

```
configure: error: The installed libgccjit failed to compile and run a test program using the libgccjit library
```

The workflow relied on the runner's default search paths to find libgccjit instead of pointing at the gcc runtime like the formula does. After a gcc bottle bump (~2026-06-19, last green build 06-18) the arm64 runners stopped resolving the gcc runtime, so every arm64 job (tahoe/sequoia/sonoma) fails while the Intel job still passes. Supplying the gcc lib path and rpath restores the build.

This is the `Build Emacs.app` half of the nightly failures; the tap-build (`Nightly`) tap-trust failure is fixed separately.

## Suggested validation

Trigger a manual `workflow_dispatch` run (e.g. version 31) to confirm the arm64 build before merging.

body:
Adds an observability + dashboards layer, and answers "which SQLite/Lapis features should back this?" in a dedicated doc.

## SQLite / Lapis features
`docs/sqlite-features.md` records the verdicts:
- **Triggers** — already power FTS5 sync (adopted); denormalized counters declined (soft-delete/approval conditions + bulk-seed cost; reads are infrequent).
- **Views** — the dynamic *listings* still use parameterized queries (a view can't capture per-request sort/time/hidden filters), but a new **`v_daily_activity`** view (migration `[110]`) backs the read-side stats rollup — a textbook view use.
- **Stored procedures** — SQLite has none; reusable query logic lives in the model layer (the convention we follow).

## Stats + dashboards
- **`utils/stats`** — site/sub totals, a zero-padded daily-activity series (from the view), top-subreddit/contributor leaderboards.
- **`/admin/stats`** (admin-gated) — site activity over 30 days + top subreddits.
- **`/r/:sub/stats`** (RBAC `approve`-gated, like the queue) — per-sub activity + top contributors.
- Charts are **server-rendered inline SVG** (`utils/chart`) — no client JS, matching the classless/Datastar-only front-end. Nav links added to the admin dashboard + queue page.

## Ops endpoints (`src/ops`)

- **`GET /health`** — JSON liveness/readiness probe (`200`/`503` on a DB ping).

Dropped the stale, self-contradictory README `## TODO` list (it showed shipped foundations as unchecked); `TODO.md` is the living roadmap. Added README API + "Operations & observability" sections; updated `TODO.md` + `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Summary

Resolves all seven open Dependabot alerts, which all target `com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind` on the **buildscript classpath** (pulled in transitively by the OWASP dependency-check plugin via `settings.gradle`).

| Alert | GHSA | Severity |

| #9 | GHSA-rmj7-2vxq-3g9f | high |
| #8 | GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm | high |
| #13 | GHSA-5hh8-q8hv-fr38 | medium |
| #12 | GHSA-9fxm-vc8v-hj55 | medium |

| #10 | GHSA-hgj6-7826-r7m5 | medium |
| #7 | GHSA-rcqc-6cw3-h962 | medium |

## Why 2.22.0 and not 2.21.4

Six of the alerts are fixed by 2.21.4, but GHSA-5jmj-h7xm-6q6v lists **2.21.5** as the fix — and 2.21.5 was never published (the 2.21.x line ends at 2.21.4). The first published version covering all seven is **2.22.0**.

## What

- Add the `ADAPTER_LLMW_*` control knobs to `workers/sample.env` so the in-process LLMWhisperer extraction running inside the file-processing workers can actually be tuned.

## Why

- Text extraction no longer runs in a separate tool container — the SDK x2text adapter runs **in-process** inside the file-processing workers (`workers/executor/executors/legacy_executor.py:_handle_extract`).
- These knobs are read via `os.getenv` in the SDK (`unstract/sdk1/.../x2text/llm_whisperer_v2/src/constants.py`) at import time, from the **worker process** env.
- Previously they were only documented/set on the backend & prompt-service envs, so the worker fell back to SDK defaults. A customer hit `Whisper client operation timed out` and there was no surfaced way to raise the wait in the worker.

## How

- Added to `workers/sample.env`:
  - `ADAPTER_LLMW_WAIT_TIMEOUT=900` (V2 — overall wait-for-completion; the timeout knob)
  - `ADAPTER_LLMW_MAX_RETRIES=3`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_RETRY_MIN_WAIT=1.0`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_RETRY_MAX_WAIT=60.0` (V2 — per-HTTP-call transient retry backoff)
  - `ADAPTER_LLMW_POLL_INTERVAL=30`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_MAX_POLLS=1000` (V1 deprecated — status polling)

## Can this PR break any existing features. If yes, please list possible items. If no, please explain why. (PS: Admins do not merge the PR without this section filled)

- No. Only adds entries to a sample env template. Values equal the existing SDK defaults, so behaviour is unchanged unless an operator overrides them.

## Database Migrations

- None

## Env Config

- New (documented) worker envs: `ADAPTER_LLMW_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_MAX_RETRIES`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_RETRY_MIN_WAIT`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_RETRY_MAX_WAIT`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_POLL_INTERVAL`, `ADAPTER_LLMW_MAX_POLLS`.

## Relevant Docs

- These knobs are currently undocumented in public docs — separate docs PR recommended.

Corrects the Home Assistant charging-mode select and removes the temporary storage-lock diagnostic button.

Root cause:
- DGN `0x1F108` is load-disconnect configuration, not charging-mode status.
- DGN `0x1F200` is charging-stage status; its low bits are stage variant/substate, not an authoritative Touring/Storage readback.
- Reading either frame after sending Storage (`0x43`, value `1`) incorrectly changed the Home Assistant select back to Touring.

Changes:
- Remove `Manager30 Toggle Storage Mode Lock` and all associated `0x4D` control code.
- Keep the selected mode after sending command `0x43`.
- Observe broadcast command `0x43` from any RedVision/bridge source so external mode changes still update Home Assistant.
- Decode `0x1F200` only as charging stage.

- `manager.cpp` passes C++17 syntax validation with the existing ESPHome interface stubs.

## Summary

body: ## What Reworks the Rich Link Previews settings and card color: - **Its own section + sub-screen.** The three `Rich Link Previews - Body / Comments / Color` rows move out of *Media* into a dedicated **Rich Link Previews** section. Its single row opens a sub-screen with **Body**, **Comments** and **Color** together — less clutter in Media, one place for everything. - **Full color picker.** The Color control is now Apple's native `UIColorPickerViewController` (grid / spectrum / sliders / eyedropper / hex), plus a row of quick swatches and a **Use Default (No Color)** reset — instead of a fixed list of presets. - **Accurate card color.** The card is now painted the **exact** color you pick (full fill), with the title/description text automatically set to black or white for contrast. Previously the color was blended into the system background at only 8–14% opacity, so even vivid choices looked muddy (Pink rendered as a dark maroon). - **Live preview.** The sub-screen has a **Card Preview** area showing sample *full* and *compact* cards that recolor live as you pick (swatch, picker drag, or Default reset), so you can see the exact color and the auto-contrast text before applying it. ## Screenshots The sub-screen, with the live **Card Preview** at the top — it recolors as you pick (here: the starting color → after choosing a new one): | Live preview — before | Live preview — after | | --- | --- | | | | The full color picker, and the card rendered with the exact color (text auto-contrasted to stay readable): | Color picker | Light fill → dark text | Dark fill → white text | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | ## Notes - The color is stored as a free-form hex (`LinkPreviewCardColorHex`); the default is the **neutral card**, so a colored card is fully opt-in. The old preset colors are intentionally *not* auto-promoted to a full-card fill on update — they only ever rendered as a faint 8–14% tint, so a sudden bold fill would look jarring. (A backup that already carries a chosen color still restores it.) - The renderer runs on Texture's background layout threads, so it reads a render-safe packed-`uint32` snapshot rather than the main-thread `NSString`, avoiding a data race on the strong pointer. ## Testing - Verified in the iOS 26 Simulator: the new section + sub-screen, the color picker, quick swatches, Default reset, and card rendering in both compact and full layouts — confirming the exact fill color and auto-contrast for light (yellow) and dark (blue) picks. - Builds clean for the shipping device target (`iphone:clang:26.0:14.0`). - Not yet tested on a physical device.

author: gregpriday
body:
## Summary

- On HiDPI/fractional-scaled displays, alt-buffer TUIs (vim, opencode, Gemini CLI) that fall back to xterm's DOM renderer show horizontal zebra stripes. At non-integer DPR, the DOM renderer computes a fractional `css.cell.height` and Chromium pixel-snaps adjacent row boundaries inconsistently, so the terminal background bleeds through the seams. xterm 6.x removed addon-canvas so there's no canvas-renderer escape hatch.
- Fix part 1: `TerminalWebGLManager` gains an `altBufferPinnedIds` set so alt-screen panes stay on WebGL through fleet DOM-mode flips, exactly like the existing focus pin. A shared `isPinned()` helper unifies all 8 exemption sites. The circuit breaker clears alt-buffer pins before `flipToDom`; the reconciliation watchdog's `shouldHaveActiveWebGL` honours them; the pin is visibility-independent so a hidden-then-revealed alt pane returns to WebGL correctly.
- Fix part 2: For panes that genuinely must use DOM (breaker tripped or hardware unavailable), a new `onRender` hook in `TerminalListenerInstaller` snaps fractional row heights to integers using a Bresenham distribution that sums exactly to the canvas height, gated on `!isWebGLActive`. Using `onRender` rather than `onResize` means it also fires on WebGL-to-DOM renderer swaps and DPR changes.

Resolves #10768

## Changes

- `TerminalWebGLManager.ts`: `altBufferPinnedIds` set, `pinAltBuffer`/`unpinAltBuffer` methods, shared `isPinned()`, circuit-breaker clear, watchdog awareness
- `TerminalListenerInstaller.ts`: `onRender` hook with Bresenham integer-snap for DOM-renderer row heights
- `TerminalInstanceService.ts`: wires `handleBufferModeChange` to call `pinAltBuffer`/`unpinAltBuffer`

## Testing

265+ targeted unit tests pass across three new/extended suites:

- `TerminalWebGLManager.test.ts`: alt-buffer pin lifecycle, focus+alt-buffer interaction, circuit-breaker clear, watchdog behaviour
- `TerminalListenerInstaller.test.ts`: DOM integer-snap correctness, Bresenham distribution, WebGL-active guard
- `TerminalInstanceService.webglVisibility.test.ts`: buffer-mode-change wiring

Typecheck clean. Reviewed adversarially before push, no critical findings.

author: kim-em
body:
This PR assembles the verified Frobenius-Schur counting endgame into the even-dimensional A₅ case of Example 5.1.3, replacing the opaque "needs the {1,3,3,4,5} dimension classification" `sorry` in `Etingof.isRealType_of_A5_even_standard` with the full counting argument and a single precisely-isolated remaining gap. Working with the Wedderburn family `W = D.columnFDRep` of `ℂ[A₅]`: there are exactly five irreducibles (`D.n = #ConjClasses A₅ = 5`), `∑ᵢ (dim Wᵢ)² = 60 = |A₅|`, the involution count `∑ᵢ FS(Wᵢ)·dim Wᵢ = #{g : g²=1} = 16`, and ambivalence makes every `Wᵢ` self-dual; the Cauchy-Schwarz endgame `frobeniusSchur_all_pos_general` then forces every `FS(Wᵢ) = 1`, and the abstract `ρ` is isomorphic to a Wedderburn column, so `FS(ρ) = 1`.

It adds the reusable lemmas `Etingof.frobeniusSchur_all_pos_general` (cardinality-5 general-index form of `A5_frobeniusSchur_all_pos`) and `Etingof.frobeniusSchurIndicator_eq_of_character_eq`, a local `IsSimpleModule ⟹ Simple (FDRep.of ρ)` bridge, and de-privatizes `IrrepDecomp.n_eq_card_conjClasses'` in `Chapter4/Corollary4_2_2.lean`. `lake build EtingofRepresentationTheory.Chapter5` succeeds.

This is partial: the per-irreducible step `FS(Wᵢ) ∈ {±1}` is isolated as `frobeniusSchurIndicator_pm_one_of_simple_selfDual` (the Frobenius-Schur trace identity `FS = dim Sym²ᴳ − dim Λ²ᴳ`, the same content as the still-open #5214), now tracked in #5261. `Etingof.Example5_1_3_A5` becomes axiom-clean only once both #5261 and #5214 land, since the even case also routes through the #5214-backed `isRealType_of_frobeniusSchurIndicator_eq_one`. #5257 is left for replan to narrow to that residual scope.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent edits to shared reusable library items from mutating historical class assignment copies and add lightweight versioning for traceability.
- Allow creators/admins to safely update metadata (and later content) with an audit trail and let teachers duplicate shared items into private copies.
- Expose a library item detail view that surfaces metadata, visibility, owner/team, content preview and a simple version history.

### Description
- Add database fields and migration to track versions and archival state: `sourceLibraryVersion` on `HomeworkAssignment`, `version`, `archivedAt`, and `updatedById` on `CurriculumHomeworkLibraryItem`, plus a new `CurriculumHomeworkLibraryItemVersion` snapshot model and migration SQL.
- Record the library version used when creating class assignment copies by writing `sourceLibraryVersion` during assignment creation.
- Implement safe metadata edits that create a `CurriculumHomeworkLibraryItemVersion` snapshot of the previous state and increment the library item `version` inside a transaction, and add `updatedById` bookkeeping.
- Add actions to duplicate a library item into an independent private copy and to archive (soft-delete) items while preserving existing assigned copies.
- Surface versions and actions in the UI by adding a library item detail page (`app/curriculum-library/[itemId]/page.tsx`), updating the list page to show `v{version}` and adding version history and content preview, and enrich `lib/curriculum-library.ts` with helper functions including `getCurriculumLibraryItemDetail` and `buildLibraryVersionSnapshot`.

author: petr0n
body:
## Problem

Spherical/domed pips cast shadows onto the tile surface. After grayscale preprocessing + binarisation, each shadow appears as a separate round blob immediately adjacent to the real pip blob — passing the circularity ≥ 0.45 test and being counted as an extra pip. This caused e.g. a 4-pip half to count as 6 on live phone video.

## Fix

Proximity dedup in `countBlobs`: after collecting all round blobs, sort by area descending (larger blob = real pip body), then suppress any smaller blob whose centre is within **1.5 × pipRadius** of a kept blob.

- Shadow blobs are always within ~1 × pipRadius of their pip → suppressed ✓  
- Actual pips on a 3×3 or 4×3 grid are spaced ≥ 2.5 × pipRadius apart → never suppressed ✓
- Each blob's centre is approximated cheaply via `cv.boundingRect`

## Verification

- `grid_eval`: **58/58** (unchanged)
- `detect_eval`: **6/6** (unchanged)
