author: psaab
body:
## Summary

- IPFIX `sendTemplates()` hardcoded `SequenceNumber: 0`. After data records had been exported, every periodic template refresh rewound the header sequence to 0.
- Loss/sequence-tracking collectors (pmacct, Elastiflow) read that rewind as packet loss or an exporter restart — false telemetry-integrity events.
- Fix: `sendTemplates()` now reads `e.seq` under `e.mu` and writes the **current cumulative** value WITHOUT incrementing it (a template-only Message carries zero Data Records).
- NetFlow v9 is intentionally unchanged.

## RFC basis

- **IPFIX / NetFlow v10 — RFC 7011 §3.1, §10.3.2**: the header Sequence Number is the cumulative count of **Data Records** sent in all prior Messages for the Observation Domain (the sequence of the *next* Data Record). A Message carrying only (Options) Template Sets contains no Data Records → it MUST NOT advance the counter, and it MUST carry the current cumulative value, not 0.
- **NetFlow v9 — RFC 3954**: the header sequence counts **export packets**, so its template send legitimately advances the counter (`e.seq++` kept). This is why the fix is IPFIX-only.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `gofmt -l` clean on touched files
- [x] `go vet ./pkg/flowexport/...` clean
- [x] `go test ./pkg/flowexport/...` ok
- [x] Added `TestIPFIXTemplateRefreshPreservesSequenceNumber` — loopback UDP collector captures real wire bytes: send 3 data records (counter→3), template refresh, send 2 more. Asserts refresh header = 3 (not 0), post-refresh data resumes at 3, final cumulative = 5 (refresh counted 0).

### Fail-on-revert proof

Reverting the fix (`SequenceNumber: 0` in `sendTemplates`):

```
--- FAIL: TestIPFIXTemplateRefreshPreservesSequenceNumber (0.00s)
    ipfix_seqnum_test.go:116: template-refresh header sequence = 0, want 3
        (RFC 7011 §3.1: cumulative data-record count, NOT reset to 0) (#2609)
```

GREEN after restore.

## Docs

- `pkg/flowexport/README.md`: new "Header sequence number — v9 vs IPFIX (#2609)" subsection documenting the divergent rule and the fail-on-revert pin.

## Refs

Closes #2609

author: rippy1911
body:
### **User description** ## Summary Three independent performance/observability improvements to the anatome API. **1. Durable Objects rate limiting** — a `RateLimiterDO` (SQLite-backed, one instance per rate-limit key) replaces the per-request KV read+write with a single-threaded in-DO counter. This **removes the KV daily-write quota as a scaling constraint** (the original issue that started this workstream). KV is kept as a fallback when the DO binding is absent (local dev / older deploys): `checkRateLimit` now branches on `env.RATE_LIMIT_DO`. `wrangler.toml` adds the `durable_objects` binding + a `v1` `new_sqlite` migration for both default and production environments. **2. MCP response cache** — deterministic `tools/call` results are cached in the edge cache keyed by `sha256(method+params)` (NOT the JSON-RPC id, which varies per request). `handleMcp` is split into a pure, cacheable `computeMcpResult` (no envelope) and a thin id-injecting wrapper; cached inner results are re-wrapped with the live request id. Skips non-deterministic `get_exercise(random=true)`. Cuts repeat KV/DO ops for common MCP queries. **3. Structured observability** — a new `lib/observability.ts` emits one JSON log line per request (`method`, `path`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `cache HIT/MISS`) via middleware — queryable in Workers Observability / `wrangler tail` / the Cloudflare Observability MCP. ## Deployment note First `wrangler deploy --env production` after merge will run the `v1` `new_sqlite` migration, creating the `RateLimiterDO` class. The KV namespace stays in place as the fallback; no data migration is needed (the DO counter starts fresh — existing KV day-counters are simply superseded). If the DO binding is somehow absent after deploy, `checkRateLimit` automatically falls back to KV, so the API stays healthy either way. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm run typecheck` clean - [x] `pnpm exec vitest run` — 37/37 pass - [x] `wrangler deploy --dry-run` builds with `env.RATE_LIMIT_DO (RateLimiterDO) Durable Object` binding present - [ ] CI: API + Frontend + Cursor Approval Agent green - [ ] Post-merge: verify `/selfTest` still 52/52 (run with ADMIN_TOKEN); spot-check `wrangler tail` shows structured request logs; confirm rate limiting still enforces (DO path) Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement ___ ### **Description** - Durable Objects rate limiting replaces per-request KV operations with single-threaded in-DO counter, eliminating KV daily-write quota constraint - MCP response cache stores deterministic `tools/call` results by method+params hash, reducing repeat KV/DO operations for common queries - Structured observability middleware emits JSON log lines per request with method, path, status, duration, and cache HIT/MISS status - KV fallback preserved for local dev and older deploys when DO binding absent ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Request"] --> B["Rate Limit Check"] B -->|DO available| C["RateLimiterDO
SQLite counter"] B -->|DO absent| D["KV Fallback"] C --> E["MCP Handler"] D --> E E -->|Cacheable call| F["Edge Cache
sha256 key"] E -->|Non-cacheable| G["Compute Result"] F -->|HIT| H["Re-wrap with ID"] F -->|MISS| G G --> H H --> I["Observability Log"] I --> J["Response"] ```

Add observability logging and MCP response caching             
api/src/index.ts
  • Added RateLimiterDO export and import for Durable Object binding
  • Integrated structured request logging middleware that captures method,

author: elkanatovey
body:
## What
Adds the off-chain **SD-CWT token library** as a minimal, domain-agnostic Python package (`tools/sd_cwt/`), plus the project's dev/CI tooling and MIT licensing. First layer of the design (`docs/DESIGN.md` §12–13): token creation/redaction is client-side; the in-TEE C++ app will only verify + store.

## `sd_cwt` — Selective Disclosure CBOR Web Tokens
A custom, minimal profile of [draft-ietf-spice-sd-cwt-08](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-spice-sd-cwt/), wrapping `pycose` + `cbor2` + `hashlib`. Domain-agnostic (arbitrary CBOR claims); the report/note schema lives in the app layer later.

**Implemented**
- COSE_Sign1 issuer-signed CWT (`issue` / `present` / `verify` / `validate`).
- **Map-entry** redaction (`redacted_claim_keys` = `simple(59)`) and **array-element** redaction (tag `60`); disclosures in the unprotected header (`sd_claims`, 17). Hash taken over the `bstr`-encoded disclosure (matches reference vectors).
- **Nested / recursive** redaction at arbitrary depth (`redact_paths`), incl. the ancestor-disclosure rule.
- **Hash-alg agility** via the protected `sd_alg` header (SHA-256/384/512).
- **Decoy padding** (`pad_to=N`) for uniform token shape; **CSPRNG** for all randomness.
- **Encoding/robustness MUSTs on untrusted input**: definite-length (s5.1), finite date-claim encodings (s5.2), map-key type/length (s5.3), duplicate-map-key (s5.4), nesting depth <=16 (s5.5), duplicate disclosed-key rejection, and audience checks (s9).

## Verification model (note for reviewers)
The disclosure hash-matching core is factored out as **`match_disclosures`** (signature-free), so trust and disclosure-resolution are separable:
- **`validate`** = `verify` (Issuer signature) + `match_disclosures` — use when the Issuer signature is the trust anchor.
- **`validate_trusted`** = `match_disclosures` with the structural/encoding MUSTs but **no signature check** — for when trust comes from a **transparency-service receipt** rather than re-checking the Issuer sig. **This is the intended path for the duplicate-proof flow.** It still hash-matches every disclosure against the (trusted) payload, so tampered/foreign disclosures are rejected.

**Key Binding Tokens** (`kbt_sign`/`kbt_verify`, RFC 8747 `cnf`) are included for **spec compliance only** — the transparency-service receipt is this project's binding anchor, so KBT is not used in the core flow. Factoring `match_disclosures` out of `verify` is part of what keeps these paths independent.

**Deliberately omitted** (see design doc): temporal *validity* comparison against a clock (values are surfaced so the app can do its own), AEAD-encrypted disclosures, pre-issuance To-Be-Redacted/Decoy tags.

## Tests & CI
- **65 passing tests**: round-trip, array (tag 60), nesting/ancestor-rule, negative/tamper, features, conformance, and pinned reference vectors.
- Cached GitHub Actions: **sd_cwt** (lint: black/isort/mypy; test: pytest) and **license-headers** (repo-wide notice-check). `checks.sh` mirrors CI locally (`-f` to auto-fix).

## Licensing
- Root **`LICENSE`** (MIT, Microsoft); MIT notice headers enforced repo-wide via `scripts/notice-check.py` (git ls-files based), excluding the vendored third-party framework submodule.
- Relicensed the derived C++ app scaffold (`app/*`, `Dockerfile`) Apache-2.0 -> MIT (Microsoft-owned).

## Not in this PR
No app runtime changes; nothing on the chain side yet (next PR: on-chain `submit_report` + receipt). Run locally: `cd tools/sd_cwt && python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e .[lint] && ./scripts/checks.sh`.

## :loudspeaker: Type of change
<!--- Put an `x` in the boxes that apply -->
- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Enhancement

## :scroll: Description
Adds a Babel plugin (sentryExpoRouterAutoWrapBabelPlugin) that auto-wraps Expo Router's per-route ErrorBoundary re-exports at build time, removing the manual call-site step introduced in #6318.

 The plugin detects this in user source files:

 ```ts
   export { ErrorBoundary } from 'expo-router';
 ```

and rewrites it to:

 ```ts
   import { ErrorBoundary as __sentryOriginalExpoErrorBoundary } from 'expo-router';
   import { wrapExpoRouterErrorBoundary as __sentryWrapExpoRouterErrorBoundary } from '@sentry/react-native';
   export const ErrorBoundary = __sentryWrapExpoRouterErrorBoundary(__sentryOriginalExpoErrorBoundary);
 ```

 So users get the full ErrorBoundary instrumentation (route context, navigation-span error tagging, breadcrumb) with zero code changes in their route files.

## :bulb: Motivation and Context
#6318 shipped Sentry.wrapExpoRouterErrorBoundary but required users to edit every route file that re-exports ErrorBoundary from expo-router. That edit is trivial & easy to forget on new routes.

author: imshashank
body:
## Summary

Adds **Nova Guard** — an in-process policy-enforcement layer — to the gateway,
plus three new providers, a control-plane client, a Noveum trace exporter, and a
bin+lib refactor that makes the whole gateway testable.

Nova Guard inspects every request and response and can **block**, **redact /
mask**, or **flag** based on policies defined in a portable `nova-guard.json`
bundle (the same format the Nova Guard SDK uses). The deterministic policy types
run entirely in-process with no network dependency, so the gateway enforces
guardrails standalone (BYOK) as well as when wired to the Noveum control plane
for hosted policies and atomic budget reservation.

## What's included

**Policy engine (`src/policy/`)**
- Extensible `PolicyRule` trait + one module per deterministic policy type:
  `regex_match` (linear-time, ReDoS-safe), `banned_substrings` (Aho-Corasick),
  `model_allowlist` (wildcards), `token_length_cap` (tiktoken), `json_schema`,
  `pii_detection`, `secrets_detection`.
- `cost_cap` + `rate_limit` evaluated against live state, with soft/hard caps and
  fail-open/closed semantics.
- Engine: priority ordering, off/shadow/enforce modes, transform composition
  (each policy sees the previous one's mutated text), terminal block.
- Provider-shaped synthetic block responses (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google),
  `synthetic_success` (HTTP 200) or `provider_error` (HTTP 403) — both chosen to
  avoid provider-SDK retry sets.
- Current (Jun 2026) model pricing table, single-sourced and reused by provider
  metrics extractors.
- Local bundle loading (file/env) + Tower middleware wiring input/output
  enforcement into the proxy path, with a zero-overhead fast path when disabled.

**Control-plane client (`src/control_plane/`)**
- Atomic budget `reserve` / `reconcile` (the hard-cap concurrency primitive) and
  ETag-conditional policy fetch, with `backon` exponential retry on transient
  failures.

**Trace exporter (`src/telemetry/exporters/noveum_trace.rs`)**
- A `MetricsExporter` that ships per-request OTel logs to `POST /v1/traces` so
  gateway traffic appears alongside SDK traffic.

**New providers** — Mistral (OpenAI-compatible), Cohere (v2 chat), Google Gemini
(maps Bearer → `x-goog-api-key`, parses `usageMetadata`). Brings provider
coverage to 9.

**Refactor** — split into a library + thin binary so the router and every
subsystem are testable via `tower::oneshot` without binding a port.

## Testing

- **138 library unit tests** + **10 end-to-end middleware integration tests**
  (block in both modes, pass-through, input PII redaction, model-allowlist block,
  output secret block + redact, shadow mode, non-JSON pass-through, disabled
  engine). All green.
- Control-plane and trace-exporter behavior covered with `wiremock`.
- New CI workflow (`docs/ci/nova-guard-ci.yml` (copy into `.github/workflows/` to enable)): `cargo fmt --check`,
  `clippy -D warnings`, build, the keyless test suites, and `cargo-llvm-cov` with
  a line-coverage threshold. **No secrets required.**
- Zero compiler warnings.

## Notes / scope

- The pre-existing `tests/run_integration_tests` suite (live provider calls) is
  **unchanged** and still requires a running gateway + provider API keys; it is
  not part of the new hermetic CI.
- Streaming responses pass through without output-phase enforcement in v1 (a
  documented limitation shared across LLM gateways); input enforcement still
  applies.
- Cohere/Google adapters handle auth, path/header mapping, and usage/cost
  extraction; full OpenAI↔provider body translation is intentionally out of
  scope here.
- The v1.5 classifier policy types (`scorer_gate`, `prompt_injection`, etc.) are
  recognized and reserved for routing to the NovaEval scoring service (shared
  with the SDK); only the deterministic types are enforced in-process in this PR.
- Dependency framework-major upgrades (axum 0.8, reqwest 0.13) are deliberately
  **not** bundled with this feature work to keep the change reviewable and green;
  the toolchain was updated and the build is warning-free on current stable.

Docs: [`docs/NOVA_GUARD.md`](docs/NOVA_GUARD.md). Example bundle:
[`examples/nova-guard.example.json`](examples/nova-guard.example.json).

author: steverowley
body:
Fixes a real bug introduced with substitutions (#626) and flagged in the Codex review of #630: **substitutes weren't rendered in the 2D match viewer.**

## The bug
`MatchViewer` built a fixed 22 dude-specs from the **starting XI by formation slot**, drawing each at its frame position or — if absent — its formation home. After a substitution:
- the substitute's id had no spec → **invisible** (and if they carried the ball, the ball had no visible owner);
- the subbed-off starter, now absent from frames, **ghosted at their home position**.

## The fix
- The viewer is given the **full squad (XI + bench)** as labels and builds bench dude-specs alongside the starters.
- During play it renders **only the players present in the current frame**, so a subbed-off (or not-yet-on) player is simply absent and a substitute appears the moment their id arrives. Before kickoff the starters still stand at their home slots; the bench never shows there.
- Threaded through **both** viewer paths: `MatchDetail` (`pickSquad` = XI + up to 5 bench) and the demo (`buildMatch` appends bench labels).

## Why it's safe
**Identity for normal matches:** with no substitutions every starter is in every frame, so nothing renders differently — bench specs exist but are never frame-present. The only behaviour that changes is the (currently broken) subs path.

## Tests
- New test: a benched team yields 16 labels/side and a substitute actually takes the field (appears in a later frame, not the first).
- `npm run check` green — typecheck clean, **1469 tests**, lint-clean. (Viewer-only; no engine/worker-twin changes.)

author: darioortegaleyva
body:
## Description

This PR fixes the `metrics_snapshot` module failing to find indexer template schemas at runtime in installed/packaged environments. The schemas were downloaded by `make deps` but never copied to the manager's `etc/indexer-plugins/` directory during installation. Additionally, `metrics-normalization.json` was missing from the download list entirely.

**Proposed Release:** v5.x
**Issue:** wazuh/wazuh#37123

---

## Proposed Changes

- **`src/Makefile`**: Added `metrics-normalization.json` to `INDEXER_TEMPLATES_SERVER_STREAMS` so `make deps` downloads all three metrics schemas.
- **`src/init/inst-functions.sh`**: Added `installIndexerTemplates()` function that copies the three streams schemas (`metrics-agents.json`, `metrics-comms.json`, `metrics-normalization.json`) from `external/indexer-plugins/` to `${INSTALLDIR}/etc/indexer-plugins/` during manager installation, with warnings on missing source directory or files. Wired it into `InstallLocal()` after `generateSchemaFiles`.
- **`src/shared_modules/schema_validator/CMakeLists.txt`**: Added `list(FILTER SCHEMA_FILES EXCLUDE REGEX "/metrics-[^/]+\\.json$")` to exclude metrics schemas from the C++ `schema_validator` shared library, these are only consumed by the Python framework at runtime.
- **`.github/actions/check_files/manager_base.csv`**: Added 4 entries (1 directory + 3 files) for the new `etc/indexer-plugins/` path so CI package integrity checks pass.

---

## Root Cause

Two bugs:

1. **Missing install step**: `make deps` downloads `metrics-agents.json` and `metrics-comms.json` to `src/external/indexer-plugins/`. The C++ `schema_validator` embeds them into a compiled `.so` at build time, but the Python `metrics_snapshot.py` reads them from the filesystem at `WAZUH_PATH/etc/indexer-plugins/` (defined in `common.py:177`). No install step ever copied the JSON files to that runtime path.

2. **Missing schema in deps**: `metrics-normalization.json` was not listed in `INDEXER_TEMPLATES_SERVER_STREAMS`, so `make deps` never downloaded it, even though it exists in the upstream `wazuh-indexer-plugins` repo and the Python code tries to load it at `metrics_snapshot.py:641`.

---

## Results and Evidence

### Evidence 1: `make deps` downloads all 3 schemas (Ubuntu 24.04 VM)

```
vagrant@ubuntu24:~/wazuh/src$ ls -la external/indexer-plugins/metrics-*.json

-rw-rw-r-- 1 vagrant vagrant 4192 Jul  1 07:45 external/indexer-plugins/metrics-comms.json
-rw-rw-r-- 1 vagrant vagrant 2448 Jul  1 07:45 external/indexer-plugins/metrics-normalization.json
```

### Evidence 2: Build succeeds, 100% compiled (Ubuntu 24.04 VM)

```
vagrant@ubuntu24:~/wazuh/src$ make TARGET=server -j$(nproc)
...
[100%] Built target wazuh-engine
[100%] Built target wazuh-manager-db

Done building manager
```

### Evidence 3: Schemas installed to runtime path after `install.sh` (Ubuntu 24.04 VM)

```
vagrant@ubuntu24:~/wazuh$ sudo ls -la /var/wazuh-manager/etc/indexer-plugins/
total 28
drwxr-x--- 2 root wazuh-manager 4096 Jul  1 07:58 .
drwxrwx--- 5 root wazuh-manager 4096 Jul  1 07:58 ..
-rw-r----- 1 root wazuh-manager 4823 Jul  1 07:58 metrics-agents.json
-rw-r----- 1 root wazuh-manager 4192 Jul  1 07:58 metrics-comms.json
-rw-r----- 1 root wazuh-manager 2448 Jul  1 07:58 metrics-normalization.json
```

Permissions match `manager_base.csv` baseline: directory `750` `root:wazuh-manager`, files `640` `root:wazuh-manager`.

### Evidence 4: Schema content is valid - all have `index_patterns` and `mappings` (Ubuntu 24.04 VM)

```
--- metrics-agents.json ---
  index_patterns: ['wazuh-metrics-agents*']
  has_mappings: True

  index_patterns: ['wazuh-metrics-comms*']

  index_patterns: ['wazuh-metrics-normalization*']

```

### Evidence 5: `_load_schema()` loads real upstream schemas without warnings

```

END-TO-END SCHEMA LOADING TEST
============================================================
PASS: metrics-agents.json       - schema type=object, properties=2,  additionalProperties=False

### Evidence 6: All 108 existing unit tests pass

$ PYTHONPATH=framework python3 -m pytest framework/wazuh/core/indexer/tests/test_metrics_snapshot.py -v

```

| Test Class | Tests | Coverage |

| `TestLoadSchema` | 6 | `_load_schema()`, missing file returns None + warning, valid file loads + caches, invalid JSON logged |
| `TestCollectAndIndexWithValidation` | 4 | Schema validation integration, no schema skips validation, with schema validates docs |

author: efiten
body:
Fixes #1726.

## Problem

A MeshCore v1.16.0 repeater configured for 2-byte path hashes (`path.hash.mode=1`) — e.g. `36f6c7c7…` (`DK_3400_RAK_TEST`) — kept showing as **"varies"** / mixed 1-byte + 2-byte for the full 7-day advert window.

Per the live data in the issue triage: of the node's ~20 recent adverts, exactly **one** (2026-06-09, across 15 distinct observer paths) was a genuine 1-byte flood advert; every other advert was 2-byte. The flip-flop heuristic in `computeNodeHashSizeInfo` weighs that stale advert equally with recent ones, so an operator who flips `path.hash.mode` mid-flight (or a single old 1-byte advert) stays flagged for the full window with no way to signal "the config is settled now."

## Fix

Two coupled changes in `cmd/server/store.go` `computeNodeHashSizeInfo`:

1. **Chronological ordering.** `byPayloadType[4]` iterates in insertion order, not timestamp order, so `HashSize = Seq[last]` could pick the wrong advert under out-of-order MQTT ingest or chunked cold-load (the "carmack" concern from triage). We now collect `(FirstSeen, size)` pairs and **stable-sort by `FirstSeen`**; ties keep insertion order, preserving prior behavior when timestamps are equal.

2. **Recency decay.** After `transitions >= 2` raises the flip-flop flag, clear it when the most recent `hashSizeRecentAgreeCount` (= **3**) non-zero-hop adverts all agree on a single size. A node still flapping (recent adverts disagree) stays flagged. `3` mirrors the existing ≥3-observation threshold used to raise the flag.

## Policy note

Triage marked this **needs-operator-input** because the decay is a behavior/policy change. This PR implements the rule the triage proposed ("if the last 3 adverts agree, clear inconsistent"), which matches the reporter's stated expectation. Happy to adjust the threshold or gate it differently per your call.

## Tests

`cmd/server/issue1726_hash_decay_test.go`:
- `TestIssue1726_SettledNodeNotInconsistent` — reporter's case (`[2,1,2,2,2]` within window) → `Inconsistent=false`, `HashSize=2`.
- `TestIssue1726_HashSizeUsesChronologicallyLatest` — out-of-order insertion still reports the chronologically-latest size.
- `TestIssue1726_ActiveFlapperStaysInconsistent` — a node whose recent adverts disagree stays flagged.

Existing flip-flop / hash-collision tests unchanged and green; full `cmd/server` package suite passes.

author: mvaligursky
body:
Reorders the per-frame render pipeline so the frame graph is built before mesh-instance and shadow-caster culling. This is preparation for driving culling from the frame graph (so a custom `RenderPassForward` can render any layer with any camera). The cull now fills the visible-instance and shadow-caster lists that the passes read at render time, so output is unchanged for the standard composition.

**Changes:**
- `Renderer.update()` now performs only the mesh-independent prepare + light-visibility phase. The mesh / shadow-caster culling (plus gsplat shadow update, GPU data update, and one-shot shadow consume) moves into a new `ForwardRenderer.cull()` phase.
- `renderComposition` orders the phases as `update` → `buildFrameGraph` → `cull` → `render`.
- `consumeOneShotShadows` moves from the end of `buildFrameGraph` to the end of `cull`, so shadow-pass building and shadow-caster culling both read the shadow update mode before it is consumed.
- Renamed the low-level `Renderer.cull(camera, drawCalls, culledInstances)` to `cullMeshInstances`, freeing the `cull()` name for the new phase.

**Behavior note:**
- `EVENT_PRECULL` / `EVENT_POSTCULL` now fire after the frame graph is built (they still bracket the mesh cull). All affected methods are internal (`@ignore`).

author: rdosinski
body:
### Description
The Shift-of-Tails product uses two quantiles of the CDF to quantify how extreme events are compared to the model climatology. Currently a SOT10 and SOT90 is produced and they are based on the 1st/10th percentiles and 90th/99th. In GRIB1, this is specified by the number key, e.g., SOT10 has number=10 and no information in MARS itself that it's 1/10.
In GRIB2, the two quantiles are encoded in the meta-data and for potential future use cases the quantile key will contain both values 1/10 and 90/99. This will allow to handle for example 90/99.5.

For the two stream enfo and defo with type sot, mars.quantile gets the two values, e.g., 1-10:100, 90-99:100 or 900:995:1000.

author: benbaichmankass
body:
## system-review follow-up #2 — BUG-049 emit-then-orphan

**Tier 2** (order-path file `src/core/coordinator.py`) — draft, awaiting operator OK to merge.

### Root cause
`Coordinator.multi_account_execute` logs the order package `status='open'` at the **top** of dispatch (line 916), **before** the eligibility filter (line 994). When `_eligible_for_dispatch` yields **zero accounts** — a strategy routed only to an unconfigured / `strategies:[]` account — the per-account loop never runs → no trade placed, no rejection journaled → the package sits `status='open'` / `linked_trade_id=NULL` and the monitor reconciler mis-stamps it **`orphaned — never executed`** at +5 min (BUG-049). `orphaned` is a red-flag status; this is really a deliberate non-fill.

### Confirmed live this review (diag pulls)
Orphaned-status pull + `/api/bot/config` + balances surfaced the dead-end-routing class:
- `trend_donchian_eth` / `trend_donchian_sol` → routed **only** to `breakout_1`, which is `configured=False` (api_ok=false, no creds) → filtered out → empty eligible list → orphan.
- Matches the prior `BL-20260601-001` note: `xauusd_trend_1h` → only `oanda_practice` (dry, `strategies:[]`) → BUG-049 dead-end.
- Plus shadow / benign-no-op packages that left no `order_package_id`-linked rejection row.

### Fix
A **post-dispatch backstop** at the end of `multi_account_execute`: when **no trade was placed** for the logged package, terminalise it `status='rejected'` with `close_reason ∈ {no_eligible_account | all_accounts_noop | no_fill_all_accounts}`. Mirrors the established prop-branch / dry-branch contract (*every emitted package reaches a terminal, accurate status*).

- Fires **only** when `not any_trade_placed` — a package that placed a trade is unchanged and links via the trade row's `order_package_id`.
- **Pure post-dispatch status hygiene**: changes no execution decision; the genuine-failure roll-up ping still fires.
- Catch-all on top of the existing dry/shadow relabel (PR #4339/#4342), covering all three observed classes (empty-eligible, benign-no-op without a linked rejection, any non-journaling branch).

Closes the emit-then-orphan (dead-end-routing) scope of **BL-20260601-001 / BUG-049**. Remaining open scope on that item is now only the *executed-then-exchange-flat-without-clean-fill / closed-pnl-attribution* class.

### Tests
2 new tests in `tests/test_s030_pr1_order_packages_log.py` (no-eligible-account terminalises; successful dispatch still left `open` for the trade link). **85 dispatch tests green locally** (excl. `test_coordinator_flow.py` which needs pandas, unavailable in sandbox — CI has it).

### Also in this PR (docs only)
- **#3 (MHG close-confirm)** verified in the health-review backlog `check_log`: the −$2530 flap was **pre-fix residue** (ran on pre-fix code 06-24 11:34–13:49; fixes deployed only at the 05:11Z 06-25 restart), it's **paper-only** (`ib_paper`), `ib_paper` is genuinely **flat** (api_ok=true, net_liq populated, 0 open), and `reconcile_orphan_history` cleaned the duplicates → **no recurrence; "#4441 not holding" was a deploy-timing misdiagnosis.** Kept open as the standing watch.

### Out of band (no change needed)
- **#4 (real-money idle)** confirmed **intended**: bybit_2 (the only live real-money account, **~$95** balance) is live + api_ok + flat; selective strategies didn't trigger on ranging BTC; the one ETH signal that fired executed fine (+$0.20). No real-money execution gap (the orphans are prop/paper). *Worth noting bybit_2 is barely funded.*

body:
## Epic #1258 Track 4 — #1262: Conclusion orientée lecteur (Acte III + Acte I contextualisés)

The 3-act conclusion was "aux antipodes" of the target: technical machinery in titles (`arg_N` + fallacy labels + verdict bands), no anchor for a reader wanting to form an opinion on the discourse. **Track 4 inverts it** — the conclusion goes to meet the reader in their existing knowledge of the context and speakers, cites what was actually said, gives a plain-language verdict, and demotes the formal machinery to reader support.

**Anti-pendule (per #1262 body)**: reorient the prompt (subtract the debate-prep framing), do NOT pile constraints; do NOT re-anonymize (Track 1 #1259 already deanonymized); keep the ReadabilityGate.

### Changes (3 files, +128/-42)

**Acte III** (`act3_conclusion_plugin.py`):
1. `Act3Evidence` gains `claim_excerpts: List[str]` — real (truncated, privacy-capped) claim text from `state.identified_arguments`. The prior evidence only carried `arg_N` counts, so the conclusion could not cite what was said.
2. `build_act3_evidence` extracts claim text via `args.values()` (values are the claim strings), truncated via `_truncate` (`_CLAIM_EXCERPT_CAP=240`, max 5).
3. `build_act3_prompt` reoriented reader-first — 3 beats shift from (synthèse / appréciations / que-faire-contrer) to (what-the-discourse-says / what-holds-vs-not / how-to-form-your-judgment). Opens naming the speaker + citing the real claims. Formal (Tweety/Dung) demoted to **APPUI**, never a title.
4. `what_next_block` rewritten: "que faire" is no longer debate-prep (how to counter / probable moves) but **reader apprenticeship** (what to receive with prudence, what is sound, why) — anti-pendule subtraction of the debate-prep framing.

**Acte I** (`act1_framing_plugin.py`):
- Drafting instruction opens beat 1 ("Le texte") on the **real speaker/arena/era** via `source_metadata` (threaded real by Track 1 #1259) — a reader situates WHO speaks, WHERE, in what CONTEXT before any analysis.

### North-Star preserved (DoD #4 — lose nothing)

Formal depth stays: strengths/weaknesses/counter-points/deliberation data + the formal grounding instruction all remain, now as reader support. Verified deterministically — all 9 depth markers present in the reoriented prompt.

### Verification

- **72 passed** (act3 + act1), including 4 new T4 tests (claim-excerpts carry real text, empty-when-no-args, prompt carries claims + debate-prep subtracted).
- Gate-compliance + renderer-contract green (the updated `_WOVEN_CONCLUSION` reader-oriented fixture **PASSES** the ReadabilityGate; the enumeration still FAILS it).
- DoD #4 verified: all 9 formal-depth markers present (strengths/weaknesses/counters/deliberation + formal grounding instruction).
- **mypy CI-exact** (`--config-file pyproject.toml`) on the 2 edited prod files: **Success — 0 issues**.
- black/flake8 are `continue-on-error` in CI (informational); `black` 26.5.0 flags pre-existing formatting on lines not touched here (CI's pinned version accepts it).

### DoD checklist (#1262)

- [x] `claim_excerpts` carries real claim text; conclusion can cite what was said
- [x] Acte III reoriented reader-first (names speaker, cites claims, plain-language verdict, formal as support)
- [x] Acte I opens on real actors/arena via `source_metadata`
- [x] Formal depth preserved (appendix of support) — DoD #4 verified
- [x] Anti-pendule: debate-prep subtracted, not re-labelled; no counter-directive
- [x] black/flake8 continue-on-error; mypy CI gate clean
- [ ] Re-run corpus_A → reader can re-link (requires LLM + corpus; coordinator relays the real Acte III to user privately — out of unit-test scope)

### Privacy HARD

Real claim text lives in the working state + gitignored artifacts. Commit/PR carry only opaque IDs + fake test claims. The real Acte III stays local (`evaluation/results/`) — the coordinator relays it to the user privately.

Closes #1262. Refs #1258. Depends on Track 1 #1259 (merged `21c0fdf4`).

author: lukaskaibel
body:
## What

Before a set group's first entry, the in-workout metric badge read a dead **`0 %`**. It now previews the bar that metric is scored against — the exercise's **current best** — in muted gray behind a `target` glyph. The instant a value is entered it switches back to the existing trend/record pill, completely unchanged.

It's not just a useful number: the current best *is* the denominator the percentage is measured against, so the idle pill previews exactly what the badge is about. The three states now tell one continuous story — **bar to beat → how far you've climbed → you cleared it.**

## Behavior

| State | Condition | Pill |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Idle | no entry yet, exercise has a current best | gray `target` + current best (value + unit) |
| Hidden | no entry, no prior best (brand-new exercise) | nothing (the info panel owns the "no data yet" state) |
| Trend / Record | a value is entered | unchanged — chevron % / `trophy.fill` |

## Notes

- **`target`, not a trophy** — `trophy.fill` is the app-wide record symbol (and this pill's own PR state), so the idle bar-to-beat had to be visually distinct. A target reads as "goal to clear," not "win already won."
- The idle value reuses the record state's value+unit view, so idle and record render alike.
- An `init` resolves the committed metric up front, so the first frame already evaluates the right metric (also removes a first-frame roll from the e1RM default).
- VoiceOver speaks the idle state as the current best.

## Verification

Zero-warning build. Verified in the simulator recorder: the new gray `target · e1RM` idle pill renders on an empty group, while the `trophy` record pill and trend pill on sibling groups are unchanged.

author: cgbarlow
body:
Defence-in-depth follow-up to #6317 (the fast-regen root-cause fix landed in #6345 / ADR-097).

## Why
ADR-097 made the regen ~64 min → ~10 s, so the board tracks `main` within ~2 min (verified in prod). But #6317 also asked for defence-in-depth: even with a fast regen the published board can still fall behind **silently** — a lost push race (#426), a starved/queued runner (#2172/#3177), the throttled `*/15` cron (#3720), or a future regression. Nothing on `main` asserted freshness or failed visibly.

## What
- **New `tools.leaderboard.freshness` gate** (pure, unit-tested): compares the published `leaderboard-ui.json` `generated_at` against the latest board-source commit — reusing `generate._latest_source_commit_z` / `_BOARD_SOURCE_PATHS`, the *same* definition that keys `generated_at` (SPEC-023-A), so a freshly-pushed board reads lag ≈ 0 and only a genuine stall trips it. Past a 30-min lag it emits a GitHub `::error::` and exits non-zero (run goes red). Indeterminate state (no artifact / no git) never false-alarms.
- **`leaderboard.yml`**: a final freshness step runs on **every** invocation (push + cron) against `origin/main` — measuring the *published* state, so a lost push race or starved pipeline that left `main` stale trips a visible alarm. Plus **`timeout-minutes: 15`** so a hung refresh fails loudly instead of producing nothing.

## Acceptance criteria (#6317)
- ✅ A board that goes >30 min stale while merges land now emits a **visible failure/alert** instead of silently serving old standings.
- ✅ A hung/starved refresh fails fast (15-min execution timeout).
- ⏭️ Deferred (ADR-098 *neglected*, follow-up): a dedicated high-frequency monitor / serialized refresh worker / self-rescheduling backstop — unwarranted now that the regen is seconds and every landing merge re-checks freshness.

## Tests
`tools/leaderboard/tests/test_freshness.py` — 12 tests (lag math, artifact parsing, fresh/stale/unknown verdicts against real git history, CLI exit codes + annotation). 66 leaderboard tests green; Gate B green. Live smoke test on the real repo: `leaderboard is fresh — lag=0m00s`.

ADR-098 + SPEC-098-A. Note: `/tools/leaderboard/` + `/.github/` are CODEOWNERS-owned, so this needs a code-owner review.

author: krasimirkralev
body:
## The "Mark Spivey" class (real customer, this week)

A device set up OpenAI in **API-key mode**, then switched to the **ChatGPT subscription** — but the agent's primary stayed pinned to **`openai/<model>`**. That lane calls `api.openai.com` with the now-invalid `sk-proj` key and **401s every turn**, while the working subscription (`codex`) sits unused. The customer only recovered by manually driving the on-box agent to rewrite the config.

**#222 (codex-home self-heal) couldn't fix this** — the `openai` *direct* lane is keyed separately (`models.providers.openai.apiKey`), which #222 never touches.

## Fix (gateway-pre-start, on every boot)

If a **`codex` OAuth profile** is configured (subscription active) but the primary is **`openai/*`**, migrate it:
- repoint primary `openai/<m>` → `codex/<m>`
- drop the stale `models.providers.openai` (the dead key)
- drop `auth.profiles.openai:default`
- strip any `openai/*` entries from `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` (e.g. the bogus `openai/gpt-5.3-codex`)

Because it runs on the gateway restart that follows **any** provider save, it covers both the wizard switch *and* the agent-driven path that bit Mark.

## Why no separate configure-route change
I scoped a wizard-side purge too, but it's redundant: a wizard subscription save already sets primary `codex/*` and restarts the gateway, so this self-heal runs anyway. The only thing a wizard purge would add is removing a *harmless, unused* leftover provider — not worth a separate auth-core edit.

## Validation
Logic validated on a **real Jetson (georgi, python3)** with a synthetic harness:
- ✅ Mark's case → `openai/gpt-5.4` → `codex/gpt-5.4`; `openai` provider/profile purged (`deepseek` kept); bad fallback dropped (`clawbox-ai/free` kept)
- ✅ no-subscription box → untouched (no false migration)
- ✅ already on `codex` → no-op

`bash -n` clean. Boot script — CI/`bash -n` cover syntax; the migration logic is the harness above. Real end-to-end needs a Codex account (georgi has none), same caveat as #222.

author: tembleking
body:
The go-update workflow detects the latest version via `go-dev detect`, which reads go.dev/VERSION?m=text. That endpoint only ever reports the latest stable, so a new minor's release candidate (e.g. 1.27rc1) was never picked up until GA, despite the README promising RC coverage within 4h. The prior RC manifests (1.25rc*, 1.26rc*) had to be added by hand.

Adds a `--include-prerelease` flag to `detect` that scans the download page and selects the highest version by semantic order (`go/version`), and wires it into the workflow alongside the stable detection. The existing manifest/PR existence checks de-dupe any overlap when no RC is ahead of stable.

The lexicographic sort in `listVersions` is intentionally untouched (its order is asserted by tests); the max is computed on a separate path.

Includes the currently-missing 1.27rc1 manifest.

author: pekkah
body:
Gated (default-off) per-token decode instrumentation for the GDN-hybrid CPU-MoE path, the diagnostic foundation for decode-perf work toward llama.cpp's tg128.

Splits each decode token's wall time into the **GPU trunk** (attn/GDN + norms) and the **CPU MoE** step (norm download + routed dots + result upload), printing a running ms/tok + % breakdown every 50 tokens. The trunk launches are async and already drained at the per-layer MoE `Download` sync, so the added per-layer sync just moves that drain earlier (≈no perturbation).

## Carnice characterization (RTX 4070 Ti, pure per-token)
```
[decode-profile] 100 tok: trunk=9.41 ms/tok moe(dl+cpu+ul)=22.32 ms/tok (trunk 30% / moe 70%)
```
- **MoE 70% (~22ms):** ~8ms RAM floor (reading ~430 MB of experts/token, shared with llama.cpp) + ~14ms coordination overhead (80 `Parallel.For` fork/joins/token, GPU↔CPU per-layer round-trips).
- **Trunk 30% (~9ms):** launch-bound (~600 kernels/token; the CPU-MoE interleaving prevents a single-token CUDA graph).

Findings it surfaced (for follow-up): CPU int8 vs FP dots are ~equal (RAM-bound, not compute); MoE thread count is ~flat 12–24 (RAM-bound); MTP self-spec *hurts* at low acceptance (26.6 t/s @ 43% vs 31.9 pure per-token).

author: th-lange
body:
Closes #94.

## Context
The production module **already** had a structure picker (NPC / Raitaru / Azbel / Sotiyo presets populating `meBonus` / `costBonus` / `structureTePct`), satisfying most of the ticket. The unshipped part was **rig bonuses**.

## What changed
- Adds **Rig ME % / Rig TE % / Rig cost %** inputs that compose onto the chosen structure preset:
  - `meBonus = structure.meBonus × (1 − rigMe%)`
  - `structureTePct = structure.tePct + rigTe%`
  - `costBonus = 1 − (1 − structure.cost)(1 − rigCost%)`

## Decision: user-supplied rig %, not auto SDE/security math
The ticket asked for **SDE-driven** bonuses. I deliberately **didn't** auto-compute rig bonuses from SDE dogma + system-security multipliers: those values vary by patch/security and I can't verify them from this environment, so guessing them would risk **wrong profit numbers**. Instead the user supplies the effective (security-adjusted) rig % — correct-by-construction and composes cleanly. The structure role bonuses themselves are stable constants. Full SDE-dogma sourcing + per-category profiles remain a future refinement (noted on the ticket).

## Tests
`npm run build` green (frontend-only change). `cargo test` unaffected.

author: consultingfuture4200
body:
## DEV-1168 — HNSW relaxed-monotonicity Open/Next/Close iterator (FR-3)

A TriDB-owned C vector iterator the TJS operator (DEV-1169) calls directly — decoupled from Postgres's `IndexScanDesc`, with the relaxed-monotonicity stop lifted out of `hnsw_gettuple`'s hardcoded constants into a caller-controlled bound, surfacing internal HNSW distance per `Next()`.

### Why a new iterator (the gap)
`hnsw_gettuple` is already a relaxed-monotonicity AM scan, but it's only reachable through `amgettuple` inside a planner-chosen IndexScan node. The TJS operator must pull ANN candidates for an arbitrary query vector reached via graph traversal, with **its** global top-k (over graph+relational-filtered survivors) deciding sufficiency. Hard fork constraint: scalar `<->` returns 0 outside an index scan, so the iterator's internal `QueryResult::GetDistance()` is the **only** real distance — no SQL recheck.

### API (`extern "C"`, backed by C++ over `HNSWIndexScan`)
```c
TridbVectorIter *tridb_vec_open(Relation index, const float *query_vec, int dim, int k);
bool tridb_vec_next(TridbVectorIter *it, TridbVectorCand *out);   // {heap_tid, distance}; false => exhausted OR stop fired
void tridb_vec_set_kth_bound(TridbVectorIter *it, float kth_best_distance);  // DEV-1169 seam
void tridb_vec_close(TridbVectorIter *it);
```
Emits **every** candidate in discovery order (matching `hnsw_gettuple`, required by DEV-1169 which expands the graph + applies the relational filter per candidate); the bound governs only **when to stop**, with an internal k-priority-queue fallback when no bound is set. `k`/inversion-tolerance are parameters, not magic constants.

### Mechanism
Ships as `scripts/patches/tridb_vector_iter.patch` (vendor/MSVBASE is gitignored + re-cloned) adding `tridb_vector_iter.{hpp,cpp}` + a test-only `tridb_vector_probe.cpp`, wired into the **unconditional** (hnswlib) `VECTORDB_SOURCES` — not behind `WITH_SPTAG` — and into `scripts/lib/msvbase_patches.sh` (idempotent, sentinel-guarded, verified, applied after the seam patch it depends on).

### Verification (x86 standin)
- approx-non-decreasing: 2 inversions / 2000 candidates (relaxed monotonicity, not strict).
- early termination: examined **8 / 2000** (0.4%) for k=5 (« 25%).
- top-k parity: **5/5** vs the no-stop full-drain oracle (≥99%).
- smoke green; **zero SPTAG** in default `vectordb.so` (DEV-1228 intact).

`test/vector_relaxed_mono_test.sql` (in `make` ENGINE_TESTS) + **ADR-0006**.

### Consumes / feeds
Built on DEV-1228's hnswlib-only vectordb + the `tridb_vector_index.hpp` seam. Feeds **DEV-1169** (TJS) via `set_kth_bound`.

author: quanru
body:
## Problem

When calling `ReportMergingTool.mergeReports(name, { rmOriginalReports: true })` with reports produced in `html-and-external-assets` (directory) mode, original report directories were **not** deleted — leaving scattered report folders behind. Reported against v1.9.8.

### Root cause

`isDirectoryModeReport()` inferred the report's mode from the filesystem:

```ts
path.basename(p) === 'index.html' && existsSync(path.join(dir, 'screenshots'))
```

The `screenshots/` directory is created **lazily**, only when the run persists its first screenshot. A directory-mode report whose run captured **no** screenshots therefore has no `screenshots/` dir, so it was misdetected as *inline*. On deletion that took the inline branch (`unlinkSync(index.html)`), removing only `index.html` and leaving the whole report directory on disk.

Reports that did capture screenshots were deleted correctly, which is why the leftovers looked partial/intermittent.

## Fix

Make reports **self-describing** instead of guessing from the filesystem:

- The generator stamps `data-screenshot-mode="inline" | "directory"` on every dump script tag (`getDumpScriptAttributes`).
- `isDirectoryModeReport()` reads that authoritative metadata. It short-circuits any non-`index.html` path before touching the file (the common inline case costs zero IO), and only falls back to the legacy `screenshots/` heuristic for older reports that predate the attribute.
- The merged report is stamped too, so merged output stays self-describing.
- The mode is resolved **once per report** and reused across selection / merge loop / deletion (previously recomputed 3×, which now means file reads).
- The screenshot-copy step is guarded with `existsSync`, so a screenshot-less directory report merges cleanly.

The attribute name and the `'inline' | 'directory'` union are centralized as `DATA_SCREENSHOT_MODE_ATTR` and `ScreenshotMode` so the writer and the reader share one source of truth.

## Tests

- `report.test.ts`: directory mode detected from metadata without a `screenshots/` dir; `rmOriginalReports` removes the **entire** directory of a screenshot-less directory report.
- `report-generator.test.ts`: writer contract — generated reports stamp `data-screenshot-mode` for both modes.

## Validation

- `npx biome check` on all changed files — clean.
- `npx nx test core` — 1184 passed, my 4 new tests green.
  - One pre-existing failure remains: `merge-browser-parse.test.ts` (merged directory-mode report size assertion). It fails identically (26.92 MB) on clean `main` (verified by stashing this change), so it is unrelated to this PR.

author: richardwooding
body:
Enables the tree-sitter cognitive-complexity walk for **five more languages** — Ruby, Scala, R, MATLAB, Perl — leaving only **Swift** unsupported. That's **15 of 16 tree-sitter languages + Go**.

## Notable
- **Anonymous-token guard**: Ruby names the `if`/`while` *keyword tokens* the same as the statement nodes (`if`, `while`), so the walk double-counted every control structure. Fixed by skipping anonymous (`!IsNamed`) nodes — they're leaf tokens, so this is general and a no-op for the other grammars.
- **Ruby's `else` is shared** between `if` and `case`; counting it would inflate every `case`/`when`, so only `elsif` is flat (trailing plain `else` under-counts by 1, as in the C-family). `case` is the switch container, `conditional` the ternary, `rescue` the catch.
- **Scala** booleans are `infix_expression` + `operator_identifier` (not read by `tsBoolOp`), so `&&`/`||` runs aren't counted (minor under-count); nesting is the dominant signal. else-if via the `alternative` field.
- **MATLAB / Perl**: distinct `elseif_clause`/`elsif` flat nodes (clean). **R**: if/for/while + `alternative` else-if.

## Testing
- 10 new reference cases (ruby/scala/r/matlab/perl nested=6, ruby-case/scala-match=1, ruby-elsif=2, matlab-elseif=3) — all green with the existing 11.
- The search-level "unavailable" test now uses **Swift** (the last unsupported language), with a skip-if-empty guard for grammar variance.
- `go build`/`vet`/`go fix` clean; content/search/mcpserver suites pass. Live smoke: Ruby cognitive=3, Scala=6.

## Remaining (#491)
**Swift only** — its grammar parsed my probe function into `ERROR` nodes (same instability behind the #432 parse-timeout cap), so a spec would yield wrong numbers. Issue retitled to track Swift; revisit when the grammar stabilises.

author: ankittelnyx
body:
## What

Restores `release-please-config.json` on `master` which was deleted when PR #281 merged.

## Why

The release PR carried a deletion from the `next` branch — staging doesn't have prod-owned files like `release-please-config.json`. When the PR merged to `master`, it wiped out the config file that `release-please` needs.

Result: the `github-release` step failed:
```
ConfigurationError: Missing required manifest config: release-please-config.json
```

No `v5.148.0` tag or GitHub release was created → `publish-gem.yml` never triggered → RubyGems stuck at v5.147.0.

## Fix

Restore the file from the commit before the merge (`d0fb7f1~1`). After merge, push to `master` will re-trigger `release-please` which sees 5.148.0 in the manifest with no existing release → creates tag + release → `publish-gem.yml` fires → publishes to RubyGems.

## Root cause (recurring)

The promote-to-prod workflow syncs staging to `next`, but staging doesn't carry prod-owned files. The release PR merge carries those deletions forward. This is the same issue as PR #280. The fix is to add `release-please-config.json` to the prod-owned restore list in the promote-to-prod workflow on staging.

author: k08200
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #581. Completes the `userId`-scoping invariant on the two **live, tenant-facing** `AttentionItem` bulk-teardown paths so the data layer self-scopes rather than relying on the route's ownership check alone.

**Grounding first (honest scope):** the originally-flagged "bulk teardown lacks userId" is **not a live isolation gap** —
- The calendar (`DELETE /api/calendar/:id`) and commitment (`DELETE /api/commitments/:id`) routes already `403` a non-owner before deleting, so the id-keyed deletes were already safe.
- `bulkResolveAttentionForPendingActions` is a **system-wide expiry sweep** over an authoritative cross-user set of uuid `sourceId`s — userId scoping doesn't apply; left unscoped + documented inline.

author: marchouze
body:
## Root cause

The intermittent Core-job flake (`bun run ci:core` → `bun test --isolate`) reported as `(unnamed) [~6160ms]` "near worker-crash logs" was **misattributed**. Pulling the failed attempt-1 Core log (reruns overwrite the conclusion to `success` and hide attempt 1; fetched via `gh api .../attempts/1/jobs`) shows the real failure is a **named** test in `tests/reg-intelligence-objective-layer.test.ts`:

```
objective layer — adopted SERVES backfill > re-fold is idempotent —
re-running the seed neither duplicates nor drops backfill edges [6804.80ms]
  ^ this test timed out after 5000ms.
```

`6804.80ms` ≈ the reported `~6160ms`. `runSeed()` (a full regulatory-objective graph seed) is ~0.9–1.1s idle but CPU+SQLite-bound, so under full-battery contention on a CI runner it balloons to ~7s, tripping Bun's **default 5000ms** per-test/hook timeout. This file fires `runSeed()` in **six** places (a `beforeAll` + three recon-gate `run()`s that each re-seed by design + the idempotency re-fold + the advisory-residual gate) and was the lone outlier carrying **no** explicit timeout — the sibling `*-fold.integration.test.ts` files already use `60_000`/`120_000` on the identical pattern.

The `(unnamed)` vs named variance is the same cause: a **`beforeAll` hook** timeout is reported by Bun with no test name; a test-body timeout shows the name. The `worker-crash.ts` stderr appears nearby only due to coincidental `--isolate` file-ordering — not causation.

## Fix

One `SEED_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` applied to all six `runSeed`-bearing hooks/tests (matching the proven sibling value), with a comment documenting the root cause. Right-sizing a legitimately-heavy deterministic op — not concealment; a genuine hang still fails inside 60s. Authority: Engineering Charter cmd 1 (root-cause before remedy), cmd 3 (no green by concealment), cmd 7 (whole-tree integrity).

## Verification

- Edited file **10/10** green in `--isolate`.
- Full battery **8116 pass / 0 fail**.
- `bun run ci` **exit 0** (core + migrate + recon-infra + recon-domain 156/0), pre- and post-rebase on `origin/main`.

author: krdivesh
body:
## Summary

Hardens `fetch_incidents` in the **Abnormal Security** integration against the failure mode where a single transient API error wedges incident ingestion indefinitely.

### Problem
`fetch_incidents` used **one shared `last_fetch` cursor** and a shared incident-count quota, advancing the cursor only on full success. When a transient error occurred (e.g. an intermittent `500` on `/cases`), the cursor stayed stale. Because the window is `[last_fetch+1ms, now]`, the stale cursor made each subsequent run's window — and therefore its workload — grow without bound, until the run exceeded the **Docker script timeout (300s)** and was killed. A killed run never reaches `setLastRun`, so the cursor never advanced: a self-reinforcing wedge requiring a manual reset. (Observed in ARN-71183: `last_fetch` stuck for >43h.)

### Changes
1. **Per-type cursors** — `last_fetch_threats`, `last_fetch_abuse_campaigns`, `last_fetch_account_takeover_cases`. Each type is fetched independently with its own try/except and advances its cursor **only when it fully drains its window with no errors**. A failing or lagging type no longer blocks the others (separation of concern). Falls back to the legacy `last_fetch` key for seamless migration.
2. **Per-run time budget** (`FETCH_TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS = 240`, comfortably under the 300s Docker limit) replaces the incident-count quota as the run limiter. Paginators now drain the full window (no artificial iteration cap), bounded by the budget. On budget exhaustion or error, the in-flight type's cursor is left unchanged and its partial results are dropped, so the next run retries that window cleanly — no data loss, no duplicates, no Docker kill.

### Design note (commit-on-completion, "Option A")
We verified against the live Abnormal API which timestamp fields each payload exposes for safe per-item checkpointing:

| Type | List item exposes cursor ts? |
|------|------------------------------|
| Cases | ✅ `last_modified` present |
| Abuse campaigns | ❌ only `campaignId` (ts only in detail) |
| Threats | ❌ only `threatId` (no top-level ts; only per-message `remediationTimestamp`) |

Because threats/campaigns list payloads carry no timestamp, items can't be safely ordered for incremental per-item checkpointing without fetching every detail first. We therefore use **commit-on-completion uniformly**: a type advances to `now` only on full window drainage. Truly incremental backlog draining is left as a follow-up.

### Testing
- Full unit suite passes under CI-equivalent `TZ=UTC` (**73 passed**). New tests cover: per-type error isolation, time-budget cutoff, legacy-cursor migration, and independent per-type windows.
- 3 message-filtering tests fail only on non-UTC dev hosts (pre-existing; the code parses the stored-UTC cursor via `.astimezone(UTC)`). They pass under `TZ=UTC`.

### Related
- Refs **INT-1959** (XSOAR incremental checkpointing).
- **INT-1960** (API-side `/v1/cases` stale-connection hardening) is tracked separately and not included here.

author: 7etsuo
body:
Goal item #2 / follow-up to #1318/#1319/#1320.

## The gap
A tool **parked waiting to acquire** (in `Semaphore.acquire` or `AsyncRwLock.withWrite` behind a prior holder) took no abort signal — so when the drain force-finalized it, the parked acquire never woke. It stayed queued until the holder ahead released, then **transiently acquired the guard after being finalized**. Now acquisition is abort-aware.

## What changed
- **AsyncRwLock** (`utils/async-rwlock.ts`): writer side rebuilt from the implicit promise-chain into an explicit `writeWaiters` FIFO of identity-carrying records with a synchronous `state: queued|granted|cancelled` claim; `withRead`/`withWrite` take an optional signal; a queued waiter aborted before grant is removed atomically (`pumpWrite` skips cancelled records); `runHeld` rechecks the signal before draining/running so a granted-then-cancelled writer hands off cleanly.
- **Semaphore** (`concurrency.ts`): identity-carrying records + **direct permit-transfer** accounting (`acquired` counted at grant time, never re-touched by the woken waiter; release forwards to a live waiter or frees). Signal threaded into **both** `shared_server` stages.
- Signal plumbed additively (`ToolRuntimeCallContext.acquireSignal` → `runToolRuntimeCall`/`ToolCallRuntime.run` → the acquire overloads); `runOne` reuses the existing `dispatchSignal`.

## Critical correctness — a double-grant bug caught in review
The draft design's `granted` cancel branch did `reject()` + forward. But `grant()` = `resolve()` is **irrevocable** in a promise model, so the post-grant `reject()` is a no-op and the caller still takes the permit; the forward grants the *next* waiter too → **two holders → `acquired` underflow**. The fix: `granted` → **no-op** (only still-`queued` waiters are removed; a granted waiter keeps its permit and releases normally). **Lost-wakeup is avoided structurally** — grant and cancel resolve under one synchronous `state` flag, and pump always forwards to the next *live* waiter. (Also fixed a regression found mid-implementation: the explicit-queue writer fast path stole the lock before a concurrent reader could register; restored with a `setImmediate` yield.)

## Tests (revert-sensitive, deterministic — no timeouts)
No-lost-wakeup (cancel the middle of 3 waiters → 3rd still acquires); **Semaphore double-grant guard** (granted-then-cancel keeps exactly one holder, exact counts — **reddens with `acquired underflow`** against the reject+forward branch); count-integrity stress (N=20 mixed cancels → `acquired===0`, `readers===0`, queues empty, every waiter settles once); FIFO; already-aborted fast path; capacity=2; + executor acceptance (a force-finalized queued `shared_server` waiter reclaims **without waiting on the holder ahead** and never transiently dispatches — reddens against the unthreaded acquire).

## Gate
- `npm run build` ✅ exit 0 · `tsc -p runtime --noEmit` ✅ clean
- full `npm run test:unit` ✅ **1582 files / 13,434 tests passed, 0 failures**
- double-grant revert-sensitivity independently re-verified: reintroducing the buggy `granted` branch reddens both guards with `Semaphore acquired underflow`; restored → green.

> Note: the design's adversarial-proposal phase failed (output-schema retry cap), so the synthesized architecture was **manually code-reviewed**, which is how the double-grant bug was caught before implementation.

body:
Closes #2625

## Summary

- `pkg/vrrp.Manager` was not Stop/Start reuse-safe: `Stop()` closes the
  run-scoped channels and cancels the context, but `Start()` never
  re-created them. A `Stop()->Start()` cycle on the same Manager broke
  three ways:
  - `Events()` returned the channel `Stop()` closed -> the next instance
    event panicked (send on closed channel).
  - A freshly-spawned link/addr watcher read the already-closed
    `watcherStop` and exited immediately -> tracking + advert-source
    re-resolution dead.
  - `watcherRunning`/`addrWatcherRunning` stayed latched true ->
    `ensure*Locked` never spawned a replacement watcher.
- Fix: `Start()` now calls a new `resetRunStateLocked` under `m.mu`.

## Channels / ctx re-initialized on Start()

`resetRunStateLocked` (under `m.mu`) re-allocates / resets:

| Field | Action |
|---|---|
| `watcherStop` | fresh `make(chan struct{})` |
| `watcherStopOnce` | reset to zero `sync.Once` |
| `eventCh` | fresh `make(chan VRRPEvent, 256)` |
| `closeEventOnce` | reset to zero `sync.Once` |
| `watcherRunning` | cleared to `false` |
| `addrWatcherRunning` | cleared to `false` |
| `m.cancel` | fresh `context.WithCancel(ctx)` (in `Start`) |

It deliberately does NOT touch `instances`, the injected seams
(`linkState`/`subscribe*`/`resolve*`/`run`/`stop`/`open`), or
`onEventDrop` — those are construction-time / caller-owned, not
run-scoped.

## Generation safety

To stay correct across concurrent/repeated Stop->Start, each watcher now
pins its run-generation `watcherStop` at spawn (`ensure*Locked` captures
the channel and passes it in) and cancels on / clears its latch against
that pinned channel. `clearLinkWatcherLatch` mirrors
`clearAddrWatcherLatch`; both are generation-gated (`m.watcherStop ==
stop`) so a lingering pre-Stop watcher cannot reset a fresh post-Start
latch. The link watcher now clears its latch on ANY exit (a single
`defer` covers the synchronous poller-fallback tail-call) — closing the
issue's third gap (`runLinkWatcher` never reset `watcherRunning`).
`Stop()` captures the channels + once-guards under `m.mu` so it cannot
race a half-swapped channel against a concurrent `Start()`.

Single-run behavior and the ~60ms failover timing are unchanged — no
advertisement or timer logic is touched. This is a LATENT lifecycle fix
(production creates the Manager once and only `Stop()`s at shutdown; a
daemon restart is a fresh process).

## Test plan

- [x] `manager_reuse_test.go` (3 tests, `-race`):
  - `WatcherRespawns` — latches cleared + fresh watcher subscribes
    (`watcherStarts == 2`) after Stop->Start.
  - `EventChannelFresh` — Start hands out a non-closed event channel;
    a send on the reused channel would panic (asserted via `recover()`).
  - `ContextRecreated` — fresh cancel func after Stop->Start.
- [x] **Fail-on-revert proven RED**: removing the `resetRunStateLocked`
  call from `Start()` fails `WatcherRespawns` (`addrWatcherRunning`
  stuck true) and `EventChannelFresh` (closed channel reused). Restored
  to green.
- [x] `go build ./...`, `gofmt -l` (clean), `go vet ./pkg/vrrp/...
  ./pkg/cluster/... ./pkg/daemon/...` (clean).
- [x] `go test -race ./pkg/vrrp/... ./pkg/cluster/...` pass;
  `go test ./pkg/daemon/...` pass.
- [ ] **`make test-failover` — REQUIRED before merge (HA/VRRP code).**
  Run by the maintainer; this PR exercises only the single-run path in
  CI, and `test-failover` is the mandated HA gate.

## Refs

- #1814 (link watcher), #2528 (addr watcher), #2156 / #2294 (instance
  lifecycle) — context for the watcher latch + generation patterns.

author: benartzi4
body:
## Summary

Sharing a `soundclash.org` link in a chat or post (WhatsApp, iMessage, Slack, Discord, X, …) previously unfurled to a bare blue link — `index.html` had `og:title`/`og:description` but no `og:image`, which is the tag that makes a rich card appear. This adds the image and the supporting tags.

- **Branded preview card** at `frontend/public/og-image.jpg` — a 1200×630 JPEG (~55 KB): the equalizer logo + two-tone **SOUND CLASH** wordmark + "Buzz in. Name the tune. Win the round." tagline on the dark teal/blue brand gradient.
- **`frontend/index.html`**: adds `og:image` (+ `secure_url`, `type`, `width`, `height`, `alt`) and `og:url`, and bumps the Twitter card from `summary` → `summary_large_image` with `twitter:image`. All image URLs are absolute (`https://soundclash.org/og-image.jpg`) — crawlers fetch them directly.
- **Static by design.** Link-preview crawlers don't run JS, so the tags live in the `index.html` the SPA serves for every route. One generic card covers the homepage and every `/join/<code>` link — no backend or edge function, keeping with the lean architecture.
- **Reproducible asset.** `tools/og-image/` holds the source (`card.html`), the headless-chromium renderer (`render.mjs`), and a README with constraints (size ceiling, caching gotcha) so the card isn't a mystery binary.

![Link preview card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BenArtzi4/Sound-Clash/feature/whatsapp-link-preview/frontend/public/og-image.jpg)

## Test plan

- `npm run build` (frontend) passes; built `dist/index.html` carries the absolute `og:image`, and `dist/og-image.jpg` is emitted by the public-assets copy.
- Image confirmed 1200×630 at 55 KB — comfortably under WhatsApp's ~300 KB render ceiling (the same card is ~415 KB as PNG, hence JPEG).
- After deploy: paste a `soundclash.org` link into WhatsApp (or run it through the Facebook Sharing Debugger) to confirm the live card. Note these platforms cache previews per-URL aggressively — use a `?v=2` variant to force a fresh scrape when iterating.

author: svtter
body:
## Summary

Replaces the v1 cache mechanism (which stored flat message-text blobs and
re-fed them into every prompt) with **true opencode session resume across
runners**.

Each persona's session is now serialized via `opencode export <sessionID>`
to a bundle on a cache server, and restored on the next runner via
`opencode import`. The new runner then issues
`client.session.prompt(existingSessionID, newDiff)` — the opencode server
reads prior context from its local DB rows, not from the prompt text, so
the LLM SDK can hit prompt-cache / KV-cache / message-reuse paths that
weren't possible with v1.

## Changes

### `multi-review/`
- **src/opencode-bundle.ts** (new) — thin wrapper around `opencode export/import` CLI (added in opencode 1.17+); no custom SQLite schema.
- **src/types.ts** — `SessionBundle`, `ReviewContextV2`, `OrchestratorOptions.existingSessions`, `ReviewResult.sessionID`, `CoordinatorResult.sessionID`.
- **src/context-cache.ts** — `loadReviewBundles` / `saveReviewBundles` (filesystem + HTTP backends); preserves v1 API for backwards compat. Stricter prNumber validation + `AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)` on every HTTP call.
- **src/orchestrator.ts** — `runParallelReviewers` / `runCoordinator` honor the `existingSessions` map (resume path) when present; otherwise fall back to create+prompt. `skipSessionCleanup` flag for the v2 export path so callers can `opencode export` the session before it's deleted.
- **src/index.ts** — loads v2 bundles → temp `XDG_DATA_HOME` for per-run DB isolation → schema bootstrap (poll for `opencode.db`, 10s cap) → bundle import → SDK start → run → bundle export → save.
- **Tests** — `opencode-bundle.test.ts` (export/import/readBundle + fake CLI), `orchestrator.test.ts` (resume, partial-resume, skipSessionCleanup, failure-path sessionID, cleanupAllSessions), 5 new v2 tests in `context-cache.test.ts`.

### `review-context-server/`
- **src/server.ts** — `/context/o/r/p/v2` route stores `.v2.json` so v1 + v2 can coexist for the same PR during the rollout window. 16 MiB body cap (returns 413). Single combined regex for routing. Lazy env reads so tests can swap between suites.
- **Tests** — `server.test.ts` (parseContextPath variants, v1/v2 file isolation, auth, 405, malformed JSON 500, body-too-large 413, DELETE, auth-disabled fallback).

### Bug fix (caught by new tests)
- `orchestrator.ts` finally-block was removing sessionIDs from the `activeSessions` set even when `skipSessionCleanup: true` — breaking `cleanupAllSessions` for the v2 export path. Now only deletes from the set when actually deleting.

### Housekeeping
- Drop PoC scripts (probe*.ts, resume-test.ts) — used bun:sqlite + monkey-patched `fetch` (would leak Authorization headers).
- Drop `better-sqlite3` devDep — superseded by the opencode CLI.

## Test plan

- ✅ Unit: 105 multi-review + 18 review-context-server tests pass locally
- ✅ CI: dist-check / multi-review / smoke-actions all green on the head commit
- ✅ Cross-runner e2e smoke (documented in `docs/journal/2026-06-25-session-resume-design.md`): process A exports a session, process B imports it on a fresh `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `session.get` / `session.messages` / `session.prompt` all roundtrip cleanly.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **opencode binary version pinning** — `opencode export/import` schema depends on the opencode binary version. `@opencode-ai/sdk` is pinned `^1.0.0` (too loose). Need to pin the opencode install in `action.yml` so two runners can't drift to incompatible schema versions.

author: nadaverell
body:
## Summary

On every initial connect, `ConnectionContext.updateFromSSE()` runs a **filterless** `queryClient.invalidateQueries()` the instant SSE delivers `connection_state=connected` — invalidating the *entire* React Query cache. The top-level bootstrap queries (`auth/me`, `contexts`, `namespaces`, `api-resources`, `capabilities`, `version-check`, `cluster/namespace-scope`, `portforwards`, `connection`, `settings`) have already fetched during the preceding `connecting` phase, so any of them that have **settled by the connect instant** get re-fetched a second time on first paint. This change stops that redundant re-fetch.

## What changed (`web/src/context/ConnectionContext.tsx`)

The blanket invalidate is only load-bearing for the cluster-data endpoints (`handleNamespaces` / `handleAPIResources` / `handleGetNamespaceScope`) that return `503` (`requireConnected`) while the cluster is still `connecting`: their first fetch errors and must be retried once the cluster is ready. So the fix preserves that recovery and drops only the wasteful part.

Distinguish **first connect** from **reconnect**:

- **First connect:** invalidate only **errored** queries (`predicate: q => q.state.status === 'error'`). The 503'd cluster-data queries recover; everything that already fetched fresh during `connecting` is left untouched — no second fetch.
- **Reconnect after a drop** (pod restart / SSE re-established): keep the **full** invalidate — the cache may be stale across the gap. Behavior unchanged.

It also guards the public `RadarApp` `queryClient` prop: a host that shares one client across cluster-scoped mounts can carry another cluster's data under identical keys, so a **warm-at-mount** cache still does a full invalidate on first connect. (Radar Hub mounts `<RadarApp key={clusterId}>` with its own client, so it always has a cold per-cluster cache and was never exposed to this — the guard just makes the library API correct regardless of how a host wires the client.)

## Impact — honest scoping

This is a **correctness/cleanliness fix that removes redundant load**, not a dramatic speedup. The amount of waste is **timing-dependent**: the invalidate only re-fetches queries that have *already settled* when SSE connects — anything still in-flight is deduped by React Query. Across real captures the visible doubling ranged from ~10 endpoints (fast local connect, where most bootstrap queries had settled) down to a single endpoint (`/api/settings`) on a run where the cluster connected later and most queries were still mid-flight. So on a typical connect the saving is modest and variable; the value is removing an unconditional full-cache invalidation that served no purpose on first connect.

## Testing

- `npm run tsc` ✓
- Verified with a query-cache subscriber + a Playwright network capture against a live `kind` cluster: before, the bootstrap endpoints re-fetched after the `connection_state=connected` event; after, they fetch once and the post-connect invalidate cascade is gone. Re-confirmed the cold-cache fast path still single-fetches after the shared-client guard was added.
- No frontend test runner is configured in this repo; `tsc` is the static gate.
- visual-test: **skipped** — the change is network/timing behavior with no rendered-UI delta; verified via network capture instead.

## Out of scope (separately tracked)

- `dashboard` / `issues` / `dashboard/crds` / `dashboard/helm` fetch twice via a distinct **query-key** change (they mount with `["dashboard",[]]`, then re-key to `["dashboard",[namespaces]]` once `namespaces` resolves) — pre-existing and unrelated to this invalidate.
- `portforwards` 401-retry is a separate retry-handling item.

## Rollout

This is the OSS repo. Radar Hub embeds `@skyhook-io/radar-app`, so reaching Cloud needs a `radar-app` release + a hub dependency bump as a follow-up.

author: edwh
body:
## Problem
`effectiveBrowseView` (isochrone/message.go) scanned `JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(settings, '$.browseView'))` into a non-nullable Go `string`. For any user who has never set `browseView`, that JSON path is **SQL NULL**, so GORM logged `converting NULL to string is unsupported` on **every such request** (observed flooding the apiv2 error log on db1/db3). The fallback to `"nearby"` still happened, so it was log noise rather than a functional break — but noisy and masking real errors.

## Fix
`COALESCE(..., '')` the value in SQL — the same pattern already used in `visualise.go:199/201` — so NULL scans cleanly to `''` and still falls through to the `"nearby"` default. No behaviour change, just no error.

The two sibling `settings` scans (`message.go:919`, `:1727`) already scan into `*string` and are NULL-safe; only this one used a bare `string`.

author: ionfwsrijan
body:
## Description

Fixes #672 — Session TTL Refresh via createdAt Hijacking

### Problem

`/api/chat` resets `createdAt` on every request, which resets the 30-min TTL expiry. An attacker can keep a session alive indefinitely with one request per 29 minutes, causing MongoDB storage exhaustion.

### Changes

**`backend/models/Session.js`:**
- Added `lastAccessedAt` field — tracks activity without affecting TTL
- Added `absoluteExpiry` field — hard 24-hour max lifetime with its own TTL index

**`backend/index.js`:**
- Changed session refresh from `$set: { createdAt }` to `$set: { lastAccessedAt }` — `createdAt` is now immutable after creation

### Impact

- Sessions expire 30 min after creation regardless of chat activity
- Hard 24-hour absolute expiry enforced by secondary TTL index
- No more indefinite session extension

author: cmgrote
body:
## Summary

Four coordinated phases delivering the three-axis separation described in BLDX-1382:
**Routes** (all \`?entrypoint=\` targets) / **Cards** (\`packageId\`-bearing entrypoints) / **Pools** (named worker pools).

### Phase 1 — Route/card split; \`packageId\` on Entrypoint (BLDX-1342)

- **\`Entrypoint.packageId: String?\`** — setting a package ID both marks the entrypoint as a marketplace UI card *and* pins its stable card ID (e.g. \`"@atlan/qlik-sense"\`). This fixes the multi-entrypoint backward-compat problem where the marketplace would auto-derive a card ID from the GMP name + entrypoint name that wouldn't match legacy Argo \`app_id\` values, blanking existing connection references in the UI.
- **Single-entrypoint apps auto-derive** \`package_id: "@atlan/{name}"\` by default — no config needed; \`marketplace_card: true\` is emitted automatically.
- **App-level \`marketplaceCard: Boolean = true\`** opt-out for purely behind-the-scenes apps with no marketplace presence; suppresses the auto-derived \`packageId\` on the implicit entrypoint.
- Entrypoints without a \`packageId\` remain fully routable via \`?entrypoint=\` but do not appear as marketplace cards.
- \`emitEntrypoints\` deprecated (superseded by per-entrypoint \`packageId\`; removal: next minor).
- New \`examples/card-split/\` — two-entrypoint app where only the primary entrypoint carries a \`packageId\`; the secondary is route-only.

### Phase 2 — \`Deployment.pkl\` source-module split (BLDX-1382)

- \`contract-toolkit/src/Deployment.pkl\` extracts \`DaprComponents\`, \`KedaTemporalConfig\`, \`KedaConfig\`, \`ResourceConfig\`, \`Pool\`, \`DeployConfig\` — deployment concerns live in one place rather than scattered across \`App.pkl\`.
- \`App.pkl\` imports and re-exports all six as typealiases — zero breaking change for consuming contracts.
- \`Pool.pkl\` deleted.

### Phase 3 — Nested \`deploy\`/\`pools\` API; \`deployOverrides\` → \`overrides\` (BLDX-1375)

- \`deploy: DeployConfig? = null\` — nullable; unset means no \`deploy:\` block is emitted and Heracles applies platform defaults.
- \`DeployConfig.pools: Mapping<KebabCase, Pool>\` — named worker-pool map; the \`deploy:\` YAML block is synthesised automatically from the first pool in insertion order when non-empty. **First pool = primary; put scale-to-zero pools last.**
- \`Pool\` class: \`keda\`, \`resources\`, \`env\`, \`envOverrides\`, \`overrides\` (per-pool escape hatch).
- \`KedaConfig.cooldownPeriod: Int?\` — per-pool KEDA cooldown knob.
- \`DeployConfig.overrides: Mapping<String, Any>\` — replaces the old app-level \`deployOverrides\`.
- New \`examples/pools/\` — hot (always-on, cooldown=300 s) + cold (scale-to-zero, cooldown=30 s) two-pool reference.
- New \`examples/deploy/\` — single-pool migration example (KEDA, resources, env, pool-level overrides).

### Phase 4 — \`@task(pool=...)\` + pool→task-queue routing (BLDX-1375)

- \`TaskMetadata.pool: str | None\` — declares which named worker pool runs a task.
- \`@task(pool="hot")\` accepted by the decorator; passed through to \`TaskMetadata\`.
- Worker reads \`ATLAN_POOL_<POOL>_QUEUE\` at construction time and passes \`task_queue\` to \`execute_activity\` when set — tasks without a pool use the workflow's own queue (identical to today).
- Pool key is kebab-case validated; POSIX env-var key substitutes \`-\` → \`_\`.
- ADR-0016 documents the multi-pool routing design.

## Test plan

- [x] Pkl tests: \`pkl test tests/*.pkl\` → 223/223, 582/582 asserts
- [x] Invariants: \`./scripts/regenerate-all.sh && ./scripts/check-invariants.sh\` — all pass, no diff on existing examples
- [x] SDK import: \`python scripts/test-sdk-import.py\` → all OK
- [x] Python unit tests: \`uv run pytest tests/unit/app/ tests/unit/execution/ -q\` → 560 pass, 1 skipped
- [x] Pre-commit: clean on all changed files
- [ ] Downstream: merge order — this PR first (triggers toolkit release), then atlan-metabase-app #143 (pin bump + un-draft)

## Breaking changes

**\`deploy\` is now nullable (\`DeployConfig? = null\`)** — apps that previously relied on the always-present \`deploy: DeployConfig\` to emit a \`deploy:\` block must now set \`deploy = new DeployConfig { ... }\` explicitly. Apps that never configured \`deploy {}\` are unaffected.

**\`deployOverrides\` removed** — replace with \`deploy.overrides\` (deployment-wide) or \`pool.overrides\` (per-pool). See \`docs/reference.md\` § Migration Notes → v0.17.0.

**\`@task(profile=...)\` renamed to \`@task(pool=...)\`** — update any tasks using the \`profile\` kwarg. The \`ATLAN_PROFILE_<PROFILE>_QUEUE\` env var is likewise replaced by \`ATLAN_POOL_<POOL>_QUEUE\`.

1. **"Taxa de conclusão 0,0%"** — não era "ninguém concluiu": nos últimos 7 dias **não houve prova oficial (dentro de janela)**, só treino. A métrica (corretamente) mede prova válida, então dava 0/0. Exibir "0,0% ↓62,9pp" engana.
2. **"Tentativas por dia" vazio** — o dado existe (18–40/dia); as barras usavam `bg-admin-accent-soft`, que no dark é vinho escuro sobre card escuro → invisível.
