author: tokuji
body:
## Sprint 55 G3 — opportunistic low-risk wins, rides the **v0.44.1** release

Three hot-path improvements, **no behaviour change**. From `copy-reduction-http1` (P1/P2) and `frame-assembly-fast-path` (Tier 1).

### P1 — `read_body()` single-chunk fast path
Collect chunks in a list and `b''.join` once, instead of O(n²) `body +=`. A single-chunk body (the common case) is returned as the **same object** — no intermediate copy.

### P2 — `_read_headers()` O(n²) → O(n)
Accumulate the header block in a `bytearray` (amortised-O(1) append) instead of `bytes +=`, then publish back as `bytes`. The loop condition and the cap check are **byte-for-byte equivalent** to the prior form (verified against the existing `header_max_total` cap test + the full HTTP/1.1 conformance suite).

### Tier 1 — H2 frame-assembly logging
The eager per-frame logging on `frame.py` / `frame_types.py` / `stream.py` no longer formats or concatenates when the level is off:
- **Deleted** (no operational value): the per-`create()` INFO trace and a bare-int `logger.info(_t)` PRIORITY leftover.
- **`isEnabledFor`-guarded** (hottest per-frame, or expensive arg): `FrameBase.__init__`, `FrameBase.save`, `Headers.save` (its `base + payload` **bytes concat** that lazy `%` can't defer), and `eos()`.
- **Plain lazy `%`-args** (rare + cheap, no guard needed): RST_STREAM `error_code`, PRIORITY fields.

> Re the guard-vs-lazy split: lazy `%`-args defer *formatting*, which is enough for cool sites; the `isEnabledFor` guard is reserved for where the **argument** itself is expensive (the `Headers.save` concat) or the site runs *per frame* (where arg-tuple packing + the call overhead matter). DEBUG output is unchanged when DEBUG is on.

### Out of scope (as planned)
P3 (memoryview parse, opt-in env), P4 (Content-Length body streaming), and Tier 2 (response-HEADERS builder) are explicitly **not** here — they're medium-risk / profiler-gated / gRPC-tied.

### Tests (+10)
`read_body` single-chunk identity, multi-chunk join, empty-chunk skip; `_read_headers` many-header/zero-header/already-terminated-prefix equivalence; a **static audit** that no eager f-string logging remains on the frame hot path, plus behavioural checks that the per-create INFO is gone and DEBUG still emits.

Full beartype suite green (2077 passed); docs build clean.

> Note: the CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` section overlaps with #95/#96 — trivial to combine on merge.

body:
## What & why
The Database dashboard renders blank because Grafana's preinstalled **`grafana-lokiexplore-app`** (Logs Drilldown) auto-updated to a **React-19 build** that requires the host to expose `react/jsx-runtime`. Grafana **11.6 under a sub-path** 404s that module, so the plugin's preload throws an uncaught rejection during page bootstrap and **intermittently crashes dashboard rendering — panels never issue a single query**.

## Evidence (live, from the pod)
- Browser repeatedly `GET /react/jsx-runtime → 404` with referer = the Database dashboard, and **zero `/api/ds/query`** calls afterward (panels never query → all blank).
- Prometheus-only dashboards (Cluster & Nodes) that don't trip the broken module render fine — which is why "some dashboards work."
- The datasources/queries themselves are healthy (verified end-to-end via `/api/ds/query`: CPU 4%, connections 5, 13,418 vectors, etc.). The failure was never the data — it was the frontend crashing before querying.

## Changes
- `GF_PLUGINS_PREINSTALL_DISABLED=true` — stop auto-pulling the unused Drilldown apps.
- `GF_PLUGINS_DISABLE_PLUGINS=grafana-lokiexplore-app` — don't load the broken one.

## Verification
- `helm template` renders the new env cleanly.
- Post-deploy: pod restarts, the failing preload is gone; will confirm the Database dashboard fires `/api/ds/query` and panels populate.

## Notes
- Proper long-term fix is upgrading Grafana to 12.x (ships `react/jsx-runtime` + matching Drilldown apps). Disabling the unused broken app resolves it now with no functional loss.

body:
## Summary
Three additions to the Autopilot plan-review flow.

### 1. Complete / Expired statuses
Resolve a plan from the reader via **Complete** or **Expired**, each with an optional "also close the linked task(s) in Todoist" checkbox (defaulted on for Complete). New `autopilot.resolve` command → `supervisor.resolvePlan` (relabels member tasks `anvil:completed`/`anvil:expired`, optionally `closeTask`). Status chips added.

### 2. Link to active session
**Link to session** attaches a plan to an existing **same-environment** active session instead of spawning a new one (`autopilot.link` → `linkPlan`). End-state matches Start: card leaves the pending grid and you jump to the session.

### 3. Account-wide Autopilot label + catch-all env + reassign
- A configurable Todoist **label** (default `Autopilot`) pulls tasks in from **any** project, bundles them against a **default environment**, and leaves them **review-only** (never auto-started). Coexists with per-project linking, deduped against linked projects. Cards show a "via label" chip.
- **Reassign env** re-evaluates a (possibly mis-routed) plan against another environment's repo — fresh read-only Opus pass, updates the card + open reader in place (`autopilot.reassign` → `reassignPlan`).
- Label + default environment are configured in the autopilot schedule settings.

New building blocks: `TodoistClient.tasksByLabel`, `planAndTagTasks`, `WorkUnit.source`, generalized `pickListDialog`.

## Testing
- Daemon + web typecheck clean (modulo a pre-existing `session-fs.ts` error on `main`).
- `autopilot-plan` + `autopilot-schedule` unit tests pass.
- Not yet covered: label-pass / reassign / resolve paths (Supervisor-importing tests flake in worktree sandboxes); deploy still needs `service.sh restart` from the canonical checkout.

Implemented a parallel "competitor run" that reuses the existing Apify plumbing but writes to new, dedicated tables — fully isolated from the news flow.

**New tables (migrations)**
- `023_create_competitors.sql` — `competitors` registry the Curve App edits (mirrors `sources`: `name`/`handle`/`url`/`source_type` ∈ {instagram, tiktok}/`enabled`), with indexes on `source_type` and `enabled`.
- `024_create_competitor_data.sql` — `competitor_snapshots` (append-only follower time series, one row per run) and `competitor_posts` (keyed by unique `guid = '{platform}:{post_id}'` with `like_count`/`comment_count`/`view_count`/`caption`/`published_at`).

**Shared Apify module**
- `ingestion/apify.py` (new) — `run_actor()` and `parse_ts()` plus `APIFY_BASE`/`APIFY_TIMEOUT`, extracted verbatim from `social.py`.
- `ingestion/social.py` — now imports those from `ingestion/apify.py`; news flow behaviour unchanged.

**Competitor run**
- `ingestion/competitors.py` (new) — `run_competitors()`: guards on `APIFY_TOKEN`, reads `get_competitors()`, and per account runs the platform actor (IG `resultsType:"details"` → `followersCount` + `latestPosts`; TikTok `clockworks~tiktok-scraper` → `authorMeta.fans` + per-video metrics). It appends a follower snapshot, applies a client-side 14-day cutoff + sort-desc + 10-post cap, and upserts posts. Per-account `try/except` with `log_source_run(name, "competitor", "ok"/"error", count)` — one bad handle never aborts the run.
- `ingestion/storage.py` — added `get_competitors()`, `insert_competitor_snapshot()`, `upsert_competitor_posts()` (`on_conflict='guid'`, `ignore_duplicates=False`).
- `config.py` — added `COMPETITOR_POST_LIMIT` (10) and `COMPETITOR_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (14); reuses existing Apify config.

**Triggers**
- `api.py` — `POST /run/competitors` (key-guarded, background task).
- `ingestion/scheduler.py` — appended `_run("competitors", run_competitors)` after `daily-brief` in `run_daily_pipeline()`.
- `main.py` — added `competitors` to `STAGES` (not date-scoped), enabling `python -m main --stage competitors`.

﻿## Summary

🚀 Adds the pp-dev 1.0 developer tooling update for PP-3449: the Request Inspector UI/API, refreshed MI-style dev panel, grouped config schema with migration support, and stronger local/CI test coverage.

🧪 The PR also reworks CI so GitHub Actions runs the full expected test surface without Docker: repo-wide audit, `npm run test`, Vitest E2E, and browser E2E against Vite, Next.js ESM, and Next.js CJS fixtures through `mock-mi` replay.

---

## 🚀 Product and Developer Features

## What

Closes the **8-skill `.eval.json` gap** the `eval-completeness` test had been WARNing on — the lone advisory item surfaced by `/ork:cover and verify all`. Eight skills shipped a `test-cases.json` but had no graded evaluation file.

author: ben-harack
body:
## Summary

`from data_models.reflection import GatheredActivity` inside `config_seed/templates/reflection/step_handlers.py::handle_gather_activity` fails at runtime with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'data_models'`.

The seeded `data_models/` package lives under `~/carpenter/config/data_models/`, but its parent dir is never added to `sys.path` at platform startup. The only existing path injection (in `verify/_schema._load_model_class`) is lazy and only fires when `validate_contract` is called.

This PR adds an eager injection in `Coordinator._install_data_models_syspath()`, called immediately after `_install_config_seeds()` succeeds. Now any template handler can `from data_models.X import Y` directly at execution time.

## Why the lazy injection in `verify/_schema.py` was NOT removed

Tests in `tests/test_data_models.py` and `tests/verify/test_schema.py` call `validate_contract` / `_load_model_class` directly without going through coordinator startup; they rely on the lazy path to add `data_models_dir` to `sys.path`. Removing it would break those tests. Leaving the safety net in place is also strictly more defensive for any future caller that bypasses `Coordinator.start()`.

## Files changed

- `carpenter/coordinator.py` (+12, -0): new `_install_data_models_syspath()` helper invoked from `_install_config_seeds()`; `sys` import added at module top
- `tests/test_data_models.py` (+50, -0): two tests for the new helper (positive: install + import works without manipulation; negative: noop when unset)

## Test plan

- [x] `~/bin/run-tests tests/test_data_models.py tests/verify/test_schema.py tests/core/test_reflection_period_pipeline.py -q` — 42 passed
- [x] `~/bin/run-tests tests/ -q` — 4807 passed, 65 skipped, 5 pre-existing failures (3 gmail package version drift + 2 taint invariant flakes that pass in isolation and reproduce identically on `upstream/main` without these changes)

author: n8n-cat-bot[bot]
body:
## Summary

Tunes the mutation-health setup so a single-file run finishes faster and never dies with nothing, addressing a poke run that hit the job wall at 87% after ~20 min and exited with no `summary.json`.

### `packages/workflow/stryker.config.mjs`
- **`incremental: true`** (+ `incrementalFile: 'reports/mutation/stryker-incremental.json'`) — caches mutant results so the property-testing edit/re-run loop only re-tests mutants whose covering tests changed. The cache lands under the already-gitignored `**/reports/mutation/` path.
- **`ignoreStatic: true`** — skips module-level (static) mutants, each of which forces a full re-instrument.
- **`timeoutMS` 60_000 → 15_000** — a string/utils mutant has no legit multi-second op, so a 15s+ run is a loop-condition mutant spinning; cap low so it fails fast instead of stalling the run.
- **Dropped the `progress`/`html` reporters** → `reporters: ['clear-text', 'json']`. These runs are non-interactive (CI / agent loop); the unused `htmlReporter` config was removed alongside it.

### `scripts/mutation-health/mutate.mjs`
- **Emit a partial `summary.json` on a non-zero / timed-out Stryker exit.** Previously any non-zero exit called `die(3)` and wrote nothing. Now it only dies when Stryker produced no `raw.json` to salvage; otherwise it builds the summary from the (partial) report and marks it `partial: true`.
- **A partial run never reports PASS** (review fix). The gate now requires `thresholdMet && !summary.partial` for both the printed verdict and the process exit code. A cut-short run can show `survived: 0` / score 100% even though mutants were never tested, so gating on `thresholdMet` alone would mark a file done with work left undone. The gate line surfaces `FAIL (partial)` in that case.
- Docstring updated: drop the stale `raw.html` output line, document the partial-summary behaviour, and note that a partial run exits 1.

### Comment cleanup (review fix)
The added config/script comments were trimmed to a single line on the *why* rather than restating the ticket.

## Scope note

The ticket lists only `packages/workflow/stryker.config.mjs` and `scripts/mutation-health/mutate.mjs`. The shared `scripts/mutation-health/stryker.default.mjs` (used by other packages' runs) is left untouched to keep this change scoped to the named files.

## Testing
- `node --test scripts/mutation-health/mutate.test.mjs` — 30 passed, 0 failed.
- Config imports cleanly with the expected values (`incremental`, `incrementalFile`, `ignoreStatic`, `timeoutMS: 15000`, `reporters: ['clear-text','json']`).
- `biome check` — clean on both files.

## Review checklist
- [x] Code changes scoped to the two ticket files
- [x] Existing unit tests pass
- [x] Lint/format clean

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary
Researcher-6 cycle branch — verified gallery contributions.

### 1. central-limit-theorem-oq-02-incomplete-01
**Bienaymé's identity with the covariance correction** — `Var[∑ᵢ Xᵢ] = ∑ᵢ Var[Xᵢ] + 2·∑_{i<j} Cov[Xᵢ, Xⱼ]`. Refines Mathlib's `variance_sum'` by extracting the diagonal variance and folding the off-diagonal into twice the strict upper triangle (`Prod.swap` involution + `covariance_comm`). 4 theorems, **0 axioms, 0 sorries**. New file + gallery entry.

### 2. erdos-72-incomplete-01 — Erdős Problem #72 (unavoidable cycle lengths)
Proved **all three density lemmas** and rehabilitated a file that previously had 3 sorries and did not compile (stale import, universe metavariables, orphaned docstrings):
- `powersOfTwo_density_zero` — count ≤ `Nat.log 2 n + 1` (injection via `Nat.log`), squeezed by `(logb 2 n + 1)/n → 0`.
- `perfectSquares_density_zero` — count ≤ `Nat.sqrt n + 1` (injection via `Nat.sqrt`), squeezed by `(√n + 1)/n = n^(-1/2)+1/n → 0`.
- `arithmeticProgression_positive_density` — lower bound count ≥ `(n-a)/d+1` forces density ≥ `1/d > 0`, contradicting density 0.
- Fixes: `import Mathlib`, `noncomputable countingFunction`, `∀ (V : Type)` universe pin, 4 orphaned `/--`→`/-`.

Result: **0 sorries, 1 axiom** (`liu_montgomery_powers_of_two`, the deep 2020 Liu–Montgomery theorem — legitimately axiomatized). The 3 density theorems depend only on `propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound`. Gallery meta sorries 3→0.

### 3. burnside-counting-oq-03-oq-02-oq-01-oq-02 (prior commit on this branch)
Cyclic necklace count in divisor-sum form ∑_{d∣n} φ(n/d)·k^d = (#necklaces)·n [verified, 0-axiom, original].

author: yauhenbichel
body:
Fixes #3022

## Describe the changes you have made in this PR -

Replaces the 818-line `app/integrations/_verification_adapters.py` monolith with a plugin-registry architecture. Each of the 50 vendor verifiers now lives in its own focused file and self-registers at import time; consumers resolve verifiers by service name through a single `get_verifier(...)` lookup.

## Why

Before this PR, adding or changing a verifier meant editing the central monolith. The dispatch contract was tangled with 47 underscore-prefixed back-compat aliases. The Slack verifier broke the uniform `VerifierFn` shape with a `send_slack_test` kwarg. Tests had to monkey-patch attributes on the monolith. New contributors had to read 818 lines to understand the verification model.

---

## Code Understanding and AI Usage

**Did you use AI assistance (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) to write any part of this code?**
- [ ] No, I wrote all the code myself
- [x] Yes, I used AI assistance (continue below)

**If you used AI assistance:**
- [x] I have reviewed every single line of the AI-generated code
- [x] I can explain the purpose and logic of each function/component I added
- [x] I have tested edge cases and understand how the code handles them
- [x] I have modified the AI output to follow this project's coding standards and conventions

**Explain your implementation approach:**

- New package `app/integrations/verification/` — registry + two factory helpers (`build_probe_verifier`, `build_validation_verifier`) + the  shorthand registration helpers (`register_probe_verifier`, `register_validation_verifier`).
- New folder `app/integrations/verifiers/` — 35 vendor files for  config-only integrations.
- New `app/services/<vendor>/verifier.py` modules — 15 vendor files  co-located with each vendor SDK client (alertmanager, argocd,  datadog, helm, etc.).
- `_verifiers_loader.py` — replaced the hand-maintained 50-line import  list with `pkgutil` auto-discovery across both verifier locations.
- `_verification_adapters.py` — deleted. All consumers  (`registry.py`, `verify.py`, tests) migrated to canonical imports.
- `IntegrationSpec.verifier: VerifierFn` field is now  `has_verifier: bool`; the callable is sourced from the registry.
- Slack: single registered `verify_slack(source, config)`. The  `--send-slack-test` flag is plumbed via a private `_send_slack_test`  config key, set by `verify_integrations(...)` before dispatch.

author: tomfarmery93
body:
## The good news

On-device testing **proved native background tracking works.** For the test walk, `gps_pings` held **22 pings, continuous every ~10–15s across the whole 5m21s walk — including the half where the app was closed and the phone locked.** The owner's `/track/` page already reads `gps_pings`, so **the customer already sees the full route.**

## The bug this fixes

The **carer's own walk screen** drew its map + ping count + distance from the **local JS array** (`gpsPoints`), which only captures foreground fixes. So it showed ~5 pings / half a route while the DB had the full 22. Pure front-end mismatch.

## Fix (`walk/index.html`)

Make the carer screen read the DB — the native service's source of truth — mirroring the track page:
- `loadPingsFromDb(full)` pulls `gps_pings` for the session (incremental or full reload).
- A native active walk **polls the DB every 8s** instead of running `navigator.geolocation` (avoids double-counting; picks up backgrounded pings on resume).
- `endWalk` and the resume-of-completed path do a **full DB load before the summary**, so distance/route/ping count are accurate.
- The `navigator.geolocation` path is kept only as the **non-native fallback** (iOS / web / plugin missing).

## Verify after merge + deploy

Do another walk (lock + close the app for part of it). The carer's live screen and the **Walk complete** summary should now show the **full route + real ping count**, matching `gps_pings` and the owner's track view.

author: boxdot
body:
The buffer header only stored the tail position. Across restarts the
persisted tail could lag the real data extent, so the circular read walked
from the stale tail through leftover data into the never-written (zero)
region and wrapped around, splicing NUL bytes into the middle of a line.
The result was huge, unreadable lines in the developer log view.

Store a total `written` counter (and a MAGIC for format detection) instead
of the bare tail, and read only the valid window: [0, written) until the
buffer wraps, then the full ring. The unwritten region can no longer leak
into the data, and files without the MAGIC (old format) are discarded on
open.

author: amanusk
body:
> Split out of #84 — this is pre-existing work that got bundled into the WS branch when it was cut from a local `master` that was one commit ahead of `origin/master`. It is independent (touches `address.rs` / `dune.rs` / `mod.rs`; no overlap with the WS change).

## Problem

The cold MetaTxs tab scanned the 5k-block tip then walked `ExtendDown` backward one
pf-query window at a time. On accounts whose meta-tx activity sits deep in history that
is slow and surfaces the **oldest** meta-txs first.

## Change

A meta-tx where the address is the intender is an `execute_from_outside*` **call** to the
address, so Dune's trace-indexed `starknet.calls` (selector-filtered, `ORDER BY block DESC`)
jumps straight to the most-recent ones. Adds a Dune fast-paint mirroring the Calls
progressive window ladder:

- **dune**: `QueryShape::ContractMetaTxCallsWindowed` = `ContractCallsWindowed` narrowed to
  the three `execute_from_outside` selectors; shared row parser extracted to avoid
  duplication. Selector literals pinned by a test.
- **address**: `emit_recent_meta_txs_via_dune` runs a 90d + hedged-365d window concurrently
  (cancel-on-fill), bulk-fetches the outer txs via pf, runs the shared classifier, and
  streams survivors via the cursor-neutral `AddressMetaTxsStreamed` so the pf scan still
  owns lifetime backfill and the private-pool / component-selector cases Dune can't see.
  Tail-latency hedge generalised and shared with Calls.

## Verification

- Windowed SQL verified against production Dune (recent-first rows).
- Both new dune guard tests pass; release build clean.

author: thesherwood
body:
## Summary

Fixes **I14 tier 2**: a `-O2` program using `__int128` for a 64×64→128 widening multiply (Embench `aha-mont64`'s `mulul64`: `(unsigned __int128)a*b >> 64`) previously fail-closed at translate with `Unsupported("integer width i128")`. The on-ramp now recognizes the idiom and lowers it **without ever materializing a 128-bit value**.

(Tier 1 — the embench `-U__SIZEOF_INT128__` harness sidestep + a funnel-shift fix — was already landed; this is the engine capability.)

## How

`lower_i128_idiom` — a new early-return hook in `translate_inst` (mirroring `lower_wide`/`lower_mask`) — tracks each i128 SSA value symbolically in a **block-local** side-table:

| LLVM | symbolic form |
|---|---|
| `zext i64 X to i128` | `Zext(X)` |
| `mul i128 (zext a) (zext b)` | `WideMul(a, b)` |
| `lshr <product> 64` | `Hi(a, b)` |
| `trunc i128 V to i64` | emit the concrete i64 op |

A concrete op is emitted **only at the `trunc`**: the source for a `Zext`, `mul` for a `WideMul` (low half), an inline schoolbook **`umulhi`** for a `Hi` (high half). The engine has no scalar high-multiply primitive, so `emit_umulhi` emits the 32×32 expansion in IR — **self-contained in `svm-llvm`**, no new op threaded across the stack.

**Fail-closed, never miscompile:** any i128 use outside the idiom — a full `add`/`sub`/variable-shift, or an `xor`/`and`/`or i128` (which clang folds bitwise combinations of `(u128)…` into) — still returns `Unsupported`. The table is block-local, so a cross-block i128 also fails closed.

## Tests

`translate.rs::{i128_widening_mul_hi, i128_widening_mul_lo_and_hi}` (the latter has the product feeding **both** a low `trunc` and a high `lshr`+`trunc` — the real `mulul64` shape) run **bit-exact, interp == JIT, vs a Rust `u128` oracle**. Full translate suite (187) green; clippy + fmt clean.

A note from building it: my first `lo ^ hi` test failed because clang folds that into `xor i128`+`trunc` (trunc distributes over bitwise ops) — a more general i128 use, correctly fail-closed. The *real* `mulul64` stores lo/hi separately, which the matcher handles; the test now mirrors that shape (shifts that don't distribute over `trunc`).

## Scope

`ISSUES.md` I14 marks tier 2 landed. The embench example **keeps** `-U__SIZEOF_INT128__` for `aha-mont64` — `modul64`'s `__int128` *variable* shift is outside this idiom, so a full-kernel `__int128` build needs more than tier 2; removing the sidestep should be validated against a real Embench checkout.

…e command (E2b)

Pass1GradingService::grade(Run) resolves the brief's technical competences at their pivot target level, builds RepoDigest once per run, calls the GraderClient once per competence, parseWithRepair, and persists in a per-competence DB transaction: per-criterion evidence + drafts (with ai_reasoning) + one pass1_competence_results rollup.

- Idempotent re-grade: delete-then-reinsert scoped to the competence; updateOrCreate on the rollup preserves operator_status/finalized_at.
- Failure isolation: unparseable/throwing competence → safe à vérifier rollup row with raw_json audit trail, no evidence/drafts; all other competences still grade; run never aborts.
- Per-competence transaction: no whole-run transaction; a crash leaves committed competences intact and the in-flight one with no rows.
- php artisan pass1:grade {run}: sets run.status (pass1_done/pass1_partial), prints a per-competence summary; exit 0 on done/partial, 1 on hard precondition failures.

Tests use FakeGraderClient — zero live network. The egress gate (glm-5.2 zero-retention) blocks only the first real run, not the build.

Respects R1 (hedged-only via E2a parser + E1 column contract; service never writes operator columns), R3 (blind, evidence-first, one call per competence at its target level), R4 (no identity in digest/prompt), R5.

Follows up #1: now that shipit has code on `main`, give its own PRs **real checks and a real reviewer**, and state the PR lifecycle in the agent-policy doc. This dogfoods the gate from the first commit (lessons-learned.lex §1d).

## What's here
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — self-contained Python gate (install + `pytest`), exposing the required `check` context. It runs on this very PR, so the loop now has a *real* check to shepherd (no longer vacuous). Migrates to `setup-pixi` + `pixi run ci` when the pixi tasks land (Steps 3/5/6); the `check` contract stays stable.
- **`.github/workflows/copilot-review.yml`** — the canonical caller that fires Copilot at PR `opened` (non-fork, non-gate). `gh-setup` already excludes it from required checks.
- **`.shipit.toml`** — source `RELEASE_TOKEN` from the local gh CLI token env var (`GH_TOKEN`, repo+workflow scope), since doppler doesn't carry it. The secret is already set on the repo, so Copilot review should fire on this PR.
- **`AGENTS.lex`** — mirror the **draft → shepherd → ready, then stop** lifecycle as a general principle for *both* tracks. It was only implicit in the feature flow before, which is what let "stop at the ready flip" get misread as "stop at draft".

## Sequencing (no deadlock)
The branch ruleset that **requires** `check` is applied by `shipit gh-setup` **after** this PR merges (so `check` exists on `main`). Requiring an off-`main` check would block every PR — including this one. So: merge this → `gh-setup` requires the check → fully onboarded.

## Verification
- ✅ 42 tests green locally.
- CI runs on this PR (watching it go green before flipping to ready).
- Copilot review expected to fire on open (RELEASE_TOKEN is set).

author: ymlyza
body:
## Problem

`e2e/tests/offline-queue.spec.ts` has been intermittently failing on CI at the **"Reconnecting" pill** assertion — it's shown as `1 flaky` (auto-retried to pass) on #5–#7 and failed the first CI run of #8, needing a manual re-run.

## Root cause

The test forced the client offline **before** closing the relay WebSocket:

```
ctxA.setOffline(true);   // network now dead
__closeRelayWS();        // close() can't complete its handshake over a dead network
```

With the network already down, the WebSocket **closing handshake can't complete** (the Close frame can't be sent/acked), so Chromium delays the `onclose` event until an internal timeout. `client-core` emits `"reconnecting"` from `onclose`, so the status pill update is delayed too — intermittently past the 10s assertion. Classic timing race → passes on retry.

## Fix

Reorder: **close while still online** (prompt, deterministic `onclose` → client emits `"reconnecting"` immediately), **then** `setOffline(true)` to block the reconnect. The client's first reconnect attempt is ~1s out (`Backoff` baseMs 1000) and `setOffline` is applied in <100ms, so the reconnect is reliably blocked — no delayed-onclose race, no reconnect-succeeds race.

Assertions are unchanged (Reconnecting pill, Queued marker, flush-on-reconnect).

## Verification

Ran the test **8/8 with `--retries=0`** (the config's `retries: 1` is what was masking the flake as "flaky") — all passed. Root-caused via systematic-debugging (traced the status flow: `onclose` → `handleClose` emits `"reconnecting"` → `status-pill.svelte`).

author: amrebeid
body:
## Bug (HIGH reliability)

`recordReceipt` (`apps/farm-os/app/(app)/purchase-requests/[prId]/actions.ts`) posted receipt movements **non-atomically** across PR line items. It claim-flipped the PR `approved → received`, then **looped** `fn_post_movement('receipt', …)` once per `purchase_request_items` row from the client.

If item index ≥ 1 failed *after* item 0 had already committed, the PR was left `received` with **only partial stock posted** AND **no clean retry path** (the claim was already consumed) → a corrupt half-received state that inflates some bins but not others. The per-item revert heuristic (release the claim only if item 0 failed) could not cover a mid-loop failure.

## Fix

Mirrors the existing atomic-RPC precedent `fn_execute_operation` (migration `0020`):

1. **New migration `20260622000024_fn_post_receipt.sql`** — a `SECURITY DEFINER` `fn_post_receipt(p_pr_id uuid)` that runs in **one transaction**:
   - **Authz** replicating exactly what `recordReceipt` relied on: `authorize('inventory.write')` (owner/farm_manager/storekeeper — the same gate `fn_post_movement` enforces and the action checked) + an **org-membership guard** (`auth.role()='anon'` rejected; a JWT user's PR must be in `user_org_ids()`), mirroring `requireMembership()` + the `fn_post_movement` cross-org guard.
   - **Claim-first** (idempotency): `update purchase_requests set status='received' where id=p_pr_id and status='approved'`; 0 rows → `raise … using errcode='23505'` (already received / not approved).
   - **Loop** `purchase_request_items` and `perform fn_post_movement(item, 'receipt', qty, …)` for each — all inside the same transaction, so any failure rolls the claim **and** every prior receipt back. The PR stays `approved` and is cleanly retryable. No app-layer revert.
   - Returns a jsonb summary `{ pr_id, items_posted, status }`.
   - **Locked down per migration `0021`**: `set search_path=''`, fully schema-qualified, `revoke all … from public`, `revoke execute … from anon`, `grant execute … to authenticated`.

2. **Rewired `recordReceipt`** to a single `sb.rpc('fn_post_receipt', { p_pr_id: prId })`, mapping the error to the existing `{ ok:false, error }` shape. The SQLSTATE→message mapping is preserved (`23505` → "الطلب غير معتمد أو تم استلامه بالفعل"; `42501` → "ليس لديك صلاحية استلام المخزون"). The obsolete client-side `authorize()` check, the client claim, and the per-item loop are removed.

3. **New pgTAP test `tests/23_post_receipt_atomic_test.sql`** asserts:
   - (a) a normal **multi-item** receipt posts every item (`on_hand` +100 / +250) and flips status `approved → received`;
   - (b) a second call is **rejected** (idempotent, `23505`) and does **not** re-post (no phantom stock IN);
   - (c) **anon cannot EXECUTE** `fn_post_receipt` (catalog `has_function_privilege`), authenticated can; plus a negative in-body authz case (accountant refused with no side effect);
   - (d) **atomicity** — a forced mid-loop failure (2nd item NULL qty → `fn_post_movement` raises) rolls the **claim + the first item's receipt** back: the PR stays `approved` and the first item's `on_hand` is unchanged.
   - `fn_post_receipt` added to the intended-RPC allow-list in invariant test `22`.

## Test results

```
PG_BIN=/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin bash apps/farm-os/supabase/test-shims/run-pgtap-local.sh
…
   22_security_invariants_test.sql          ok=8  not_ok=0 todo=0
   23_post_receipt_atomic_test.sql          ok=13 not_ok=0 todo=0
==> TOTAL ok=150 not_ok=0
```

App (`apps/farm-os`): `tsc --noEmit` ✓ · `eslint` ✓ · `next build` ✓ (all routes compiled). `package-lock.json` left unmodified (npm-install dirtying reverted).

## ⚠️ STOCK-ENGINE change — NOT applied to prod

This is a **STOCK-ENGINE change — NOT applied to prod**; it needs **Owner review/ratification per PROJECT RULES before any prod db push**. The new migration `0024` has not been pushed to the live Supabase DB.

author: zoltan118
body:
Three follow-ups to the slim one-row nav (#187), each reproduced and verified in the dev-server preview.

## 1. Tools dropdown did nothing on tap
The nav tab strip is an `overflow-x:auto` scroll container, and an overflow container clips its positioned descendants. The menu *was* opening but got clipped to invisible. **Fix:** render the menu in a portal to `<body>` with `position:fixed` coords measured from the trigger's rect; the outside-click and reposition handlers now account for the portaled node.

## 2. Theme toggle re-animated on every tab change
The nav (and the switcher) remounts on each navigation. `useTheme` started at the default theme and corrected to the stored one in an effect, sliding the thumb on every remount. **Fix:**
- `useTheme` now reads `<html data-theme>` synchronously in its `useState` lazy initializer, so the first render already matches and there's no flip.
- The thumb's slide is gated behind an `is-animatable` class added ~80ms after mount via `setTimeout` (rAF is paused in backgrounded tabs and would leave the toggle non-animating). First-load hydration no longer animates; real user toggles still slide.

## 3. Trailing space after Tools on wider phones
The left-aligned strip didn't fill the row at ≥390px. **Fix:** `justify-content: space-between` so Tools sits flush right. When the tabs overflow on a narrow screen there's no free space to distribute, so they pack and scroll as before.

## Verification (preview)
- Menu: portaled to `body`, `position:fixed`, hit-test at its top lands on a menu item (visible, not clipped).
- Switcher: across PSE → Governance → Analytics it stays `is-dark` with the thumb already at the correct position (no flip); a real toggle still animates (transition `0.25s` once `is-animatable`).
- Tab strip at 390px: `gapAfterLast: 0` (Tools flush right), no overflow.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: pekbart
body:
Should resolve https://github.com/NordSecurity/uniffi-bindgen-go/issues/83. The issue is already well documented, so just a quick recap:

An empty `String`/`Vec` lowers to a `RustBuffer` whose `data` field is Rust's `NonNull::dangling()` sentinel. Because that field is typed as `*C.uchar` Go's GC treats it as a managed pointer. If a `copystack` runs while the value is on the stack, Go's runtime treats it as invalid pointer and crashes.

This PR changes `data` from `uint8_t*` to `uintptr_t`, so the GC no longer scans it as a pointer. I've also added a `capacity == 0` guard in `AsReader`/`ToGoBytes`/`Data` so the dangling sentinel is never turned back into a Go pointer.

from Rails. This converges every miss site onto Rails'
`raise_record_not_found_exception!` (`finder_methods.rb:417-434`):

- scalar miss `find(1)` / single-element-array miss `find([1])` →
  `Couldn't find <Model> with '<pk>'=<id>` (single-id branch — no pluralize/suffix)
- multi-id aggregate miss `find([1, 2])` →
  `Couldn't find all <Models> with '<pk>': (1, 2) (found N results, but was looking for M).`
- composite-PK misses (single tuple and list-of-tuples) → the same aggregate
  branch (Ruby's recursive `Array#join` → `(1, 2, 3, 4)`)

The three aggregate sites share a new `raiseCouldntFindAll` helper that mirrors
the Rails else-branch (`name.pluralize` + `(found … results, but was looking
for …).`). `RecordNotFound` payload (`model`, `primaryKey`, `id`) is unchanged.

## Review responses

1. **Missing `name.pluralize`** — fixed. All three aggregate messages now go
   through `raiseCouldntFindAll`, which calls `pluralize(name)` (e.g. `Users`).
   Test assertions at `finder.test.ts` updated to the plural form.
2. **Missing result/expected counts** — fixed. `Core#find` already has the
   counts at each site (`records.length` vs requested size; `0`/`1` for the
   composite single-tuple `find_one` case), threaded into the suffix.
3. **Dead code at the empty-tuples guard** — removed. The unreachable
   `tuples.length === 0` check sat inside the `id.length > 0` branch, so it
   never executed; removal is behavior-preserving. The composite `find([])`
   path is unchanged (it never entered this branch).

## Inter-path note

`Core#find` is now byte-faithful to Rails. The relation path (`performFind` →
`raiseNotFoundSingle`/`raiseNotFoundAll`) still uses the simplified form; its
convergence onto the same full builder is tracked by the existing
**`performfind-converge-raise-record-not-found-builder`** story (RFC 0023),
which restores full model↔relation parity without overloading this PR.

## Test plan

- `pnpm vitest run packages/activerecord/src/finder.test.ts` — pass
- `pnpm vitest run packages/activerecord/src/base.test.ts` — pass

No method signatures changed (api:compare delta 0) and no test names changed
(test:compare delta 0).

Closes-story: core-find-record-not-found-message-format-fidelity

## Review response — shared-DB id flake (CI)

The MariaDB/PostgreSQL CI failure at the `find with missing IDs throws` test
was a hardcoded-id assumption: auto-increment/sequence are not reset on
transactional-fixture rollback, so `find([1, 999])` searched an id that did
not exist and the count read `found 0` instead of `found 1`. Fixed both that
test and its sibling `find with multiple IDs` (which hardcoded `[1, 3]`) to
derive ids from the created records.

Converting the inline `User` to the canonical `User` model is not viable here:
this file uses a wholesale **bespoke local `TEST_SCHEMA`** (finder.test.ts:14)
where `users` is `{name, email, age, active, role, score}`, which is
incompatible with the canonical `User` model (`hasSecureToken` /
`hasSecurePassword` require `token`/`auth_token`/`password_digest`). The
canonical conversion of this grandfathered file is RFC 0019 (canonical-schema
burndown) scope, not this Core#find story. Deriving ids from created records
removes the nondeterminism without a cross-shape collision.

author: rickylabs
body:
## Why

The atomic JSR publish aborted partway (14/31 packages landed, then failed). This is **root cause #2** — distinct from the per-member publish-loop bug already fixed in #123.

~15 member `deno.json` files mapped sibling `@netscript/*` imports to **relative file paths** (`../sibling/mod.ts`). On a real `deno publish`, each member's tarball is rooted at its own directory, so `../sibling/mod.ts` escapes the tarball boundary and the module graph fails to build. `--dry-run` resolves those paths against the local filesystem (where the sibling exists), so **both local and CI dry-runs passed green while the real publish failed** — which is why the run landed packages incrementally then aborted.

## What

1. **Strip all 111 relative `@netscript/*` import entries** across `packages/` + `plugins/`. Deno workspace resolution + each target's declared `jsr:` exports cover bare-name and subpath imports, and rewrite them to `jsr:@netscript/X@<version>` on publish. Every stripped subpath was verified against the target package's declared `exports`.
2. **Add the aspire `./public` declared export** (`./src/public/mod.ts`). `aspire@0.0.1-alpha.1` shipped without it, leaving the plugins' `AspireNSPluginContribution` surface reachable only through a relative path. The 9 plugin import sites are repointed `@netscript/aspire` → `@netscript/aspire/public` (identical target file — symbol-identical).
3. **Atomic single-version bump** of all 31 published members + root to `0.0.1-alpha.2`. `alpha.1` is immutable, the new aspire export requires a new version, and the publish is whole-workspace aligned. The CLI scaffold's emitted version tracks `cli/deno.json` via `jsr-specifiers.ts` automatically; the 5 CLI scaffold-test expectations are bumped to match.

## Validation

- `deno publish --dry-run` (root) — **green: exactly 31 packages @ 0.0.1-alpha.2, 0 tarball escapes**
- `deno task check` — **1729 files, 0 errors**
- Affected aspire-contribution + CLI resolver/scaffold tests — **15 passed, 0 failed**

After this change the relative-escape failure mode is structurally eliminated, so the root dry-run + `deno check` are a faithful pre-flight.

author: sanjacob99
body:
## Summary

Scaffolds a new **Structured Output** peripheral node end-to-end — the next item (#3) on the [2026 modernization roadmap](docs/roadmap/2026-modernization.md). Structured/JSON-schema-constrained output is now table stakes across the agent ecosystem (OpenAI structured outputs, Anthropic tool-schema enforcement, tool-call-as-schema), and the builder had no first-class surface for it.

The node constrains an agent's final response to a JSON Schema, validates it, and applies a configurable failure policy.

## What's included

Follows the established node pattern used by the Telemetry/Guardrails nodes:

- **Node type** `structuredOutput` (`src/types/nodes.ts`) with strict/lenient mode, a provider response-format hint (`json_schema` / `json_object` / `none`), and a failure policy (`repair` / `error` / `passthrough`)
- **Resolution** into a single optional `AgentConfig.structuredOutput` (`ResolvedStructuredOutputConfig`). Unlike telemetry/guardrails (arrays), an agent has one final-response contract, so the first connected *enabled* node wins. The schema text is pre-parsed at resolve time into `schemaJson`.
- **Server engine** `server/runtime/structured-output-engine.ts` — dependency-free (no `ajv`/`zod`):
  - `extractJson` pulls JSON out of free-form / fenced messages
  - `validate` — a JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12 subset) validator: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `enum`, `const`, numeric/string/array bounds, `pattern`
  - `enforceFinalResponse`, `buildRepairInstruction`, `buildSchemaPromptGuidance`, `responseFormatPayload`
- **UI**: node component, property editor with live schema-parse feedback, sidebar palette entry, theme colors
- **Docs**: concept doc + manifest entry, README palette row, roadmap item marked *scaffolded*

## Tests

- 24 new unit tests for the engine (extraction, validation, enforcement, repair/provider helpers)
- Full suite green: **1118 passed / 2 skipped**, `tsc -b` clean

## Remaining integration step (documented)

Wire `enforceFinalResponse` into the finalize step of `server/agents/run-coordinator.ts` (validate the final message, run the repair loop up to `maxRepairAttempts`, attach `responseFormatPayload` to the model request) and fold `buildSchemaPromptGuidance` into the system prompt. Until then this is an extension surface, consistent with how the Telemetry node landed.

author: emapp-urnan
body:
## What & why (red-team HIGH, 3-lens verified)

The signing JWT is the apartment owner's **bearer credential** for the no-auth `/sign/:token` route. pino redacted `req.params.token` but **not `req.url`**, where the full `/api/v1/sign/<jwt>` path lands verbatim on every GET/POST. A pino censor only runs on its configured `paths`, so the `/sign/[REDACTED]` regex **never fired on the URL** — the in-code "token never in logs" guarantee was false. Anyone with log access (Sentry breadcrumbs, log aggregation, ops, a log-store breach) could lift a live 7-day single-use token and **sign as the owner**.

## Fix (root cause, not plaster)

- Add `req.url` (+ `req.query.token`) to `LOG_REDACT_PATHS`.
- Make `logRedactCensor` **path-aware**: on the `url`/`query` leaf it surgically scrubs only the embedded credential (the `/sign/<jwt>` segment + sensitive query *values*) and **keeps the route legible**. A naive "add `req.url` to paths" would blanket-redact every URL to `[REDACTED]` — trading the leak for an **observability regression** (ops blind to which endpoint was hit). Every other redacted leaf (credential/PII) is still fully `[REDACTED]`.
- **Back-compatible:** a no-path call keeps the original behavior → existing tests unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest log-redact.spec.ts` → **23/23 green** (11 original + 12 new), `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Regression test encodes the exact leak: full `/api/v1/sign/<jwt>` on the `req.url` leaf → `/api/v1/sign/[REDACTED]` (token absent).
- Observability guard test: `/api/v1/projects?limit=25&status=…` on `req.url` is **preserved**, not redacted.

Found by the standing email/link/cross-entity red-team loop. First of a triaged backlog of 41 confirmed-real defects (21 HIGH / 20 MED); this is the headline token-security one.

author: agners
body:
## Proposed change

Run the `mypy` pre-commit hook the same way CI does, with `mypy supervisor`.

mypy is a whole-program checker, but the hook was configured to check only the changed files (the default `pass_filenames` behavior) and added `--ignore-missing-imports`. Neither matches the CI command (`mypy supervisor`), which leads to two problems:

- **Different results than CI.** Checking only the changed files instead of the whole package can both miss and invent errors compared to a full run, so the hook and CI can disagree. See [python/mypy#13916](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/13916) for the whole-program-vs-per-file rationale.
- **Intermittent `INTERNAL ERROR` crashes.** When several `supervisor/` files change, pre-commit splits the file list and runs the hook concurrently. Since mypy 2.0 the SQLite cache is enabled by default, and the parallel mypy processes race on the shared `.mypy_cache/cache.db`: SQLite reports `database is locked` ([python/mypy#21525](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/21525)), and an interrupted write can leave the database `malformed`. This is the failure mode that the cache-cleanup runbook in #6971 works around; this PR addresses the root cause instead.

The fix aligns the hook with CI:

- `pass_filenames: false` and an explicit `supervisor` target so the hook always checks the whole package in a single invocation.
- `require_serial: true` as a safeguard against pre-commit ever running the hook concurrently.
- Drop `--ignore-missing-imports`, which CI does not use and which is redundant anyway: `[tool.mypy]` already disables the `import-not-found` and `import-untyped` error codes.

author: larry-yatch
body:
## Summary
Two new fail-safe reconciliation steps in `check_forge_built_no_pr` (`scripts/heal_pipeline_stall.py`) eliminate two confirmed false-positive classes that drove G-rule `forge-built-no-pr-retry1-fp-001` to its 3/3 alert threshold.

- **Pattern A — `_forge_retry_pr_exists` (step 1e):** a `-retry<N>` redispatch opened the PR. Suppresses when a PR in the open+merged union has a retry-branch task_id matching `^<task>-retry\d+$`, OR an archived `<task>-retry*.json` outbox shows a PR via `_outbox_shows_pr` (aged-out case). Production driver: `reconcile-hardening-mission-shipped-001` (its `-001-retry1` opened OPEN PR #699).
- **Pattern B — `_forge_rebase_target_shipped` (step 1f):** a `rebase-`-class task operates on an existing PR by design and opens none. Tightly scoped to `task_id.startswith('rebase-')`. Suppresses when the archived `result` names `#<N>` and PR #<N> is present in the open+merged union. Production driver: `rebase-forge-post-open-mergeable-687-001` (rebased PR #687, now merged with branch deleted, so branch/title match both failed).

Both helpers are fail-safe to `None` on any miss/ambiguity/exception, so they can only REMOVE false stalls, never mask a real one. Each call-site branch logs a distinct `FORGE_NO_PR_SKIP` reason (`retry_pr_exists`, `rebase_target_shipped`). Reuses existing conventions (`_task_id_from_branch`, `_load_forge_outbox`, `_outbox_shows_pr`, `all_prs`); no existing reconciliation step, alert-translations.json, or G-rule registry touched.

## Test plan
- [x] A1: `-retry1` OPEN PR in `all_prs` suppresses the original task's stall
- [x] retry MERGED PR also suppresses (gh-truth union)
- [x] A2: aged-out retry-sibling outbox (PR absent from `all_prs`) suppresses via archive anchor
- [x] B1: `rebase-` task whose result names a PR present in the union is suppressed
- [x] Negative A: task with no retry PR anywhere still fires
- [x] Negative A: retry outbox without PR proof (PROCEED-only) does not suppress
- [x] Negative B: `rebase-` task whose referenced PR is absent from the union still fires
- [x] Scope guard: non-`rebase-` task naming a present PR is not a rebase candidate

## Summary

Fixes #172.

This removes the repeated docs search data from every static page payload. The static payload generator now writes locale-level search indexes under `/__static/docs-search/{locale}.json`, and the docs shell lazy-loads that index when search opens.

## Root cause

Each generated page payload embedded the same `pages` search list. With the full docs set this repeated about the same search data across every static page payload, inflating `public/__static/docs` and `dist/client/__static/docs` by hundreds of MB. The app build still spends most time in TanStack/Fumadocs transforms, but the static output duplication was safe to remove without skipping any pages, routes, OpenAPI sync, or validation.

The payload generator also disables `publicDir` for its temporary Vite bundles so it does not copy the already-generated public payload tree into `node_modules/.tmp/docs-static-payload`.

## Before / after

Baseline from this branch before the change:

- `openapi:sync`: 0.057s
- `docs:static-payload`: 64.319s
- `build:app:static`: 119.556s
- `public/__static/docs`: 1761 files, 451M
- `dist/client`: 996M
- `dist/client/__static/docs`: 515M

After the change:

- `docs:static-payload`: 58.723s in the earlier isolated timing run
- full `npm run build`: real 176.17s in the final logged run
- `public/__static/docs`: 48M
- `public/__static/docs-search`: 496K
- `dist/client`: 532M
- `dist/client/__static/docs`: 50M
- `dist/client/__static/docs-search`: 576K

Static output audit after build:

- page payload JSON files: 1761
- payloads with embedded `pages`: 0
- search index files: `en.json`, `zh-CN.json`
- search index includes normal docs pages and generated OpenAPI endpoint pages
- dist output has the same payload/search-index shape

Minimal PoC to validate the DigiSign Identify provider flow end-to-end before designing the production integration.

## Flow
- `POST /api/identifications` → create identification with configured scenario ID
- `POST /api/identifications/{id}/start` → obtain verification URL
- Top-level browser redirect to verification URL (not iframe)
- DigiSign redirects back to `/Callback` → displays returned query params

- **`Pages/Callback`** – logs and renders all callback query parameters

- **`README.md`** – setup steps including `dotnet user-secrets` for secrets

## Configuration
Secrets kept out of source via .NET User Secrets:
```bash
dotnet user-secrets set "DigiSign:BearerToken" "<token>"
dotnet user-secrets set "DigiSign:ScenarioId" "<id>"
```

author: theweihu
body:
## What

Adds a **Skills** section to the dashboard Profile tab that shows which slash-command skills (`/continue`, `/distill`, `/ship`, …) get invoked and how that mix changes over time.

## Why

Skill invocations were already captured in the prompt log but never surfaced. The Profile tab is the natural home — it already has the Typed/Bot/All toggle and a date-window picker.

## How it's shown

Two linked charts, between the Parallelism and Cost sections:

1. **Skills Called · Over Time** — full-width stacked bar chart. Auto bins (daily → weekly → 4-week → quarterly by window span), colored by the top-8 skills + "other", capped bar width so sparse windows don't read as slabs, per-column hover breakdown, and a clickable legend.
2. **Most-Called Skills** — lollipop ranking by total count, scrollable, click-through to the source prompts.

Rank→color is shared across both charts, so a skill reads the same in each.

## Design note

Detection keys off the prompt **text** (first token is `/skill`), not the classified `kind` — so an autonomous `/continue` (classified `nightshift`) still counts. The existing Typed/Bot/All toggle then gives a meaningful split:

- **Typed** → skills you ran at the keyboard (diverse mix)
- **Bot** → the autonomous nightshift loop (mostly `/continue`)
- **All** → both

Without this, `/continue` (1623 of 1658 calls in the live data) would swamp the chart.

## Verification

- Rendered live against real `~/devbrain-data`; confirmed Typed vs Bot split, legend + lollipop click-throughs, daily-bin layout.
- Inline JS parses clean; existing dashboard dogfood suite passes 21/0.

author: oussamalakhdar90
body:
The **one cheap LLM step** of the feature index (design #17, §3.2): it canonicalises the deterministic `FeatureSeeder` seed by **merging** buckets that describe the same capability — semantic synonyms the stemmer can't (login/authentication) and the same feature seen from different sources. **This is the step that finally clusters the `ciam-policies` "Get policy" issue + the `GET /policies` endpoint into one `IMPLEMENTED` feature** (when a real Copilot is connected). Builds on the merged Phase 3a seed. Purely additive — not wired into `TestStrategyService` yet.

## What's here
- **`FeatureTagger`** (`@Component`) — sends only `{ref, name, sample titles}` per seed bucket (**never full unit text**), one **ECONOMY**-tier call, following the established `generateSection` pattern (`PromptComposer.compose` + `LlmGateway.complete` + `JsonBlockExtractor` + `ResponseSchemaValidator` + `ModelSelector` + `CostRecorder`). It **only merges** (the seed is conservative); never splits.
- **Graceful degradation** — returns the deterministic seed unchanged when the LLM is unavailable, there's ≤1 feature, or the reply is unusable (malformed / schema-invalid). The pipeline never breaks for want of the LLM.
- **Safety** — `apply()` can only merge *existing* seeds: it consumes ref ids from the seed, dedupes a ref across groups (each unit lands in exactly one feature), re-adds unmerged seeds verbatim, recomputes the content-derived `featureId` + status, and surfaces any unassigned units. So even a compromised reply can't fabricate, drop, or split a unit. Seed titles are **fenced as untrusted** before composition.
- `feature-tagger.prompt.md` + `feature-tagger.schema.json`; `MockLlmGateway` gains a `[FEATURE-TAGGER]` case (returns no merge groups — the mock can't cluster, so the deterministic seed stands).

## Review-hardened
Adversarial review (2 lenses → verify → **GO, no blockers**). The reviewer independently confirmed the merge-only safety argument and the untrusted-title fencing. Applied its two cheap nits: filter merged ids to those present (so `unitIds` and the status basis can't diverge), and a **single-echo `featureId`-stability test** (pins the hash the override carry-forward will depend on).

## Verification
`mvn test` **365 green** — `FeatureTaggerTest` covers the cross-source merge, every degradation path, dedup-across-groups, single-echo identity, and schema-file validity.

## Next
**Phase 3c:** `GapDetector` (§3.3) + lineage-level `FeatureIndex` persistence (where a non-empty `unassignedUnitIds` becomes a fail-loud preview banner, and chunk-and-merge tagging is added for scale).

## Problem

The Solr heap in `docker/docker-compose-rest.yml` is hardcoded to `-m 4g`. With
`-XX:+AlwaysPreTouch` the container commits the full 4 GB on start — wasteful on shared dev
hosts running several DSpace stacks, and not lowerable without editing a tracked file.

Backport of dataquest-dev/dspace-angular#1309 to `customer/TUL`.
Tracking issue: dataquest-dev/dspace-customers#746

## Change set

Single-line change to the `dspacesolr` entrypoint in `docker/docker-compose-rest.yml`:

```diff
-      exec solr -p 8983 -f -m 4g
+      exec solr -p 8983 -f -m "${SOLR_HEAP:-4g}"
```

**Translated, not cherry-picked** (per the FE backport model). On this branch (7.5 family) the Solr launch uses `-p 8983`,
so only the `-m 4g` argument changed; the port and every other line are untouched. The value
is quoted to survive word-splitting, matching the source PR follow-up.

Out of scope: the default heap value (stays `4g`), other services, ports, Solr image/version,
and `AlwaysPreTouch`.

## Test evidence

- Post-change marker present (line 137): `-m "${SOLR_HEAP:-4g}"`

author: caioalexanderx
body:
## Contexto
Dois fixes na shell premium da federação de karatê (`components/karate/KarateShell.tsx`, redesign #315): ícones virando retângulo vazio + logos Aura Karatê / FPKT no header.

## Item 3 (prioridade) — Ícones viravam retângulo (tofu)
**Causa-raiz:** a shell (e o kit Shoji) renderizava ícones via `@expo/vector-icons` `Ionicons`. **`@expo/vector-icons` não é dependência deste app** — o app inteiro usa um motor de ícones próprio em SVG-inline (`components/Icon.tsx`). Como a fonte de glifos do Ionicons nunca é carregada na web (não há `Font.loadAsync(Ionicons.font)` em lugar nenhum — `useShojiFonts` só injeta as fontes de texto do Google Fonts), todo `<Ionicons>` renderizava o caractere de fallback da fonte → **caixa/retângulo vazio**. Não era ordem de render nem nome inválido; era a fonte de ícones que jamais existiu no bundle web.

**Fix:** a shell passa a renderizar ícones via `<Icon>` (`components/Icon.tsx`), o mesmo componente usado em todo o resto do app — SVG inline, sem fonte, sem gate de carregamento, glyph sempre presente.

- `components/Icon.tsx` (aditivo): adicionados os glifos que faltavam para a nav mapear semanticamente — `bell` (sino), `activity` (pulse → Saúde da Rede), `building` (Dojôs), `network` (Conexões), `ribbon` (Certificados), `trophy` (Competições) — mais aliases das variantes `-outline` (ex.: `notifications-outline`→`bell`, `git-network-outline`→`network`) por robustez. Nenhum glifo existente foi alterado.
- `KarateShell.tsx`: `import { Icon }` no lugar de `Ionicons`; `NAV_ITEMS.icon` e topbar/chip/bottom-tabs usam chaves válidas do `Icon`.

## Itens 1 e 2 — Logos no header
A topbar oxblood agora abre com **dois quadrantes**, antes do breadcrumb:
1. **Aura Karatê** — selo 空 (vermelho) + wordmark "Aura Karatê" (ê em destaque), claros sobre o oxblood.
2. **FPKT** — `FpktLogo` (bitmap oficial da federação, `assets/karate/logo-fpkt.png`) num chip claro + nome da federação.

Breadcrumb, busca global (`→ /karate/praticantes?q=`) e sino preservados, reposicionados após os logos com um filete separador claro. **Mobile/bottom-tabs e chip de usuário intactos** (#315 não regredido).

### ⚠️ Logo que falta (para o Caio)
**Não existe asset de imagem dedicado da "Aura Karatê".** Os únicos logos de marca no repo são: `assets/karate/logo-fpkt.png` (FPKT, da federação) e `components/studio/AuraStudioMark.tsx` (específico do Studio). A marca "Aura Karatê" usada aqui é a composição **selo 空 + wordmark** já estabelecida na sidebar (não inventei asset). Se quiser um logo/lockup próprio da Aura Karatê no 1º quadrante, é só fornecer o arquivo (PNG/SVG) que eu troco a marca composta por ele.

## Verificação
- Ícones renderizam como SVG (sem dependência de fonte, nomes válidos no `Icon`).
- Logos Aura Karatê (1º) + FPKT (2º) no header; breadcrumb/busca/sino preservados.
- Chip de usuário, sidebar refinada, navegação e mobile/bottom-tabs intactos.
- Entradas top-level de `StyleSheet.create` são objetos (sem string solta → sem crash weakmap RN-web).
- Sem dependência nova; mudança no `Icon.tsx` puramente aditiva.

## 改动
解决两个手机端体验问题（安卓 Chrome）：

### 软键盘挤压布局（对齐 iOS）
安卓 Chrome 默认在软键盘弹出时压缩布局视口，把整个界面挤一下；iOS 是悬浮覆盖。
- `index.html`：viewport 加 `interactive-widget=overlays-content`（与已有 `maximum-scale=1` 合并）。
- `main.tsx`：启用 `navigator.virtualKeyboard.overlaysContent = true`，暴露 `env(keyboard-inset-height)`。

### PWA 可安装性
- `manifest.webmanifest` 补 `192x192` 图标（Chrome 期望 192+512，之前仅 512）+ 新增 `logo-mark-192.png`。

<details><summary>Why this changed (source: PR #2941)</summary>

When select_protocol returns SyncProtocol::None (entity roots agree, no entity walk needed) and the peer advertises a non-None scope_root, the sync manager now computes a scope_verdict. If the verdict is GovDiverged (local and peer scope_roots differ despite identical entity roots), it pulls the namespace governance DAG from that peer and returns early, bypassing the entity walk entirely. This fills the gap where a governance rotation or ACL change — invisible to the entity Merkle — would otherwise persist uncorrected across every sync tick because the post-sync P6.S2 hook only fires after HC/LevelWise actually runs.

The return type of query_peer_dag_state was extended from Option<(Hash, Vec<[u8; DIGEST_SIZE]>)> to Option<(Hash, Vec<[u8; DIGEST_SIZE]>, Option<Hash>)>. The scope_root field from DagHeadsResponse, previously matched as scope_root: _ (discarded), is now captured and threaded back to all callers.

The pre-sync governance divergence check gates the datastore read on peer_scope_root being Some. When a peer sends scope_root: None (cold projection or non-group context) the store is never touched and scope_verdict is never computed, keeping the common already-in-sync path free of I/O.

The namespace-resolution + sync_namespace_from_peer logic previously existed only inside the ProtocolDispatch trait impl. It is now an inherent async method on SyncManager so both the pre-sync (P6.S3) path and the post-sync (P6.S2) trait forwarder can call it. The trait impl now contains a one-line delegation: SyncManager::pull_namespace_governance(self, …).await.

After successfully issuing a pre-sync governance pull the manager emits a debug-level log with marker = "gov_divergence_pull_complete". This pairs with the existing gov_divergence_pull_triggered info log so operators and e2e report steps can correlate the trigger event with its completion rather than seeing an Ok(None) indistinguishable from 'already in sync'.

</details>

author: gabbopalma
body:
## Summary

Adds a full documentation website with live, interactive examples, wires up CI to build and deploy it to GitHub Pages, and slims the README down to a landing page that links out to it.

## What's included

### Documentation website
- New MkDocs (Material) site under `website/` covering getting started, camera, annotations, layers, expressions, offline regions, PMTiles, migration, the feature matrix and architecture.
- Each page embeds a **live, interactive example** from the Flutter web demo via same-origin iframes, plus a set of `doc_*` example screens in `maplibre_gl_example`.

### CI / deploy
- New reusable `_build.yml` and an extended `flutter_ci.yml` that build the web demo and the MkDocs site, assemble a single Pages bundle, and deploy on `main`.
- Deploys serialize (no cancel-in-progress on `main`) so a publish is never torn down mid-flight.

### Site layout
- The **documentation homepage is served at the site root** and the **Flutter web demo lives under `/demo/`**.
- Web demo built with a matching `--base-href /flutter-maplibre-gl/demo/`; `mkdocs site_url` points at the root; every example iframe and the homepage demo CTA point at `/demo/`.

### Example / iframe fixes
- Load example iframes via a same-origin relative URL so they work over HTTPS.
- Repair broken marker and cluster live examples; drop `const` on a `GeojsonSourceProperties` built from runtime data.
- Note that the upstream PMTiles demo archive can be intermittently down.

### README
- Trimmed to a slim landing page: hero, quick start, feature matrix, contributing, and a contributors avatar grid, now that the docs site covers everything in depth.
- Highlights the **live demo** and **documentation** as prominent CTAs and fixes the API reference link to point at the API view rather than the rendered README.

## Resulting URLs
- `maplibre.github.io/flutter-maplibre-gl/` -> docs homepage
- `maplibre.github.io/flutter-maplibre-gl/demo/` -> live Flutter demo
- `maplibre.github.io/flutter-maplibre-gl/getting-started/`, `.../migration/`, etc. -> doc pages

## Notes
- The docs site has never been deployed to `main`, so the new layout ships directly with no old public URLs to redirect.

author: lucabello
body:
The grafana_dashboard library was generating a new UUID every time `_upset_dashboards_on_relation()` was called, even when the dashboard templates hadn't changed. This caused continuous databag updates and unnecessary relation-changed events on the consumer side.

The fix compares the new templates with the existing templates in the relation databag before updating. If they're identical, no update is made and the UUID remains stable.

This change affects both `GrafanaDashboardProvider` and `GrafanaDashboardAggregator` classes.

Fixes: canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator#331

author: andresabinoxp-ops
body:
## Why this revert

PR #51 caused a catastrophic regression on Chon Buri. User-reported numbers after PR #51 was merged:

| | Before PR #51 (i.e. with just PR #50 merged) | After PR #51 |
|---|---|---|
| Proposed coverage | 364 stores | **204 stores** ← 160 stores dropped |
| Rep 1 utilisation | 95% (overloaded) | 46% (under) |
| Rep 2 utilisation | 65% | 61% |
| Rep 3 utilisation | 15% | 40% |
| Rep 4 utilisation | 60% | 52% |
| Fleet utilisation | 70% | 50% |

PR #51 was supposed to fix the daily overload by relaxing the candidate filter. Instead it caused mass drops. Reverting now to restore the pre-#51 behaviour while we design a proper fix.

## Root cause of PR #51

PR #51 made `_is_removable()` return True for any non-protected gap store when aggressive mode is on. The expanded candidate pool let Pass 1 mark ~60 stores per rep as removable (Pass 1 keeps removing until each day fits ≤ 528 min). But:

- **Pass 2** (move to another day of the same rep) couldn't find destinations because all 5 weekdays of Rep 1 were at/near cap after Pass 1.
- **Pass 3** (hand to neighbour rep) couldn't either — Reps 2/3/4 also cover Pattaya and were similarly overloaded.
- **Pass 4** dropped the stores with `exclusion_reason`.

Net effect: 160 stores that were previously routed (even if over-capacity) became uncovered.

## What this revert restores

- `_is_removable()` goes back to the strict pre-#51 filter ("far from rep centroid AND in bottom 30% of rep scores")
- PR #50's count-cap lift (`MAX_REMOVALS_PER_DAY: 2 → 100` when box ticked) **stays in place** — it does nothing on its own with the strict filter back, but the checkbox UI is left intact
- Chon Buri returns to the pre-PR-51 state: 364 proposed coverage, Rep 1 at 95% with overloaded Monday/Tuesday

## What's still broken (back to where we started)

Chon Buri's Rep 1 Monday/Tuesday will go back to 1,107–1,363 min. This is the original problem we were trying to fix. We did not solve it. We just stopped making it worse.

## What I'm going to think about before the next attempt

A proper aggressive-rebalance must SWAP stores between days WITHOUT dropping any. The next attempt should:
- Identify pairs of (over-day, under-day) for the same rep
- Find stores that could be swapped (preserves total per rep)
- Apply the geographic check on BOTH sides of the swap
- Never produce an `_overflow` list that goes through Pass 4

I want to design + run before/after comparisons on Recife / Malaysia / Oman input files BEFORE proposing the next PR.

## Test plan for this revert

- [ ] Re-run Chon Buri pipeline → numbers should match pre-PR-51 state (364 proposed, Rep 1 ~95%, Monday over 1,300 min)
- [ ] Re-run Recife / Malaysia / Oman → numbers should match pre-PR-50 state (PR #50's flag default-OFF means no change)

author: vitkyrka
body:
### What does this PR do?

Make Autodiscovery change the config source in the final instance configuration when the configruation comes from configuration discovery. The `config.provider` field in inventory metadata is derived from the prefix of `Config.Source` (split on `:`). Until now it was always `file` or `container`, making it impossible to tell whether configuration discovery was involved. This will be useful to track adoption of configuration discovery.

`Config.Provider` is intentionally left unchanged — it's used by the secret resolver security mechanism.

### Motivation

https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/DSCVR-573
https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DSCVR/pages/6895337633/

### Describe how you validated your changes

CI.

### Additional Notes

**Required follow-up (backend):** the EPRW decoder (`agentmetadata_decoder.go`) has a check `provider == file` that creates the `datadog_agent_integrations_configurations` resource. It needs to be updated to also handle the new provider strings.

author: olivmertens
body:
## What

The PDF uploader showed Streamlit's default `Limit 200MB per file`, which is misleading: it is **not processable**.

Both Mistral Document AI models on Azure AI Foundry hard-cap each request at **30 MB / 30 pages**:
- `mistral-ocr-4-0` (Preview)
- `mistral-document-ai-2512`

The app already rejected >30 MB in `_validate_upload` and chunks at 30 pages — but only **after** the file was uploaded over localhost. A user could transfer up to 200 MB only to be rejected.

## Change

author: kaosensei
body:
## Summary

`get_training_status` crashes with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` whenever any nested sub-section of the API response is explicitly `null`. Replaces `dict.get(key, {})` with `dict.get(key) or {}` on every vulnerable chain.

Closes #172.

## Root cause

The Garmin API returns explicit `null` (not missing keys) for sub-sections the user has no data in:

| User profile | Field that's null |
|---|---|
| Pure runner (no cycling activities) | `mostRecentVO2Max.cycling` |
| Pure cyclist (#172) | `mostRecentVO2Max.generic` |
| New user / sparse history | `mostRecentTrainingStatus`, `mostRecentTrainingLoadBalance` |
| Inactive day | `acuteTrainingLoadDTO` |

`dict.get(key, default)` only returns `default` when the key is **missing** — when the value is explicitly `None`, it returns `None`, and the next `.get()` in the chain raises `AttributeError`.

## Reproducer (runner case)

Confirmed against my own Forerunner 970 data dump:

```python
status = garmin_client.get_training_status("2026-06-23")
# status["mostRecentVO2Max"]["cycling"] is None (I never cycle)

cycling_vo2_data = status.get("mostRecentVO2Max", {}).get("cycling", {})
# cycling_vo2_data is None, not {}
cycling_vo2_data.get("vo2MaxValue")
# 💥 AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
```

This is the same root cause as #172, just a different `null` field — `or {}` coalesces both missing-key and explicit-null cases, so the patch covers every sub-section in one go.

## Fix

Two-character change applied consistently: `.get(key, {})` → `.get(key) or {}` on every chain that touches an API field with a possible explicit null. Also added an inline comment explaining the `or {}` idiom for future contributors who would otherwise default to `.get(key, {})`.

## Verification

Before patch (date with a real run, `cycling=null`):
```
Error retrieving training status data: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
```

After patch (same date, same data):
```json
{
  "training_status": 7,
  "training_status_feedback": "PRODUCTIVE_2",
  "acute_load": 318,
  "chronic_load": 219,
  "load_ratio": 1.4,
  "acwr_status": "OPTIMAL",
  "vo2_max": 52.0,
  "vo2_max_precise": 52.2,
  "monthly_load_aerobic_low": 494.2,
  "monthly_load_aerobic_high": 212.4,
  "monthly_load_anaerobic": 0.0,
  "training_balance_feedback": "AEROBIC_HIGH_SHORTAGE"
}
```

End-to-end tested by loading the patched module via `register_tools` and calling the actual tool function — not just the inner extraction logic.

## Out of scope (separate issues to follow)

While auditing I noticed two other functions reading the same nested structure that have related but distinct bugs (both wrapped in `try/except: pass` so they silently lose data rather than crash):

- `get_training_load_trend` (line 738): assigns `status_data` to the device-id map without iterating, so `status_data.get("acuteTrainingLoadDTO")` always misses. Needs device iteration + `or {}` coalescing.
- `get_vo2max_trend` (line 893): same `mostRecentVO2Max.generic` chain — works for users with running VO2max but would silently drop days for cycling-only users (#172's profile).

Happy to send follow-up PRs for those if the maintainers prefer focused PRs, or fold them in here.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduce crash on real data (runner, `cycling=null`)
- [x] Patch produces complete curated payload
- [x] End-to-end via `register_tools` (not just unit-level)
- [ ] Reproduce #172's profile (cyclist with `generic=null`) — don't have access to that account, but the fix targets both null fields symmetrically

author: aaronbassett
body:
## Summary

Fixes `rover fetch` failing on bot-protected sites (e.g. `https://midnight.network/nightforce`) with the misleading output:

```
WARN chromiumoxide::browser: Browser was not closed manually...
ERROR chromiumoxide::handler: WS Connection error: Ws(Protocol(ResetWithoutClosingHandshake))
rover: fetching URL
```

**Root cause:** the chromiumoxide lines were a red herring — the browser was never broken. The target is behind a **Vercel bot-challenge** (`x-vercel-mitigated: challenge`) that returns **HTTP 429** to any plain HTTP client. Rover's reqwest fetch retried 4× and failed, but the real cause was hidden behind `eprintln!("rover: {e}")` (no `{e:#}`), and the eagerly-launched-then-dropped headless renderer emitted scary teardown noise on the way out.

## What changed

- **Surface the real error** — print the full `anyhow` chain (`{e:#}`); silence chromiumoxide's internal logs by default (`chromiumoxide=off`, overridable via `RUST_LOG`).
- **Detect bot-challenges** — recognise Vercel/Cloudflare challenge markers, surface a typed `FetcherError::BotChallenge` (fatal, no wasted retries) with a clear, actionable message; dedicated `bot_challenge` MCP error code.
- **Lazy headless renderer** — a `HeadlessHandle` that launches Chromium only when a render actually happens (SPA detected or challenge bypass), instead of on every Auto-mode fetch. Static pages launch nothing.
- **Clean shutdown** — close the browser before aborting the handler task (the CDP close handshake needs the handler pumping), and tear down on every CLI exit path. No more teardown warnings — even on failed fetches.
- **Bot-challenge bypass** — in Auto mode, route a challenge through the headless renderer (new headless mode), which executes the JS challenge like a real browser and reaches the page.
- **Configurable pre-render delay** — new `[headless] launch_delay_secs` (default `2`, `0` disables): a pause between detecting that a render is needed and launching the browser, giving the origin a breather between the lightweight fetch and the heavier browser hit. Auto mode only.

## Verification

- `https://midnight.network/nightforce` now returns the real page (`title: "Midnight | Nightforce Program"`, `extraction_quality: 1.00`) with clean stderr.
- A static page (`example.com`) launches no browser and produces no noise.
- The no-headless build reports a clear "enable headless rendering" message on a challenge.
- 733 tests pass (incl. new challenge-detection, no-retry, and config tests); all real-Chrome headless integration tests pass; `cargo fmt` + `clippy` clean. Each commit builds standalone.

## Notes

- The delay is scoped to **Auto mode** (whole seconds, matching the sibling `timeout_secs`); `On` mode has no detection step and is unaffected.
- Pre-existing, out of scope: `block_service_workers` is documented as honoured via `set_bypass_service_worker` but that call doesn't exist anywhere — currently a no-op.

body:
## Problem

The Solr heap in `docker/docker-compose-rest.yml` is hardcoded to `-m 4g`. With
`-XX:+AlwaysPreTouch` the container commits the full 4 GB on start — wasteful on shared dev
hosts running several DSpace stacks, and not lowerable without editing a tracked file.

Backport of dataquest-dev/dspace-angular#1309 to `customer/sav`.
Tracking issue: dataquest-dev/dspace-customers#746

## Change set

Single-line change to the `dspacesolr` entrypoint in `docker/docker-compose-rest.yml`:

```diff
-      exec solr -f -m 4g
+      exec solr -f -m "${SOLR_HEAP:-4g}"
```

**Translated, not cherry-picked** (per the FE backport model). On this branch (7.6.1 family) the Solr launch has no `-p` flag (default port),
so only the `-m 4g` argument changed; the port and every other line are untouched. The value
is quoted to survive word-splitting, matching the source PR follow-up.

Out of scope: the default heap value (stays `4g`), other services, ports, Solr image/version,
and `AlwaysPreTouch`.

## Test evidence

- Post-change marker present (line 175): `-m "${SOLR_HEAP:-4g}"`
- Pre-change marker `-m 4g` no longer present (grep count 0)
- Compose YAML re-parses cleanly (`yaml.safe_load`); edit sits inside the entrypoint scalar
- Default/override: `SOLR_HEAP` unset -> 4g, `SOLR_HEAP=1g` -> 1g

author: jan-auer
body:
Adds gated heap profiling to production builds using jemalloc's built-in sampling. Profiling is compiled in via a new `profiling` Cargo feature (enabled in release/CI builds, off for debug) and dormant at startup. It can be activated on demand via HTTP endpoints, which dump a symbolized gzipped pprof profile.

- Outputs symbolized `pprof`, so profiles are self-contained and analyzable with `go tool pprof` without shipping the binary separately.
- Endpoints are loopback-only (peer IP check), reachable via `kubectl port-forward` or an ephemeral debug container. Normal service/ingress traffic never presents a loopback peer, so no separate listener or auth are needed.
- Profile sampling rate is set to 512 KiB mean interval which has negligible steady-state overhead without the feature being active.
- By default, sampling never runs unless explicitly enabled via the endpoint.

The CPU overhead with profiling enabled on typical workloads is about 5%. There is no measurable overhead while profiling is disabled.

Ref FS-318
