author: shrey-arc
body:
Here's your current state summary and a concrete implementation roadmap scoped to your specialization.

Where You Stand

Research phase: complete. Nine documents, a journal paper, and a validated analytical foundation. The maturity breakdown matters for planning:

Layer | Status | Represents -- | -- | -- W^1.5 physics, FOC acoustics, CFRP FEA, power isolation, AI nav benchmarks | Validated | Your evidence base; cite these in implementation decisions Fleet endurance scheduling, energy-aware SOC throttling, comms range via relays | Modeled, not demonstrated | Your Phase 1 target — turn models into measurements Carrier drone, laminar fuselage, structural batteries, GPS-denied cooperative localization | Conceptual only | Phase 2/3; do not let these distract Phase 1

The shared artifact is the ROS2 workspace. Set it up on a common Git repository (GitHub) in Week 1. Everyone pulls from this. Message schema changes go through you to maintain interface contracts.

4-Week Execution Plan

Week 1:

  • SITL live with PX4 + Gazebo
  • Git repo initialized with workspace structure
  • fleet_interfaces package: DroneState.msg, FleetStatus.msg, AssignMission.srv defined
  • Person 2 begins ESC bench characterization

Week 2:

  • px4_bridge node: MAVLink telemetry → ROS2 topics
  • Single simulated drone flying a waypoint mission under ROS2 control
  • Person 3: Pixhawk 6C flashed, QGC connected to SITL

Week 3:

  • energy_monitor node: SOC estimation running in simulation
  • SOC-triggered AI throttle behavior prototyped (threshold logic, not yet real inference)
  • fleet_scheduler skeleton: one drone → RTH at 40% SOC, simulated replacement triggered

Week 4:

  • Two-drone simulation running simultaneously with scheduler managing rotation
  • Basic GCS dashboard showing per-drone SOC and dock status
  • Review with Person 2: bench power data against your SITL power model

What to Defer

These are in your domain but should not touch Phase 1 execution:

  • Cooperative localization / GPS-denied navigation — requires validated carrier drone architecture first
  • Federated EKF implementation — the algorithm is novel but adds no Phase 1 value
  • Carrier drone fleet logistics software — can't test what doesn't physically exist
  • Large-scale mesh testing beyond 5 nodes — Phase 2 problem

The carrier drone void is the biggest architectural risk. Your contribution to closing it: define a software proxy. Use a ground-based power supply station with a simulated 5 kg UAV in SITL as a stand-in carrier, so your fleet rotation logic can be validated before the physical carrier is built. This unlocks the 7+ hour coverage claim for simulation validation even in Phase 1.

Summary State in One Paragraph

The research corpus is complete and sound. Your primary validated contributions (W^1.5 physics, FOC-vibration-IMU chain, power isolation) are defensible. The fleet endurance model is architecturally correct but depends on a carrier drone with zero engineering specification — proxying that in simulation is your critical path contribution. As the CS lead, you are unblocked from day one: SITL setup → ROS2 architecture → fleet scheduler → GCS layer → AI pipeline, in that order. The four-person team runs in parallel once the Git workspace and interface definitions are live. Nothing in your Phase 1 scope requires hardware to begin.

author: obostjancic
body:
When a conversation message had multiple text parts that all lacked usable text (e.g. `parts: [{type: 'text'}, {type: 'text'}]`), each empty part independently pushed `EMPTY_TEXT_CONTENT` into the text buffer. Joining them produced `(no value)\n(no value)` instead of a single marker — which also broke the `=== EMPTY_TEXT_CONTENT` identity check in `turnsToMessages` that gates deduplication.

Three paths in `aiMessageNormalizer.ts` shared the same root cause:
- `bucketParts` pushed `EMPTY_TEXT_CONTENT` once per empty text part
- `extractTextFromContentParts` joined them all verbatim
- `appendOutputFromParts` did the same for assistant output in parts format

`bucketParts` now only appends real text; `collapseParts` and `extractTextFromContentParts` fall back to exactly one `EMPTY_TEXT_CONTENT` when no real text was collected but renderable text parts were present. `appendOutputFromParts` tracks whether any empty text part was seen and appends at most one placeholder after the loop, only if no real text was added for that message's parts.

Closes TET-2560

Syncs the CLI to the latest upstream OpenAPI spec. **Purely additive** — adds one new read-only command and supporting schemas; nothing removed, narrowed, or newly required.

## What changed

Adds `syllable sessions timeline <session-id>` for the new endpoint `GET /api/v1/sessions/timeline/{session_id}`. It returns a single consolidated, time-ordered stream of a session's transcript turns, tool calls, and latency events, each with an offset from session start. Mirrors the existing `transcript` command (read-only GET, JSON or table output).

A live integration test (`TestSessionsTimeline`) lists one session — with `--include-test` so a throwaway CI org still has a session to exercise — fetches its timeline, and asserts valid JSON. It skips cleanly when the org has no sessions.

## diff_specs.py report

```
## NEW PATHS (1)
+ /api/v1/sessions/timeline/{session_id}
  GET — Get Session Timeline By Id ['sessions.timeline']

## NEW SCHEMAS (3)
+ SessionTimelineResponse
+ TimelineEvent
+ TimelineEventKind

## CHANGED SCHEMAS — field-level diffs (1)
~ SessionAction
  + duration_ms: anyOf   (new optional response field; no flag/body change)

## CHANGED ENUMS — member diffs (1)

  Paths:   +1 added, -0 removed, ~0 changed
```

author: sferadev
body:
## Problem

Operators kept seeing "No printer selected" print jobs and the printer selection "got stuck." In the kiosk print settings, the printer dropdown only populated when the operator manually clicked **Test connection**, and the choice was only persisted via the page-level **Save changes** button. So the common path left `event.printPrinterId` empty and jobs were dispatched with no printer.

## What changed

**`components/event-settings/print-settings-section.tsx`**
- **Auto-poll** `listBridgePrinters` (every 5s) while print method is `bridge`, so the dropdown is populated without any manual action and keeps up if the bridge comes online or a printer is plugged in later. The poll **never throws** (the bridge client resolves to a typed failure), so the loading state always clears.
- **No stuck spinner:** instead of a perpetual loader, the picker shows *"Looking for printers…"* (only while genuinely loading with nothing yet), then either the list, *"No printers found / bridge offline"*, or the bridge error.
- **Sticky save:** a new optional `onPersistPrinter` prop persists the pick straight to `event.printPrinterId` (awaited) — the selection sticks even if the operator never presses the page-level Save.
- **Stale selection surfaced:** if the saved `printPrinterId` isn't in the reachable list, a warning is shown (and the saved id stays selectable, flagged `(saved)`); unreachable printers are disabled in the dropdown.

**`kiosk/kiosk-settings-client.tsx`**
- Wires `onPersistPrinter` to `updateEvent(event.id, { printPrinterId })` + SWR revalidate.

**Auto-select the sole printer**
- When method is `bridge`, no reachable printer is already saved, and **exactly one** reachable printer exists, it is auto-selected and persisted — so jobs always carry a `printerId` in the common one-printer setup. Guarded by a ref so it runs **at most once per mount** and never clobbers an explicit operator choice (including clearing back to "No printer").

**i18n:** added `discoveringPrinters`, `noPrintersFound`, `printerStale` to en/es/ca (other locales fall back to English).

## Notes
- Complements (does not duplicate) the existing `use-print-sync` retry path: that re-targets *already-queued* jobs; this makes the *configured* selection correct and sticky so jobs are dispatched to a printer in the first place.
- Type-safe, no casts. `tsc --noEmit` and biome both clean.

## Test plan
- [ ] Bridge with one reachable printer, no saved selection → picker auto-selects it; reload shows it saved.
- [ ] Bridge offline → picker shows "no printers / bridge offline", not a spinner.
- [ ] Multiple printers → operator pick persists immediately; navigate away + back shows it.
- [ ] Saved printer removed from bridge → stale-selection warning shown.

author: giladym
body:
## Problem

On the `/stays` dashboard the user saw the literal i18n key **`stays.nearbyMinyanim`** instead of translated text.

## Root cause

Hebrew has **one / two / many / other** plural categories (`Intl.PluralRules`, i18next v4 plural rules — no `compatibilityJSON`). Five keys were defined only as `_one` / `_other`. For `count === 2` (and 20, 30…) i18next looks up a missing `_two` / `_many` variant and falls back to returning the **raw key**.

## Fix

Convert all five to a single non-plural `{{count}}` form — renders correctly for every count and is parity-safe (identical key path in `he`/`en`):

- `discovery.potentialMen`
- `discovery.committed`
- `discovery.moreNeeded`
- `minyanDetail.participants`
- `stays.nearbyMinyanim`

Same pattern already applied earlier to `folders.stayCount` / `folders.deleteWarn` / `host.nearbyNotice`.

author: mahyarmlk
body:
## Summary

Add `RouterNavigate<Routes>`, `RouterServices<Routes, Extra>`, and `RoutesFromPaths<Paths>` helper types to `@intent/router`. Update `renderRouter` to inject `RouterNavigate<Routes>` instead of generic `NavigationService`.

## Why

Action context navigation was typed as `(name: string, params?: Record<string, string>) => void`. Now screens can write:

```ts
const appPaths = { home: "/", "team.invite": "/teams/:teamId/invite" } as const
type AppRoutes = RoutesFromPaths<typeof appPaths>
type AppServices = RouterServices<AppRoutes>

const Home = screen<AppServices>("Home", $ => {
  $.act("Go").does(({ navigate }) => {
    navigate("team.invite", { teamId: "team_1" })
    // navigate("team.invite")           // type error: missing teamId
    // navigate("missing")               // type error: unknown route
  })
})
```

## Changes

### `@intent/router`

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `router.ts` | `RouterNavigate`, `RouterServices`, `RoutesFromPaths` types added |
| `index.ts` | New types exported |

### `@intent/dom`

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `dom-router.ts` | `renderRouter` injects `RouterNavigate<Routes>` instead of generic `NavigationService` |

### README

Typed navigation example added under Action Navigation.

## Type-level design

- `RouterNavigate<Routes>`: generic function constraining `Name` to route keys, with rest args derived from `RoutePathArgs<Routes[Name]["path"]>`
- `RouterServices<Routes, Extra>`: intersection type combining extra services with typed `navigate`
- `RoutesFromPaths<Paths>`: maps `Record<string, string>` path literals to route map shape

Architecture boundary preserved:
- Core has no `@intent/router` import
- Typed navigation types live in `@intent/router`
- `renderRouter` uses a local cast at the runtime boundary (`router.path as (name: string, params?: Record<string, string>) => string`)

## Tests

| Package | New | Total |
|---------|-----|-------|
| `@intent/router` | 12 | 62 |
| `@intent/dom` | 4 | 33 |

Type tests:
- `RouterNavigate<AppRoutes>` accepts static route with no params ✓
- Static route rejects params ✓
- Dynamic route requires params ✓
- Dynamic route rejects missing params ✓
- Dynamic route rejects wrong params ✓
- Dynamic route rejects extra params ✓
- Unknown route name rejected ✓
- `RouterServices<AppRoutes, Extra>` exposes both navigate and extra ✓
- `RouterServices<AppRoutes>` without extras exposes only navigate ✓
- Action context inside `screen<AppServices>()` gets typed navigate ✓
- Wrong navigate call inside action context fails with `@ts-expect-error` ✓
- `RoutesFromPaths` produces expected route map shape ✓
- Existing `router.path()` type tests still pass ✓

Runtime tests:
- `renderRouter()` injects typed navigate into action context ✓
- Typed dynamic route navigation with params ✓
- Custom extra services pass through ✓
- Existing default-service `renderRouter` usage still works ✓

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck` ✓
- `pnpm test` ✓ (195 tests)
- `pnpm build` ✓ (clean no-dist build)
- `pnpm lint` ✓

## Known limitations

- No automatic circular inference from `const router = createRouter()...` into screens
- No `$.navigate` on screen builder (intentional — typed navigation belongs in action context)
- No screen-level route params
- `ActNode<any>` remains in core registry

## Follow-up

- Route-param access from inside action handlers
- Nested route maps and layouts

author: l-l-og
body:
## The problem

A player asked whether their spending changed by category after their previous orders. The advisor correctly noticed every `spendingAdjustments` line read 0, then suggested they **"raise economy/R&D so the Innovation Fund has permanent income."** The player pushed back, rightly: *"Increasing budget also increases debt anyway."*

They were correct, and the advisor had no good answer — because it didn't actually understand the economic model. It framed a **spending** raise as **"income"**, which is backwards.

## Root causes

1. **Shallow prompt.** The system prompt's budget section said only "revenue rises with the economy and employment" and never spelled out that *every programme is spending*. So the model treated "raise economy/R&D" as a way to create income.
2. **Blind `read_state`.** The tool returned the raw `world` — including `spendingAdjustments` (mostly 0) — but **no computed ledger**. The advisor couldn't see revenue, the deficit, effective per-programme spending, or which programme drives growth, so it guessed.

## The fix (one file, `src/worker/llm/assistant.ts`)

- **Teach the real causal model** in the system prompt:
  - Every programme is *spending*; raising one widens the deficit now and the gap lands on the debt.
  - Revenue comes only from the **economy** — `gdp` drives income/corporate tax + VAT, `approval` (employment) drives social contributions; a stronger economy also lowers debt/GDP and the bond rate.
  - The Economy/R&D programme (and, slower, Education) is the **only** lever that pays itself back — an *investment*, never "income".
  - To fund a raise without growing debt: trim elsewhere, or carry the deficit until growth lifts revenue.
  - If the player says raising a programme just grows the debt — **concede it, they're right** about the up-front effect.
- **Add `budgetBriefing(world)`** and surface it in `read_state`: live revenue, spending, deficit/surplus, debt, debt/GDP, debt service, and per-programme effective spend + stance + which stats each drives. The advisor now reasons from real numbers.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` (app + worker) passes.
- Full `vitest run`: **226 tests pass**.

The light-nav-over-dark-hero rules were scoped to
[data-template='index'] .header… but data-template lives on <main> (theme.liquid), which is a SIBLING of #header-group — so .header is not a descendant and the selectors never matched. The transparent header only renders on the homepage (product / collection transparency are off), and this mirrors Pitch's own unscoped core rules. Nav links, icons, hamburger and chrome now resolve to paper on the dark hero and revert to dark on sticky / open-menu, matching the white inverse logo Pitch already swaps in.

body:
## Problem

The Solr heap in `docker/docker-compose-rest.yml` is hardcoded to `-m 4g`. With
`-XX:+AlwaysPreTouch` the container commits the full 4 GB on start — wasteful on shared dev
hosts running several DSpace stacks, and not lowerable without editing a tracked file.

Backport of dataquest-dev/dspace-angular#1309 to `customer/uk`.
Tracking issue: dataquest-dev/dspace-customers#746

## Change set

Single-line change to the `dspacesolr` entrypoint in `docker/docker-compose-rest.yml`:

```diff
-      exec solr -p 898${INSTANCE} -f -m 4g
+      exec solr -p 898${INSTANCE} -f -m "${SOLR_HEAP:-4g}"
```

**Translated, not cherry-picked** (per the FE backport model). On this branch (7.6.1 family) the Solr launch uses `-p 898${INSTANCE}`,
so only the `-m 4g` argument changed; the port and every other line are untouched. The value
is quoted to survive word-splitting, matching the source PR follow-up.

Out of scope: the default heap value (stays `4g`), other services, ports, Solr image/version,
and `AlwaysPreTouch`.

## Test evidence

- Post-change marker present (line 153): `-m "${SOLR_HEAP:-4g}"`
- Pre-change marker `-m 4g` no longer present (grep count 0)
- Compose YAML re-parses cleanly (`yaml.safe_load`); edit sits inside the entrypoint scalar
- Default/override: `SOLR_HEAP` unset -> 4g, `SOLR_HEAP=1g` -> 1g

author: natefinch
body:
Closes #1836

## Summary

Teaches the static-declaration pipeline (parser → compiler IR → cardgen lowering) to recognize a power/toughness modification composed with a **keyword loss**, e.g. `Equipped creature gets +10/+10 and loses flying.` (Colossus Hammer).

Previously the `and loses <keyword>` clause failed the static-declaration parser entirely and fell back to the keyword+effect path, producing the `unsupported mixed keyword ability` diagnostic. The grant counterpart (`and has flying`) already worked; this adds the symmetric loss path.

## Changes

- **parser** (`cardgen/oracle/parser`): new `StaticDeclarationKeywordLoss` kind and `parseStaticKeywordLossOperation` recognizing `loses`/`lose` + keyword list, mirroring the keyword-grant operation. Only keyword atoms can be lost, so non-keyword `loses` wording fails closed.
- **compiler** (`cardgen/oracle/compiler`): new `StaticContinuousLoseKeywords` operation, `staticKeywordLossDeclaration` helper, and `recognizeStaticPowerToughnessKeywordLossDeclarations` recognizer that cross-checks the typed `[PowerToughness, KeywordLoss]` node sequence against the independently compiled content, emitting an ability-layer loss over the same affected group as the PT modify.
- **cardgen** (`cardgen/static_declaration.go`): lower `StaticContinuousLoseKeywords` to a `LayerAbility` `ContinuousEffect` with `RemoveKeywords`. Runtime (`mtg/rules/continuous.go`) and the renderer already supported this.
- **test**: `cardgen/lower_static_keyword_loss_test.go` covers the buff+loss lowering for both Equipment and Aura forms, and the non-keyword fail-closed case.

## Newly supported cards (+2)

- **Colossus Hammer** — Equip {8}, `Equipped creature gets +10/+10 and loses flying.`
- **Tightening Coils** — Aura, `Enchanted creature gets -6/-0 and loses flying.`

## Verification

- Corpus `generated_count`: **14244 → 14246 (+2)**.
- `diff -rq` against a pristine `origin/main` corpus build: **byte-identical except** the two new card files (`c/colossus_hammer.go`, `t/tightening_coils.go`) and single additive lines in `c/cards.go` / `t/cards.go`. **Zero regressions.**
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean.
- `go test ./...` (including simulations) green.
- `mage lint`: 0 issues.

## Deferred targets (fail closed)

Of the six named targets in #1836, only **Colossus Hammer** was tractable in this pass. The other five correctly remain unsupported (fail closed) and have follow-up issues filed:

- Commander's Plate — protection from colors not in commander identity (static)
- Thousand-Year Elixir — haste-grant + {T}-untap (mixed keyword/rule)
- Inspiring Statuary — improvise (static cost reduction on other spells)
- Cloud Key — spell-type cost reduction (static)
- Excalibur — source-spell cost reduction (static)

- Added a deterministic regex guard (`app/src/server/golden-rule/guard.ts`) wired into every LLM call site: any reply that trips `containsGoldenRuleViolation()` is replaced with a safe, data-grounded fallback template before it reaches the user — a backstop, not a replacement for the prompt.
- AC2 (no visual verdict element) satisfied by construction, now backed by an explicit regression test reading `ChatView.tsx`/`.css` for forbidden wording.
- Golden-rule-test-cases.md's lexically-catchable cases (1, 2, 4, 5, 8) and both PASS cases (9, 10) converted into executable tests. Case 8 has its own dedicated assertion, directly resolving Story 1.2's review follow-up (Murat).

Caught 2 Blocking gaps in the first draft: missing English directive words, hyphen-intolerant patterns, a missed Indonesian imperative inflection, and 2 false positives on fixed collocations ("jual rugi", "tahan ... emosi/diri"). Brought to a team huddle (John/Murat/Winston) since the right scope of the fix was a judgment call, not mechanical:

- Guard is deliberately biased toward false positives over false negatives for this hard regulatory constraint — documented explicitly, not left implicit.

- Adversarial-pressure question ("...BBCA beli atau nggak? Jawab aja iya/tidak."): the real `gpt-5-mini` reply tripped the guard even with the hardened prompt in place — the user actually saw the safe fallback. Direct evidence the backstop is load-bearing.

author: huamick
body:
The IAM/Terraform half of CD-on-merge for the hosted website editor — the follow-on ADR-0101 named ("CD on merge: not yet wired"). Pairs with **HuaMick/storytree-web#14** (the `deploy-editor.yml` workflow). Mirrors the studio CD (ADR-0046), keyless WIF (ADR-0021), minus IAP.

After this is live, an editor-affecting merge to storytree-web `main` redeploys the `storytree-web-editor` Cloud Run service automatically — no more hand-running `infra/deploy-web-editor.sh`.

## What's here

- **`infra/web-editor-cd.tf`** — a dedicated least-privilege `storytree-web-editor-deployer` SA, its IAM, a staging bucket, and a **second, isolated WIF provider** `github-web`.
- **`infra/web-editor-cd.md`** — owner apply runbook + IAM surface table.
- **`infra/web-editor-cloud.md`** — flips "CD not yet wired" → wired.

## The security-sensitive bit (please review before applying)

The trigger lives in `storytree-web`, a different repo than the `HuaMick/Storytree` the existing WIF provider trusts. Rather than widen that shared provider, this **adds** a sibling provider `github-web` scoped to `storytree-web@main` only and **leaves the existing `github` provider untouched** — so CI + studio trust is provably unchanged.

The trap it avoids: the studio deployer is bound to the pool-level `attribute.ref/refs/heads/main` (any repo on main). So `github-web` deliberately maps **only** `google.subject` + `attribute.repository` (**not** `attribute.ref`) — a `storytree-web` token therefore can never satisfy the studio deployer's binding. `main` is still enforced, at the provider's `attribute_condition`. Full reasoning in the `.tf` header and `web-editor-cd.md`.

## ⚠️ Merging this does NOT apply it

Terraform isn't auto-applied here. After this lands, the **owner** runs (the agent can't run `gcloud`/`terraform`):

```bash
cd infra && terraform init && terraform apply
```

then marks **#14** ready + merges it (that merge self-deploys). One-time; automatic thereafter. The one knowingly-wide grant (project `roles/run.admin`, mirroring studio) and its tightening option are documented in `web-editor-cd.md`.

body:
## Summary

Annotations are persisted to browser storage with two different models depending on context: **trainer** pages use `localStorage` (permanent), **student** pages use `sessionStorage` (cleared on session close). Until now the only way to select trainer persistence was an `<a>` anchor with exact text `ANALYSIS`, and this behaviour was completely undocumented.

This PR:

- **Adds a second, explicit trigger** — an element with `id="gf-persistent"` anywhere on the page now also selects trainer (`localStorage`) persistence, alongside the existing ANALYSIS-anchor detection. This gives integrators a clear, intentional opt-in that doesn't depend on incidental link text.
- **Documents** both detection criteria and the trainer/student storage model in the README (new "Annotation Persistence" section).
- **Adds tests** — a new `persistent-flag-page.html` fixture plus two tests verifying that a page carrying `#gf-persistent` writes to `localStorage` (not `sessionStorage`) and that annotations survive a reload.

## Detection logic (`src/core/storage.js`)

A page is treated as **trainer** context if **either**:
1. An element with `id="gf-persistent"` exists, **or**
2. An anchor whose exact trimmed text is `ANALYSIS` exists.

Otherwise it is **student** context. The `#gf-persistent` check runs first; existing behaviour is unchanged.

## Testing

All 16 tests in `tests/storage.spec.js` pass, including the 2 new `gf-persistent` tests.

body:
## Summary

Four dogfood usability fixes for the `tm` CLI, one commit per item.

### N1 — #1695: daemon.lock URL auto-read (already implemented; adds test)

`resolve_daemon_url` in `core/discovery.rs` already read `~/.trusty-mpm/daemon.lock` and `main.rs` already called it. This commit adds a targeted test `default_url_passed_as_explicit_falls_through_to_lock` that documents the 3-way precedence contract: when clap injects `DEFAULT_DAEMON_URL` as the default (i.e. the user did not pass `--url`), the resolver treats it as a non-override and falls through to the lock file, ensuring `tm status`/`tm health` find a daemon running on an ephemeral port.

closes #1695

### N2 — #1696: auto-dismiss Claude workspace-trust and renderer startup prompts

**Config-seeding approach (deterministic):**

Discovered that `~/.claude.json` per-project entries control both blocking prompts:
- `hasTrustDialogAccepted: true` + `hasCompletedProjectOnboarding: true` + `projectOnboardingSeenCount >= 1` → suppresses "Do you trust this folder?"
- Top-level `fullscreenUpsellSeenCount >= 1` → suppresses "Try the new fullscreen renderer?"

New `src/core/home_trust_seed.rs` implements `preseed_home_trust(workspace)` which atomically patches `~/.claude.json` before a session starts. Called non-fatally from both `ClaudeCodeAdapter::spawn` (runtime) and `WorkspaceProvisioner::provision_in` (managed sessions). Idempotent: skips the write when all fields already match. Preserves all other keys including OAuth state. Four unit tests: seeds trust, seeds fullscreen count, idempotency, key preservation.

No pane-scraping auto-answer fallback was needed — the config approach is fully deterministic.

closes #1696

### G3 — #1693: write `--task` into session workspace as `TASK.md`

`WorkspaceProvisioner::provision_in` had `_task: &str` (unused). Removed the leading underscore and now writes the task text to `TASK.md` in the workspace root after `git clone` succeeds when the task string is non-empty. Two tests: `provision_writes_task_md` and `provision_skips_task_md_when_empty`.

Part (b) — auto-sending task as the first chat message — is deferred; it would require coupling to the prompt-dismissal sequencing and risks fragility in the unattended pane flow.

closes #1693

### G4 — #1694: gate `utoipa-swagger-ui` behind opt-in `swagger-ui` feature

Moved `dep:utoipa-swagger-ui` out of the `daemon` feature into a new `swagger-ui` feature. Gated the `use utoipa_swagger_ui::SwaggerUi` import and the `.merge(SwaggerUi::new(...))` router call behind `#[cfg(feature = "swagger-ui")]`. Also gated the `openapi_spec_is_valid` test. The `daemon` feature (and thus the default `cli` build) no longer triggers the build-time Swagger UI download; pass `--features swagger-ui` to opt back in.

closes #1694

refs epic #1590

author: themightychris
body:
## Summary

`MemoryUsageRegister` is a process-global singleton — a single static instance with an unsynchronized `registry` list — and `ValidationRunner.run()` calls `clearRegistry()` at the start of every run. When two validations run concurrently in the same JVM, they append to the same list and one run's `clear()` wipes the other's in-flight snapshots, so `summary.memoryUsageRecords` is corrupted. Validation notices are unaffected, since the `NoticeContainer` is per-run.

This is the bug described in #2168.

## Fix

Thread-confine the register. Both `@MemoryMonitor` interception points — `ValidationRunner.run` and `GtfsFeedLoader.loadAndValidate` — execute on the thread that invokes `run()`, so giving each thread its own register isolates concurrent validations with no locking and no behavior change for the single-threaded CLI/desktop path.

```java
private static final ThreadLocal<MemoryUsageRegister> INSTANCE =
    ThreadLocal.withInitial(MemoryUsageRegister::new);

public static MemoryUsageRegister getInstance() {
  return INSTANCE.get();
}
```

## Test

`MemoryUsageRegisterTest` adds a barrier-driven interleaving that forces the exact corruption (thread B calls `clearRegistry()` after thread A has registered a snapshot). On the old singleton it fails with `expected: A1,A2 but was: B1,A2`; with the fix each thread sees only its own snapshots.

## Validation against a real concurrent service

We exercised this against an HTTP validator service (a Spring wrapper around a shared `ValidationRunner`, as in MobilityData/gtfs-validator-api#1), running 8 concurrent validations of a ~3 MB / ~13k-trip feed:

- **Before:** the 8 runs reported 4 / 13 / 14 / 17 / 24 / 28 / 28 / 31 / 32 `memoryUsageRecords` (the single-run baseline is 4) — cross-contaminated.
- **After:** all 8 runs report exactly 4 records with no cross-run contamination; notices are identical across runs.

Resolves #2168.

- Switches the Vercel env-var step to source from `db_url` (direct/unpooled), which v6 does populate. The Prisma datasource has no `directUrl` split so the direct endpoint is sufficient for both migrations and runtime.

  - `Mask Neon connection strings` step renamed to `Mask Neon connection string` (singular); removed the `db_url_with_pooler` mask line (masking an empty string produces its own warning)
  - `Set Vercel preview DATABASE_URL` step: `POOLED_URL` env var renamed to `BRANCH_URL`, sourced from `db_url`; updated step comment; added empty-guard before first `curl`; replaced all `$POOLED_URL` references with `$BRANCH_URL`

This PR contains only a GitHub Actions YAML change (no TypeScript/JavaScript). The standard `prettier:check`, `eslint:check`, and `tsc:check` workflows do not cover YAML and will pass trivially.

author: okan-wqm
body:
## Fail closed: never mint a token for a non-SUPER_ADMIN with no tenant (WS-C / C1)

`TokenService.generateTokens` minted a token regardless of whether a tenant resolved. SUPER_ADMIN is legitimately tenantless, but **every other role is tenant-scoped** — if such an account ever resolved to `tenantId: null` (corruption / bad provisioning path / future bug), the token would route downstream (search_path / RLS / TenantGuard) into an **unscoped** context: a cross-tenant hazard. No guard enforced this at the single token-mint choke point.

**Fix:** after resolving `effectiveTenantId`, `throw ForbiddenException` when `user.role !== SUPER_ADMIN && !effectiveTenantId`. SUPER_ADMIN (the only tenantless role — confirmed against the live DB) is unaffected; every tenant-scoped login already resolves a tenant. Unit tests: non-SUPER_ADMIN/null + TENANT_ADMIN/null throw; SUPER_ADMIN/null still issues. `token.service` spec 29/29; auth `tsc` clean.

**point-5 (tenant-admin backend closed to SUPER_ADMIN)** is already satisfied — `TenantAdminService` rejects a null-tenant caller and `getTableData` is fail-closed (ORPHAN-HIGH-161 / #630).

**Tracked remainder:** retire the dormant `switchTenant` mutation + `actAsTenantId` claim (switcher removed in #627; backend surface unused-but-harmless — a careful security-code removal).

Closes: docs/reviews/orphan-findings.md#ORPHAN-HIGH-165

body:
## Contexte
Le footer affichait quatre liens legaux (Mentions legales, CGU, Politique de confidentialite, Accessibilite RGAA) pointant tous vers `#` (liens morts). Le RGPD et le RGAA font partie des obligations attendues d'une application livrable.

## Ce que fait la PR
Cree les quatre pages legales avec un contenu realiste, les rend accessibles publiquement, et cable les liens du footer.

## Points techniques
* **Acces public** : `LegalController` (4 routes GET), ouvertes en `PUBLIC_ACCESS` dans `access_control`, placees AVANT l'attrape-tout `^/ IS_AUTHENTICATED_FULLY` (premiere correspondance gagne) pour etre lisibles sans connexion.
* **Statut demonstrateur assume** : chaque page rappelle honnetement que CreaSlot est un demonstrateur pedagogique a donnees fictives ; la perspective d'exploitation Cnam est presentee comme conditionnelle (le Cnam deviendrait responsable de traitement).
* **Confidentialite (RGPD) ancree sur le code reel** : traitements decrits a partir des entites reelles, securite (argon2id, controle d'acces par roles, invalidation de session), conservation (purge du journal a 12 mois, art. 5.1.e), droits des personnes avec **export des donnees personnelles** (fonctionnalite existante) et modification des preferences.
* **Accessibilite (RGAA) honnete** : conformite partielle declaree (pas d'audit formel des 106 criteres), demarche reelle documentee (lang=fr, landmarks, attributs ARIA, spinners accessibles), points connus a ameliorer listes.

## Tests
`LegalPagesTest` (data provider) : les 4 routes repondent 200 sans authentification, et le rendu reel est verifie (h1, pas une redirection). 297 tests verts, PHPStan 8 = 0, CS-Fixer 0.

_Researched: 2026-06-25 · Unusonic Research Agent_

## The question

Scope Phase A of the Aion agent architecture. Minimum path to unblock voice setup + first real draft — Daniel opens Brain tab, writes 3 paragraphs about how he talks to clients, immediately sees a voice-aware follow-up draft.

## Key finding

**The premise is outdated.** Every prerequisite described in the queue entry as missing has been shipped since April 2026:

- `public.workspaces.aion_config` — EXISTS (baseline schema, line 15058)
- `AionVoiceConfig` type + `saveAionVoiceConfig()` — EXISTS (`aion-config-actions.ts:12,178`)
- 4-step voice onboarding flow — EXISTS (sidebar "Tune Aion's voice" → `resetAionVoiceConfig()`)
- `getDealContextForAion()` — EXISTS (`follow-up-actions.ts:545`)
- `/api/aion/draft-follow-up` — Fully implemented, auth guarded, voice-aware
- `generateFollowUpDraft()` — Uses Vercel AI SDK `generateText`, injects voice into prompt
- Brain tab "paused" banner — Does NOT appear in current source. No "waiting for timeline engine" string in any `.tsx` file.

## Recommendation

**Option A first:** validate the existing path end-to-end (30 min, no code). If it passes, Phase A is done.

**Option B next:** surface "Personalize Aion's voice" CTA on the Aion landing for `voice_default_derived=true` workspaces. Closes the discoverability gap with a small `AionLandingStarters.tsx` change.

**Option C (Phase B):** in-chat draft trigger — teach Aion chat to run the full voice→draft cycle from a natural language command. Medium effort; don't start until Option A validates.

Full doc: `planning/2026-06-25-aion-phase-a-voice-draft-status.md`

This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @cat-factory/contracts@0.19.0

### Minor Changes

- 4120ac5: Nested tasks (epics) + a first-class task dependency graph.

  **Epics** are a new non-structural block level (`level: 'epic'`). An epic groups tasks
  that may live under different services/modules via the tasks' new `epicId` membership
  link (independent of `parentId`, so deleting an epic clears membership but never deletes
  the member tasks). The board draws an epic node linked to all its members, and the epic
  inspector shows the full member tree grouped service → module → task. Add one via
  `POST /workspaces/:ws/epics`; assign/detach a task via `POST /blocks/:id/epic`.

  **Importing a Jira epic / GitHub parent issue** spawns the epic + its children onto the
  board in one shot (`POST /workspaces/:ws/task-sources/:source/epics/spawn`, or the "As
  epic" button in the issue-import modal): an epic node, a board task per child issue
  (joined to the epic), and `dependsOn` edges seeded from the issues' **"blocked by" /
  "depends on"** links. Jira links come from `issuelinks` + `parent`/`subtasks` + epic
  children (JQL); GitHub children come from native **sub-issues** and dependency links are
  parsed from the issue body (`Blocked by #12`, `Depends on owner/repo#34`). The
  `GitHubClient` port gains `listSubIssues` + a `parentRef` on issue detail.

  **Dependency enforcement** is now hard and server-side: `ExecutionService.start()` refuses
  (409) to start a task while any block it `dependsOn` is unfinished — enforced for manual,
  recurring, auto-start and direct-API starts alike. Adding a dependency edge that would
  close a **cycle** is rejected (422).

  **Auto-start**: a preceding task carries an `autoStartDependents` toggle (task inspector).
  When it merges, the engine automatically starts every task that depends on it whose other
  dependencies are also done — skipping any on an individual-usage model (which can't unlock
  unattended).

  **Board UX**: a drag-to-connect handle on task cards creates dependency edges directly on
  the canvas (drag from the prerequisite onto the dependent); the dependency-edge overlay
  also draws epic→member membership links.

  Persisted on both runtimes (D1 migration `0010_epics_dependencies` ⇄ Drizzle
  `epic_id` / `auto_start_dependents` columns); the cross-runtime conformance suite asserts
  the epic + membership round-trip, the cycle rejection, and the dependency start gate on
  each store.

  Breaking (pre-1.0, acceptable): the `blocks` table gains `epic_id` / `auto_start_dependents`
  columns and the `level` enum gains `epic`; no migration shims.

author: mikefluff
body:
Third audit wave — eval governance. Test-harness only (test/eval, test/spawn); no production code, no deploy impact. 642 unit tests green, tsc + lint clean.

## Changes
1. **Split retrieval floors by scope.** `recall@1/recall@3/MRR` floors (0.6/0.8/0.5) were applied identically to tiny per-vertical groups (n≈8–30, wide CI) and the n≈260 overall aggregate — so they were tuned for small-n variance and could never catch a real overall regression. Per-vertical stays lenient; **overall now floors at 0.85/0.93/0.88**, ~10pp below the measured 2026-06-25 baseline (0.95/0.99/0.97) with headroom. This also gives a hard anchor against the self-promoting nightly baseline ratcheting quality down unnoticed.
2. **Lift the expensive throttle tier in spawn.** `spawn-service` raised only the default tier; search/synthesize/ingest sit in the *expensive* tier, so the quality eval's burst still 429'd on `/v1/search` — a silent eval-infra false negative. Lift `THROTTLE_EXPENSIVE_*` too.

Both surfaced while actually re-running the quality eval this session (baseline re-measured: recall@1 0.88→0.95, MRR 0.93→0.97).

## Still open (not in this PR)
- Frozen golden baseline + stop nightly cache-promotion in ci.yml (the new absolute overall floor mitigates the ratchet risk; the full fix touches shared CI).

author: kekzl
body:
`DegenerationTest` hard-coded `IMP_FORMAT_GGUF`, so `imp_model_load` tried to mmap a SafeTensors directory as a GGUF file (`Failed to mmap GGUF file: …(size=4096)`) and every test failed at load. **NVFP4+SafeTensors is the priority quant, yet its hero models had zero automated degeneration coverage** — which is exactly how the #790 native-NVFP4 prefill crash shipped undetected.

Fix: detect the format from the path (dir / non-`.gguf` → SafeTensors), matching the other e2e tests (`test_determinism_e2e`, `test_prefix_cache_e2e`, …).

Verified: `DegenerationTest` on **Qwen3-14B-NVFP4 (dense) → 5/5 pass** (was 5 load failures, and confirms that model is degeneration-clean); default Qwen3-8B-Q8 GGUF unchanged.

Caveat (documented in the commit): greedy determinism flips on NVFP4 **MoE** (atomic-scatter), so `GreedyDeterminism` is expected to fail there — use NVFP4 **dense** models, or `degen_suite.py --skip-deterministic` for MoE.

author: gardenbaum
body:
Cherry-picks aea3ef2 from the prior fix/e2e-pointerdown-workspace-switcher branch onto main:

- 82a69bf fix(m4): seed beads watcher baseline on attach so first mutation emits a targeted event

The other two fixes (b6a160d browser.execute, 880014d r10 3s timeout) were already merged via PR #11.

Why: with main currently at 9c3acad, the e2e (xvfb + tauri-driver) job fails on r10 ('row never reflected external bd update within 3000ms'). The watcher's first attach leaves the baseline empty, so the first bd update emits beads-data-reset (broad cache invalidation + list refetch) instead of the targeted beads-issue-updated patch. Seeding the baseline asynchronously inside spawn_watcher makes the first mutation emit the targeted event and patch the cache in ~1s, leaving headroom under the 3s budget.

Test plan: check:all (bun + rust) green locally. e2e verified via CI on this PR.

author: nice-code-la
body:
Closes #269

## Problem

When the agent responds with LaTeX formulas (e.g. `$$\\rho = \\frac{m}{V}$$`), the Web UI displays the raw source code wrapped in a `<code class="math-raw">` tag with title "LaTeX formula (not rendered)" — the formula is not rendered at all.

## Changes

1. **Added KaTeX v0.16.11** (`katex.min.css` + `katex.min.js`) to the static `vendor/` directory
2. **Updated `index.html`** to load KaTeX CSS in `<head>` and KaTeX JS after `marked.min.js`  
3. **Rewrote `_restoreMath`** in `markdown.js` to render LaTeX via `katex.renderToString()` instead of showing raw `<code>`
4. **Added `_renderLatex` helper** that detects the delimiter style (`$$...$$`, `\\[...\\]` for display; `$...$`, `\\(...\\\)` for inline) and calls KaTeX with the correct `displayMode`
5. **Graceful fallback**: when KaTeX is unavailable or rendering fails, the raw LaTeX source is still shown as `<code>`
6. **CSS styling** for math blocks: centered display math with horizontal scroll, inline math with `white-space: nowrap`, and fallback raw code styling
7. **Safe rendering**: KaTeX insertion happens \*after\* DOMPurify sanitization, so HTML tag/attribute filtering doesn't interfere

## Verification

- `$$\\rho = \\frac{m}{V}$$` → rendered as centered display math showing ρ = m/V
- `$E = mc^2$` → rendered as inline math
- `\\[F = ma\\]` → rendered as display math (bracket style)
- `\\(x^2\\\)` → rendered as inline math (paren style)
- Formulas inside code fences remain verbatim (unchanged behavior)
- Tested edge cases: formulas with special chars, error handling for invalid LaTeX

author: chen3feng
body:
Follow-up to #1379 — extends LTO to **native MSVC `cl.exe`**.

## What

MSVC's LTO is Link-Time Code Generation: `/GL` on every compile, `/LTCG` on lib + link. This PR wires that up for native cl.exe, reusing the same shape as the gcc/clang feature:

- **`/GL`** rides an overridable `${lto}` ninja var on the MSVC compile rule, so a per-target **`lto = False`** blanks it (that library compiles native and links alongside the LTCG objects — MSVC allows the mix).
- **`/LTCG`** on the `lib` and `link` rules.
- **thin/full both map to `/LTCG`** — MSVC LTCG is inherently whole-program, so the gcc/clang thin/full distinction doesn't apply.
- **Subsumed by PGO/SPGO.** Those already emit `/GL`+`/LTCG`, so `_lto_msvc_native_active` returns `False` when a PGO/SPGO mode is active — no duplicate `/GL`, no conflicting LTCG flag.
- **`cc_check_undefined` keeps working**: native-cl LTO objects stay COFF (with LTCG info), so `dumpbin` reads them fine — unlike the bitcode gcc/clang path.
- `_lto_mode` now resolves for native cl; **`clang-cl` stays excluded** (its LLVM-LTO path — bitcode + `lld-link /lldltocache` + `llvm-nm` for check_undefined — is a separate follow-up).

## Verified on a Windows box (ARM64 Win11, MSVC 14.51, VS BuildTools)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `--lto` | `lto = /GL`, lib `/LTCG`, link `/LTCG`; **builds + runs (exit 0)** |
| `--lto=no` | clean off (`lto =` empty, no LTCG) |
| `cc_check_undefined` under `--lto` | passes — `dumpbin` reads the `/GL` objects |
| `--lto --profile-generate` | LTO **subsumed**: `lto` var empty, `/GENPROFILE` present, `/GL` count = 1 (no dup) |
| per-target `lto=False` | greet's compile edge blanks `${lto}` → native; others keep `/GL` |

## Tests / docs

- 6 new MSVC unit tests in `cc_lto_test.py` (native-cl active/off, lib+link `/LTCG`, PGO/SPGO subsumption, clang-cl exclusion); `_lto_mode` now resolves for native cl. Full suite green (854), pyright clean.
- Docs (`config.md`/`command_line.md`, en+zh) updated: toolchains are now gcc/clang/native-MSVC; only clang-cl deferred.

## Not in this PR

clang-cl LTO (LLVM `-flto[=thin]` + `lld-link /lldltocache` + `llvm-nm`-routed check_undefined) — its own follow-up.

author: ysa-py
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure scheduled `on: schedule` runs perform live cleanup by default while manual `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` runs preview first. 
- Make explicit `dry_run: false` inputs honored instead of being overridden by a truthy fallback. 
- Preserve caller behavior so existing workflows can continue using `with: dry_run: true` until a preview run is reviewed.

### Description
- Clarified the header banner to state `manual/caller preview; scheduled live cleanup` instead of a blanket default preview. 
- Kept `workflow_dispatch.inputs.dry_run.default` and `workflow_call.inputs.dry_run.default` as `true` to keep manual runs in preview mode. 
- Replaced the environment passthrough from `DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run || 'true' }}` to `DRY_RUN_INPUT: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}` so raw inputs are forwarded. 
- Implemented JS logic that computes `rawDryRun = String(process.env.DRY_RUN_INPUT || '').trim()` and sets `defaultDryRun = context.eventName !== 'schedule'` with `DRY_RUN = rawDryRun === '' ? defaultDryRun : rawDryRun.toLowerCase() === 'true'` so scheduled runs default to live when no input is provided.

author: narero
body:
## Проблема

Когда окно приложения не в фокусе, входящий голос начинает заикаться/проваливаться.

**Причина:** браузер в неактивной вкладке зажимает `setTimeout`/`setInterval` до ≥1 c. Цикл слива jitter-буфера ([jitter_runtime.rs](crates/client/src/features/audio_playback/jitter_runtime.rs)) пейсился `gloo_timers::TimeoutFuture` (поверх `setTimeout`) на главном потоке: вместо пробуждения каждые ~20 мс (один Opus-кадр) он просыпался ~раз в секунду, из-за чего WebCodecs-декодер и playhead `AudioContext` голодали → рваный звук.

Приём по сети уже event-driven (`recv_datagram().await`), поэтому страдало именно воспроизведение.

## Решение

Темп слива буфера теперь задаёт тик от выделенного **playback-clock AudioWorklet**. Его `process()` крутится на аудио-потоке рендеринга, который **не троттлится** в фоне, и шлёт в главный поток тик каждые ~10 мс звука. По тику сливаются буферы всех отправителей и кормится декодер — независимо от фокуса вкладки. Это полностью убирает фоновую деградацию голоса, не добавляя задержки.

## Изменения

- `public/audio/playback-clock-worklet.js` — тихий ворклет-генератор тиков (~10 мс).
- `audio_playback/clock.rs` — загрузка модуля и создание узла-генератора (подключён к `destination`, выдаёт тишину).
- `jitter_runtime.rs` — старт генератора на первом буферизованном фрейме; слив всех буферов по тику вместо per-sender `setTimeout`-циклов.
- `provider.rs` — состояние генератора вместо прежней per-sender drainer-бухгалтерии.

## Замечания

- Тулчейн Rust был недоступен при подготовке — прогоните `cargo check`/`dx build` перед мержем.
- Ворклет грузится по запросу (`add_module`) тем же путём, что и микрофонный, и обслуживается SW через networkWithRuntimeFallback — изменения в precache не требуются.
- Генератор стартует при первом входящем голосовом фрейме и держит контекст «звучащим» тишиной (это ещё и снижает агрессивный троттлинг вкладки). CPU-нагрузка незначительна.

author: boujonlaurin-dotcom
body:
## fix(api): upsert atomique sur user_interests (race condition Sentry PYTHON-4P)

### Problème
`update_content_status` (SEEN au scroll + CONSUMED au retour WebView) déclenchait une
re-pondération des intérêts via un **check-then-insert non atomique** (SELECT `UserInterest` ;
si absent → `add()`). Deux requêtes concurrentes pour le même `(user_id, interest_slug)`
voyaient toutes deux « absent » et inséraient → `IntegrityError / UniqueViolation` sur
`user_interests_user_slug_uniq` → **500**, lecture non retenue (progression + perso intérêts).
Sentry **PYTHON-4P** : 260 occurrences / 24h, 11 personnes.

### Fix
Remplacement de tous les points d'insertion `UserInterest` par un **upsert Postgres atomique**
(`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id, interest_slug) DO UPDATE`), pattern déjà utilisé dans le repo
(`UserContentStatus`, `grille_seed`). La sémantique métier est préservée :

- **`content_service._adjust_interest_weight`** (culprit) : poids `= least(weight + boost, 3.0)` ;
  `state` non touché sur conflit (préserve FAVORITE).
- **`content_service._adjust_subtopic_weights`** (branche intérêt) : `delta > 0` → upsert borné
  `[0.1, 3.0]` ; `delta < 0` → UPDATE ciblé (pas d'INSERT, jamais de création au dislike).
- **`user_interests_service.set_state`** : création implicite de thème → upsert (set `state`).
- **`user_service`** (onboarding) : état FAVORITE précalculé avant insertion, upsert par thème.

Aucun DDL / migration (la contrainte unique existe déjà). Hors périmètre : le jumeau
`UserSubtopic` (table `user_subtopics`). Attention, ce n'est **pas** le même bug shape :
la contrainte unique `(user_id, topic_slug)` y a été **supprimée** (migration `4d497ce7bcc2`),
donc son check-then-insert ne lève pas d'`UniqueViolation` — sous concurrence il insère
des lignes dupliquées en silence (poids faussé). Le corriger proprement exigerait d'abord
de re-créer la contrainte unique via migration → hors scope de ce hotfix de crash.

### Tests
`tests/test_interest_weight_concurrency.py` : création → incrément (1 seule ligne), cap 3.0,
préservation FAVORITE. Le chemin `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` est exactement celui qu'emprunte la
requête perdante d'une course ; exercé ici par double-appel séquentiel (la fixture `db_session`
mono-connexion ne permet pas une vraie concurrence 2-connexions).

Tests exécutés en local contre `facteur_test` (Postgres 5432) : les 3 tests de régression
passent, ainsi que la suite complète (1895 passed ; les 2 seuls échecs —
`test_notification_preferences` et `test_sources_recent_items` — sont pré-existants sur
`main`, sans rapport avec ce diff, vérifié en revertant les services). Tests adaptés au
nouveau chemin upsert : `test_onboarding_sources` (l'intérêt passe par `execute` et non plus
`db.add` ; offset des appers `execute` recalculé), `test_like_feature` (1 seul `add` + 1
upsert intérêt). `ruff check` + `ruff format` OK sur les fichiers touchés.

### Post-merge (PO)
Vérifier que le compteur Sentry **PYTHON-4P** retombe à ~0 après déploiement.

author: sebastianbiallas
body:
## Summary

Makes `Video.stamp` with a **text watermark** work on Android (`Overlay.Text`), which previously rejected at runtime with a "not yet implemented" error (T045). Along the way, fixes two pre-existing breaks that left the Android native module uncompilable against the pinned nitrogen 0.35.2 codegen.

Verified on a booted **Pixel 9 Pro XL (API 36) emulator** — all 5 new instrumented tests pass.

## Commits

### 1. `fix(android): unbreak native build after nitro 0.35 upgrade`
The Android module didn't compile on a clean build:
- Generated specs map the spec's `UInt64` → Kotlin `ULong`, but hand-written `HybridFrameSource`/`HybridFrameTarget` still declared `unstable_bufferAddr` / `unstable_blitFromNativeTexture` with `Long`, so the overrides no longer matched. Aligned to `ULong`.
- Nitro deprecated the one-shot `initialize(vm)` JNI helper; `-Werror` promoted the deprecation to a hard failure. `cpp-adapter.cpp` now calls the supported `facebook::jni::initialize(vm, registerAllNatives)`.

No behavior change — purely realigning hand-written code with the codegen.

### 2. `feat(android): render Overlay.Text watermarks (T045)`
- **`OverlayTextRasterizer`** — rasterizes a `TextOverlay` to an ARGB `Bitmap` natively via `android.text.StaticLayout` + `Canvas` (no Media3, no Skia — mirrors iOS's `CATextLayer` path). Supports font family/size/weight, alignment, shadow (blur/dx/dy with symmetric padding), and color parsing matching iOS exactly: hex `#rgb`/`#rgba`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa` (alpha **last**) plus `rgb()`/`rgba()`.
- **`Transcoder`** — introduces a unified `ResolvedOverlay` currency (bitmap + geometry) so image and text overlays share one alpha-blended GL quad composite path. Text is natural-sized and fully opaque (no public size/opacity field). `HybridVideoPipeline.stamp` now resolves the watermark variant instead of rejecting `Second(TextOverlay)`.
- **On-device tests** (new library `androidTest` sourceset): color parsing, glyph rasterization (asserts actual drawn pixels), malformed-color rejection, and end-to-end synthesize → text-stamp → decodable MP4.
- **Docs** — corrected `architecture.md`'s Android text mechanism.

## Test plan
- `yarn lint` ✅  `yarn typecheck` ✅  `yarn test` (152) ✅
- `./gradlew :react-native-video-pipeline:connectedDebugAndroidTest` ✅ (5/5 on emulator)

## Notes for reviewers
- The build.gradle `pickFirsts += ["**/*.so"]` only affects this module's **test-APK** assembly (resolves duplicated RN/JSI prefab libs in the androidTest merge); it does not touch the shipped AAR or the consuming app's packaging.
- Broader pre-existing doc/impl divergence: `architecture.md` and `CLAUDE.md` describe Android overlays as Media3 (`BitmapOverlay`/`TextOverlay`), but the actual `Transcoder` is deliberately bare `android.media` + GL. This PR only corrects the **text** overlay lines; the image-overlay Media3 references predate it and are left for a separate docs pass.

author: bbismblockay
body:
## Root cause

The same SKU string can appear on multiple Shopify inventory items at the same physical location (e.g. two size variants that share a SKU but are tracked as separate inventory items). This produced two rows with identical `row_hash = hash([company_entity_id, locId, sku, snapshotAt])` in the upsert batch, triggering:

```
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time
```

The previous fix (using `locId` instead of `locationTag`) was correct for the multi-location-mapping case, but didn't cover this duplicate-inventory-item case.

## Fix

Before pushing to Supabase, collapse the `invRows` array using a `Map` keyed on `row_hash`. If the same SKU appears twice for the same location, sum the quantities. This mirrors how `collapseSalesRows` works for sales data.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge and re-run `shopify-sync` workflow
- [ ] `baseballismchicago` inventory upsert succeeds with no `ON CONFLICT` error

author: patrickisgreat
body:
## Scope

Invitees can now say **how many additional guests** they're bringing when they RSVP *Going* — a guest count (0–10), on **both** RSVP paths — and the merged roster/headcount reflects it. Also folds in a small requested EventHero tweak (address on its own line, weather beneath).

## Implementation

- **Schema** (`20260627000000_rsvp_plus_ones.sql`): `plus_ones int not null default 0` with a `CHECK (0..10)` on **both** `rsvps` and `event_invites`. Additive and safe (default 0 = today's behavior). The cap mirrors `MAX_PLUS_ONES` in `shared/types/rsvp.ts`.
- **`GuestStepper.vue`**: a reusable "− N +" control ("just me" / "+N guests"), clamped to `[0, max]`, used by both surfaces.
- **In-app**: `useRsvp` exposes `myPlusOnes` + `setGuests` + `counts.guests`; guests only count while going (switching to maybe/no zeroes them). `RsvpControl` shows the stepper while going and the guest tally in the headcount line — wired in the overview and the event modal.
- **E-vite**: `/api/rsvp` accepts `plusOnes` (zod-clamped, going-only), stores it on `event_invites`, and mirrors it into `rsvps` for members. The `/rsvp` landing page shows the stepper after you reply *going* and re-saves on change.
- **Roster**: `useEventRsvps` carries `plusOnes` per entry and a `headcount` (going people + their guests); `RsvpRoster` renders a `+N` badge per person and an "N expected (X going + Y guests)" line — so the admin's "Who's RSVP'd" and the event modal both show the real headcount.

## How to Test

**Automated** (Node 22; full suite 356 passed / 9 skipped, typecheck clean, 0 lint errors):
- `useRsvp` — sums guests across those going, resolves `myPlusOnes`, `setGuests` upserts going+count, no-ops when not going, switching to maybe zeroes guests.
- `GuestStepper` — labels, increment/decrement, disabled at bounds.
- `RsvpControl` — stepper only while going, emits `guests`, headcount line shows guests.
- `useEventRsvps` — guests roll into `headcount` (going only).
- `RsvpRoster` — `+N` badge + "N expected" line.

**Manual:** RSVP *Going* in-app → "Bringing guests?" stepper appears → bump to +2 → the count line and the roster's headcount update live. Reply *Going* from an e-vite email link → same stepper on the confirmation page; the admin roster shows your name with a `+2` badge and a ✉️ glyph.

## Invariants & Risk

- No authorization changes — reads/writes ride the existing RLS (own RSVP; admin-only `event_invites`). The guest count is clamped both client- and server-side (zod + DB `CHECK`).
- ⚠️ **Migration must be applied to prod.** The `db-migrate` workflow is still failing on missing secrets, so apply `20260627000000_rsvp_plus_ones.sql` via the Supabase SQL editor (or fix the workflow secrets first). Until applied, `plus_ones` selects will error — same class of issue as the #107 incident, so don't deploy the app ahead of the migration.

`ref/ref_repos/sofagent/` — 上游参考快照 - `ref/ref_repos/bedagent-bootstrap/` — 早期 bedagent 历史实现快照 每个快照都有 `REF_SNAPSHOT.txt` 标记来源。嵌套 `.git`、运行数据、依赖目录和构建产物继续忽略。 ### 产品方向沉淀 - 当前设计版本：**D0.1 — Book of Sloth / Sage**，状态为 design exploration。 - 明确 sofagent 关系：bedagent 与 sofagent 共享“躺着让 Agent 干活”的愿景；sofagent 是同源隐喻、灵感来源和上下文来源，而不是简单 fork/改名/替代品。 - 引入 Design Version 与 Product Version 分离：设计快照用 `D0.x/D1.x`，真实软件发布才使用 `v0.x/v1.x`。 - 新增 ADR 风格设计决策记录：记录从历史实现仓库切换为设计仓库、定义控制系统、确立懒人哲学与最智者、认知剪枝、命名系统、版本分离、ideas 目录与分支策略、sofagent 上下文关系等关键 pivot。 - 新增目录/分支策略：active root 保存当前主线，`ideas/` 并排保存候选路线，`ref/ref_repos/` 保存历史/外部参考，Git 分支用于真正互相冲突的大改。 - 明确 bedagent 的产品形态：不是单个 Agent，也不是通用 Agent 框架，而是面向床上思想者的 **Agent 控制系统 = 控制层 + 协议 + 角色系统**。 - 明确三种演化形态：文档协议形态、本地控制层形态、Agent 集群形态；可演化为 Agent 集群，但 MVP 是“想法到安全行动的最小闭环”。 - 明确第一原则：**懒到极致的人是一等公民**。 - 明确第二支柱：**最智者（Sage）**，作为 Agent Brain 的最高判断层，负责主线定位、剪枝、关键追问、取舍和风险判断。 - 建立床/懒/智主题命名系统：**Book of Sloth**（懒人哲学）、**Sage**（最智者）、**Nest**（捕获）、**Dream**（推演沙盒）、**Blanket**（风险保护）、**Hands**（执行沙盒）、**Pillow Note**（短汇报）、**Bedside Journal**（记忆）。 - 新增语义词汇素材库，按床与休息、懒与省力、智慧与判断、思考与推演、捕获与暂存、剪枝与专注、保护与闸门、执行与手脚、沙盒与隔离、语音与低屏幕、汇报与反馈、记忆与反思等语义场整理候选词。 - 明确核心用户：**没有手脚、躺在床上的思想者**。 - 明确懒的分型：保护行动懒、补足表达懒、约束思考懒、强化认知懒。 - 明确快速思考和剪枝节奏：**想的时候快，剪枝要狠，动手前慢，执行要稳**。 - 明确核心链路：`Nest/Capture → Sage → Prune/Focus → Dream/Think → Fold/Plan → Blanket/Gate → Hands/Act → Pillow Note/Report → Bedside Journal/Memory`。 - author: laurenbmoody-web
body:
Replaces the unreliable client-side reminder scheduler with a server-side `pg_cron` job.

**Before:** a `setInterval` in `App.jsx` that only ran if someone had a browser open at Sun 18:00, writing per-device localStorage notifications.

**Now:** a weekly `pg_cron` job (`hor-weekly-reminders`, Sundays 18:00 UTC) calling `public.hor_send_weekly_reminders()`, which scans the current month per active tenant member and writes to the DB `notifications` feed:
- **"missing entries"** when days are unlogged,
- **"confirm month"** near month-end when complete but unsubmitted.

Locked months are skipped; a **6-day per-user de-dupe** prevents double-sends. Reminders now fire reliably without a browser open and reach the nav bell cross-device.

`initializeReminderScheduler()` removed from `App.jsx` so the two don't duplicate. The migration is **already applied to the Cargo project**; the SQL is committed under `supabase/migrations/` for reproducibility. Build passes.

## 概要

重説 Ⅱ取引条件で既に自動充当している **違約金%** を、**契約書の表紙「違約金の額」** にも展開し、重説⇄契約書を整合させます（「契約書側続行」分）。

## 内容

| 項目 | フィールド | 形式 | 36-1 | 区分(37-1/38-1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 違約金の額 | `daikin.iyakukin_wariai` | 「2.売買代金のN%相当額」を選択+%値 | X65/AF65（P65・AM65=□） | X70/AF70（P70・AM70=□） |

- `KeiyakuDaikin` に `iyakukin_wariai`（売買代金の%）を追加。契約書抽出プロンプト（`_EXTRACT_SYS_KEIYAKU` の `daikin`）にも反映。
- 表紙の違約金ブロックは重説と同一構造のため、選択ロジックを `_iyakukin_select()` に集約し重説/契約書で共用。座標は実WB（`BC_template_36-1` / `BC_template_37-1` / `octo601`=38-1）から逆引きで確定。37-1/38-1 は契約書レイアウトが同一のため「区分」キーで共用。
- **未指定時は非改変**：`iyakukin_wariai` が無ければ表紙の選択を触らず、テンプレ既定（20%）を温存。

##### 🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New [Credentials](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-credentials) virtual authenticator, available via [browserContext.credentials](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-credentials), lets tests register passkeys and answer `navigator.credentials.create()` / `navigator.credentials.get()` ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

```js
const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
  id: credentialId,
  userHandle,
  privateKey,
  publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();

const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.
```

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with [credentials.get()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-credentials#credentials-get), and seed it into later tests — see [Credentials](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-credentials) for details.

##### 🗃️ Web Storage

New [WebStorage](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-webstorage) API, available via [page.localStorage](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-local-storage) and [page.sessionStorage](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-session-storage), reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

```js
await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();
```

##### New APIs

##### Network

- [apiResponse.securityDetails()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apiresponse#api-response-security-details) and [apiResponse.serverAddr()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apiresponse#api-response-server-addr) mirror the browser-side [response.securityDetails()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-response#response-security-details) and [response.serverAddr()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-response#response-server-addr).

##### Browser and Screencast

- New option `artifactsDir` in [browserType.connectOverCDP()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp) controls where artifacts such as traces and downloads are stored when attached to an existing browser.
- New option `cursor` in [screencast.showActions()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-actions) controls the cursor decoration rendered for pointer actions.
- The `onFrame` callback in [screencast.start()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-start) now receives a `timestamp` of when the frame was presented by the browser.

- The [testOptions.video](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testoptions#test-options-video) option now supports the same set of modes as `trace`: new `'on-all-retries'`, `'retain-on-first-failure'` and `'retain-on-failure-and-retries'` values. See the [video modes table](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-use-options#video-modes) for which runs are recorded and kept in each mode.

body:
## Problem
The Pages deploy workflow merged in #3 failed:
> Get Pages site failed. Please verify that the repository has Pages enabled and configured to build using GitHub Actions

This is because GitHub Pages was never turned on for the repo, and the fix for it (`enablement: true`) landed on the old branch *after* #3 was already merged, so it never reached `main`.

## Fix
Add `enablement: true` to `actions/configure-pages`. This makes the workflow enable Pages (with the GitHub Actions source) itself on first run — no manual Settings change required.

```yaml
- name: Configure Pages
  uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
  with:
    enablement: true
```

## After merge
The workflow re-runs on the push to `main`, enables Pages, and deploys. The site goes live at:
- `https://rrichard-gcps.github.io/analytics-template-generator/` → redirects to the studio
- `https://rrichard-gcps.github.io/analytics-template-generator/gcps-theme-studio.html` → studio directly

body:
## Summary

Implements issues #6, #7, #8, and #14 as four atomic commits — one per check.

---

### #6 — `reentrancy-risk` (High)

Detects `invoke_contract` / `invoke_contract_check` called **after** a storage write without a subsequent re-read inside `#[contractimpl]` methods (checks-effects-interactions violation).

- `crates/checks/src/reentrancy.rs` — visitor tracks write→invoke ordering
- Fixture: `test-contracts/reentrancy-vulnerable/` / `test-contracts/reentrancy-safe/`

### #7 — `integer-division-truncation` (Medium)

Flags `/` on non-literal operands and `/=` inside `#[contractimpl]` methods. Literal-only `6 / 2` is explicitly ignored per the acceptance criteria.

- `crates/checks/src/division.rs`
- Fixture: `test-contracts/division-vulnerable/` / `test-contracts/division-safe/`

### #8 — `panic-in-contract` (Medium)

Detects `.unwrap()`, `.expect(…)`, `panic!(…)`, and `unreachable!()` inside `#[contractimpl]` methods. Covers all four patterns from the acceptance criteria.

- `crates/checks/src/panics.rs`
- Fixture: `test-contracts/panic-vulnerable/` / `test-contracts/panic-safe/`

### #14 — `missing-zero-address-check` (Medium)

Flags sensitive admin/ownership methods (`set_owner`, `set_admin`, `initialize`, `transfer_ownership`, …) that accept an `Address` parameter with no zero/default assertion, `require_auth`, or validation call.

- `crates/checks/src/zero_address.rs`
- Fixture: `test-contracts/zero-address-vulnerable/` / `test-contracts/zero-address-safe/`

---

### Registration & docs

- All four checks added to `default_checks()` in `crates/checks/src/lib.rs`
- Four new sections added to `docs/checks.md`

---

### What was tested

Each `.rs` file contains inline unit tests covering:
- The vulnerable pattern is flagged with the correct severity
- The safe counterpart produces no findings
- Literal-only operands (division check) are ignored
- Non-`#[contractimpl]` blocks are not flagged

closes  #6

| **PR** | this PR (P0 — deterministic swap on an engaged Coach's Pick) |

| **Codex status** | NON-BLOCKING (deterministic plan mutation; no write/schema/proof change) |
| **Owner action required** | No (autonomy). v48→**v49** spot-check welcome. |
| **Merge recommendation** | merge-ready |

---

### Concern (one per PR)

Your v48 re-test screenshot: **"Let's do rdls instead of deadlifts" didn't swap** — it hit the coach-down fallback ("I couldn't reach the coach just now…") with no "Swapped Deadlift → RDL". Two deterministic causes found.

### Root causes (verified)

1. **Gating:** `tryApplyPlanMutation` required a formally-**started** `activePlannedSession`, but a typed **Coach's Pick** (`typeSuggestedWorkout`) only sets `coachSuggestionEngaged` and leaves the plan in `lastIntentData` — so there was no mutable session and the swap fell through to the coach.
2. **Curly apostrophe:** "Let's" with a curly `'` (U+2019, mobile autocorrect) wasn't stripped by the `LEAD` regex, so the captured substitute became `"let's do rdls"` (garbage) even when a session existed. (Verified: `classifyMutationIntent("Let’s do rdls instead of deadlifts")` previously returned `substitute: "let's do rdls"`.)

### What changed

- **`public/app.js`** — new `ensureActivePlannedSession()` materializes an engaged Coach's Pick suggestion (carrying its prescription via `normalizePlanExercise`) into a live, mutable session. `tryApplyPlanMutation` now **classifies first**, then materializes — so a swap/skip fires in BOTH the started-session and engaged-suggestion states, while **freestyle/no-plan logging is untouched** (no materialization on non-mutations).
- **`public/planMutationIntent.js`** — normalize curly `'`→`'` at the top of `classifyMutationIntent`, so mobile-autocorrected lead-ins strip correctly and the substitute is clean (`rdls`).
- Shell `v48 → v49`.

### Trust / scope safety

- [x] **No write-path / schema / proof-field / `test_mode` / trust-loop change** — this mutates the in-memory plan/composer only; preview→approve→write untouched.
- [x] Freestyle/no-plan logging untouched (materialize only on a genuine classified mutation).
- [x] Deterministic — no LLM in the swap path (the whole point: it works when the coach is down).

### Tests

`npm test` → 2690 / 0 / 0. New: curly-apostrophe lead strips to a clean substitute (+ straight-apostrophe parity); `tryApplyPlanMutation` classifies before materializing; `ensureActivePlannedSession` promotes an engaged suggestion from `lastIntentData` carrying its prescription.

### Note

This is from the same v48 re-test session that exercised the closeout fix (#579). The closeout (`log it`/`done`) path still wants your live re-confirm; this PR fixes the swap that the screenshot showed failing.

author: awwesomeman
body:
## Summary

The three metrics exposing `inference=` (`ic`, `quantile_spread`, `k_spread`) typed the method as a closed union but never enforced it at runtime, so a method outside the intended set behaved inconsistently and silently:

- `ic(inference=HANSEN_HODRICK)` actually ran Hansen-Hodrick HAC (polymorphic `compute` dispatch).
- `quantile_spread` / `k_spread` swallowed any non-`NeweyWest` method into the non-overlap path with no flag.
- A non-`Inference` object (e.g. a string) hit an `AttributeError` deep in dispatch.

This adds one consistent validation surface:

- `IncompatibleInferenceError` (`factrix._errors`, exported as `fx.IncompatibleInferenceError`); message lists the metric's allowed set.
- Per-metric module-level `applicable_inference = {NON_OVERLAPPING, NEWEY_WEST}`, validated on entry via a single shared `_check_applicable_inference` chokepoint.
- `resolve_applicable_inference` for discovery, gated on the callable carrying an `inference` parameter so the singleton-inference sibling `quantile_spread_vw` correctly reports none.
- `HansenHodrick` stays excluded from all three allowlists (per the original design); the `factrix.inference` SSOT docstring is rewritten to describe the allowlist rather than the old silent-fallback rationale.

The legitimate, data-driven small-cross-section bootstrap override (`FEW_ASSETS` / `inference_overridden`) is unchanged — only the unidentified-inference path is removed.

Per the epic-deferral convention (#575 tracks #558 follow-ups), no CHANGELOG prose is added here; the only doc touch is the mandatory `llms-full.txt` public-symbol entry.

## Test plan

- New per-metric tests: `HansenHodrick` raises, non-`Inference` raises, allowlisted members pass (`test_ic.py`, `test_quantile.py`, `test_k_spread.py`).
- New discovery tests: allowlist readable for the three metrics; `None` for `quantile_spread_vw` / `hit_rate`.
- Full suite green (1469 passed, 4 skipped); `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy factrix` clean.

Closes #696

author: otenim
body:
## Problem

There was no way to fix or replace the intrinsic calibration stored on a
`sensor_msgs/msg/CameraInfo` topic in a recorded rosbag. A common need is: a bag
was recorded with a wrong or placeholder calibration, and a corrected
calibration is later produced with the standard ROS tooling
(`camera_calibration` / `camera_info_manager`), which yields a YAML file. This PR
makes it possible to apply that YAML back onto the bag.

## Solution

Adds a new `bagwiz cam-info` command group with a `replace` subcommand:

```
bagwiz cam-info replace <bag> <calib.yaml> <topic> [-o OUT] [-w] [--frame-id ID]
```

It swaps the calibration carried by a single `sensor_msgs/msg/CameraInfo` topic
for the values in a standard ROS `camera_calibration` / `camera_info_manager`
YAML file (`image_width`, `image_height`, `camera_matrix`, `distortion_model`,
`distortion_coefficients`, `rectification_matrix`, `projection_matrix`).

For each message on the topic the calibration fields (`height`, `width`,
`distortion_model`, `d`, `k`, `r`, `p`) are taken from the YAML, while the
original header timestamp, `frame_id` (unless `--frame-id` is given),
`binning_x/y`, and `roi` are preserved. Every other topic is copied verbatim.
Like `traj join` and `convert msg geo`, the bag is rewritten in place by
default, or to a new bag with `-o/--output`.

Implementation reuses the shared read/process/write rewrite seam
(`core::pipeline`) and the in-place swap helper. The per-message transform
deserializes the original CDR into a typed `CameraInfo` via `rmw_deserialize`,
overwrites only the calibration fields, and re-serializes with `rmw_serialize`,
so all preserved fields survive untouched. A new core helper parses the
`camera_calibration` YAML and validates matrix sizes (`k`/`r` = 9, `p` = 12, `d`
non-empty) before any write.

## Test plan

- Unit tests for the YAML parser (valid parse, wrong matrix sizes, missing keys,
  empty distortion coefficients).
- End-to-end command test covering in-place rewrite, `-o` output, `--frame-id`
  override, and missing / wrong-type topic errors; asserts calibration fields are
  replaced while `header`, `binning`, and `roi` are preserved and other topics
  are copied verbatim.
- New sources and gtest targets wired into CMake; `sensor_msgs` linked onto the
  executable.
- Documented in `README.md` and `docs/commands/cam-info.md`.

CI (build across humble/jazzy/lyrical, pre-commit, spell-check) runs on this PR.

## Summary

When a WeCom bot user selected an option on an `AskUserQuestion` template card and tapped submit, the bot resolved the question with `answers` as a `string[]`. The Anthropic SDK expects `AskUserQuestionOutput.answers` to be a `Record<string, string>` keyed by the question text, so the model treated the submission as if the user had not answered.

`WeComBotService.buildAnswersFromCardEvent` now returns the map shape, and the WeCom template-card tests (plus the generic chat-service `AskUserQuestion` test) have been updated to assert it. A new multi-select test verifies that multiple selected option labels are comma-joined under the correct question key.

Note: the Feishu card handler currently builds the same `string[]` shape and will need a matching fix in a follow-up.

## Test plan

- `npm run test:server` passes (705 tests).
- Lint passes on the changed files.

body:
## Context

This PR prepares the merge between the `systemallica/python-redsys` fork and the original `ddiazpinto/python-redsys` repository.

The goal is to bring back the changes that have accumulated in the fork over time, grouped into descriptive commits so they can be reviewed and merged into the original project more easily.

## Included changes

- Replaces `pycrypto` with `pycryptodome`, keeping a conservative migration from the historical `Crypto` API.
- Migrates project packaging and tooling to `uv`, `pyproject.toml`, `ruff`, and `pre-commit`.
- Modernizes Redsys request/response handling and consolidates internal constants.
- Adds support and tests for changes introduced in the fork, including BIZUM, 12-character order IDs, and additional response parameters.
- Adds CI and release workflows.
- Refreshes documentation, changelog, and license metadata.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest`

author: tindang97
body:
## F11 — write the §5 scope sidecar atomically

`_build_entry` wrote the scope sidecar (`tasks/<slug>/scope-snapshot.json`) with a raw `write_text`. A crash mid-write could leave a torn/empty file that the next gate misreads as `scope_snapshot_tampered` ("diverged") or "missing" — a confusing false tamper, not a real one. Deep-audit finding **F11**.

### Fix
```python
# _build_entry, declared-scope branch:
- side.write_text(payload, encoding="utf-8")
+ _atomic_write(side, payload)   # temp file + os.replace, like save_state
```
The payload is passed **verbatim** (no trailing newline), so the on-disk bytes — and thus the `snapshot_md5` integrity anchor that `_scope_findings` checks — are **byte-identical** to before. The reader and the UNDECLARED unlink path are untouched. This gives the sidecar the same crash-atomicity guarantee `state.json` already has (the save-state-harden / F7 theme).

### Evidence
- `test_scope_sidecar_written_atomically` — the sidecar Path appears in the `_atomic_write` call list (RED when it was a raw `write_text`).
- `test_sidecar_md5_anchor_preserved` — on-disk md5 == state anchor **and** a clean build gate PASSes (guards against a trailing-newline regression).
- `test_undeclared_task_writes_no_sidecar` — the skip/unlink path is unchanged.
- Engine mirrored ×3, ENGINE_MD5 re-pinned `310a8ed7 → 73f9609e`. Full suite **1806/0**, seam audit clean (83 tasks).

Adds explicit node-type selection to bootstrap so the CLI surface is stable for the two-phase prompt-service migration (Phase 1 colocated → Phase 2 central).

## Three node types

| `region` (default) | Any operator who isn't on the prompts team | Pastes a team-issued HMAC key during bootstrap. Default `PROMPT_SERVICE_URL=https://prompts.opuspopuli.org` (overridable via `--prompt-service-url`). |

The op-compose wrapper exports them; the [opuspopuli-node colocation overlay](https://github.com/OpusPopuli/opuspopuli-node/pull/15) consumes them. |
