body:
This pull request adds the GUT (Godot Unit Test) testing framework as an addon and establishes the core project structure for a Pathfinder 2e campaign adaptation.

## Summary
The changes introduce a complete testing infrastructure via the GUT addon and organize the project with a modular directory structure for game development. The GUT addon provides unit testing capabilities for Godot, while the new directory structure supports organizing game mechanics, data, and UI components.

## Key Changes

### GUT Testing Framework (addons/gut/)
- Added complete GUT addon with 100+ files including:
  - Core testing engine (`gut.gd`, `gut_config.gd`, `gut_loader.gd`)
  - CLI support for command-line test execution (`cli/optparse.gd`, `cli/gut_cli.gd`)
  - GUI components for test result visualization (`gui/GutBottomPanel.gd`, `gui/ResultsTree.gd`, `gui/OutputText.gd`)
  - Test utilities: input mocking (`input_sender.gd`, `input_factory.gd`), object doubling (`doubler.gd`), stubbing (`stubber.gd`, `stub_params.gd`), and spying (`spy.gd`)
  - Result export functionality (`junit_xml_export.gd`, `result_exporter.gd`)
  - Supporting utilities for string manipulation, logging, error tracking, and signal watching

### Project Structure
- **core/**: Game mechanics foundation
  - `dice.gd`, `degrees.gd`, `ids.gd` - Core game systems
  - `checks/`, `modifiers/`, `actions/` - Organized subsystems with placeholder directories
  - Additional placeholder directories for conditions, creatures, difficulty, encounters, progression, and variant rules

- **data/**: Game content organization
  - Placeholder directories for ancestries, armor, backgrounds, classes, conditions, creatures, feats, heritages, items, mythic content, runes, spells, and weapons

- **game/**: Runtime game systems
  - Placeholder directories for autoload, character, combat, HUD, sprites, and UI

### Configuration
- Added `.gitignore` for Godot 4 project files
- Updated `README.md` with project description
- Added `plugin.cfg` for GUT addon registration

## Notable Implementation Details
- GUT provides comprehensive testing features including parameterized tests, signal watching, input simulation, and object mocking
- The framework includes both editor integration (bottom panel, shortcuts) and CLI support for CI/CD pipelines
- Project uses Godot 4 format with `.uid` files for resource identification
- Modular structure allows for organized development of PF2e mechanics and content

author: davedbase
body:
This introduces a new package, `@solid-primitives/animation`, providing reactive and imperative wrappers for the [Web Animations API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Animations_API). All primitives follow the existing `make` / `create` convention: `make*` is imperative and returns immediately, `create*` is a reactive wrapper that re-runs on dependency change and cancels on owner disposal.

**Primitives:**

- **`makeAnimate` / `createAnimate`** — thin wrapper around `element.animate()`, the reactive version re-runs whenever `target`, `keyframes`, or `options` change
- **`makeScrollAnimation` / `createScrollAnimation`** — scroll-driven animation via `ScrollTimeline`; no scroll listeners or RAF loops needed
- **`makeViewAnimation` / `createViewAnimation`** — viewport-driven animation via `ViewTimeline`; replaces the IntersectionObserver + class-toggle pattern. Includes `rangeStart`/`rangeEnd` options (defaulting to `"entry 0%"` / `"entry 100%"`) to scope animation to the entry phase only
- **`makeFlip`** — FLIP layout animation; `snapshot()` before the DOM change, `flip()` after
- **`makeStagger` / `createStagger`** — staggered WAAPI animation across a list of elements with a per-element delay offset
- **`makeAnimationGroup` / `createAnimationGroup`** — coordinates a list of `Animation` objects as a single unit; all five control methods (`play`, `pause`, `cancel`, `reverse`, `finish`) forwarded simultaneously. The reactive variant re-derives the group via `createMemo` whenever the animation list changes
- **`makeMotionPath` / `createMotionPath`** — animates an element along a CSS `offset-path` using `offsetDistance`; sets `offsetAnchor: center` so the element center tracks the path
- **`makeSequence`** — chains animation factories into a sequential playlist; factories are called lazily, each only when its predecessor finishes

Also includes a full Storybook stories file with interactive demos for each primitive, and a Vitest test suite covering the reactive wrappers, lifecycle cancellation, and option forwarding.

  * Added a new animation package with helpers for basic, scroll-driven, view-driven, FLIP, staggered, grouped, sequential, motion-path, and presence animations.

author: ignaciomagana
body:
## Summary

Reverts `33a94ae` ("fix mock data selection"), which changed the GW selection-injection proposal in both mock generators from the **population-matched** draw to a **broad uniform** draw. That change is the dominant cause of the spectral-siren recovery blowing up (gamma/alpha railing to the prior edges on both `powerlaw+peak` and `gp1d_m1`).

## Why the broad proposal breaks recovery

The selection integral mu(theta) is importance-sampled over the injections with weight `p_pop(theta)/pdraw`. Its effective sample size enters the likelihood twice:

- `selection_log_correction` returns **`-inf` when `Neff <= 5*Nobs`** (Vitale 2022), and
- adds **`+Nobs*(Nobs+3)/(2*Neff)`**, which *grows* as Neff shrinks.

Measured on a matched mock (nobs=120):

| proposal | Neff at truth | alpha: truth->5.85 |
|---|---|---|
| broad uniform (33a94ae) | **492**  (< 5*Nobs=600 -> `logL(truth) = -inf`) | **+25** (rails) |
| population-matched (this revert) | **133,394** | **-11** (truth preferred) |

The broad proposal wastes ~68% of injections beyond the mass taper, so Neff at the truth falls below the `5*Nobs` cliff -> the likelihood is `-inf` at the injected truth and the sampler is forced to the only finite region (extreme params). The population-matched proposal gives Neff >> cliff at the truth and *collapses* only at extreme theta, where the cliff correctly excludes it. After the revert the real (unpatched) likelihood is finite at the truth and prefers the injected alpha.

## Verification

- Generator restored to the population proposal in both `generate_mock_data.py` and `generate_mock_bright_sirens.py`.
- `tests/test_mock_generator_taper.py`: the 5 taper tests pass; the selection-proposal regression test added in 33a94ae is removed with the revert (it asserted the harmful broad-proposal behaviour).
- The inference code is **bit-identical** between the current master and the older "known-good" commits (40e76d2, c589c1b) on the spectral-siren path, so this was never an inference regression.

## Known residual (separate, pre-existing, milder)

Even on a clean population-proposal mock, gamma drifts toward the prior edge. Root cause: **the generator never injects gamma** -- `pop.gamma` is stored but never used in the redshift draw (hosts are drawn `~ dV_c/dz` regardless), so the effective injected rate is flat-comoving (= inference gamma=1, not 0), and at `zmax=0.1` there is almost no lever arm to constrain gamma. This needs a generator change (modulate the redshift draw by `(1+z)^(gamma-1)`) and/or a larger zmax; it is not an inference bug. Tracked separately.

Supersedes #108 (that PR rewrote the selection regression test this revert removes).

---

## Update: also inject the rate evolution (gamma) — second commit

Follow-up diagnosis of the *residual* gamma drift (which persisted with higher nlive and on a clean mock): the generator drew host/event redshifts `~ dV_c/dz` **regardless of `pop.gamma`**, while the inference model is `p(z) ~ dV_c/dz (1+z)^(gamma-1)`. So the data effectively carried gamma=1 (flat comoving) but was labelled gamma=0 — gamma could never be recovered at its nominal value, and with no redshift lever arm at `zmax~0.1` it railed to the prior edge (no amount of nlive helps — there is no information).

Second commit weights GW-event host acceptance by `(1+z)^(gamma-1)` so detected events follow the inference model, and adds a `--gamma` CLI arg. Verified at zmax=0.5: **recovered gamma now tracks the injected value with unit slope** (inj 0 → peak ~0–1 with sharp PE; inj 3 → peak shifts by +3). 

Two caveats, both expected (not code bugs): gamma is only constrainable with enough redshift lever arm (`zmax >= ~0.3`); and a residual high-gamma offset grows with the PE distance uncertainty (PE-smeared events vs noise-free injections through the steep `dV_c/dz` prior) — a PE-realism effect, separate from this fix.

author: antonelli182
body:
## Context

`ce-code-review` of the three merged follow-up PRs (#104/#105/#106) surfaced two real defects introduced by the atomic-write change in #104, plus one doc gap. This PR fixes them.

## Findings fixed

**P1 — `.env` left world-readable; tighter perms clobbered.** The create-temp-then-`renameSync` in `writeEnvVar` produces a fresh file at the umask default (`0644`) and, on an existing file, *replaces* it — discarding any `0600` the old in-place write preserved. The file holds the **durable** Machina `X-Api-Token`. Fix: `chmodSync(.env, 0600)` after the rename, best-effort, matching the repo's existing secrets-file convention (`credentials.ts:110`, `anthropic-oauth.ts:203`). Flagged independently by **security + correctness + learnings**.

**P2 — orphaned `.tmp` on rename failure.** `writeEnvVar` and `saveMcpConfigs` left the temp file behind if `renameSync` threw after the temp write. Wrap both in try/catch that unlinks the temp and rethrows; the original target stays intact. (reliability + testing)

**P3 — incomplete tool contract.** `get_agent_config` description listed `name/provider/url` but omitted `hasToken`. Added. (api-contract)

## Tests

- Assert `.env` is `0600` after `writeEnvVar` (POSIX-guarded skip on Windows).
- Cover the `Authorization`-header branch of `summarizeMcpServers` `hasToken` (was only `X-Api-Token`).
- Correct the `atomic-config-writes` header comment that overclaimed `saveMcpConfigs` coverage.

## Deliberately deferred (separate follow-ups)

- **Extract a shared `atomicWriteFileSync` helper** — the idiom is now in 6 files (maintainability P2). Best done as its own codebase-wide refactor, not half-applied here.
- `durability.ts` non-randomised `.tmp` suffix (pre-existing race); `summarizeMcpServers` URL with embedded query-string creds (pre-existing edge); concurrent-writer lost-update (inherent to read-modify-write, documented in `token-ledger.ts`).

## Verification

`npm run build` clean; `atomic-config-writes` + `mcp-helpers` + `connections` 32/32 (the `0600` assertion runs and passes on macOS CI/Linux).

author: crayy8
body:
Two comparison sites used case-sensitive macros (TSTRCMP / TSTRNCMP) where the filesystem requires case-insensitive comparison:

1. get_inum_from_directory_path (exact-match cache hit check): TSTRCMP -> TSTRICMP The cache stores paths in actual disk case (from FindFirstFileW). When the caller's path has different case, TSTRCMP failed even though the cache held an exact logical match. The code fell through and started search_directory_recursive FROM the matched directory (treating it as a parent prefix), so no child ever matched the target and the lookup returned LOGICAL_INVALID_INUM. Bug triggered on second+ access once cache was warm; first access (cache cold) always succeeded via TSTRICMP in the walk itself.

2. search_directory_recursive (cache warm-up path decision): TSTRNCMP -> _wcsnicmp Decides whether to promote an intermediate directory to always_cache=true. With case mismatch between current_path (disk case) and target_path (caller case), the promotion never fired, leaving the search path in the cache only opportunistically.

There is no TSTRNICMP macro in tsk_os.h so _wcsnicmp is used directly at site 2; it is already used at four other sites in this file.

author: samfreund-qc
body:
## Summary

Adds `QcPerfNpuLogger`, a standalone systemd-compatible daemon that uses the public `qcperf_*` API to continuously sample all four NPU metrics and write a point-in-time snapshot to `/var/log/qcperf/npu_metrics.log` once per second.

## What it does

The daemon connects to `QC_PERF_BACKEND_DSP_NPU`, samples at 100 ms intervals, and fires a streaming callback every 1000 ms. Each callback atomically replaces the output file (write to `.npu_metrics.tmp`, then `rename(2)`) so readers never observe a partial write. The most recent sample per metric within each streaming window is kept; earlier samples are discarded.

Output format:
```
Q6 Utilization:42.50
Q6 Clock:614400.00
HVX Utilization:12.30
HMX Utilization:8.70
```

## Files added

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `qcperf/npu_logger/src/qcperf_npu_logger.c` | Daemon implementation (`main`, callbacks, helpers) |
| `qcperf/npu_logger/systemd/qcperf-npu-logger.service` | systemd unit with hardened sandbox |
| `qcperf/npu_logger/CMakeLists.txt` | Build rules, opt-in via `-DBUILD_NPU_LOGGER=ON` |

## Build

```bash
cmake -S qcperf -B build-linux-aarch64-release \
    -DTARGET_ARCH=linux-aarch64 \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DProjectVersion="0.1.0.0" \
    -DBACKENDS="CPU;NPU;DUMMY" \
    -DBUILD_NPU_LOGGER=ON
cmake --build build-linux-aarch64-release
```

The target is off by default. Enabling it without `NPU` in `BACKENDS` emits a CMake warning and skips the build gracefully.

## Runtime requirement

`/usr/lib/libcdsprpc.so` must be present on the target device. If absent, the dynamic linker fails at process startup — this is a constraint of the underlying FastRPC transport, not something the daemon can work around.

## systemd unit highlights

- `ProtectSystem=strict` + `LogsDirectory=qcperf` (creates `/var/log/qcperf` before the namespace is set up, required for first install)
- `PrivateTmp=true`, `NoNewPrivileges=true`
- `Restart=on-failure` with a 5 s back-off
- Logs to the systemd journal via `SyslogIdentifier=qcperf-npu-logger`

## Testing

Run on a Qualcomm Linux ARM64 device with `libcdsprpc.so` present:

```bash
# Start the daemon manually
/usr/bin/QcPerfNpuLogger &

# Verify output
cat /var/log/qcperf/npu_metrics.log

# Or via systemd
systemctl enable --now qcperf-npu-logger
journalctl -u qcperf-npu-logger -f
```

## Checklist

- [x] BSD 3-Clause copyright header present
- [x] Single exit point per function
- [x] All variables declared at top of function (C89 style)
- [x] No `goto`, no always-true loops
- [x] Yoda-style null checks (`NULL == ptr`)
- [x] `calloc` used instead of `malloc`; pointers set to `NULL` after `free`
- [x] `snake_case` / `PascalCase` / `UPPER_CASE` naming conventions followed
- [x] Doxygen comments on all functions
- [ ] `clang-format` — `clang-format` not available on the development host; please run before merge: `clang-format -i qcperf/npu_logger/src/qcperf_npu_logger.c`

author: ggondim
body:
> **Stacks on #30 (P2).** Because #30 isn't merged, the diff below includes P2's
> changes too. Review #30 first; the **P7-specific** files are:
> `src/db/migrations/20260601000007_add-fact-origin.cjs`, `src/memory/provenance.js`
> (+test), `src/memory/facts/store.js` (insertFact stamp, +`store-origin.test.js`),
> and the `created_by_origin` edits in `src/memory/search/filters.js` /
> `hybrid.js` / `visibility.integration.test.js`.

## Problem (a gap P2 leaves open)

P2 enforces private-kind visibility off `created_by_device_id` — an **INTEGER FK
to `device`**, which is only populated for **paired** devices. Local CLI/hook
writes stamp it **NULL**, and NULL rows are always visible. So the moment two
**people** share one DB + namespace via ordinary local installs, they see each
other's `private` / `session` facts — private memory isn't actually private
between people (only between paired devices of one owner).

## Fix

Introduce **`created_by_origin`** (TEXT): a stable per-owner identity stamped on
**every** write, resolved by a single helper used by **both** sides so read and
write can never drift:

- `src/memory/provenance.js` — `currentOrigin(ctx)`: paired RPC device id →
  `ctx.device.id` → local install id from `config.json` (`device.id`, a UUID) →
  `null`. Returned as text.
- **Write:** `insertFact` stamps `created_by_origin = currentOrigin()`.
- **Read:** `resolvePrivacyScope` resolves the same `currentOrigin(ctx)`, and
  `buildVisibilityClause` now scopes private kinds by `created_by_origin`
  (plain TEXT compare — no more INTEGER/UUID coercion). Legacy `NULL`-origin
  rows stay globally visible (back-compat, no backfill).

`created_by_device_id` / `created_by_agent` are untouched (still provenance for
paired devices / the `--device`/`--agent` filters).

## Migration

`20260601000007_add-fact-origin` — adds the nullable TEXT column + index.
Additive and back-compatible: a pre-P7 build ignores the column; a P7 build
treats existing NULL rows as legacy-visible.

## Tests

```
npx vitest run src/memory/provenance.test.js \
  src/memory/facts/store-origin.test.js \
  src/memory/search/visibility.integration.test.js
```

- `provenance.test.js` — `currentOrigin` precedence (RPC → ctx → config → null).
- `store-origin.test.js` — `insertFact` persists `created_by_origin`.
- `visibility.integration.test.js` (PGlite, real SQL) — updated to the origin
  column: owner A's private fact hidden from owner B, visible to A; shared
  visible to both; legacy NULL visible to both; `scope=off` / no-origin fail open.

Full suite green except the pre-existing, unrelated `cli.connect.test.js`
environmental failure.

author: benjaminpkane
body:
## What

Adds an `onChangeCommitted` callback to `BaseSlider` (and the `SingleValueSlider`/`MultiValueSlider` variants). It fires **once when an interaction completes** — a knob drag release, a track click, or an input blur — as distinct from the continuous, debounced `onChange`.

## Why

Today the only outbound callback is `onChange`, which is debounced (`debounceDelay`, default 200ms). That forces a choice: a high debounce gives one late update (≈ on release) but no live feedback during a drag; `debounceDelay={0}` gives live updates but fires on every intermediate value.

`onChangeCommitted` lets a consumer have both: pair a responsive `onChange` (`debounceDelay={0}`) for live preview during a drag with a **single commit on release**.

## Changes

- `SliderBar`: fire `onChangeCommitted` on drag-end (the document `mouseup` that ends a knob drag — tracking the last dragged value, since `mouseup` carries no position) and on track click.
- `Slider`: fire `onChangeCommitted` on numeric input blur; thread the prop through `SingleValueSlider`/`MultiValueSlider`; document it.

No behavior change for existing consumers — `onChangeCommitted` is optional and additive.

Stories demonstrating it are in a companion design-system-documentation PR.

`RAPPORT.html` was capped at `900px` with tight spacing, making it cramped on wide monitors and sub-optimal for A4 PDF export. All changes are CSS-only; no content was touched.

## Layout & typography
- `max-width: 900px → 1100px`, `padding: 2rem → 3rem 4rem`
- `font-size: 10.5pt → 11pt`, `line-height: 1.7 → 1.8`

author: 0xpatrickbot
body:
Gap-revealing prototype of the ocap-disciplined SWE loop design session
recorded at journal2 `entries/2026/06/25/133528Z-artifact-liaison-718bf0.md`
(slate item P0). There is no separate design PR — the lifecycle described
in the job spec IS the spec; this probe surfaces the gaps that sharpen the
D1 (exec/Spawner) and D2 (clone+worktree provisioning) design jobs.

**This PR stays DRAFT.** The panel/cleaner/fixer/un-draft chain does not
apply. The maintainer reads the gap report, revises the design jobs, and
either authorizes a follow-up build or closes this probe as superseded.

---

## Gaps surfaced

### Gap 1: No clone operation on any capability surface

**Where in the design.** `packages/exo-git/src/git.js` (full `GitBackend`
typedef), `packages/git/src/native-git-backend.js` (full implementation),
`packages/exo-git/src/git-remote.js` (`GitRemote` exo), and
`packages/daemon/src/host.js` `provideGit`.

**Verbatim quote.** From the job spec: "clone a repo" — step 1 of the
target loop. From the code: `provideGit(mountCap, petName)` — mints a
Git cap over an EXISTING daemon-minted mount.

**What's needed to implement.** A primitive that, given a source URL
(or another `GitRemote` fetch policy) and a destination mount, runs
`git clone` into the destination and returns a new Git cap over the
populated worktree. The caller's code-mode agent cannot touch host paths
directly; the operation must go through a host-controlled capability.

**Candidate resolutions.**
- **A.** Add a `clone(url, destMount, petName, credential)` method to
  `EndoHost` parallel to `provideGit`. The daemon runs `git clone`
  into the `destMount`'s backing path, then calls `formulateGit` on it
  and returns the cap. Trade-off: simple and consistent with the
  existing `provideGit` shape; requires the caller already hold a
  destination `Mount` cap (which the code-mode agent cannot mint either
  — see Gap 2's connection to provisioning).
- **B.** Extend `GitRemote` with a `clone(destMount, petName)` operation.
  The `GitRemote` already holds the URL and credential; a `clone` method
  on it would be ergonomic. Trade-off: blurs the `GitRemote` as a
  "live-repo remote" abstraction into a "provisioning" abstraction.
- **C.** Introduce a separate `GitProvisioner` capability (daemon-minted,
  bound to a local bare-remote URL or `GitRemote` policy) that the host
  grants into code-mode specifically for SWE-loop work. Trade-off:
  cleanest conceptual separation but a new top-level cap type.

**Maintainer's call:** design revision — the protocol for handing a
cloned-repo `Git` cap into code-mode needs to be specified before
implementation can proceed.

---

### Gap 2: No worktree-add operation on the EndoGit surface

**Where in the design.** `packages/exo-git/src/git.js` line 308
(`worktree()` method) and the full `GitBackend` typedef (no
`addWorktree` / `worktreeAdd` method).

**Verbatim quote.** Job spec Gap 2: "`worktree()` (`packages/exo-git/src/git.js:308`)
returns the *current* worktree authority; nothing *mints* a new worktree."
Confirmed against code: `worktree()` is `return worktreeAuthority()`,
which returns the `EndoMount` the cap was constructed over. There is no
`worktreeAdd` on `GitBackend`, `EndoGit`, or `NativeGitBackend`.

**What's needed to implement.** A primitive that runs `git worktree add
<path> <branch>` and returns a new `(Git, Mount)` pair bound to the
freshly-created linked worktree, confined to that path.

**Candidate resolutions.**
- **A.** Add `addLinkedWorktree(branch, destMount, petName)` to the
  `EndoGit` exo, backed by a new `GitBackend.addLinkedWorktree` method
  on the native backend. Returns a new `Git` cap over `destMount`.
  Trade-off: keeps the worktree operation on the cap that owns the
  common git dir; but the `destMount` cannot be minted by code-mode
  (see Gap 1's provisioning connection).
- **B.** Delegate worktree provisioning to `EndoHost.provideLinkedWorktree(gitCap, destMount, branch, petName)`.
  The host mints the linked worktree and returns a fresh `Git` cap.
  Trade-off: consistent pattern with `provideGit`; explicit host
  authority over the `git worktree add` operation.
- **C.** Treat linked worktrees as a deferred concern: the SWE-loop
  probe can be scoped to single-worktree repos (no `git worktree add`
  needed) and worktree support added later. Trade-off: reduces the
  scope of the initial design job but defers a real user need.

**Maintainer's call:** design revision — whether worktree-add is in
scope for D2 or deferred is a design decision.

---

### Gap 3: No exec/spawn power in code-mode

**Where in the design.** `packages/agentry/src/execute/preset.js`
`CodeModePowers` typedef (no `exec` or `spawn` field);
`packages/genie/src/tools/spawner.js` (`Spawner` type + `makeHostSpawner`);
`packages/genie/src/tools/sandbox-spawner.js` (`makeSandboxSpawner`).

**Verbatim quote.** Job spec Gap 3: "no subprocess power is granted into
code-mode. Subprocess machinery exists (`packages/platform/src/proc.js`
`systemCapture`; the genie `Spawner` seam in
`packages/genie/src/tools/spawner.js` + `sandbox-spawner.js`,
cwd-confined) but is not a code-mode lexical cap. `yarn install` and
`npm test` both need this. What is the confinement boundary and program
allow-list?"

Confirmed: `CodeModePowers` has `workspace` and `git` only. The
genie's `Spawner` interface is a well-defined seam (`spawn(argv, opts):
Promise<ProcessLike>`) but it is not wired into `makeCodeModeAgent` or
`makeCodeModeGlobals`. The `SandboxHandle.spawn` route (via
`makeSandboxSpawner`) has a tighter confinement boundary (bwrap/podman
slice, cwd confined to `/workspace`) but also lives entirely in genie.

**What's needed to implement.** A code-mode `exec` power whose type
is a lexically-bound `Spawner` (or an exo wrapping one), along with:
(a) a program allow-list decision (which programs are permitted: only
`yarn`/`npm`? any PATH-resolved binary? only a closed list?),
(b) a cwd confinement decision (must cwd stay within the workspace
mount root?), and (c) a policy on stdout/stderr capture size limits.

**Candidate resolutions.**
- **A.** Add `exec` as a new `CodeModePower` field backed by the
  genie's `makeHostSpawner` (or `makeSandboxSpawner` when the genie
  is daemon-hosted). The allow-list and cwd confinement are policy
  fields on the power itself, parallel to `gitMode: 'readOnly'`.
  Trade-off: direct, minimal surface; requires the allow-list be
  designed (an allow-list of `['yarn', 'npm', 'node']` is a starting
  point but is not specified today).
- **B.** Introduce a separate `ExecCap` exo (daemon-minted) that wraps
  a `Spawner` and enforces the allow-list + cwd confinement at the
  exo guard level, similar to how `GitRemote` enforces the push-refspec
  policy at the exo level. The code-mode agent receives an `exec`
  lexical binding pointing at this `ExecCap`. Trade-off: cleaner ocap
  discipline; more design work (new exo type, new formula type, new
  daemon host method).
- **C.** Scope the initial SWE loop to operations that do NOT require
  subprocess spawn (file edit + git add/commit only; no install or test
  run). Defer exec to a follow-up design. Trade-off: the loop is
  incomplete (cannot verify `yarn install` or run tests through the cap
  boundary) but the clone/edit/commit/push core can be specced first.

**Maintainer's call:** design revision — the D1 design job should
specify the `ExecCap` or `Spawner`-as-power shape, the allow-list,
and the cwd confinement boundary.

---

### Gap 4: GitRemote not accessible as a code-mode lexical power; local-transport URL blocked by default

**Where in the design.** `packages/exo-git/src/git-remote.js`
`normalizeRemoteUrl` (line 156–178); `packages/daemon/src/host.js`
`provideGitRemote` (line 502–540); `packages/agentry/src/execute/preset.js`
`CodeModePowers` (no `remote` field).

**Verbatim quote.** Job spec Gap 4: "`GitRemote.push()` and its native
backend exist but are gated by a daemon-minted, audience-bound creden

author: thestoryportal
body:
## R-FS-1 standalone arc — `B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-EFFECT-BEARING`, closed as the **TOOL_STEP slice**

Bundled-absorption **CP spec v1.64 → v1.65** (CP-only, **NO runtime delta** — the #738 shape) + impl + tests + clearance + arc-ledger + spine ledger + dashboard regen. The WORKER effect-bearing maybe-ran residual the v1.62 re-fire-safe slice left, built for the **TOOL_STEP** kind.

### Two mechanisms
1. **The live effect-fence ambiguous-pause composed through the fan-out barrier.** A fan-out branch (PARALLELIZATION peer OR ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS / HIERARCHICAL worker) whose OWN dispatch raises `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError` (C-RT-31 §14.22) is captured as a NON-terminal effect-fence-paused disposition (a new `EffectFencePausedBranchResumeState` carrier, disjoint from terminal `branches` + `paused_child_branches`, drop-when-empty) → a genuine §26.2 `EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS` PAUSE, instead of being swallowed by the generic `except` → recorded `completed` → cascade. Resume re-enters the branch with the operator's key-bound `EffectFenceResolution` (reusing the LINEAR v1.51/v1.52 machinery verbatim → CP-only).
2. **The fence-recoverable TOOL_STEP maybe-ran crash-resume relaxation.** A maybe-ran TOOL_STEP now RECOVERS (re-dispatch re-reaches the auto-active fence → at-most-once at the tool sink) instead of the v1.62 unconditional effect-bearing fail-closed — **PROVIDED the RESUMED branch's `step_kind` is ALSO TOOL_STEP** (the changed-kind guard).

### The genuine in-flight regression caught + fixed
The in-flight WIP keyed fence-recovery on the dispatch-MARKER kind ALONE → re-opened the exact v1.62 changed-manifest at-most-once hole (a TOOL→DECLARATIVE resume reaches no fence → the original tool effect silently abandoned). Fix: require BOTH the marker kind AND the **resumed** `step_kind` be TOOL_STEP, at the incomplete-recovery + cardinality-only sites. The §14.22 key is per-`(run, step, tool)` but `step_payload` is opaque to the driver, so tool-swap-under-same-step_id is **accepted parity with the cleared linear path** (per-key at-most-once preserved), documented not registered.

### Decorrelated verification
- **advisor** (full-transcript): confirmed the changed-manifest failure is a CODE bug not a stale test; sharpened the tool-swap key-composition question; directed front-loading the real-fence witness; pre-done caught the fail-class honesty + cascade-cancel witness gaps.
- **out-of-family Codex (gpt-5.5), 4 rounds → converged code-clean at R4**: R1 = 3 disposition-edge fixes (ABORT→terminal FAILED / pause_reason→EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS / cascade-cancel store-capture) + 1 by-design (PROCEED); R2 = 1 [P1] (live-pause changed-kind, the §1 analogue of §2); R3 = 1 [P2] (fence-resume-requires-strict-tier under a PROCEED resume); R4 = code-clean.
- **Real-fence witnesses** (front-loaded, the load-bearing proof): BOTH live-composition sites (`_execute_parallelization` + `_execute_orchestrator_workers`), BOTH halves (PAUSE + key-bound resume) + ABORT + changed-kind + PROCEED-resume + cascade-cancel-store witnesses.
- harness-cp **1306** + 1 xfailed; harness-runtime 2115; harness-cxa 28; pyright 0/0/0; ruff clean; `just overlay-check` OK 330 nodes 31/31 seams.

### Accounting (honest FULL-SPEC)
Closes the parent arc as the TOOL_STEP slice + registers THREE narrower follow-ons (a split, NOT a defer): `B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT` (recursive child) + `B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-UNFENCED-EXTERNAL` (managed-agents fence extension) + `B-FANOUT-EFFECT-FENCE-PER-BRANCH-RESOLUTION` (key→resolution map). `standalone_registered` **4 → 6**; `arc_ledger --check` OK 46/0/4/6. R-FS-1 stays ACTIVE. 4 additive free-text `RunResult.fail_class` strings (NOT the closed `ValidatorRetryExitClass` taxonomy). NO contract / closed-enum / committed-invariant change; at-most-once PRESERVED.

author: luke-lacina
body:
## What

The OAuth login button on the add-account wizard called `startOAuthLogin` with no in-flight guard. A double-click (or any rapid re-trigger before the step flips to `oauth-waiting`) opened **two** system-browser auth flows; the second authorization request overwrote the first in the server session, so the slower callback failed with `authorization_request_not_found` and the external browser rendered `auth-failed.html` — **even though the first flow had already created the account and synced mail**.

This is the **E** bug from the v0.1.0 release smoke (todo.md "v0.1.0 smoke — otevrene bugy").

## How

Add an `oauthStarting` flag in [`settings/accounts/new/+page.svelte`](../blob/main/frontend/src/routes/settings/accounts/new/+page.svelte):

- `handleOAuthLogin` returns early while a start is in flight,
- the login button is `disabled` until the start resolves.

Only one flow can begin, so the duplicate callback can no longer happen. Genuine failures still surface `auth-failed.html` (deliberately not softened — the static page can't know whether an account was created, and a generic "maybe it worked" message would mislead real failures).

## Tests

OAuth start hands off to the system browser, so the flow itself isn't e2e-testable; the guard is verified by manual smoke. `npm run check` / `lint` / `knip` green; the accounts functional e2e suite (14 tests) re-run against a fresh build stays green (the `disabled` default is `false`, so existing visibility assertions are unaffected).

author: tar-ive
body:
## Summary

Wires up the remaining local-only interaction data (likes, saves, follows) to persist via the existing `PUT /me` API, completing story 1.3 (profile sync across devices) from #28.

**Before:** `toggleLike`/`toggleSave`/`toggleFollow` wrote only to localStorage (`giftmaxxing_post_state`). Follows weren't persisted at all (in-memory only). A fresh device had no interaction history.

**After:** Every like/save/follow change triggers a debounced `syncToCloud()` that merges the onboarding profile + `postState` + `follows` into a single `saveMe(userId, payload)` call. On a fresh-device sign-in, `AccountSync` restores interaction data from the cloud alongside the profile and dispatches `giftmaxxing:interactions-restored` so the store re-hydrates in-flight.

New module `web/lib/sync.ts`:
```ts
// Shared localStorage r/w for postState + follows (replaces store.tsx locals)
export { loadPostState, savePostState, loadFollows, saveFollows }

// Cloud helpers
buildCloudPayload()   // { ...profile, postState, follows }
restoreInteractionData(cloud)  // extracts postState/follows → localStorage
syncToCloud()          // debounced (2s) saveMe with full payload; no-ops when API not configured
```

Key changes in `store.tsx`:
- Imports `loadPostState`/`savePostState`/`loadFollows`/`saveFollows` from `sync.ts` (removes duplicate local definitions)
- `toggleFollow` now persists to localStorage + triggers cloud sync
- Follows initialize from `loadFollows()` (was empty `Set`)
- Listens for `giftmaxxing:interactions-restored` to re-hydrate after cloud restore

Key changes in `account-sync.tsx`:
- On sign-in push: sends `buildCloudPayload()` (profile + interactions) instead of just the profile
- On fresh-device restore: calls `restoreInteractionData(remote)` + dispatches restore event
- Listens for `giftmaxxing:interaction` events alongside `giftmaxxing:profile`

Falls back gracefully to localStorage when `isApiConfigured()` is false — no behavioral change for users without a backend.

Partially addresses #28 (Epic 1, story 1.3).

author: chielochi
body:
### Kubesec Performance Summary


Security & RBAC Hardening:

- Achieved kubesec scores of 11+ (11 for web/worker/hocuspocus, 12 for cron) by standardizing container security contexts: disabled privilege escalation, dropped all capabilities (ALL), and enforced non-root execution (runAsNonRoot: true).

body:
# Description

Follow-up cleanup to the now-merged #6029 (zvol create event on purge).

The zfsmanager device watcher's create handler stored an event for every
path that appeared under `/dev/zvol`, including the intermediate directories
(`persist`, `vault`, `volumes`) that mdev creates alongside the zvol symlinks.
Those directories resolve on disk, so the reconcile step published a
`ZVolStatus` for each one. `volumemgr` matches `ZVolStatus` by exact dataset,
so the bogus entries never harmed anything, but they cluttered pubsub and the
logs and flapped on every purge.

This skips non-symlinks in the create handler, mirroring the symlink filter
already used by the startup walk (`processRecursive`). The directories are
still watched; only the spurious publish is dropped.

## How to test and validate this PR

On a ZFS-mode device, create and purge an app with a volume and watch
`zfsmanager`: there should no longer be `processed add`/`ZVolStatus` entries
for `/dev/zvol/persist`, `/dev/zvol/persist/vault`, or
`/dev/zvol/persist/vault/volumes`, only for the actual
`.../volumes/<uuid>.<gen>` device symlinks. Existing `cmd/zfsmanager` unit
tests still pass; behavior for real zvol devices is unchanged.

## Changelog notes

No user-facing changes.

## PR Backports

Not needed — cosmetic cleanup, no functional change.

author: dustinbyrne
body:
## Problem

`getServerSidePostHog(ctx)` awaited the shared node-client cache and then called `enterContext()` before returning the client. Because `enterContext()` uses `AsyncLocalStorage.enterWith()`, setting context after an `await` inside the helper does not propagate back to the caller's `getServerSideProps` continuation.

That means Pages Router server-side flag evaluation/capture could miss the request's cookie/tracing identity even though the helper looked scoped.

## Changes

- Mirror the App Router `getPostHog()` request-scoping approach for `getServerSidePostHog()`.
- Return a proxy that wraps method calls in `client.withContext(contextData, ...)` instead of calling `client.enterContext()` after async initialization.
- Keep disabled/no-key and opted-out paths returning the raw client without context wrapping.
- Update tests to assert method calls after `await getServerSidePostHog(ctx)` are wrapped with the expected request context.
- Add a patch changeset for `@posthog/next`.

Validation:

pnpm --filter @posthog/next test:unit -- getPostHog.test.ts getServerSidePostHog.test.ts

body:
When transferring an order to a table that already has an open order, identical products are merged into a single line. If both orders were already sent to the kitchen printer, the merged line was incorrectly marked as new and had to be sent again.

Steps to reproduce:
-------------------
* Open table 1, add product A (2 units) and product B, send to kitchen
* Open table 2, add product A (3 units) and product C, send to kitchen
* On table 2, transfer/merge the order to table 1

> Observation:
product A shows 2 units as new and must be sent to the kitchen printer again, although all quantities were already sent.

Why the fix:
------------
When merging preparation history for identical lines, handlePreparationHistory overwrote the destination sent quantity with the source one instead of summing both. The kitchen diff then treated the missing quantity as new changes.

A unit test will be added in 18.3.

author: gavdoubleu
body:
## Problem

Three related issues made `VenueManager` unreliable:

**1. No single source of truth.** Venues were stored in multiple redundant collections (`self.venues`, `venues_by_type`, `venues_by_type_and_name`). These could diverge silently, and callers had no consistent way to query them.

**2. Silent venue loss.** The type-and-name index used a `(type, name)` key. Venues sharing a name within a type would overwrite each other in the dict — later additions silently dropped earlier ones. There was no error, no warning, just missing venues at query time. Real name duplicates were confirmed to exist — even for the same venue type within the same geographical unit. These duplicates should be caught and handled in the input data, not silently discarded by MAY.

**3. `Venue.id` was not a stable unique identifier.** `id` was a naming convention set in two different places in two different ways, scoped only within a venue type. It could not safely be used as a dict key across all venues, and it was mutable after construction.

## Changes

- Replace all redundant collections with a single `venues_by_type_and_id` dict as the authoritative store
- Make `Venue.id` globally unique and immutable on construction
- Remove derived/redundant queries; all venue access goes through `venues_by_type_and_id`
- Fix `random.sample` on `dict.values()` in `world.py` using index-based sampling (O(k) memory)
- Update tests to match the simplified API

author: jrjones
body:
Fixes #46

## Summary

Two bugs in the HTTP request-body path (`src/http/request.rs`), both affecting uploads (`POST /empty`):

1. **Fixed-length bodies are read in rigid 1024-byte `read_exact` chunks**, counting `buffer.len()` (always 1024) per iteration. A `Content-Length` that is **not a multiple of 1024** therefore (a) over-reads the final chunk, consuming bytes of the next pipelined request, and (b) against a peer that keeps the connection open, **blocks forever in `read_exact`** waiting for the missing tail of the final chunk — hanging the upload until the client times out / disconnects. Clients pad upload payloads to a 1024 boundary to avoid this; the fix removes that need.
2. **`Expect: 100-continue` is never answered.** Clients that use it (curl and many HTTP libraries) wait out their continue-timeout (**~1s for curl**) before sending the body on *every* upload.

## Root cause

```rust
// BodyType::Fixed (before)
let mut buffer = [0; 1024];
let mut len: usize = 0;
loop {
    let bytes_read = buf_reader.read_exact(&mut buffer).await; // demands a FULL 1024 bytes
    match bytes_read {
        Ok(_) => { len += buffer.len();                        // always +1024, not actual
                   if len >= body_size as usize { break; } }
        Err(_) => break,
        // ...
    }
}
```

`read_exact` completes only once the whole 1024-byte buffer is filled, so the last partial chunk of a non-aligned body never completes against a still-open connection. And `len += buffer.len()` counts 1024 regardless of what was actually read, so the loop can stop 1–1023 bytes past the body. The `Expect` header is simply never inspected before the body read.

## Fix

- Read the body with `read` (not `read_exact`) into a 64 KiB buffer, decrementing by the **actual** bytes returned and stopping exactly at `Content-Length`. Safe for any length; the larger buffer also cuts per-1 KiB read-syscall overhead.
- Before reading the body, if the request carries `Expect: 100-continue`, write the interim `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n` (RFC 9110 §10.1.1).

## Validation

**New regression tests** (`src/http/request.rs`) that **fail on `master`** and pass with the fix:

| test | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| non-1024-multiple body not over-read into a pipelined request | FAIL — 1 response instead of 2 (the pipelined GET is swallowed) | ok |
| `Expect: 100-continue` receives an interim 100 | FAIL — no `100 Continue` emitted | ok |

**End-to-end** (release build, vs unpatched `master` on a second port):

| scenario | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| non-1024-multiple upload, client keeps socket open | **hangs — no response in 8s** | **200 OK, immediate** |
| upload with `Expect: 100-continue` (curl default) | ~1.07 s | **~0.03 s** |
| upload throughput (Expect disabled, 50 MB) | ~8 Gbps | **~14 Gbps** |
| `GET /empty` ping · 100 MB `garbage` download | — | unchanged |

`cargo build --release` and `cargo clippy` are clean.

author: thewrz
body:
## Why
Completes PDF spec ingest (#65, **slice 3/3**): scanned/image PDFs and font-corrupted text layers. After #245
(text-layer PDFs), a scanned PDF dropped into the demo's dropzone only emitted a "needs OCR" deferral — this makes
it actually OCR into the same AST + coordination panels, and repairs mojibake-corrupted text layers.

## What
- **OCR fallback** (`src/parser/pdf/ocr.ts`): when #245's `detectPdfOcrNeed` flags a scanned/`mixed` PDF,
  rasterize the affected pages (unpdf `renderPageAsImage` + `@napi-rs/canvas`) → `tesseract.js` → splice OCR text
  back per page → existing #64 hierarchy inference. `mixed` keeps good text-layer pages and OCRs only the empty
  ones. The recognizer + renderer are dependency-injected.
- **Font-encoding recovery** (`src/parser/pdf/font-encoding.ts`): detects mojibake (char-frequency + `chardet`
  fingerprint), remaps via `iconv-lite`. Decodes items in coherent adjacent groups and **rejects any remap that
  introduces a new `�`**, so valid non-ASCII (`70°F`, `±`) is never destroyed and sequences split across PDF items
  aren't corrupted. Genuinely unrecoverable corruption is flagged, never silently passed.
- **Warnings**: `pdf-ocr-applied`, `pdf-ocr-low-confidence`, `pdf-ocr-unusable`, `pdf-font-encoding-remapped`,
  `pdf-font-encoding-unrecoverable`.
- **Graceful degradation**: primary → pdfjs fallback → OCR / encoding remap → partial result with `warnings[]` →
  typed hard error. Never a silent empty/garbled parse.
- Deps per ADR-034 §3: `tesseract.js` 7 (Apache-2.0, WASM, offline) + `@napi-rs/canvas` (MIT, prebuilt). `pnpm
  audit` clean — 0 new advisories vs `main`. Model loaded from a gitignored cache (NOT vendored in git);
  tesseract's build script left unapproved.

## Testing
- [x] Build (`tsc`) clean
- [x] Unit 1131 (OCR + font-encoding exercised via injected fakes — no model/network needed in CI)
- [x] Integration 693 (orchestrator-run, isolated Postgres)
- [x] **Real-OCR end-to-end** (orchestrator-run, `SPECR_OCR_E2E=1`): an image-only PDF → genuine tesseract model
      download + recognize → recovers `PART 1 - GENERAL` + `pdf-ocr-applied`. CI skips it (no model); `skipIf`-gated.
- [x] Lint (eslint + tsc + prettier) + `redocly lint openapi.yaml` valid (9 pre-existing warnings)
- [ ] Manual: drop a scanned PDF into the demo dropzone → OCR'd into the tree (vs. the prior "needs OCR" deferral)
- [ ] CI green (runs when moved out of draft)

## Review notes
- Implemented autonomously by **Codex (gpt-5.5 xhigh)** in an isolated worktree (TDD), under **Claude Opus 4.8**
  orchestration: dependency vetting + install, orchestrator-run integration + the real-OCR e2e, and an adversarial
  Codex review gate that caught 2 P2 font-encoding corruption bugs (valid non-ASCII destroyed; split-item
  mojibake) — both fixed here.
- The `eng.traineddata` model downloads on first OCR to a gitignored cache (offline after first fetch). For
  air-gapped deploys, pre-seed the cache or set `OCR_LANG_PATH`.

🤖 Co-authored by Codex (gpt-5.5 xhigh — implementation) under Claude Opus 4.8 (orchestration + review + deps).

author: casey451
body:
## Why
On the CPU vision box, the model often runs out of context emitting a dense calendar's event list, so the JSON arrives **truncated mid-array** and `json.loads` fails. The old code then dropped **every** event the model read — the "reads 0 events" symptom. Confirmed by direct probe: an untiled July calendar returned **16.6 KB of correct events** but unterminated JSON → 0 kept; even a half-image tile (18.3 KB) truncated.

## Fix
When the strict parse fails, walk the `events` array and keep each balanced, individually-parseable object up to the cut, instead of discarding the whole tile. Brace-in-string safe. Combined with raising `VISION_CALENDAR_TILES`, the scraper now degrades gracefully — a truncated tile still contributes the events it completed, and everything still lands PENDING for `/admin` review.

## Tests
+4 (salvage recovers complete objects; brace-in-string safety; valid JSON unaffected; updated the prior `truncated → []` contract test to assert recovery). `pytest tests/test_vision_calendar.py` → 26 passed; `ruff` clean.

## Note
This is the durable half of the calendar fix. I'm separately validating the right `VISION_CALENDAR_TILES` value on the box (a box-env change, not code) so each tile's list also fits the window.

author: yusufbesirarslan
body:
## Summary

Add a detailed security, backend logic, and data-layer audit document (`FIXES.md`) generated from a 3-agent deep-dive review. The codebase is mature and well-hardened with no Critical or High security vulnerabilities, but contains correctness issues and schema-management drift that warrant prioritized fixes.

## Key findings

**High priority (correctness & schema):**
- **B1**: Weekly rollover uses naive UTC instead of Istanbul timezone, causing XP/awards to be computed against misaligned day boundaries
- **S1**: `referral_code` column length inconsistent (12 vs 16 chars) across `db_init.py` ALTERs, model, and Alembic migrations
- **S2**: Triple schema-management mechanism (create_all + legacy ALTERs + Alembic) is drift-prone; CI guard is non-blocking

**Medium priority (logic & operations):**
- **B2**: Protein goal nudge uses `created_at` (UTC) instead of canonical `tarih` (Istanbul day)
- **B6**: Boot-time data UPDATEs re-run every start, overwriting intentional changes
- **S3**: Weekly rollover has no reliable scheduler (only before_request hook + external cron)
- **S4**: `create_all()` + auto-upgrade on every boot assumes single worker; races on multi-instance

**Low priority (defense-in-depth & code quality):**
- 10 backend logic issues (weight-gain message, supplement XP gate, TDEE fallback, etc.)
- 10 structural/data issues (dependency pins, quest seeding, logging, god-modules, etc.)
- 4 security hardening notes (no-op principal check, health endpoint leaks, etc.)

## Verified healthy

- IDOR, MCP, SSRF, XSS, secrets handling, CSRF, CSP all correctly implemented
- Migration chain is linear with complete FK coverage
- Config and feature flags are solid

## Recommendation

Prioritize **B1, B2** (correctness of XP & nudges) → **S1, S2** (schema drift) before addressing lower-priority items. Document that legacy `db_init.py` ALTERs are source-of-truth for legacy prod DBs only until migrated to Alembic.

body: ## Summary by cubic Adds OpenAI-compatible LLM service launch and routing with autoscaling (token pressure and active streams), request affinity, metrics, and `llm.route` event tracking. Introduces nested `serving` metadata across API/SDK/CLI (with staged compatibility fields removed), a vLLM integration, a GitHub deploy builder, LLM smoke tools, and moves deploy agent assets out of `beta9`. - **New Features** - Gateway/API: adds nested `serving` (`appKind`, `servingProtocol`, `llm`) and removes top‑level compatibility fields; app responses include pool, running containers, `isService`, and `serving`; exposes `llm.route` history and a summary endpoint; deployments list includes `appId`; Swagger/proto updated; ScaleDeployment centralizes fixed replica bounds via `StubConfig.SetFixedReplicaCount` and preserves LLM autoscaler type. - Pod: inspects OpenAI paths, estimates tokens, tracks per-request pressure, and sets prefix/affinity keys; scrapes LLM engine readiness/metrics with staleness handling; autoscaler scales by active streams and token pressure; emits `llm.route` events. - Metrics: adds `pod_llm_request_duration_ms`, `pod_llm_time_to_first_ms`, `pod_llm_estimated_tokens`. - SDK/CLI: adds `ServingConfig`, `LLMConfig`, `LLMTokenPressureAutoscaler`; `Service`/`Pod` accept `serving` (defaults GPU to `GpuType.Any` when LLM is set or only a GPU count is provided); vLLM integration via `beta9.abstractions.integrations.vllm`; deploy flags `--llm` and `--llm-*` with helpers in `beta9.cli.llm` (auto-detects model/tokenizer from env, Dockerfile, and command). - Builder/Smoke: `deploy/github-builder` image with `beta9-github-deploy`; OpenAI-compatible smoke/bench tools; deploy agent assets moved out of `beta9`. - **Migration** - Use `serving=ServingConfig(llm=LLMConfig(...))`; top‑level `app_kind`/`serving_protocol`/`llm` fields are removed. Update to the latest SDK/CLI and pass `--llm` flags as needed. - Cache reconciliation is enabled by default; set `cache.reconciliation.enabled=false` to restore prior behavior. author: raisyroo
body:
### Motivation

- Introduce a single canonical flyer manifest so flyer records can scale to hundreds without per-event code changes.
- Prevent duplicated runtime paths by moving verified local flyers into a single source of truth and keeping card behavior identical.
- Provide automated validation to catch ID mismatches, duplicate paths, unsupported formats, and local-file mismatches for Ray’s checkout.

### Description

- Add `data/eventFlyers.ts`, a typed manifest keyed by event id where each record has `src`, `assetMode` (`'local' | 'hosted'`), and optional `ticketsUrl`, and include only the two verified entries: `romeo-peach` → `/event-media/flyers/romeo-peach-festival.webp` and `goodells-fair` → `/event-media/flyers/goodells-fair.webp`.
- Add `resolveEventFlyerSrc` and `getEventFlyer` helpers and update the safe card flow in `data/safeEventCard.ts` to resolve flyer paths from the catalog first while preserving existing flyer-card appearance and runtime paths.
- Remove the two verified flyer paths from their `ATLAS_EVENTS` records so the manifest is the single source of truth and keep legacy `AtlasEvent.flyerSrc` support (now expanded to also accept `https://` hosted URLs) for backwards compatibility.
- Add `scripts/validate-flyers.ts` which validates event IDs, duplicate catalog entries, duplicate paths, `assetMode` semantics, rejects runtime paths containing `/public/`, enforces local runtime prefix for `local` assets, enforces `https:` for `hosted` assets and `ticketsUrl`, and supports a local-only check when run with `--local` that verifies files under `public/event-media/flyers/`.
- Wire validation into the build by adding `validate:flyers` and `validate:flyers:local` npm scripts and running `npm run validate:flyers` before `next build` in `package.json`.
- Preserve that public hosting is intentionally deferred and future hosted assets will be supported by the manifest shape rather than adding external hosting in this change.

### Testing

- Ran `git diff --check` which reported no whitespace errors and passed.  
- Ran `npm run validate:flyers` which validated the catalog against `ATLAS_EVENTS` and printed success.  
- Ran `npm run lint` which completed successfully with existing unrelated `@next/next/no-img-element` warnings.  
- Ran `npm run build` which runs the non-local flyer validation and then completed a successful Next.js production build.

Additional notes: the exact local command to verify Ray’s ignored binary flyers is `npm run validate:flyers:local`, and to add a batch of 100 flyers add 100 keyed records to `data/eventFlyers.ts`, place matching files under `public/event-media/flyers/` in the local checkout, then run `npm run validate:flyers` and `npm run validate:flyers:local` as applicable.

author: genspark-ai-developer[bot]
body:
## Summary
Fixes the Railway web service "page not showing" issue and cleans up a placeholder in the login page footer.

## Root Cause (Railway page not showing)
The web container's nginx was listening on a **fixed port 80** instead of Railway's runtime-injected `$PORT`, so Railway's router could never reach it. The old config also did `proxy_pass http://sira_api:3001` — a docker-compose service name that does **not** resolve between separate Railway services, which breaks nginx startup entirely.

## Changes
- **`apps/web/nginx.conf.template`** (new): nginx listens on `${PORT}`, SPA fallback to `index.html`, static-asset caching, lightweight `/healthz` endpoint, and **no `proxy_pass`** — the web app calls the API directly via `VITE_API_BASE_URL`.
- **`apps/web/Dockerfile`**: installs the template into `/etc/nginx/templates/` so `nginx:alpine` runs `envsubst` on `$PORT` at container start; `ENV PORT=80` default for local/docker; healthcheck now hits `/healthz`.
- **`railway-web.json`**: `healthcheckPath` `/` → `/healthz`.
- **`apps/web/vite.config.ts`**: `minify` `terser` → `esbuild` to avoid OOM (EXIT 137) on low-memory build environments. `terser` is **kept** in deps because `@vitejs/plugin-legacy` (LEGACY_BUILD=true / build:apk) requires it.
- **`apps/web/src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx`**: replaced garbage placeholder footer text with `© {year} Seera Platform · v4.0`.

## ⚠️ Required Railway env (action for deployer)
Because `proxy_pass` was removed, the **web** service must be told where the API is. Set a build arg on the Railway **web** service:
```
VITE_API_BASE_URL = https://<your-api-service>.up.railway.app
```
The frontend appends `/api/v1` automatically.

## Testing
- Web build with esbuild minify: ✅ `built in ~42s`, 2424 modules.
- Local serve test: `GET /` → 200, JS asset → 200.
- Login page renders; footer fixed.

## Notes
- `terser` intentionally retained for legacy/APK builds.

author: arnabnandy7
body:
<!--
Thank you for helping us improve the Azure IoT Java SDK!

Here's a little checklist of things that will help it make its way to the repository: Note that you don't have to check all the boxes, we can help you with that.
This being said, the more you do, the quicker it'll go through our gated build!
-->

# Checklist
- [x] I have read the [contribution guidelines] (https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-java/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I added or modified the existing tests to cover the change (we do not allow our test coverage to go down).
- I submitted this PR against the correct branch:
  - [x] This pull-request is submitted against the `main` branch.

# Reference/Link to the issue solved with this PR (if any)

Fixes #1803

# Description of the problem

For correlated device client operations such as `getTwinAsync` and `updateReportedPropertiesAsync`, `onResponseReceived` could be skipped in a race condition.

In `IotHubTransport.onMessageReceived`, the received message was added to the receive queue before the matching `CorrelationCallbackContext` was read from `correlationCallbacks`. Adding the message to the queue wakes the receive task, which may acknowledge the message and remove the correlation callback before `onMessageReceived` looks it up. When that happens, the response callback is never invoked.

# Description of the solution

Capture the `CorrelationCallbackContext` before adding the received message to the receive queue. `onResponseReceived` now uses that saved context, so it still fires even if the receive task acknowledges the message and removes the callback entry immediately afterward.

Added a regression unit test that simulates the correlation callback being removed while the received message is queued, and verifies that `onResponseReceived` is still called.

## Summary

Adds an `e2e` job to mero-js CI so the e2e suite runs on **every mero-js PR**, against the **latest released merod** — the consumer-side half of the contract gate (mero-js CI had no e2e before; only unit/typecheck/lint/build).

The job: download released merod from `calimero-network/core` → boot single node with embedded auth → `pnpm test:e2e`. The harness self-provisions (installs kv-store via `ensureApplication`, records coverage) and reads `NODE_URL`/`MERO_E2E_USER`, so there's no manual token/install bootstrapping.

#25 (the original "enable E2E in CI") was conflicting and predated the self-provisioning harness (#57) — it hand-rolled the merod boot + `dev/dev` token + manual kv-store install. This is the slimmed, current-suite version. #25 closed with a pointer here.

- **core #2895 `sdk-e2e`**: core PR vs **PR-built** merod — "did my core change break the SDK?" (core breaks first)

Both needed; neither redundant.

author: hevi-public
body:
## T2.5 — Unique persona slug

`persona.slug` is the URL key used in profile links, and `findBySlug` (`PersonaRepository.findBySlug`) assumes uniqueness via `firstOrNull`. But the column was never `UNIQUE`, so two same-named personas produced the same slug and shadowed each other's profile page.

### V16 — dedupe BEFORE indexing
A bare `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` would fail on any DB that already holds duplicate slugs. The important case is **empty slugs**: `slug` was added in V5 with `DEFAULT ''`, so every row predating V5 carries `slug = ''` — a built-in duplicate the moment there are ≥2 such rows (exactly what `MigrationPipelineTest` seeds). `V16__persona_slug_unique.sql` therefore resolves collisions first, then adds the index:

```sql
-- 1. Empty/NULL slugs → the row's id (PRIMARY KEY, already unique).
UPDATE persona SET slug = id WHERE slug IS NULL OR slug = '';

-- 2. Suffix remaining non-empty duplicates deterministically: keep the first
--    by rowid, append -2, -3, … (matching insert's runtime scheme).
UPDATE persona
SET slug = slug || '-' || d.rn
FROM (
    SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY slug ORDER BY rowid) AS rn
    FROM persona
) d
WHERE persona.id = d.id AND d.rn > 1;

-- 3. Enforce it going forward.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_persona_slug ON persona(slug);
```

This applies cleanly on a fresh DB (no duplicates → both `UPDATE`s are no-ops) and upgrades any existing/messy DB (empty-slug rows and same-name duplicates are resolved deterministically before the index is created). The xerial SQLite build supports the window function and `UPDATE … FROM`.

### insert-time collision suffixing
`PersonaRepository.insert` now computes the first free slug **before** the INSERT, so it never trips the new unique index (no relying on catching the constraint violation): it reads the small set of slugs matching `slug` / `slug-%`, returns the bare `slug` if free, else the lowest `slug-2`, `slug-3`, … not already taken. A single "Ada" still gets `ada`; only collisions get suffixed. `handle` behaviour is unchanged (task scope is `slug`).

### Tests
- `MigrationPipelineTest`: `MAX(version)` bumped to **16**; the inline pre-existing-row assertion updated to the post-V16 value, plus a new block proving the two seeded empty-slug rows end with **distinct, non-empty** slugs (proof the dedupe worked).
- `PersonaRepositoryTest` (Tier 1, real SQLite): inserting three "Ada"s yields `ada` / `ada-2` / `ada-3`, and `findBySlug` resolves each to the right persona; a sole persona keeps its bare slug.

`./gradlew verifyAll --no-build-cache` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL** (all tiers + acceptance green).

### Note for the stacked T2.6
T2.6 (composite index V17) stacks on this branch and will take `MigrationPipelineTest`'s version assertion from 16 → 17.

author: hdrake
body:
Fixes #712.

## Problem

For a grid with `face_connections`, `xgcm.padding.pad` could fill connected halo cells with the **wrong** neighbor face, and **which** result you got depended on `PYTHONHASHSEED` — i.e. the same grid gave correct connectivity in one Python process and incorrect connectivity in the next.

Minimal demonstration on `master` (cubed-sphere connectivity; pad a field equal to the face index and read face 0's right-edge halo, which connects to face 1):

```
PYTHONHASHSEED=0  face0 right-edge halo = [5, 5, 5, 5, 5]   # WRONG (face 5 is the UP neighbor)
PYTHONHASHSEED=2  face0 right-edge halo = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]   # OK
PYTHONHASHSEED=6  face0 right-edge halo = [5, 5, 5, 5, 5]   # WRONG
```

## Root cause

In `_pad_face_connections`, each source slice is `squeeze()`-d (dropping the length-1 `target_dim`), but the dim was only restored via `expand_dims` **when `target_dim` carried a coordinate variable**:

```python
if target_dim in target_slice.coords:
    if target_dim not in source_slice.dims:
        source_slice = source_slice.expand_dims([target_dim])
    ...
```

On a grid whose padded dims have **no coordinates**, that branch is skipped, so the source slice stays 1-D. `xr.concat(..., join="override")` then silently transposes and broadcasts it, clobbering the orthogonal axis's already-filled connected edge. Because `pad_axes` is built from a `set` (hash-seed-dependent iteration order), whichever axis is padded *last* wins and the other axis's connected edges come out wrong — so the corruption is non-deterministic across processes.

This is why it went unnoticed: the existing cubed-sphere tests pad `data_c`, which *has* coordinates, so they always took the working branch.

## Fix

1. Restore the squeezed `target_dim` **unconditionally** (keep only the coordinate *blanking* gated on the dim having a coordinate).
2. `transpose` the source slice to the target's dimension order before concatenating, so the result no longer depends on axis iteration order.

## Tests

Added `test_cubed_sphere_scalar_pad_connected_halos`: pads a coordinate-less face-index field on the cubed-sphere fixture and asserts every connected halo reads the declared neighbor face. It fails on `master` for several hash seeds and passes deterministically with this fix.

- `test_padding.py` + `test_faceconnections.py`: **147 passed, 28 xfailed** (unchanged).
- Full suite green except pre-existing `test_transform.py … [*-distributed_client]` failures, which are `dask.distributed` import errors unrelated to this change (they fail identically on pristine `master`).
- With the fix, the cubed-sphere halos are correct **and** byte-identical across `PYTHONHASHSEED` values.

body:
Resumes **BL-05** (spell riders, un-paused now that BL-52 is done). RD-6 is the first genuinely-new engine mechanic left: a **temp-HP / absorb shield**. Split for review: **RD-6a = the mechanic** (this PR); **RD-6b = the HUD health-bar coloring** (green absorb / blue overflow — immediate follow-up, per Matías's Q4).

## Model (Matías worksheet)
A pool that soaks damage **before** real HP. Granted by a new `BuffKind::Shielded`; **persists (no timer) until depleted**; same-kind doesn't stack (take-higher refresh); healing doesn't refill it; shows as a buff.

## Implementation
- **`Health`** — new per-instance `absorb` pool (scaled u32). `change_by` soaks a damaging change through `absorb` first, only the overflow reaches `current`; positive (healing) changes bypass it. Accessors `absorb()` / `raise_absorb_to` (take-higher) / `clear_absorb`. Rides the existing `Health` serde sync automatically; **not DB-persisted → no migration**.
- **`BuffKind::Shielded`** — positive marker buff, **no per-tick effect** (the pool is granted on buff-add); full plumbing (differentiate, cmd parsers, voxygen title/desc/icon, `buff-shielded` i18n).
- **Lifecycle (server)** — on `Shielded`-add → `raise_absorb_to(strength)`; a damaging hit that drains absorb to 0 → remove `Shielded` (in the HealthChange handler); a **centralized post-removal check** clears `absorb` whenever the last `Shielded` buff is dropped by **any** path — dispel, expiry, deplete, and the **on-death `RemoveByCategory` strip** — preserving the invariant *absorb > 0 ⟺ a Shielded buff is active*.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all --check` ✅ · full CI clippy + voxygen publish clippy ✅ · `cargo test -p veloren-common` ✅ 185 pass (absorb soak/overflow, healing-bypass, take-higher/clear, Shielded positive+empty-effects).
- **`ecs-design-reviewer`**: found a real **BLOCKER** — the death path (`RemoveByCategory`) stripped `Shielded` without clearing `absorb` → phantom revive shield. **Fixed** via the centralized post-removal check. Verdict after fix: merge with minors (a `/health` admin-command deplete edge is noted as a minor follow-up).

Try it: `/buff shielded <amount>` then take a hit — damage eats the shield first.

## Next
**RD-6b** (HUD bar: green absorb / blue overflow), then **RD-7** (on-expire bleed-detonate) → BL-05 engine complete.

body:
The rebuilt v0.7.0 beta (build 46568094) never reached TestFlight. CI was green, but the iOS upload step actually failed:

```
ERROR: [altool] Failed to determine the Apple ID from Bundle ID 'com.ccwmap.ccwmap' with platform 'IOS'. A required agreement is missing or has expired. (403)
```

`apple-actions/upload-testflight-build@v3` swallowed altool's non-zero exit, so the job (and the whole run) reported success while nothing uploaded. `production.yml` had the identical step — a tagged production release could likewise fail to reach the App Store while showing green.

**Fix:** replace the action with a direct `xcrun altool --upload-app` call in both `release.yml` and `production.yml`. A bare `run:` block uses `bash -eo pipefail`, so a non-zero altool exit now fails the job. Also removes the `release-notes` input (v3 no longer accepts it — it was already ignored); TestFlight/App Store "What's New" is set in App Store Connect, and Play still gets notes via `whatsNewDirectory`.

Note: this cannot be fully exercised until the pending App Store Connect agreement is re-accepted (Account Holder, ASC → Agreements, Tax, and Banking). After that, the upload will succeed — or fail loudly.

author: jeffdafoe
body:
## LLM-116 — smith production choice

A multi-output crafter (the smith: skillet + nail) no longer auto-produces every good in parallel under `produce_tick`. It forges **one thing at a time**, chosen via a new `craft` tool, with a demand-aware cue so it leans toward what's actually selling.

### What changed
- **`Actor.ProductionFocus`** (restart-lossy) — `produce_tick` fills ONLY the focus for a >1-produce-entry crafter; single-output producers (farmers, cooks) are unchanged.
- **`craft` tool** + `SetProductionFocus` command — the crafter picks the good to forge; the command validates it actually produces it (model-facing error otherwise). Advertised only at the forge (`gateTools`, on the cue's own signal — discussion-109 invariant).
- **"## At your forge" cue** — each makeable good with per-unit time, stock vs cap, and weekly made/sold counts; current focus marked. Demand reuses `sellerRecentSales`; "made N" reads a new `RecentProduce` ring of ACTUAL mints (not at-cap anchor advances).
- **Standing self-state** — `You are making <item>.` on every tick, so a PC walking up to ask gets an answer.
- **Wake-warrant** (`production_choice_tick.go`) — a once-a-minute producer wakes an idle at-forge crafter (unfocused or maxed) so it ticks and chooses; force-ticks past the noop-skip gate; stops when everything is at cap. Needed because gating `produce_tick` on an LLM choice means an otherwise-idle smith would never get ticked to pick.

### Tests
- Unit (`production_focus_test.go`): produce_tick gating (focus→only focus; unfocused→nothing; single-output unchanged), `SetProductionFocus` rejection, the wake producer (wakes idle, skips focused).
- Golden: `smith_choosing_at_forge` scenario + `TestForgeCueOnlyForMultiOutputCrafterAtForge` cross-scenario invariant.
- `go build`/`vet`/`test ./sim/...` + `gofmt` all green.

### Deploy
No migration — the nail recipe + Ezekiel's `produce:nail` entry are already live (added via the umbilical). Engine code → needs an engine restart.

— Work

author: hongjian-gu
body:
## Summary
- Refs #5 — Slice 3a (#524, table) + Slice 3b (#527, worker dual-write) + this Slice 3c (read flip) close the Slice 3 architecture loop
- \`GET /api/v1/trials/{id}/events?after_seq=N\` + \`/stream\` now read from the indexed Postgres \`trial_events\` table; MinIO becomes the fallback for legacy trials only
- Response shape unchanged — SPA + API consumers transparent

## What's in
- \`_read_events_from_postgres\` (new helper) — pulls payloads from \`trial_events\` indexed on (trial_id, seq)
- \`_read_events_with_minio_fallback\` (new helper) — Postgres first, MinIO fallback when the trial state suggests events should exist but Postgres has 0 rows
- \`list_events_by_seq\` + \`stream_events\` (the inner SSE poll loop) — both updated to use the new helper
- The SSE \`/stream\` route gets a small per-iteration \`_read_loop_chunk\` helper so the events read + trial-state check happen in the same session lifecycle
- INFO log \`events_minio_fallback\` so operators can monitor the fallback hit rate and decide when to remove the fallback path in a future cleanup

## What's NOT in
- **No backfill of legacy trials.** MinIO remains the source for pre-Slice-3b trials via the fallback; once the fallback rate drops to ~0, the MinIO read path can be removed.
- **No LISTEN/NOTIFY push yet.** The SSE inner loop is still poll-based against Postgres now instead of MinIO. The push flip is a follow-up slice — the table supports it; only the route's inner loop changes.
- **No SPA EventSource consumer yet.** Slice 1's frontend deferral still applies; that's a separate follow-up PR.

## Test plan
- [x] 3 new integration tests: reads-from-postgres-when-present (marker check), falls-back-to-minio-for-legacy-trial (existing fixture exercises this), stream-serves-postgres-events
- [x] 11 unit tests for the MinIO helpers still pass — they cover the fallback path now
- [x] 8 existing route-integration tests still pass via the MinIO fallback (their fixture has no Postgres rows seeded)
- [x] \`uv run ruff check src tests\` + \`uv run mypy\` — clean (272 source files)

## Performance note
The (trial_id, seq) UNIQUE index makes the primary read O(log N) instead of the previous "fetch + split the entire MinIO JSONL" O(N). For a 100k-event trial, that's the difference between a per-poll multi-MB object fetch and an indexed lookup over up to 200 rows.

author: kelvinxxle
body:
## Summary

Shared M1 `PlayerControls` bug, surfaced during M3. The right-hand transport group (`src/components/player/PlayerControls.tsx`) used `flex-1` without `min-w-0`, and the `type="range"` scrubber inside it was also `flex-1` with no `min-w-0`.

A flex child will not shrink below its content's intrinsic minimum width unless its `min-width` is `0`. So the scrubber refused to shrink, and the whole group overflowed its column to the right.

## User-facing impact

The left workbench `<section>` (transport) and the right pseudocode `<aside>` are siblings. Because the aside is painted after the section, it stacks on top of any content the section overflows into its lane. On a tall-pseudocode topic (Union-Find has a 13-line pseudocode panel) the overflowing speed buttons slid under the pseudocode panel, so a click on `4x` landed on the pseudocode line (`data-line="13"`) instead. The `4x` speed control was effectively unclickable at the standard desktop viewport.

## Fix

Minimal and surgical: add `min-w-0` to the right-hand group and to the scrubber so the range can actually shrink, keeping the speed buttons inside their column with nothing overlaying them. No other restyling, no behavior change otherwise. Two class additions:

- group: `flex flex-1 ...` to `flex min-w-0 flex-1 ...`
- scrubber: `h-1 flex-1 ...` to `h-1 min-w-0 flex-1 ...`

## RED-first regression

`e2e/player-controls.spec.ts` (new, focused spec). jsdom cannot compute layout or hit-testing, so this guard is a Playwright e2e. It loads Union-Find at the default desktop viewport (1280) and asserts the `4x` button owns its own click target (nothing overlays its center) and that clicking it actually selects `4x` (`aria-pressed` becomes `true`).

Verified RED before the fix: on the unfixed build the element at the `4x` button's center is the pseudocode `data-line="13"` div, so the test fails. Verified GREEN after the fix.

## Scope note

The workbench chrome is fixed at 256px (left nav) plus 384px (pseudocode aside), so the transport row needs roughly 1280px of viewport to lay out in a single line. This PR resolves the flexbox overflow at that design width, which is where the bug reproduces and where the Playwright Desktop Chrome viewport sits. A responsive redesign of the single-row controls for sub-1280 widths (wrapping or a collapsed scrubber) is a separate concern and intentionally out of scope here.

## Definition of done

- `npm run format:check`: pass
- `npm run lint`: 0
- `npm run typecheck`: 0
- `npm test`: 703 passed
- `npm run build`: success
- `npm run test:e2e` (isolated server, workers=1): 69 passed, including the new spec
- `npm audit --audit-level=high`: 0 vulnerabilities

author: 10d9e
body:
## Model

opus 4.8

## Approach

Fuse forward len=64 + len=16 stages into one radix-16 pass
The two strided radix-4 forward stages (half-blocks 64 and 16) each
round-tripped the full xab spectrum through linear memory. Fuse them into a
single radix-16 = radix-4(len=64) ∘ radix-4(len=16) pass: for each 256-block
and offset jj in 0..16, gather the 16 elements at stride 16, run both radix-4
sub-stages in registers, and scatter back — halving this section's memory
traffic (~1 store + 1 load per element per prime removed).

Two details make it a win rather than the regression a naive version gives:
  * The 16-element tile is held in sixteen explicit named locals, not a [L;16]
    array — under the strided gather/scatter LLVM keeps named locals in wasm
    locals (free), whereas the array fails SROA and spills to memory.
  * The loop is column(jj)-outer so each butterfly's five twiddle vectors are
    loaded once and reused across the four 256-blocks, matching the hoisting
    the separate butterfly-outer stages had.

Sub-stage A (len=64) twiddles are w^{4jj+64k} for group k; sub-stage B (len=16)
shares w^{16jj}. Output is bit-identical (same wasm checksums; native gate and
all 32 fixtures pass). WORK 8325888 -> 8009088.

## Validation

`bash scripts/evaluate.sh` passed locally; only `src/algorithm/` changed.

## Summary

Closes #93 (and largely overlaps #89's pre-submit guard ask).

Pre-fix: the only pre-submit gate on §10 internal-customer DNs checked warehouse/GIT routing. Item-sync was checked **post-submit** in \`_run_preconditions\` — misses landed on Drift + Failed Sync Record *after* the DN already submitted. The reporter (DL-260578 on \`live16version.frappe.cloud\`) wanted the save itself blocked with a clear, actionable message naming the unsynced item_code.

## Implementation

Refactored the Item-Map check into a shared helper \`_unmapped_items_for_dn(dn)\` and wired it into **both** surfaces:
- \`_run_preconditions\` (post-submit, accumulates to Drift) — unchanged behaviour, just refactored to use the helper
- \`validate_pre_submit\` (pre-submit, throws to block save) — **new guard**

Both surfaces use the same source of truth so they stay consistent.

**HARD RULE preserved**: the guard is scoped to internal-customer / §10 DNs only. External-customer Delivery Notes are completely unaffected (the existing \`is_section10\` short-circuit at the top of \`validate_pre_submit\` handles this).

## Throw message shape

> \`DN line(s) reference Item(s) not yet synced to EasyEcom: 'FG20077', 'FG20088'. Run §8d Item Push (open each Item and click Push to EasyEcom, or use Push All Pending Items from the EasyEcom Account form) before saving this internal-transfer Delivery Note.\`

Names every unsynced item_code in one throw so the FDE doesn't have to re-save after each fix.

## Test plan

- [x] 6 unit tests in \`test_validate_pre_submit_item_map_guard.py\`:
  - Single unsynced item → actionable throw with item_code named
  - Multiple unsynced items → all listed in one throw
  - All synced → passes through silently
  - **External-customer DN → completely unaffected** (verified \`frappe.db.exists\` is never even called)
  - Helper \`_unmapped_items_for_dn\` returns correct list
  - §10 routing throw (Transfer From/To missing) still runs **before** the Item Map check (ordering preservation)
